jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Account Officer Staff
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Business Parter (Petugas Lapangan)
jobs.description:
amartha membuka kesempatan berkarier sebagai business parter (petugas lapangan) untuk penempatan kerja di wilayah banjar, hulu sungai, tanah laut, dan tanah bumbu (regional kalimantan). bertanggung jawab dalam menyusun strategi sales dan marketing sebagai arahan tim guna mencapai target yang ditentukan. fasilitas dan benefit yang disediakan meliputi gaji umk, thr, uang bensin sebesar 50 ribu per minggu, tunjangan servis kendaraan, jenjang karier, serta fasilitas mess atau tempat tinggal.

kandidat memiliki pendidikan minimal sma/smk sederajat. terbuka bagi pelamar berpengalaman maupun lulusan baru (fresh graduate). mampu menyusun strategi penjualan dan pemasaran untuk panduan tim mencapai target. memiliki kendaraan bermotor pribadi dan sim c aktif. bersedia untuk ditempatkan di seluruh wilayah kerja amartha wilayah regional kalimantan.

jobs.title: Team Event Bandung
jobs.description:
pt. primafood international membuka lowongan kerja untuk posisi team event penempatan bandung. posisi ini bertanggung jawab dalam pengelolaan event promosi, pelaksanaan strategi pemasaran ritel modern, analisis data penjualan atau event, serta siap melakukan mobilitas atau perjalanan kerja di area bandung dan sekitarnya.

pria atau wanita. terbuka untuk lulusan s1 maupun sma/smk semua jurusan. memiliki pengalaman kerja minimal 1 tahun di bidang retail, sales marketing, atau event organizer. memiliki kemampuan negosiasi, public speaking, dan pengelolaan event. memahami alur bisnis ritel modern, pemasaran, serta analisa data dengan baik. menguasai pengoperasian ms. office. bersedia melakukan mobilitas kerja. memiliki kendaraan bermotor pribadi beserta sim c, diutamakan memiliki sim a dan bisa mengendarai mobil. menyiapkan surat lamaran dan cv terbaru.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Supervisor
jobs.description:
posisi middle mile supervisor di spx express bertanggung jawab untuk memantau dan memimpin operasional middle mile baik dari pihak 3pl maupun internal. tugas utamanya meliputi kolaborasi dengan tim terkait untuk mengelola lead time, durasi pengiriman, dan kebutuhan trip, berkoordinasi dengan tim fleet untuk memastikan kesiapan unit, melakukan pemetaan rute, memaksimalkan penggunaan unit, serta mengalokasikan perencanaan sumber daya untuk implementasi baru di distribution center.

pendidikan minimal sma atau diploma dari semua jurusan. memiliki pengalaman kerja selama 3-5 tahun di industri transportasi, logistik, atau rantai pasokan. berpengalaman dalam menangani operasi darat, udara, maupun laut. mahir menggunakan microsoft office dan memiliki keterampilan komunikasi yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shifting dan ditempatkan di area yang telah ditentukan.

pendidikan minimal sma atau diploma dari jurusan apapun. memiliki pengalaman kerja selama 3-5 tahun di industri transportasi, logistik, atau rantai pasokan. berpengalaman dalam menangani operasi darat, udara, maupun laut. mahir mengoperasikan microsoft office dan memiliki keterampilan komunikasi yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shifting dan ditempatkan di area yang telah ditentukan.

jobs.title: Sortation Center Shift Lead
jobs.description:
bertanggung jawab memantau operasional harian sortation center (soc) mencakup pengawasan proses inbound, sortation, bagging, reprocessing, dan outbound. memastikan operasional berjalan sesuai standard operating procedure (sop), merencanakan alokasi tenaga kerja sesuai fluktuasi volume harian, memantau kapasitas serta produktivitas peralatan, dan memimpin pengarahan tim rutin terkait laporan performa kerja serta penerapan 5s.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk sederajat atau lebih tinggi. memiliki pengalaman kerja 2-3 tahun di bidang logistik, pergudangan, atau sejenis dengan jabatan kepala gudang atau supervisor. memiliki keterampilan komunikasi dan kepemimpinan yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shift dan siap ditempatkan di dungingi dc, kota gorontalo.

jobs.title: Deputy Safety Advisor - Syria (national position)
jobs.description:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organisation (INSO) is an international non-governmental organisation that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations and training. INSO works in 26 of the world’s most insecure countries, with its headquarters in The Hague, the international city of peace and justice.

**INSO Syria**

The Syria program supports more than 290 NGOs to deliver vitally needed aid and assistance to an estimated 13.1 million people in need across the country. First launched as an emergency response operation in 2014, INSO Syria has grown to become a program covering all Syrian governorates, with a Country Office in Damascus.

The Syria conflict is unique and complex; you will find that every day is different and there is always more to learn.

**Job summary**

The Deputy Safety Advisor works with the Safety Advisor (SA) to fulfil INSO’s core mission of helping NGOs in a given region understand the context and mitigate risks. The Deputy Safety Advisor is involved in information collection and data input, analysis and reporting, crisis management support, networking with various stakeholders, among other areas. The DSA supports the SA in ensuring INSO services are relevant and correspond to evolving partners’ needs in the field (principle of proximity). Moreover, this position supports SA in the management of a local information network and manages the team/office in SA absence.

**This position covers the East region (covering Deir Ez Zor and Hasakeh governorates) and is based in INSO’s Qamishli office. Periodic travel to conduct assessments, field visits, and meet partners is required.**

**Main Responsibilities**

- Assist the SA with the regional representation of INSO and the delivery of services.
- Coordinate the national team in the region and lead service delivery in SA’s absence.
- Collect and verify incidents and events in the region that relate to the safety of NGO workers operating in the area.
- Manage and update incident databases to ensure the organisation’s records are accurate and complete. Support and verify incident entries made by ASA to CHDC.
- Assist the Safety Advisor in preparing and issuing regular reports, area assessments, and other INSO products requested by the aid community.
- Work with the Safety Advisor to analyse the operating environment and identify trends. Use data and databases to create charts, data visualisations, and maps.
- Lead and deliver on-the-ground assessments by conducting frequent field missions and engaging with stakeholders/authorities.
- Work in proximity with NGO partners in the field
- Attend regular humanitarian coordination meetings to build relations with partners and remain up to date on humanitarian activities in the area.
- Work with the Safety Advisor and the SA Assistant to identify, hire, and train field monitors for the purposes of ensuring robust and even information collection.
- Translate relevant communications from local language(s) into the working language of the country office (English/Arabic) and vice versa.
- Monitor and interpret security dynamics at both the national and regional levels affecting humanitarian operations across the East region.
- Provide support to the East region in information collection, verification, analysis, and reporting, including the management of CHDC.
- Attend regular humanitarian coordination meetings to build relations with partners and remain up to date on humanitarian activities in the area.
- Lead the delivery of field assessments by conducting frequent field missions and engaging with stakeholders/authorities.
- Support the SA and, at times, lead in the production of security alerts, reports, snapshots and thematic reports.
- Provide support to NGOs during security incidents when requested.
- Coordinate and lead service delivery in the absence of the SA.
- Represent INSO and uphold the organisation’s principles of independence, neutrality, and impartiality in all engagements.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Experience**

- Minimum of two years' experience with NGO security and/or project management.
- Hands-on experience working with humanitarian organisations (UN, INGO, NGO or donor organisation) in Syria, either in a security, safety, access or programmatic position. Other relevant experience within the humanitarian sector will be considered.
- Working knowledge of security and conflict dynamics across all regions of Syria.
- Experience drafting reports with proven written and analytical skills and close attention to detail.
- Working proficiency in English and Arabic with excellent written and spoken skills.
- A strong understanding of NGO safety management best practices and a willingness to learn.
- A proven ability to develop and maintain working relationships with partners.
- Strong IT proficiency, including extensive experience using Windows and Microsoft Office applications.
- Willingness to periodically travel to conduct assessments and meet with partners.
- University degree (Bachelor) in social sciences, humanitarian affairs, security, or a related field, or relevant practical experience instead of a degree.

*Nice to Have*

- Experience in project/team management.
- Experience in crisis management and support to NGOs.
- Capacity to work with minimum supervision and maintain a high level of engagement.

**Core Competencies**

- Adaptability-Demonstrates flexibility, proactivity, and resilience in responding to changing priorities, diverse stakeholder needs, and high-pressure environments.
- Analytical Thinking-Applies critical thinking and sound judgment to analyze information, solve problems, identify risks, and make well-informed decisions.
- Integrity-Maintains the highest standards of confidentiality, ethics, and professionalism, while actively preventing conflicts of interest and fostering trust.
- Collaboration-Builds positive working relationships, communicates effectively, and works collaboratively within teams and multicultural environments to achieve common goals.
- Organization-Plans, prioritizes, and manages work effectively, demonstrating strong attention to detail and the ability to deliver high-quality results within deadlines.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable fixed-term contract, 1.75 working days annual leave per month, private health insurance coverage or allowance.

jobs.title: Global Protection Coordinator
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is seeking a highly qualified and experienced global protection coordinator to join the dynamic and ambitious global protection team (GPT).

**About the job**

The Global Protection Coordinator will be part of the global protection team and contribute to and enable DRC to continue developing and advancing its expertise, competencies, and role as a leading protection actor. The position is responsible for delivering technical advice and support to country offices in East Africa, Myanmar and Bangladesh to ensure high-quality protection programming, and will lead DRC’s component on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Support to Project Delivery and Programme Quality

- Contextualize DRC’s global protection sectoral standards, policies, and guidance, and provide technical support to country offices to ensure their effective application and adherence to quality protection programme standards.
- Provide strategic direction to country operations to ensure protection sectoral programming and approaches align with DRC’s mandate, align with donor priorities and the sectors comparative advantage
- Provide technical support and capacity building to country offices and DRC partners to ensure quality analysis, strategies, and measurement of responses, in adherence with DRC's global standards and principles.
- Support country offices in protection sectoral preparedness planning, including analysis, scenario planning, and technical input into contingency plans.
- Support quality assurance and learning in line with the Protection Program Quality Framework, including technical capacity assessments, technical quality assurance and capacity building efforts through in person and remote methods.

Support to Project and proposal development

- Provide protection sectoral technical review and/or support the development of proposals at the country level to ensure technical capacities and resources are appropriately planned, and donors’ requirements are met.
- Where relevant, promote integrated and innovative programmatic approaches through coordination with other sectors, incorporating climate resilience and environmental considerations, and advancing DRC’s localization commitments.

Support to global efforts and advocacy

- Contribute to the development and enhancement of DRC’s program approaches and guidelines, tools and standards based on evidence and learning from country offices.
- Promote the piloting, documentation, and scale-up of innovative sectoral approaches and tools, based on field experience and emerging trends.
- Engage with and represent DRC, where relevant, in fora and meetings with donors and external stakeholders with evidence-based learning in close collaboration with PAER.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect we expect you to have a minimum of 7 years of significant, progressively responsible experience in protection programming in the context of conflict and forced displacement, with a technical background in Mental health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- Proven experience of working with international organisation(s) in the field of protection at both the field and global levels
- Significant and demonstrable experience in providing high quality, in person and remote protection technical and strategic advice and support to country operations, across the project cycle.
- Demonstratable capacity building skills, including the design and facilitation of trainings / workshops
- Demonstrable problem-solving skills and ability to adopt flexible, creative, innovative approaches
- Significant experience with effectively coordinating with national partners, local/government authorities, NGO partners, UN and other relevant stakeholders.
- English proficiency is a requirement while ability to work in French is desirable.

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Minimum 12 months, but depending on the country and contract terms, the duration might be longer.

Work location: Nairobi, Kampala, Tunis or Copenhagen

Start date: February 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with DRC’s terms of employment.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Brennan Webert, Global Lead for Protection. We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [**drc.ngo**](https://drc.ngo/).

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

jobs.title: Global Protection Advisor – Gender-Based Violence in Emergencies (GBViE)
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is seeking a highly qualified and experienced global GBViE advisor to join the dynamic and ambitious global protection team (GPT).

**About the job**

The Global GBViE Advisor will be part of the global protection team and contribute to and enable DRC to continue developing and advancing its expertise, competencies, and role as a leading protection actor. The position is responsible for providing technical advisory services, including: 1) development of technical resources in the area of GBViE; 2) technical support to country offices implementing GBViE; 3) support to project and proposal development; and 4) support to global efforts and advocacy. Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Provision of high-level technical protection sectoral oversight and advisory support in GBV in Emergencies to ensure quality, consistency, and compliance across DRC programming.

**Protection Sectoral Technical Responsibility**

Technically responsible for the development and roll-out of global guidance, tools and capacity development on GBV in Emergencies. This may include, but is not limited to:

- Map and assess DRC’s existing GBViE interventions, technical capacities and gaps within protection programming. Identify good practices, priorities for strengthening specialized GBV prevention and response, and opportunities for integration with DRC’s core sectors.

jobs.title: PIR Caseworker
jobs.description:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

**Job Overview:**
The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. The role works closely with clients, internal teams, and external partners to develop and implement individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients to appropriate financial, medical, social, vocational, and community resources in alignment with program requirements, eligibility guidelines, and IRC standards.

**Major Responsibilities:**
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure clients have access to housing, food, medical care, transportation, and community orientation.
- Conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery and public transportation orientation, and other field-based services to address immediate client needs.
- Purchase and transport program-related items; lift, move, and deliver materials necessary for service delivery.
- Conduct client intake assessments and develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with clients.
- Provide ongoing case management through direct services, referrals, advocacy, and coordination with internal and external service providers.
- Monitor client progress toward established goals, identify barriers, and adjust service plans as needed.
- Document all client interactions accurately and in compliance with program requirements; enter and maintain client data in required databases and tracking tools.
- Support Preferred Communities programming and intensive case management services, as assigned.
- Collaborate with colleagues across programs and grants to ensure clients access all eligible services.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and service providers.
- Participate in program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with grant requirements.
- Use a personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation to travel within the service delivery area as needed.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required.
- Experience providing casework, pre-arrival, or intensive case management services preferred.
- Demonstrated experience navigating program eligibility requirements and ensuring accurate service documentation.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, diplomacy, and networking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to use digital tools for data entry, research, and reporting.
- Ability to lift and carry items weighing 50+ pounds, including furniture and household goods.
- Ability to drive a large van or passenger vehicle, as required for program delivery.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Working Environment**

This position operates in a hybrid environment that includes office-based work, remote work, and fieldwork within the service delivery area. Typically, the role is based in the office four days per week and remotely one day per week, with field responsibilities possible on all workdays. jobs.title: Terms of Reference for Knowledge Products Development Consultancy
jobs.description:
**The consultant reports to:**

Micheal Ojediran; micheal.ojediran@cbm-global.org; +234(0)816 333 4217

**Name of consultant:**

**(“Consultant”)**

**Description of consultancy**

Lead the development of a case study compendium showing how locally led partnerships with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and National Civil Society Organizations deliver sustainable, disability-inclusive change.

## Background and rationale

CBM Global Disability Inclusion Nigeria is committed to advancing disability-inclusive development through a localisation approach that places local actors at the centre of programming. Rather than directly implementing interventions within communities, CBM Global Nigeria works through a network of selected and supported implementing partners, including Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Youth-Led Organisations (YLOs), Women-Led Organisations (WLOs), National NGOs, and government institutions. This approach recognises that sustainable development outcomes are best achieved when indigenous organisations possess the skills, systems, resources, and leadership required to drive change within their own communities.

Over the years in Nigeria, CBM Global has invested significantly in strengthening the institutional capacity, technical expertise, governance structures, advocacy capabilities, and program delivery mechanisms of these implementing partners. These investments have enabled local actors to become more influential, resilient, and effective in promoting the rights and inclusion of persons with disabilities.

As the global development sector increasingly embraces localization, there is a need to systematically document lessons, evidence, successes, innovations, and challenges emerging from CBM Global Nigeria's partnership model. This case study compendium will serve as an important knowledge product that captures the experiences of partner organizations and demonstrates the value of shifting power and ownership to local actors.

## Purpose

The purpose of this consultancy is to document and communicate how CBM Global Nigeria's localised partnership model strengthens OPDs and other implementing partners and produces sustainable, inclusive results for persons with disabilities and communities. The Case Study Compendium will seek to achieve the following objectives:

1. **Document evidence of institutional strengthening** among OPDs and other implementing partners supported by CBM Global.
2. **Demonstrate the impact of localisation** by illustrating how investments in local leadership contribute to more effective, inclusive, and sustainable development and humanitarian outcomes.
3. **Capture lessons learned, innovations, and good practices** emerging from CBM Global’s partnership approach.
4. **Provide evidence for advocacy and resource mobilisation** by showcasing successful examples of locally led disability-inclusive development.
5. **Strengthen organizational learning and knowledge management** by preserving institutional experiences and insights that can inform future strategies and partnerships.
6. **Position CBM Global Nigeria as a thought leader** on disability-inclusive localisation and partnership-based programming within Nigeria and internationally.

## **Scope of Work**

The consultant will be responsible for:

- Conducting a comprehensive desk review of relevant CBM Global’s policy documents, project documents, project review or donor reports, project evaluations, and learning products of its Country Programmes to identify evidence, themes, and potential case studies related to localisation and partner strengthening.
- Engaging key stakeholders and partners, including OPDs, YLOs, WLOs, government institutions, and CBM Global staff, through interviews and consultations to gather insights, experiences, and stories of change.
- Document and develop at a minimum 10–15 high-quality case studies that showcase how CBM Global's support has strengthened implementing partner organisations, enhanced leadership of those organizations, promoted disability inclusion, and contributed to sustainable impact.
- Analyse findings and synthesise lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations on localization and locally led development to inform future programming, advocacy, and partnership approaches.
- Produce a publication-ready Case Study Compendium, including drafting, facilitating validation with stakeholders, incorporating feedback, and supporting the design and finalization of the knowledge product and accompanying summary materials

## Timeframe and duration

This is a 15‑day, consultancy requiring a fast‑paced and collaborative approach. The consultant will be expected to deliver:

**Deliverable**

**Timeline**

**Inception Meeting, Document Review and Detailed Work Plan**

Week 1

**Data Collection Tools, Interview Guides and Case Study Framework**

Week 1

**Stakeholder Consultations, Partner Interviews and Story Collection**

Week 2-3

**First Draft Case Study Compendium**

Week 4

**Validation Presentation and Workshop Report**

Week 5

**Revised Draft**

Week 6

**Final Publication-Ready Compendium (Designed and Edited)**

Week 8

**2-Page Case Study Snapshots**

Week 8

**PowerPoint Presentation of Findings and Key Insights**

Week 8

## Place/ location of service delivered

The consultancy will be primarily desk-based, with a combination of document review, virtual consultations, and stakeholder interviews.

1. **Required Expert Profile**

The consultant may be an individual or a small team. CBM Global is looking for:

- Minimum of seven (7) years' experience in research, knowledge management, documentation, organizational learning, or communications.
- Demonstrated experience developing high-quality case studies, learning publications, impact reports, or knowledge products for international NGOs, development agencies, or donors.
- Experience facilitating qualitative research and stakeholder consultations.
- Strong understanding of localisation-in-practice, locally led development, civil society strengthening, and disability-inclusive programming.
- Experience working with Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) will be an added advantage.

## Payment schedule

The consultancy attracts a professional fee payable upon satisfactory completion of all deliverables.

The schedule of payment for this consultancy includes:

- Signing Contract: First advance – 25%.
- Submission and acceptance of inception report, data tools and first draft: Second advance – 25%.
- Submission and acceptance of final report, datasets, transcripts, and PowerPoint Summary by CBM Global: Final payment – 50%.

jobs.title: Administration & Government Liaison Specialist
jobs.description:
**Vacancy Announcement: Administration & Government Liaison Specialist, Damascus, Syria**

**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

**Medecins du Monde Turkey (MDM-T) /** **Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**Organisation:**

DDD (MdM Türkiye)

**Duty Station:**

Damascus, Syria

**Contract Duration:**

6 months, renewable

**Reporting to:**

DAM Office Manager

**About the role**

DDD is recruiting an Administration & Government Liaison Specialist, based in the Damascus operational office, to coordinate the day-to-day administration of the office and provide administrative support to other locations in Syria as assigned by the Office Manager. The Specialist will oversee routine office services, travel arrangements and official visits, and follow up on DDD’s registrations, authorisations and other administrative procedures with the relevant public authorities.

The Specialist will maintain administrative records and calendars, coordinate with service providers and legal advisers as required, and keep the Office Manager informed of deadlines, outstanding decisions and issues that may affect operations.

**Key responsibilities**

*Office management and administrative support*

- Coordinate routine services for the Damascus office, including premises, utilities, office supplies and maintenance requests, liaising with IT support and Logistics as required.
- Monitor office leases and administrative service contracts, track renewal dates and prepare the documentation required for review and approval.
- Coordinate travel arrangements, accommodation, official visits and related administrative support for staff movements in accordance with DDD procedures.
- Support the administrative arrangements for opening, relocating or expanding offices, and provide practical support to other Syria field locations as required.
- Coordinate facilities, equipment and office service requests with Logistics & Assets and IT & Systems, follow up on service delivery and flag issues that affect office continuity.
- Prepare supporting documentation for administrative expenditure and commitments and route it through the established approval process.

*Government liaison and administrative formalities*

- Maintain working contacts with the relevant ministries, public administrations and local authorities for routine administrative procedures.
- Compile and track documentation for organisational registrations, authorisations, renewals and other administrative formalities, in coordination with country management, HQ and legal advisers as appropriate.
- Prepare draft official correspondence and coordinate the submission, collection and follow-up of documents within delegated authority, keeping a record of submissions, responses and outstanding actions.
- Maintain a calendar of formal obligations and notify the relevant teams of upcoming deadlines, changes in administrative requirements and delays that may affect operations.
- Coordinate external follow-up for employment-related submissions when required, using documentation prepared and verified by HR and, where applicable, Finance.
- Organise the administrative and protocol arrangements for meetings and official visits involving public authorities.

*Records and administrative procedures*

- Maintain orderly records for registrations, authorisations, leases, service contracts, official correspondence and supporting documentation.
- Establish practical registers, checklists and filing rules for recurring administrative procedures, and clarify how offices submit requests and how pending actions are tracked.
- Provide periodic updates on office administration, pending government procedures and decisions requiring management attention.
- Prepare administrative records for internal reviews, audits and compliance checks.

The Specialist reports to the Office Manager and works with HR, Finance and the relevant Logistics and IT counterparts on matters requiring their input. The Specialist maintains functional coordination with HQ General Services and works with legal advisers on documentation and formalities as required. The Specialist handles routine administrative contact and follow-up with public authorities, including assigned procedures concerning DDD’s registrations and authorisations in Syria. Institutional representation, formal commitments and signatures remain with the Country Director or the authorised signatory, in accordance with DDD’s delegation of authority.

**Initial priorities**

- Review the Damascus office’s administrative arrangements, including premises, utilities, service contracts and outstanding commitments.
- Establish a register of DDD’s registrations, authorisations, official correspondence and pending administrative procedures in Syria.
- Put in place routine procedures for office services, travel, document filing and follow-up with public authorities.

**Required profile**

- Relevant university qualification in business administration, management, law, public administration or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience in office administration and in dealing with public authorities, official documentation or administrative formalities in Syria.
- Experience coordinating office services, liaising with service providers and maintaining accurate administrative records.
- Ability to draft formal correspondence in Arabic and communicate with country management, HQ and external counterparts.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to track multiple procedures, deadlines and documents.
- Professional working proficiency in Arabic and English.

**Expected professional competencies**

- Organisational judgement: identifies administrative priorities, anticipates deadlines and distinguishes material compliance risks from routine issues.
- Operational autonomy: organises priorities, takes initiative and resolves day-to-day administrative problems without continuous supervision.
- Practical problem-solving: develops simple, reliable and workable administrative solutions adapted to operational constraints.
- Collaboration: maintains constructive working relationships with operational teams, HQ counterparts, public administrations and external advisers.
- Reliability and confidentiality: commitment to accurate administrative records, professional discretion, data confidentiality and consistent application of procedures.
- Adaptability: willingness to work in an evolving organisational environment where some systems, procedures and responsibilities remain under development.

**Compliance & Ethics**
Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**
Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.

**NB:** Considering the purpose and values of the organisation, DDD requests to its employee complete flexibility in term of duties and commitment, as their job description and job title can be adjusted throughout the year according to needs and priorities.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Please be advised that female candidates are highly encouraged.

*Dünya Doktorları Derneği is an equal opportunity employer whereby we ensure all hiring and employment decisions, and operates all programs, services, and functions without the practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information or any other status or characteristic protected under applicable law.*

**Closure Date: 30.11.2026**

Due to the urgency to fill this post, DDD reserves the right to review the CVs on a rolling basis and selected candidates may be interviewed prior to the closing dates listed, therefore early applications are encouraged.
DDD is not in a position to respond to every applicant individually due to the anticipated high number of applications.
Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the first interview.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

**General Information**
DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.

jobs.title: Human Resources Officer - Damascus
jobs.description:
The HR Officer ensures that HR administration at DCA Syria is accurate, timely, confidential and compliant with DCA policies, staff regulations and applicable national labour law. Reporting to the HR Coordinator, the position covers personnel files, recruitment support, contract administration, onboarding and offboarding, and leave and attendance for all staff across the country office and its field locations. It acts as the first point of contact for line managers on HR matters, prepares documents for the HR Coordinator’s approval, escalates complex or sensitive cases, and handles confidential data under strict access and retention rules.

**Functional Responsibilities**

- Acts as first point of contact for line managers on HR administration of their teams, escalating complex or sensitive cases to the HR Coordinator when necessary.
- Ensures HR practice complies with DCA policies, staff regulations, HR procedures and applicable national labour law, including social security requirements.
- Contributes to drafting local HR policies, procedures and tools (such as salary scales, promotion procedures and personnel file standards) and implements them once approved.
- Contributes to implementing the country office’s HR priorities and annual HR strategy so that HR supports operational needs.
- Creates and maintains complete, confidential personnel files (physical and digital) for all staff: contracts, ID copies, certificates, performance evaluations, training records, and disciplinary or grievance documents.
- Runs quarterly file audits against a standard checklist and follows up on missing or expired documents.
- Keeps the HRIS and staff lists up to date with new hires, changes and separations.
- Applies data-protection and confidentiality rules, including access control, retention and archiving.
- Supports recruitment by screening applications, preparing shortlists, arranging interviews and conducting reference checks, in line with DCA procedures.
- Prepares contracts, amendments, extensions, transfers, acting-up arrangements and separation documents for approval by the HR Coordinator.
- Confirms with line managers and Finance that contract terms match approved job descriptions, grades, budgets and donor funding.
- Maintains a contract tracker and alerts line managers at least 60 days before contract end dates, and ahead of probation reviews and renewals.
- Prepares employment, salary and other HR letters on request, for approval by the HR Coordinator.
- Ensures onboarding (induction documentation, policy acknowledgements) and offboarding (clearance, final entitlements, exit documents) are completed and filed.
- Follows up probation evaluations with line managers and files the DCA form signed by staff and line manager.
- Supports the performance management cycle with reminders, collection of evaluations and filing.
- Maintains training records for all staff and ensures training logistics are in place to support learning and development.
- Maintains accurate records of all leave types (annual, sick, maternity and paternity, unpaid, special) and up-to-date leave balances.
- Verifies timesheets, attendance and overtime against leave records, and advises staff and managers on leave entitlements on request.
- Provides Finance with verified monthly HR inputs for payroll (contract changes, leave, attendance).
- Prepares monthly or quarterly reports (headcount, turnover, contract expiries, leave liabilities) and supports audits and donor verification.
- Maintains and improves HR forms, templates and filing systems, and supports HR projects.

**Minimum qualifications and experience**

- Bachelor’s degree in human resources, business administration or a related field.
- At least 4 years of HR experience covering HR administration, recruitment and personnel management, and payroll support.
- Working knowledge of Syrian labour law and social security procedures.
- Fluent written and spoken Arabic and English.
- Good command of MS Office (especially Excel), and experience with HRIS or HR databases.
- High level of discretion, attention to detail and ability to work to deadlines.

jobs.title: Compliance and data security analyst
jobs.description:
**We're hiring**

**Compliance and data security analyst**

**LOCATION: Amsterdam, Netherlands**
0.8 FTE / 32 hours per week

**GROSS SALARY RANGE: EUR 33,446-38,275**

Laterite is looking for a Compliance and Data Security Analyst to help our research teams meet privacy, information-security and client obligations. You will improve how we manage compliance, set up missing processes and work with colleagues across our country offices to put agreed actions into practice.

**This position is open to candidates of all nationalities who have the legal right to work in the Netherlands. Please note that we are unable to provide sponsorship.**

**WHO WE ARE**

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex international development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 80+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles.

**THE ENVIRONMENT YOU'RE STEPPING INTO**

You will join our Netherlands team in a collaborative and engaging environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won't be micromanaged here. We want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced teams and improve the systems you work with. You will report to our Operations Manager and work closely with our Analytics team, Data Protection Officers, and research, operations and technical colleagues across country offices. Your work will help keep compliance practical and manageable for colleagues.

**HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT**

You will help protect the data entrusted to Laterite and make compliance easier to maintain across our research and operations. During your first six months, you will take over recurring work and help address an agreed set of priority gaps.

***An important note on this role***

**You will help build and improve our compliance processes.** Some routines are already in place, while others need to be developed with the Operations Manager and DPOs. We are developing processes that colleagues can use without unnecessary administration.

**Laterite is not a technology company but is building tech products to complement our research and social impact work.** Your experience on Laterite's Analytics team will be unique and likely dissimilar to similar roles within technology companies.

**The DPOs lead on local requirements and regulatory changes.** You will help coordinate follow-up across countries and help check that agreed actions are implemented. Management retains policy approval and risk decisions. This role is not an appointment as DPO or sole legal or technical security lead.

**Technical work will reflect your experience and the agreed scope**. This includes routine Google Workspace administration and assessing device-management improvements with technical colleagues. Implementation and any wider endpoint responsibilities will be agreed separately.

Your responsibilities will include:

- **Design and set up missing compliance processes**, working with the Operations Manager and DPOs to address applicable legal requirements and agreed priorities.
- **Improve how we manage compliance with the Operations Manager**. Make processes easy to maintain and reduce unnecessary work for colleagues.
- **Coordinate the DPO group and follow up implementation across countries**. The DPOs lead on local requirements and regulatory changes. Keep actions moving and flag gaps or delays to the Operations Manager.
- **Help assess and roll out device-management improvements with technical colleagues**. Follow up security reviews and agreed actions on access, backups, incident procedures and secure software development.
- **Support privacy work across research projects**, including processing records, initial privacy checks, approved agreements and notices, training, and follow-up on data requests or incidents. Arrange specialist review where needed.
- **Prepare client security questionnaires and keep supplier and subprocessor records current**, including AI services. Check that responses are supported by evidence and reviewed before submission.
- **Maintain compliance records and supporting evidence**. Follow up agreed actions with colleagues and prepare short progress updates.
- **Carry out agreed Google Workspace administration**, such as account setup and closure, using approved procedures. Technical duties will reflect your experience and agreed responsibilities.

You will manage agreed routines independently, ask for specialist input when needed and keep colleagues informed of progress. The Operations Manager, DPOs and technical colleagues will support you in the areas they lead.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

You have one to three years of practical experience in privacy, information security, compliance or operations, with examples of improving processes and completing work independently. You enjoy bringing structure to complex workflows and draw energy from working on data and cybersecurity.

Specifically, you have:

- A bachelor's or master's degree in law, cybersecurity, information systems, business information technology, security studies or a related field.
- Working knowledge of GDPR and the ability to explain privacy and security requirements clearly.
- Experience keeping reliable records, checking evidence and following up actions independently.
- The ability to design workable processes and reduce unnecessary administration.
- Confidence coordinating teams across offices and raising gaps or delays constructively.
- Clear written and spoken English. Dutch is not required or preferred.
- Good judgment about when to seek legal or technical advice.

In addition, we welcome:

- Experience with client questionnaires, audits or supplier and subprocessor reviews.
- Experience in research, international operations or international development.
- Familiarity with Google Workspace administration, endpoint security or device management.
- Interest in learning across privacy, information security and operations.
- Familiarity with secure software development.

We consider practical experience alongside qualifications. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be exactly who we're looking for.

**WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU**

- **Competitive compensation.** EUR 33,446-38,275 gross per year at 0.8 FTE, including holiday allowance, commensurate with experience, plus 18.4 days of annual leave. Salaries are pegged against Laterite's pay matrix and grades are reviewed every 12 months.
- **Professional growth.** Laterite provides an annual learning budget of up to USD 1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year. You will also have the chance to apply your skills in an organisation working in the social sectors.
- **Flexibility.** 32 hours per week (0.8 FTE), with 0.6 or 1 FTE open for discussion. You can work from home a couple of days per week and from a remote location of your choice for up to 6 weeks per year. Our office is in the heart of Amsterdam, about a fifteen-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal Station.

jobs.title: Climate Fundraising Expert
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate Fundraising Expert!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The EcoShift project aims to enable MSF to access new, non-cannibalising funding streams for climate mitigation and adaptation in support of our medical humanitarian mission by establishing the strategic, operational, and fundraising foundations required to engage effectively with climate-focused donors. Sponsored by MSF Operational Center Geneva and funded by the Transformational Investment Capacity, it is intended for the entire MSF movement.

Within the ecoShift project, the Climate Fundraising Expert develops a compelling case for support and a fundraising strategy for MSF’s international Climate Fund to mobilise donor support across the movement. Central to the role is building the knowledge, skills and confidence of philanthropy teams in MSF sections to navigate the specificities of climate fundraising, including donor motivations and expectations and the links between climate action and MSF’s medical humanitarian mission. The Expert works alongside these teams to translate this expertise into effective implementation of the strategy in their respective markets.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

The core responsibilities of the ecoShift Climate Fundraising expert are:

- Create a robust, donor-ready case for support, translating MSF’s climate-relevant work into compelling, fundable propositions and clearly articulating the links between climate action and MSF’s medical humanitarian mission. Develop the corresponding donor-facing materials and content, including fundraising brochures, and presentations, ensuring consistent and compelling messaging across formats.
- Building on ecoShift phase 1, develop a fundraising strategy for the Climate Fund, defining fundraising objectives, priority donor segments and a donor engagement roadmap. Ground the strategy in an assessment of climate-aligned donor prospects and funding opportunities - including philanthropic and institutional donors and climate-specific funding mechanisms - considering their priorities, eligibility criteria and funding modalities, with a particular focus on donors new to MSF.
- Build the capacity of philanthropy teams in priority markets to engage in climate fundraising through practical tools, a dedicated SharePoint site, ongoing guidance, and peer learning, focusing on climate terminology and concepts, donor motivations and expectations, and communicating climate-related impact within MSF’s medical humanitarian mission.
- Work alongside philanthropy teams in MSF sections to adapt and implement the strategy in their markets. Jointly develop and implement donor-specific engagement plans, supporting, when relevant, initial relationship-building, donor presentations and follow-up, while strengthening teams’ capacity through practical experience and shared learning.
- Monitor progress against fundraising objectives and the development of the donor pipeline with participating sections. Use results, donor feedback and teams’ experience to refine the strategy, engagement approaches and capacity-building support.
- Contribute to the preparation and implementation of the handover plan for the International Office (IO) fundraising team, ensuring continuity of the fundraising strategy, support to section teams and climate fundraising expertise during the transition to “Business As Usual” phase, that the Expert may be part of.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University degree in Business Management, Marketing, Environmental studies, Communications, or International Relations or equivalent professional experience

*Experience*

- At least five years’ experience in philanthropy or institutional fundraising, including demonstrated success in securing support for climate-related initiatives.
- Proven experience developing fundraising strategies, compelling cases for support and tailored donor proposals.
- Experience designing and delivering training, coaching or practical support to fundraising teams.
- Experience working across countries and organisational entities.
- Familiarity with MSF or medical humanitarian organisations is an asset.

*Languages*

- English and French are the working languages of MSF Switzerland. Excellent written and spoken English, C1 necessary.
- French, B2 an asset.

*Technical & Functional Knowledge*

- Strong understanding of climate philanthropy and relevant funding mechanisms, including donor priorities, eligibility requirements and funding modalities.
- Sound knowledge of climate concepts, including mitigation, adaptation, resilience and decarbonisation, and their connections to health and humanitarian action.
- Ability to translate technical climate information into credible fundraising propositions and communicate climate-related results accurately.
- Knowledge of prospect research, donor cultivation, proposal development, stewardship and pipeline management.
- Familiarity with adult learning approaches and the development of practical fundraising resources.

*Skills*

- Strategic thinking combined with the ability to translate plans into practical action.
- Excellent writing, presentation and interpersonal communication skills.
- Strong facilitation and coaching skills, with the ability to adapt support to different levels of knowledge and experience.
- Ability to build trust, influence and coordinate across teams without direct managerial authority.
- Strong analytical, organisational and project management skills.
- Excellent ability to work in a multicultural environment successfully and to demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviour and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Part-time position 80% (32h/week)
- Fixed-term contract, until 31.07.2027
- Working place: Any MSF HQ office that allows sufficient overlap with the team’s working hours.
- Ideal start date: February 1st, 2027
- The position may be hosted by different MSF entities. The final contracting entity, duty station and applicable employment conditions will be determined by MSF according to organisational needs, contractual feasibility and internal validation.

jobs.title: Human Resources Assistant (Daily-Worker) - Damascus
jobs.description:
The HR Assistant is responsible for the day-to-day running of HR data archiving (physical and digital) and the administrative side of the recruitment process. The role works under the guidance of the HR Coordinator, handles confidential information, and does not take selection or approval decisions.

**Functional Responsibilities**

- Organise, scan, index and file HR documents (physical and digital) following the DCA personnel file standard and naming convention.
- Create and complete new joiner files from the checklist, and update existing files as documents change.
- Track missing or expired documents, and prepare follow-up lists for the HR Coordinator.
- Support the collection and filing of documents from staff, including during all-staff document requests.
- Maintain the archive index and staff document trackers, and make sure files are retrievable on request.
- Apply confidentiality, access-control, retention and archiving rules, and keep files secure at all times.
- Prepare and publish vacancy announcements as instructed, and keep the vacancy tracker up to date.
- Receive and register applications, and keep the recruitment records and candidate data organised.
- Prepare longlists and screening sheets for review by the HR Coordinator and hiring managers.
- Schedule interviews and tests, contact candidates, prepare interview packs, and record interview outcomes.
- Send reference check forms and regret messages as instructed, and file the replies.
- Compile complete recruitment files for each vacancy (advertisement, applications, scoring sheets, selection reports, references).
- Support onboarding by collecting and filing new joiner documents.
- Keep candidate information strictly confidential.
- Prepare reports and summaries on archive status and recruitment activity (open vacancies, files complete or incomplete) when requested.
- Suggest improvements to filing systems, forms and templates.

**Minimum qualifications and experience**

- University degree or diploma in human resources, business administration, management or a related field.
- At least 1 year of experience in HR or administrative support, including filing and documentation.
- Good command of MS Office (Word and Excel); able to scan, index and manage digital files.
- Fluent Arabic and good working English.
- Strong attention to detail, organisation and discretion with confidential information.

jobs.title: OFICIAL DE ADMINISTRACION Y FINANZAS
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
**OBJETIVO DEL TRABAJO**

El (la) oficial de administración y finanzas, garantizará el cumplimiento de los procedimientos administrativos, de recursos humanos (RRHH) y finanzas de acuerdo con las políticas internas de ACTED y de los donantes en la base de Carabobo.

El (la) oficial de administración y finanzas, trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del gerente de base y en coordinación con los diferentes de departamentos de la oficina central de Caracas.

**Funciones y Responsabilidades**

**1. Finanzas**

- Asegurar el seguimiento del presupuesto/control de gastos de los proyectos a través del BFU proporcionado desde el departamento financiero de Caracas.
- Apoyar en la elaboración de presupuestos para nuevos proyectos cuando sea requerido.
- Monitorear la conformidad de los documentos financieros.
- Gestionar la tesorería de la base de Carabobo.
- Realizar y gestionar los pagos en efectivos cuando sean autorizados según los procedimientos internos de ACTED y la regulación de los donantes.
- Realizar el arqueo de caja y completar el CFU semanalmente.
- Apoyar en la evaluación de las necesidades mensuales de efectivo para la base.
- Elaborar y verificar las cuentas de cobro del personal para la gestión efectiva de sus honorarios profesionales.
- Garantizar la ejecución oportuna de pagos a proveedores.
- Apoyo en auditorias, escaneo verificación, corrección de piezas y expedientes, hasta cerrar de manera satisfactoria los archivos para la organización y donantes.
- Recibir, enviar, registrar, distribuir, archivar y mantener física y digitalmente los documentos de archivo en las unidades de conservación e instalación de acuerdo con los procedimientos.

**2. Administración**

- Apoyar técnicamente el proceso de transferencias documentales.
- Elaborar, tramitar y mantener seguimiento oportuno de las actividades y procedimientos a desarrollar.
- Apoyo logístico, organizar las solicitudes de compra y/o servicio de acuerdo con los procedimientos de la organización y de los donantes.
- Desarrollar y actualizar los procesos administrativos de Acted: reglamento interno, Manual de procedimientos, memos, etc.
- Seguimiento y actualización de los procesos legales: representación legal, registros diversos (Ministerios e instituciones Públicas, etc.).
- Gestionar los contratos administrativos (oficinas, guest-house) y el seguimiento administrativo (renovación de contratos, relación con los puntos focales, etc.).

**3. Recursos Humanos**

- Asegurarse de que los equipos de la base conocen, entienden, aplican y respetan el reglamento interno de ACTED.
- Reclutamiento (en coordinación con el Departamento de Recursos Humanos) del personal nacional de la base.
- Revisión de los TDR de los equipos a fin de actualizarlos y ajustarlos a los contratos laborales.
- Gestionar el seguimiento administrativo de los documentos de los empleados (seguimiento de las vacaciones, de las ausencias, del pago de los cargos sociales, etc.).
- Junto con el gerente de base hacer el seguimiento de las evaluaciones anuales.
- Proponer planes de formaciones de los empleados cuando es necesario.
- Soporte en relaciones laborales y administración del personal.
- Apoyar el establecimiento de buenas relaciones interpersonales de trabajo en la base. (Resolución de conflictos).
- Controlar los archivos de Recursos Humanos.
- Liquidación de nómina, gestión de seguridad social y novedades relacionados con los contratos del personal contratado.
- Apoyar el desarrollo y actualización de las políticas de gestión nacional de recursos humanos.
- Atender y dar respuesta oportuna a los requerimientos, dudas o solicitudes administrativas presentadas por el staff.
- ## Requisitos
- Obligatorios:
- Profesional graduado titulado (a) como administrador de empresas, ingeniero industrial, contador público o carreras afines.
- Al menos tres (3) años de experiencia en administración y finanzas. (Preferiblemente en una ONG internacional).
- Experiencia en el trato con socios nacionales y autoridades locales/gubernamentales
- Experiencia en habilidades organizativas comprobadas.
- Experiencia trabajando en entornos de trabajo multicultural
- Manejo avanzado de herramientas de reporte financiero y control de gastos.
- Conocimiento de procesos de procura y normativas de transparencia.
- Dominio de Paquete Microsoft Office
- Habilidades blandas: dinamismo, liderazgo, gestión de equipo, autonomía, alta atención al detalle, responsabilidad, comunicación asertiva, orientación a resultados, transparencia, flexibilidad.
- **Competencias:**
- Compromiso con la transparencia en el manejo de fondos y procesos de selección.
- Capacidad para la organización y priorización de actividades.
- Orientación al servicio: disposición para dar respuesta a los requerimientos con amabilidad, empatía y respeto, incluso en situaciones bajo presión.
- Capacidad de atención al detalle.

## Condiciones

- Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de Honorarios Profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de ACTED en Carabobo - Venezuela.
- Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.

Trabajo presencial y posibles viajes a las bases.
