jobs.title: Protection Assistant - 1 Tal Abyad, 1 Ras Al-Ayn
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Protection Assistant supports the day-to-day implementation of protection activities within the project, ensuring that interventions are delivered in a safe, inclusive, dignified, and conflict-sensitive manner and in accordance with approved project objectives, workplans, protection standards, and organizational policies.

The position assists with activity preparation and implementation, community engagement, protection awareness sessions, monitoring, data collection, referrals, and reporting. The Protection Assistant works closely with the Protection Officer, Project Coordinator, protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and other relevant project staff to identify protection concerns, support access to available services, and ensure that children, adults, and vulnerable groups can participate safely and meaningfully in project activities.

The position is also responsible for maintaining accurate activity records, sharing field observations and emerging concerns with the relevant supervisor, and adhering to organizational requirements related to safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, accountability, and the protection of sensitive information.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Protection Programme Implementation and Field Support**

- Support the implementation of protection activities in line with approved project plans, the DIP, performance framework, protection standards, and humanitarian principles.
- Assist protection facilitators, volunteers, and community structures in organizing and delivering protection activities.
- Support the identification of protection needs, risks, vulnerabilities, and barriers to accessing services among targeted communities.
- Assist in adapting activities to the local context and the specific needs of children, women, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable groups.
- Promote safe, inclusive, gender-sensitive, child-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive approaches during activity implementation.
- Ensure that protection activities are conducted in accordance with Do No Harm, confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, participation, and non-discrimination principles.
- Report implementation challenges, emerging needs, and any protection concerns to the Protection Officer/Project Coordinator in a timely manner.

**Protection Monitoring, Risk Identification and Referrals:**

- Support the identification and documentation of protection risks, concerns, trends, and barriers affecting children, adults, and vulnerable groups.
- Assist in conducting protection assessments, community consultations, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and other data collection activities.
- Identify individuals who may require additional or specialized protection support and report concerns through established internal procedures.
- Support safe referrals to relevant service providers through established referral pathways, with informed consent and in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
- Maintain and regularly update information on available protection services and referral mechanisms.
- Follow up on referrals within the scope of the position and in coordination with the Protection Officer, while respecting confidentiality and data protection requirements.
- Immediately communicate urgent protection concerns and emerging risks to the Protection Officer/Project Coordinator.
- Support community awareness activities on available protection services, rights, and referral mechanisms.

**Activity Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Capacity Building Support**

- Support the preparation and implementation of protection activity plans, schedules, and field implementation arrangements.
- Monitor activity participation, coverage, and progress against agreed protection indicators and targets.
- Conduct regular field visits to follow up on activity implementation and identify operational challenges.
- Support the collection, verification, and organization of protection-related data and ensure that records are accurate and submitted on time.
- Report implementation gaps, quality concerns, and emerging needs to the Protection Officer and support the implementation of agreed corrective actions.
- Assist in identifying capacity-building needs among protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and community structures.
- Support the organization and delivery of training, coaching, awareness sessions, and community-based activities on relevant protection topics, including protection principles, safeguarding, PSEA, referral mechanisms, and safe programming.
- Apply technical guidance and feedback received from the Protection Officer to improve the quality of field implementation.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement:**

- Coordinate with relevant Protection Sector/Sub-Sector actors, authorities, partners, community representatives, service providers, and other stakeholders as required.
- Participate in relevant protection coordination meetings, working groups, technical discussions, and inter-agency coordination mechanisms.
- Engage with communities to understand protection concerns, priorities, barriers, and feedback and ensure that programme responses are appropriate and context-sensitive.
- Support community-based protection mechanisms and promote meaningful participation of women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, and other potentially marginalized groups.
- Coordinate with other project sectors to ensure protection is appropriately mainstreamed across programme interventions, including Education, WASH, FSL, PSS, and other relevant sectors.
- Promote safe, dignified, accessible, and inclusive programme approaches and support teams to identify and mitigate protection risks.
- Support the identification and strengthening of referral pathways and linkages with specialized services

**Reporting, Documentation and Learning:**

- Prepare regular protection activity updates and contribute to project reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other programme documentation.
- Maintain comprehensive and secure records of protection activities, including attendance, training, monitoring, assessments, community consultations, referrals, and field visits, in accordance with data protection requirements.
- Document protection trends, challenges, achievements, good practices, lessons learned, and success stories while ensuring confidentiality and protection of sensitive information.
- Support the implementation of community feedback and response mechanisms and ensure relevant protection-related feedback is appropriately followed up.
- Support the preparation and review of protection-related proposals, budgets, activity plans, indicators, and project documents as required.
- Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality, monitoring, accountability, and learning processes.
- Ensure protection documentation is maintained in accordance with organizational, donor, safeguarding, and data protection requirements.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- At least 1–2 years of relevant experience in protection, humanitarian, development, or community-based programming, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Experience implementing or monitoring protection, child protection, community-based protection, protection monitoring, awareness-raising, or referral activities is desirable.
- Experience working with children, families, displaced populations, vulnerable groups, and communities affected by conflict or displacement.
- Experience providing technical support, coaching, mentoring, or capacity building to staff, volunteers, community structures, or partner organizations.
- Experience working with Protection Sector/Sub-Sector coordination mechanisms, referral networks, local authorities, service providers, or other humanitarian actors is an advantage.

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, Law, International Development, Social Sciences, or another relevant field.
- Additional qualifications or training in Protection, Child Protection, GBV, PSEA, Safeguarding, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related areas are an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Good knowledge of Protection programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
- Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
- Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
- Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.
- Ability to work effectively with partners, community representatives, education

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

Arabic and basic English is desirable

jobs.title: Project Officer (Health) - Hasaka
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Health Officer is responsible for the technical follow-up, coordination, monitoring, and quality assurance of health and nutrition activities implemented through partner organizations under the project, ensuring that services are delivered effectively, safely, inclusively, and in line with approved project objectives, workplans, relevant health and nutrition standards, and donor requirements. The position supports the implementation of primary healthcare services through two fixed health facilities in Ras Al Ain and Tell Abiad, with a focus on outpatient consultations, reproductive health, maternal and child health, preventive and therapeutic nutrition services, and community health and nutrition education.

The Health Officer works closely with the Project Coordinator, implementing partners, relevant health and nutrition technical teams, MEAL colleagues, and other stakeholders to monitor partner performance, identify implementation gaps, strengthen service quality, and ensure that health and nutrition activities respond to the needs of vulnerable communities. The position also supports capacity building for project and partner staff on relevant health topics, including infection prevention and control (IPC), reproductive health (RH), antimicrobial resistance (AMR), non-communicable diseases (NCDs), community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), and infant and young child feeding (IYCF). The Health Officer contributes to accurate reporting, accountability, coordination, and evidence-based programme improvement while ensuring that clinical services and technical decisions remain the responsibility of qualified and authorized health professionals within the implementing partner facilities.

cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

1. **Health Programme Implementation and Partner Coordination 30%**

- Health Programme Implementation and Partner Coordination
- Support the planning, coordination, and follow-up of health and nutrition activities implemented by partner organizations in the two fixed health facilities in Ras Al Ain and Tell Abiad.
- Maintain regular communication with implementing partners to follow up on approved workplans, activity schedules, service delivery, staffing, operational challenges, and progress against agreed targets.
- Conduct regular monitoring visits to partner-supported health facilities and community activity locations to assess operational status, service availability, implementation progress, and compliance with agreed programme requirements.
- Review partner implementation plans and identify potential delays, gaps in service delivery, and resource or operational constraints requiring follow-up.
- Support partners in addressing implementation challenges and coordinate with the Project Coordinator and relevant technical focal points to facilitate timely solutions.
- Monitor the availability and continuity of planned primary healthcare, maternal and child health, and nutrition services through partner facilities, escalating service interruptions and significant gaps.
- Ensure that health and nutrition activities are implemented in accordance with the approved project design, Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP), performance framework, budget, and donor requirements.
- Promote equitable and non-discriminatory access to services for women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable groups.

1. **Primary Healthcare and Maternal and Child Health Service Quality Monitoring 20%**

- Monitor the delivery of outpatient primary healthcare consultations through the two partner-supported fixed health facilities, ensuring progress against agreed service delivery targets.
- Follow up with partners on the availability and continuity of planned primary healthcare services, including maternal and child health and reproductive health services, within the scope of the approved project.
- Review service utilization data, disaggregated by sex, age, and disability where applicable, to identify access barriers, underserved groups, service utilization trends, and potential gaps in coverage.
- Monitor partner compliance with agreed health service standards, relevant clinical protocols, patient safety requirements, and organizational and donor expectations through observation, documentation review, and coordination with qualified health professionals.
- Follow up on partner staff capacity-building activities related to IPC, RH, AMR, NCDs, and other relevant health topics, as identified in the project workplan.
- Support partners in identifying service quality gaps and developing appropriate follow-up actions, referring clinical or specialized technical matters to qualified health professionals and designated technical focal points.
- Monitor the documentation of consultations through the relevant health information systems, including the SAMS Health Information System (HIS), and follow up on missing, inconsistent, or incomplete records.
- Escalate significant service interruptions, patient safety concerns, or other issues that may compromise access to or the quality of healthcare services.

1. **Nutrition Programme Monitoring and Technical Follow-Up 20%**

- Monitor the implementation of preventive and therapeutic nutrition activities delivered through implementing partners at facility and community levels.
- Follow up on partner delivery of CMAM services, including screening, identification, admission, referral, treatment, and follow-up of children with moderate and severe acute malnutrition (MAM and SAM), in accordance with approved protocols.
- Monitor the implementation and quality of IYCF counselling, including counselling for caregivers on appropriate infant and young child feeding practices, within the scope of the project.
- Track the implementation of nutrition screening activities using mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) for children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), as applicable to the approved programme.
- Review partner nutrition activity data, including screening records, admission registers, IYCF registration records, CMAM databases, and relevant reports, to monitor progress against targets and identify inconsistencies or service delivery gaps.
- Follow up on partner capacity-building activities on CMAM, IYCF, and other relevant nutrition topics, ensuring that training activities and supporting documentation are maintained.
- Monitor health and nutrition education sessions delivered by trained community health workers (CHWs), including session coverage, participation, documentation, and relevance to identified community needs.
- Coordinate with partner nutrition focal points and relevant technical specialists to address identified gaps and ensure that cases requiring specialized support are managed through established clinical and referral pathways.
- Ensure that nutrition-related data is reviewed and reported accurately, with appropriate disaggregation and confidentiality safeguards

1. **Capacity Building and Technical Support to Partners 20%**

- Support the identification of training and capacity-building needs among implementing partner health and nutrition staff and relevant project personnel.
- Coordinate with qualified technical specialists and partners to facilitate training on relevant health topics, including IPC, RH, AMR, NCDs, CMAM, IYCF, and other agreed topics.
- Follow up on training plans, participant attendance, completion records, training reports, and certificates, where applicable.
- Monitor the application of relevant training content through partner follow-up discussions, field monitoring, documentation review, and feedback from technical focal points.
- Support knowledge sharing and the dissemination of approved technical guidance, tools, and reference materials to relevant partner and project staff.
- Identify additional capacity gaps and communicate recommendations to the Project Coordinator and relevant technical teams.
- Support partners in strengthening documentation, reporting, and monitoring practices related to health and nutrition service delivery.

1. **Monitoring, Data Quality, Reporting, and Documentation 10%**

- Monitor progress against agreed health and nutrition indicators, targets, workplans, and milestones, maintaining an updated overview of implementation progress.
- Collect, review, verify, and consolidate health and nutrition data and supporting documentation submitted by implementing partners.
- Follow up on key programme indicators, including outpatient consultations, staff trained on health topics, nutrition staff trained, IYCF counselling sessions, MAM and SAM admissions, MUAC screenings, and health and nutrition education activities.
- Review relevant sources of verification, including partner workplans, health facility operationality trackers, digital patient records through the SAMS HIS, monthly verification reports (MVRs), attendance sheets, training reports, CMAM databases, IYCF records, and activity reports.
- Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality assurance, verification, indicator tracking, monitoring visits, and other relevant monitoring processes.
- Prepare regular health and nutrition activity updates and contribute to project progress reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other required programme documentation.
- Document achievements, implementation challenges, lessons learned, good practices, and recommendations for programme improvement.
- Ensure that partner reports and supporting evidence are submitted accurately and on time, and promptly follow up on missing or inconsistent information.
- Maintain appropriate confidentiality and ensure that personal and sensitive patient information is handled in accordance with applicable data protection and health information management requirements

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Health Sciences, Nursing, Medicine, Nutrition, Midwifery, or another relevant health-related field.
- Additional training or certification in public health, primary healthcare, reproductive health, maternal and child health, nutrition, CMAM, IYCF, IPC, or health programme management is an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge, experience and skills**

- At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in health, public health, nutrition, humanitarian response, or health programme coordination, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Good understanding of primary health and nutrition services delivery and programme implementation in humanitarian and early recovery contexts.
- Experience in monitoring and coordinating primary health and nutrition projects including maternal and child health, reproductive health, community health, and nutrition activities.
- High coordination skills for health projects including coordinating with health authorities, health service providers, local partners, or relevant humanitarian coordination mechanisms is desirable.
- Experience in following up on activity implementation, workplans, service delivery, reporting, and agreed programme targets.
- Understanding of nutrition programming, including CMAM, MAM and SAM management, IYCF counselling, MUAC screening, and community-level nutrition interventions.
- Experience supporting training, capacity building, or technical follow-up for health and nutrition staff is an advantage.
- Experience in managing medical stocks at primary health settings including pharmaceuticals and other medical supplies.
- Good knowledge of health data collection and analysis including the use of health information systems and relevant programme databases.
- Experience reviewing health and nutrition data, maintaining programme documentation, and contributing to donor or project reports.
- Strong communication, interpersonal, coordination, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams
- Good computer skills, particularly Microsoft Word and Excel; familiarity with mobile data collection and reporting tools is an advantage.
- Understanding of safeguarding, PSEA, confidentiality, informed consent, accountability to affected populations, and protection mainstreaming.

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

jobs.title: Physiotherapist (Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Position: **PHYSIOTHERAPIST**.

Duty Station: **Garowe city, Puntland, Somalia**.
Employment Type: **Full-time / Project-based**
Contract Duration: **5 months (January – May 2027)**
Number of Positions: **1**
Reports To: **Project Manager** **About the Project**

Created in 1982, Humanity & Inclusion/ formerly known as Handicap International (HI) is an independent and impartial international aid organization working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. Working alongside people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups, our actions are focused on responding to their essential needs, improving their living conditions and promoting respect for their dignity and their fundamental rights.

HI is implementing a project titled “Providing Community-Based Rehabilitation and Assistive Technology Services for Persons with Disabilities in Crisis-Affected Communities in **Garowe, Puntland, Somalia**. The project aims to increase access to quality rehabilitation services and appropriate assistive devices and technologies for persons with disabilities and individuals experiencing functional limitations due to injury, illness, or long-term impairments, to enhance their mobility, independence, and participation in daily life.

**Job Summary**

The Physiotherapist will be responsible for providing quality, person-centered physical rehabilitation and physiotherapy services to project beneficiaries.

The position will conduct physical and functional assessments, develop individualized rehabilitation plans, provide physiotherapy and home-based rehabilitation, train beneficiaries and caregivers, support assistive-device provision, facilitate referrals, and contribute to monitoring, documentation, quality assurance, and project learning.

The Physiotherapist will work closely with rehabilitation personnel, health professionals, P&O service providers, MHPSS service providers, OPDs, caregivers, community workers, community structures and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated and continuous rehabilitation services.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Physical and Functional Assessment**

- Conduct comprehensive physical and functional assessments of beneficiaries to identify impairments, functional limitations, rehabilitation needs, and participation barriers.
- Develop individualized rehabilitation goals and treatment plans in consultation with beneficiaries and caregivers.
- Assess mobility, gait, balance, strength, range of motion, coordination, pain, endurance, and functional independence.
- Regularly reassess beneficiaries and modify rehabilitation plans according to their progress and needs.

**Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation**

- Provide individualized physiotherapy and physical rehabilitation services to assigned beneficiaries.
- Provide therapeutic exercises, strengthening, stretching, mobility and gait training, balance and coordination exercises, positioning, and functional rehabilitation as appropriate.
- Provide home-based rehabilitation programmes and follow-up support.
- Promote functional independence, safe mobility, prevention of secondary complications, and participation in daily activities.
- Ensure rehabilitation interventions are safe, appropriate, evidence-informed, and responsive to individual needs.

**Beneficiary Screening and Identification**

- Support the orientation and training of data collectors on the appropriate use of the Washington Group Questions (WGQs) for disability identification and screening in project target areas.
- Supervise and provide technical guidance to data collectors conducting disability identification and screening using the WGQs within the assigned project area.
- Ensure that beneficiary screening and identification are conducted accurately, ethically, confidentially, and in accordance with approved project procedures.
- Work closely with the MEAL team to review and analyze screening data and identify individuals requiring physical rehabilitation, assistive devices, or other specialized support.
- Support the categorization of identified beneficiaries according to their rehabilitation needs and eligibility criteria.
- Prioritize beneficiaries requiring urgent, specialized, or time-sensitive rehabilitation interventions and facilitate their timely assessment and referral.
- Verify and follow up on identified cases to ensure that beneficiaries requiring rehabilitation and assistive-device services are appropriately assessed and linked to available services.

**Caregiver Training and Community Rehabilitation**

- Train caregivers on home-based rehabilitation, positioning, mobility, exercises, transfers, and safe care practices.
- Demonstrate appropriate exercises and rehabilitation techniques to beneficiaries and caregivers.
- Provide guidance on prevention of complications and promotion of functional independence.
- Conduct follow-up visits and provide appropriate recommendations for continued rehabilitation at home.

**Assistive Devices**

- Conduct assessment of beneficiaries in need of assistive devices including wheelchairs, crutches, walkers, toilet seats, walking sticks…
- Prescribe assistive devices based on beneficiaries’ functional needs and living environments.
- Fitting, adjustment, and functional testing of assistive devices within the scope of professional practice.
- Train beneficiaries and caregivers on safe use, maintenance, and care of assistive devices.

**Referral and Coordination**

- Identify beneficiaries requiring specialized health, rehabilitation, P&O or other services.
- Initiate referrals through established referral mechanisms.
- Coordinate with health facilities, rehabilitation providers, P&O services, MHPSS providers, and other relevant service providers.
- Follow up on referrals and document referral outcomes.

**Documentation, Monitoring and Quality Assurance**

- Maintain accurate, complete, and confidential beneficiary and clinical records.
- Document assessments, treatment plans, interventions, progress, referrals, and follow-up.
- Contribute to routine monitoring and quality-assurance activities.
- Monitor beneficiary outcomes against individualized rehabilitation goals and project indicators.
- Participate in field supervision, case reviews, supportive monitoring, and service-quality improvement activities.
- Collect beneficiary feedback and contribute to improving rehabilitation services.
- Ensure compliance with safeguarding, confidentiality, accountability, informed-consent, and data-protection requirements.

**Reporting and Learning**

- Prepare and submit regular activity and rehabilitation reports as required.
- Contribute to project monitoring and donor reporting.
- Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, and recommendations.
- Participate in project review, learning, handover, and close-out activities.
- Support the project team in reviewing achievements against planned outputs and outcomes.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Bachelor's degree in **Physiotherapy/Physical Therapy** from a recognized institution.
- Minimum of **2–3 years of relevant professional experience** in physiotherapy and physical rehabilitation.
- Demonstrated experience in physical and functional assessment and individualized rehabilitation planning.
- Experience providing therapeutic exercise, mobility and gait training, positioning, functional rehabilitation, and home-based rehabilitation.
- Experience working with persons with disabilities and vulnerable or conflict-affected populations is highly desirable.
- Experience in community-based rehabilitation and caregiver training is an advantage.
- Experience with assistive-device assessment, fitting, and user training is highly desirable.
- Experience working with multidisciplinary teams and referral networks.
- Knowledge of the Washington Group Questions and disability-inclusive programming is an advantage.
- Strong understanding of safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, and protection principles.
- Strong communication, documentation, reporting, and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
- Fluency in spoken and written English & Somali is required.

**Key Competencies**

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

- Strong clinical and rehabilitation skills.
- Person-centered and rights-based approach to service delivery.
- Commitment to disability inclusion and equal access to services.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Strong teamwork and coordination skills.
- Good problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in challenging field environments.
- Strong organizational and documentation skills.
- Commitment to safeguarding, professional ethics, confidentiality, and accountability.

jobs.title: Regional Humanitarian Manager - Horn, Eastern, Central and Southern Africa
jobs.description:
Cordaid is an international organisation for development and humanitarian assistance, working especially in fragile and conflict-affected regions. Guided by Christian values of human dignity, justice and compassion, we work towards a world without poverty and with equitable opportunities for all.

More than 1.9 billion people live in fragile contexts where access to essential services and opportunities is limited. Together with our partners, we support locally led programmes in longer term development that strengthen healthcare, education, agrifood and justice systems. When crises occur, we work alongside local organisations to provide humanitarian assistance.

Cordaid has regional offices in Europe, West-Africa, Horn, East, Central and South Africa and in the Middle East and Asia.

Cordaid operates through a domain-based model. Our regional and country teams work with local partners so they can lead humanitarian response. Cordaid provides the local actors with capacity, technical advice and helps them meet humanitarian standards, engage with donors and fulfil their commitments.

Cordaid is looking for a

**Regional Humanitarian Manager - Horn, Eastern, Central and Southern Africa (HECSA)**

**(Fulltime, home-based in the HECSA region)**

As our Regional Humanitarian Manager for HECSA, you provide strategic leadership for humanitarian action, emergency preparedness, and crisis response across the region. Working at the interface between the HECSA Regional Core and the global Humanitarian Assistance Platform, you ensure that humanitarian responses are principled, locally led, and effectively integrated into regional strategies and Country Engagement Models (triple nexus approach). You serve as the organization's primary regional humanitarian focal point, representing HECSA in regional humanitarian coordination, policy, and advocacy spaces, and building strategic relationships with key stakeholders, first and above our networks of Caritas and ACT Alliance and also including UN agencies, donors, INGOs, regional bodies, and local humanitarian actors. Rather than managing direct programme implementation, you enable local partners to lead by strengthening preparedness, technical quality, and organisational readiness. You report directly to the HECSA Regional Director and to the global humanitarian manager.

**What you do**

- **Humanitarian Leadership & Strategy**: Provide strategic leadership and advice on humanitarian action across the HECSA region, supporting Regional Directors and Country Engagement Models in rapid crisis decision-making
- **Emergency Preparedness & Response**: Strengthen regional preparedness and crisis readiness by coordinating regional contingency planning and supporting emergency response activations,
- **Humanitarian Partnerships & Localisation**: Foster equitable partnerships with national and local humanitarian partners across HECSA, with a partner led approach.
- **Triple Nexus & Sectoral Integration**: Spearhead the humanitarian-development-peace nexus approach across the region, linking emergency response and recovery to longer-term resilience, climate adaptation, and systems strengthening.
- **Technical quality and accountability**: Work with Cordaid’s global humanitarian team to uphold humanitarian principles, apply the Core Humanitarian Standard and the Sphere Standards, integrate protection across programmes, and ensure that crisis-affected people can give feedback and receive a response.
- **Resource Mobilization & Positioning**: Support engagement with major institutional humanitarian donors (ECHO, BHA, Dutch Relief Alliance, UN agencies) and work closely with the Business Development Manager to build a healthy regional humanitarian funding pipeline.
- **Networking, Representation & Advocacy**: Represent the Regional Core in regional humanitarian coordination clusters, UN/OCHA meetings, ACT Alliance and Caritas (country) fora, INGO platforms, and donor forums to advance strategic priorities and advocate for locally led responses.
- **Risk Management, Safeguarding & Integrity**: Implement Cordaid’s Integrity Compliance Framework, manage operational and contextual risks in fragile environments, and champion high standards of duty of care and safety.

**Who you are**

- You hold a Master’s degree in Humanitarian Assistance, International Development, Disaster Management, International Relations, or a related field.
- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian leadership, emergency response, and crisis management in complex, fragile, and conflict-affected environments.
- Evidence of leading emergency responses in fragile settings, working with local partners that lead delivery, and representing an organisation with donors and humanitarian coordination bodies.
- Deep knowledge of the humanitarian sector and complex crisis dynamics across Horn, Eastern, Central or Southern Africa (HECSA).
- Sound practical expertise in Core Humanitarian Standards (CHS), SPHERE guidelines, cash transfer modalities, protection mainstreaming, and the triple nexus approach.
- Proven track record in working through national/local partners, driving localisation, and supporting partner capacity sharing in emergency settings.
- Demonstrated experience engaging with institutional humanitarian donors (ECHO, BHA, DRA, UN/CBHF) and multi-stakeholder humanitarian networks.
- Strong strategic thinking, decision-making, analytical, and financial management skills.
- Exceptional oral and written communication skills in English. Proficiency in French, Portuguese, Arabic, or relevant regional languages is a distinct advantage.
- Willingness to be home-based in the HECSA region with flexibility to travel up to 50% of the time within the region.
- You recognize yourself in Cordaid’s mission and values.

**What we offer**

- A high-profile senior leadership position within an international, professional organization with a focus on social impact.
- A varied, highly impactful, and autonomous role where strategic initiative and vision are essential.
- A global organization with a strong commitment to social entrepreneurship and locally led impact.
- Good international working conditions and excellent secondary benefits.
- An initial contract for 1 year with the intention of extending, home-based within the HECSA region.

jobs.title: IT Assistant - Damascus
jobs.description:
**Background/IRC Summary:**

The Syria crisis is often described as the worst humanitarian catastrophe since the end of the Cold War. Today, 13.4 million people in Syria - more than half of the country's population - are in need of humanitarian assistance with needs increasingly being exacerbated by economic decline. Of these, 6.8 million are refugees and asylum-seekers who have fled the country. This is no short-term humanitarian episode. The devastating human consequences to huge numbers of people will endure for decades. The destruction of relationships, communities, livelihoods, homes and infrastructure will take years to repair.

IRC is offering a robust humanitarian response to the Syria crisis a rapidly expanding portfolio, supported by more than 1000+ staff in Syria Country Program. IRC is undertaking programs in Syria and the neighboring countries of Turkey, Iraq, Lebanon and Jordan in the fields of health, child protection, early childhood development, education, women’s protection and empowerment, non-food items and food distribution, cash assistance, water and sanitation, protection and rule of law, and livelihood programming. Our work in these challenging settings gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, security, funding and coordination.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The ICT Assistant will be responsible for ensuring particular focus on ICT support, including assisting and facilitating the installation and configuration of IT and communications infrastructure, staff training and operations of IT activities in Damascus office, and field offices. The IT Assistant will work closely with the IT Manager and all program sectors to ensure proper IT functioning and support.

**Responsibilities:**

**Installation & Configuration and management of:**

- Desktop/laptop hardware and software, and peripherals, using IRC standard windows 11 operating system image.
- Local Area Network, wireless network, peer-to-peer, or client-server architecture, as appropriate.

**IT Support - Provide Level 1 and Level 2 Support**

- Work with end-users or IT colleagues (or Service Desk) on assisting in resolving Level 1 issues in CP.
- Provide Microsoft Windows & Office applications support.
- Diagnose hardware and software faults by questioning clients patiently about a problem and explaining the procedures to them.
- Ensure data backups for individual users are being completed and provide the necessary training on the use of these back-up solutions.
- Work towards a successful resolution of the problems clients present.
- Perform preventative maintenance on all IRC computers and network resources in the field.

**Maintenance, Repair & Security:**

- Perform preventative maintenance on all IRC computers and network resources.
- Update appropriate network security and data loss prevention procedures to safeguard the system from physical harm, viruses, unauthorized users, and damage to data.
- Create and maintain IRC computer software/hardware inventory ensuring accuracy.
- Create and maintain network documentation to include IP address, system access, email creation system, upgrades, and changes to original network, etc.
- Managing/Monitoring firewall to ensure accessing internet is in line with IRC standards.
- Investigate local Internet connectivity options to obtain adequate bandwidth for Intranet and application connectivity.
- Closely collaborate with IT Manager, International IT and HQ IT team on helpdesk, connectivity and other in country and global IRC IT projects.
- Track and monitor all IT equipment across IRC Damascus offices, ensuring accurate records of equipment allocation, location, condition, and assigned users.
- Maintain and regularly update the IT asset inventory for all Damascus offices, including laptops, desktops, monitors, printers, networking equipment, and other IT peripherals.
- Conduct regular physical verification and reconciliation of IT assets to ensure inventory accuracy and identify missing, damaged, or unaccounted-for equipment.
- Coordinate with the Administration, Supply Chain, and relevant departments to ensure proper asset handover, tracking, and accountability.

**Training, Evaluation, & Testing:**

- Deliver staff basic training about email, password change /complexity.
- Prepare and submit reports that provide sufficient detail to the direct technical manager to understand the field office’s computer environment and needs.
- Test and evaluate new technology as requested by Field Director or IT Supervisor
- Conduct regular site visits to field offices in Idleb and provide required technical support.

**Various Projects** – Position will need to assist on various IT projects as needed.

**Required Experience/qualification/Skills:**

- The requirements should establish a baseline (minimum) for educational background, previous work experience, professional knowledge or certification, specific skills and strengths and any other skill necessary to perform the essential functions of the job.
- **Education:** College or Institute degree in Computer Science or other advanced technical qualifications.
- **Work Experience:** At least two years of experience in IT profession.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values, and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Experience installing, configuring, and managing both wired and wireless LAN, and firewalls.
- Computer imaging skills required.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills required.
- Highly developed skills in troubleshooting and IT problems identification
- Strong written and interpersonal skills; customer service experience
- Able to work independently within a team environment.

Able to work and provide support remotely and in a complex, unpredictable, and fluid operating environment.

**Language/Travel:**

- Arabic/ Acceptable level of English Knowledge is required.
- This post will require regular filed visits to the field sites.
- **Certificates or Licenses**: CCNA & MCP knowledge is desired.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to: IT Manager**
**Position directly supervises: N/A**
- **Indirect Reporting: Field Director / Regional IT Coordinator MENA**
- **Other Internal and/or external contacts**
- **Internal: All departments and users**
- **External: Internet service providers**

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based and are currently located outside of your home country and possess over two years of international work experience, the Middle East Region has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

jobs.title: WASH Program Manager- Re-advertised - Syria Aleppo & Idleb
jobs.description:
**General Description of the Programme:**

Established in 1977, GOAL is an international humanitarian and development agency, committed to working with communities to achieve sustainable and innovative early response in crises, and lasting solutions to poverty and vulnerability. GOAL has worked in over 60 countries and has responded to almost every major humanitarian disaster. We are currently operational in 18 countries.

GOAL began operations in Syria in 2013 responding to the acute needs of conflict-affected communities. GOAL's areas of operations include but not limited to Aleppo, Idleb and Damascus Programmes focus on Food and Nutrition Security, WASH, Shelter, Livelihoods/ERMS and Emergency Response with an emphasis on cash and voucher modalities. GOAL Syria implements its programmes directly, with staff based in Syria, and through Syrian NGO partners. GOAL's programme works at the household and community levels to improve community resilience and household coping strategies.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

**Objective 1: Technical Support:**

- Develop detailed activity plans aligned with WASH programme objectives and donor-approved work plans, ensuring timely implementation and that any expected delays or modifications are communicated proactively to the WASH and Shelter Coordinator.
- Monitor WASH programme performance against activity plans, output targets, and approved indicators, taking corrective action in coordination with the WASH and Shelter Coordinator to ensure objectives are met within allotted time and budget.
- Ensure all WASH activities are designed and implemented in line with Sphere standards, WASH Cluster technical guidelines, and GOAL's internal quality standards.
- Provide technical oversight of all water infrastructure activities, including the rehabilitation and maintenance of water networks, pipeline repair/extension, pumping stations, storage facilities, and solar-powered water systems; and all sanitation infrastructure activities, including sewage network rehabilitation, wastewater systems, and sewer lines.
- Oversee the construction and rehabilitation of latrines, toilet blocks, and sanitation facilities in IDP settlements and collective centres, ensuring designs are gender-sensitive, disability-inclusive, and contextually appropriate; and supervise solid waste management activities including waste collection systems and disposal sites.
- Oversee water quality monitoring activities and provide technical supervision of the laboratory team, ensuring results are documented, acted upon, and reported in a timely manner.
- Contribute to the design of new WASH projects and proposal development and improve programme quality through supervisory support to key staff, analysis and dissemination of M&E data and lessons learned, and review of GOAL and sector best practice guidelines.

**Objective 2: Leadership & Coordination:**

- Directly manage a multidisciplinary WASH team of 10–30 staff (including Deputy Programme Managers, Engineers, Data Team, Community Liaison Officers, and Laboratory Team), ensuring all staff have clearly defined job descriptions, individual work plans, and a thorough understanding of their roles and responsibilities.
- Conduct regular performance appraisals and support the development of individual staff development plans, identifying capacity gaps and providing coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job training as needed.
- Ensure effective coordination, information sharing, and liaison with WASH and other humanitarian actors operational in GOAL's areas, identifying opportunities for complementarity and reducing the risk of duplication.
- Actively participate in WASH Cluster coordination mechanisms at field level, representing GOAL and contributing to sector-wide planning, information sharing, and gap analysis.
- Coordinate with the relevant departments at GOAL Offices — including Logistics, Finance, HR, and Security — on all operational needs related to the WASH programme across Syria.
- Integrate conflict-sensitive programming and do-no-harm principles into all WASH activities, ensuring that programming does not inadvertently exacerbate tensions or vulnerabilities within target communities.

**Objective 3: Reporting:**

- Prepare accurate and timely weekly programme reports and share them with the WASH and Shelter Coordinator.
- Lead on the preparation of high-quality donor reports (monthly, quarterly, and final) in line with ECHO/EU, DoS, UN OCHA Pooled Funds, SDC, and other institutional donors reporting formats and requirements, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with donor guidelines.
- Ensure all programme documentation — including activity reports, field visit reports, assessment findings, and lessons learned — is systematically filed and maintained in GOAL's programme documentation system.
- Contribute to situation reports, emergency updates, and other ad hoc reporting as required by the WASH and Shelter Coordinator.
- Work with Water Units and partner staff to strengthen their reporting skills and ensure timely and accurate data flows from the field.
- Ensure that financial reporting aligns with programme reporting, tracking budget utilisation against activities and flagging variances to the WASH and Shelter Coordinator and Finance team in a timely manner.

**Objective 4: Partners Support:**

- Work closely with WASH project partners to ensure project objectives and activity plans are clearly understood, agreed roles and responsibilities are met by all parties, and partnership agreements are adhered to.
- Identify staff and partner capacity building requirements and work with the WASH and Shelter Coordinator and other team members to design and deliver effective training, mentoring, and other activities to address identified capacity gaps.

**Objective 5: Procurement:**

- Prepare procurement plans in coordination with the WASH and Shelter Coordinator, ensuring alignment with programme activity plans and donor procurement rules (including ECHO/EU, DoS, UN OCHA Pooled Funds, SDC, and other institutional donors’ thresholds and regulations).
- Conduct regular meetings with the procurement team at the Saraqib Office to follow up on the status of all WASH procurement and ensure no delays in delivery to field sites.
- Coordinate with the WASH and Shelter Coordinator and the Logistics and Procurement department at the Saraqib Office to ensure timely sourcing and delivery of all WASH materials required for programme implementation.
- Monitor budget versus actual expenditure in coordination with the Finance team, tracking burn rates against procurement plans and flagging risks of under- or over-spend in a timely manner.
- Ensure all procurement processes adhere to GOAL's anti-fraud policies and comply with applicable donor regulations.

**Objective 6: Monitoring & Evaluation:**

- Coordinate with the M&E team to ensure the development and implementation of appropriate M&E frameworks, programme management tools, and community feedback mechanisms.
- Track WASH-specific output and outcome indicators (including but not limited to litres per person per day, % of population with access to safe water, sanitation coverage, and hygiene promotion reach) and ensure results are regularly reported and analysed.
- Ensure that community accountability and feedback mechanisms are functional, accessible, and inclusive — with particular attention to the needs of women, children, elderly persons, and persons with disabilities.
- Travel frequently to programme locations to directly monitor WASH activities, providing clear and actionable feedback to field staff and/or partners on changes or improvements required.
- Support the use of GOAL's MIS and data management systems to ensure data quality, completeness, and timeliness across all WASH reporting streams.

**Objective 7: Other:**

- Ensure adherence to all GOAL policies, guidelines, and manuals — including the Code of Conduct, Child Protection Policy, Financial Manual, and whistleblowing mechanisms — at all times.
- Ensure appropriate HR planning, training, and resource allocation, and full compliance with all donor requirements, including timely and quality reporting.
- Perform other related tasks as requested by the WASH and Shelter Coordinator.

**Requirements (essential)**

- Fluency in Arabic and English, professional working proficiency (written and spoken) is mandatory.
- Bachelor’s degree in civil, Water, Environmental, or related Engineering discipline.
- Minimum **5 years** of experience in WASH programme implementation in humanitarian contexts and/or a combination of WASH and Shelter.
- Minimum **3 years** of experience in **a managerial role**, with demonstrated ability to lead and develop large, multidisciplinary teams.
- Demonstrated experience **preparing and submitting reports** to institutional donors — must include at least one of: ECHO/EU, DoS, UN OCHA Pooled Funds, or SDC.
- Proven experience working with NGO/INGOs in conflict-affected or displacement settings, with strong familiarity with IDP camp WASH, infrastructure rehabilitation, and/or remote field operations.
- Experience managing programme budgets of **at least USD 1 million annually**, including budget monitoring, financial reporting, and variance management.
- Strong budgetary control and financial management skills.
- Flexible and creative approach with a proven ability to resolve issues and identify solutions under pressure.
- Excellent time management skills and ability to prioritise competing demands.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Commitment to beneficiary accountability, protection mainstreaming, and humanitarian principles.
- Proposal and report writing experience, writing samples may be requested.
- Excellent computer literacy, including advanced Excel, Word, and familiarity with data management/MIS tools and reporting platforms.

**Requirements (desired)**

- Proven experience working with public water and sanitation authorities for at least 3 years.
- Experience with WASH Cluster coordination at field or governorate level.
- Experience integrating gender-sensitive and protection-mainstreamed approaches into WASH programme design and implementation.
- Experience managing large, diverse teams in remote or insecure environments.
- Experience with cost recovery mechanisms in WASH programming.
- Proficiency in engineering software for water and sewage systems design, including CAD, EPANET, ETABS, sewage network design tools, or solar systems design software (certificates to be shared with application).
- Proven experience in the preparation and finalization of technical assessments related to water infrastructure projects.
- Certification in project or programme management (e.g., PMD Pro, PMP, or equivalent).

**General terms and conditions**

**Safeguarding**

Children and vulnerable adults must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury and any other harm. One of the ways that GOAL shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**Safeguarding Statement**
GOAL has zero tolerance for safeguarding violations. All staff are expected to adhere to GOAL’s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies, including the prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (PSEAH). Recruitment is subject to safeguarding checks, including reference verification

**Accountability within GOAL**

Alongside our safeguarding policy, GOAL is an equal opportunities employer and has a set of integrity policies. Any candidate offered a job with GOAL will be expected to adhere to the following key areas of accountability:

- Comply with GOAL’s policies and procedures with respect to safeguarding, Code of Conduct, health and safety, data protection and confidentiality, do no harm principles and unacceptable behaviour protocols.
- Report any concerns about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult or any wrongdoings within our programming area.
- Report any concerns about inappropriate behaviour of a GOAL staff or partner.

*This Job Description only serves as a guide for the position available. GOAL reserves the right to change this document. Any published closing dates are estimated. Due to the nature of GOAL’s work we aim to fill vacancies as quickly as possible. This means that we will close adverts as soon as we have found the right candidate and this may be before the published closing date. We would therefore advise interested applicants to submit an application as early as possible.*

**Thank you.**

jobs.title: Logistics Assistant-Damascus
jobs.description:
**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the **world’s worst humanitarian crises** and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives.

The IRC has long-term programs based in Baghdad and Erbil, as well as emergency response programs supporting Syrian refugees and war-affected Syrian internally displaced persons (IDPs). The IRC is seeking for dynamic individuals to support it in the delivery of services and support to communities affected by conflict in Syria.

Working in coordination with the humanitarian community, the IRC currently addresses the needs of Syrian IDPs. Our activities in northern Syria focus primarily on the supply of vital medications and medical equipment, non-food items, food and vouchers and form part of an over-arching humanitarian response in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, and Syria that seeks to assist those in need to survive conflict and displacement.

As part of its regional response and efforts, the IRC is now expanding its operations inside Syria by establishing programs for health, protection, economic and food support to vulnerable families in Raqqa, Syria.

**SCOPE OF WORK**:

The logistics assistant will be responsible to play a vital role in managing logistics activities related to Damascus office ,He/she will be responsible to ensure that IRC standards are met assuring maximum support to all thematic areas operational in Damascus office and its adjacent locations.
