jobs.title: Science Networks and Knowledge Management Adviser
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Science Networks and Knowledge Management Adviser** will be responsible for providing high-level support on technical content development and knowledge management for SPC FAME programmes/projects to enable SPC FAME to enhance its scientific communication and knowledge management effectiveness to achieve better research and development outcomes.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Facilitate the development and curation of scientific and technical knowledge products**

- Supporting national and regional access to regionally accumulated scientific and technical knowledge from SPC FAME programmes.
- Supporting the management of the SPC Digital Library and act as the focal point for the SPC FAME Digital Library

\- Maintain and update SPC FAME content in the Digital Library

\- Upload SPC FAME knowledge products with appropriate metadata

\- Create and manage collections of documents

\- Work with the SPC knowledge management community to maintain consistency

- Coordinating the publication of reference technical bulletins. Specifically:

\- scientific and technical review and editing of articles for the Fisheries Newsletter bulletin

\- coordination of the external editing process and dissemination of the Newsletter

- Supporting SPC Member and partner authors in communicating their work in the SPC Fisheries Newsletter bulletin. This includes mentoring the author in developing and refining the content.
- Supporting SPC FAME communication and publication activities, including the consistent use of language and style, as well as wider dissemination and reach of SPC FAME’s scientific and technical outputs.

**Develop, maintain, and update content for the SPC FAME website and web portals**

- Identify and curate technical content for the OneSPC website, SPC FAME online portals, and the Pacific Data Hub, ensuring consistency across materials.
- Develop technical and scientific content for the OneSPC website and SPC FAME online portals, including identifying and addressing current information gaps.
- Ensure that SPC FAME knowledge products available online are curated so that information available includes that which is current, relevant and aligns with SPC FAME’s strategic direction and advice to members and partners.
- Coordinate the production, editing, and dissemination of information for SPC FAME’s large regional stakeholder meetings.

**Develop knowledge management capacity**

- Provide training, mentoring and support to SPC FAME staff in relation to the publication and development of scientific and technical knowledge products.
- Provide training, mentoring and support to SPC FAME staff in relation to knowledge management more broadly, including sustainable management of scientific and technical knowledge products.
- Support SPC FAME team members to enhance internal knowledge sharing and knowledge management systems and approaches.
- Contribute to the SPC Information and Knowledge Management community of practice to ensure coherence with cross-divisional approaches to knowledge management.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Postgraduate degree in a relevant field such as science, natural resource management, knowledge management, international development or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7 years of experience in knowledge management, scientific networking, or scientific communications and publishing.
- Experience of the peer-review publishing process for scientific publications.
- Experience in international organisations, including knowledge sharing and stakeholder engagement.
- Proven record in developing technical and scientific knowledge products, scientific analysis and knowledge dissemination.
- Skilled in the use of databases and systems for visualising, entering, processing/cleaning and extracting data, including experience with web-based monitoring and reporting systems.
- Strategic thinker with well-developed analytical skills and meticulous attention to detail.
- Experience in stakeholder consultation processes and the development of knowledge management systems.
- Ability to train and motivate divisional staff on knowledge sharing and technical content development for a broad range of audiences.

**Language skills**

- A high level of proficiency in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Strong people skills (influencing and relationship building) and ability to work in a multicultural and gender-sensitive environment.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted until 31 December 2029 and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Science Networks and Knowledge Management Adviser** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,727-4,562 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 537,766-658,322 (USD 4,994-6,114; EUR 4,506-5,517). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Senior Specialist - Management & Operations Expertise Hub
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Job Summary

Are you ready to make an impact in the world? Join Habitat for Humanity’s Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub as we multiply Habitat’s impact in the United States.

Habitat for Humanity International’s U.S. Expertise Hubs are teams of subject matter experts and collaborative thought partners that – in partnership with local affiliate staff and leaders from across the country – create, connect and curate resources, trainings, and promising practices along dedicated practice areas in support of capability building within the U.S. affiliated network. The Management and Operations Expertise Hub drives the aggregation and exchange of practice-based knowledge and application among affiliates and other subject matter experts in nonprofit management and operations, including topics such as governance and board management, finance, human resources, information technology, administration, compliance and risk management, and other day-to-day operational topics.

The Sr. Specialist will manage and support the development, delivery/facilitation, evaluation and socialization of new and refreshed resource/training content, services, and support within the Management and Operations Expertise Hub to maximize the management and operations of U.S. Habitat affiliates. The role supports the thoughtful and intentional curation of existing content/expertise from both the Habitat community and external partnerships to advance promising practices. The role must collaborate closely with HFHI affiliate-facing learning professionals to ensure that hub content is packaged and delivered in the most accessible and useful way to be relevant and accessible to Habitat’s diverse network, and is responsible for that delivery and facilitation.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## **Senior Specialist – Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub**

**Help strengthen the organizations that help families build a better future.**

Bring your expertise in nonprofit management, learning, and relationship building to Habitat for Humanity International. In this role, you’ll turn knowledge into practical tools, connect affiliate leaders with promising practices, and facilitate learning experiences that strengthen Habitat’s impact across the United States.

**Work setting:** Remote/home office (may work in-person or hybrid if desired and near an HFHI office and space is available)

**Location:** US REMOTE
**Domestic travel:** 20%

### **Essential Duties**

#### **Product and Services Development, Delivery, and Evaluation (60%)**

- Lead and/or contribute to the review, refresh, development, design, testing, delivery, and evaluation of quality, relevant, and timely content, products, and services (e.g., templates, toolkits, websites, webinars, peer learning and connection experiences, trainings, and other innovative learning approaches) aligned with hub topic areas for affiliate capability/capacity building and organizational/departmental standards and processes
- Collaborate across applicable HFHI departments, including affiliate learning consultants, external subject matter experts, and the affiliated network to ensure that resource content and support aligns with best practices, mission, values, and guiding principles.
- Design, coordinate, and facilitate Communities of Practice, Peer Connection Chats, and other training experiences for the affiliate network, applying strong project management practices, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
- Stay informed on nonprofit management and operations trends, risks, and opportunities (e.g. topics such as governance and board management, finance, human resources, information technology, administration, compliance and risk management, and other day-to-day operational topics) to ensure content, resources, and services are relevant, timely, and impactful for the US affiliate network.
- Support other key initiatives, as directed, through project management, stakeholder engagement, subject matter expertise, and effective use of data and content curation tools.

#### **Network Outreach, Engagement, Relationship Building, and General/SME Support (40%)**

- Provide high-quality service and support to the affiliate network, answering inquiries, identifying needs, and creating opportunities for peer-to-peer learning and community building.
- Collaborate on marketing, communications, knowledge management, and outreach efforts to elevate the hub as a go-to resource for affiliate leaders, including leveraging and supporting MyHabitat, Viva Engage communities, regional and Affiliate Support Organization events and offerings, Affiliate Support Center inquiries, practitioner cohorts, and other opportunities for building awareness, usage, and satisfaction through subject matter expertise
- Foster engagement (in Viva Engage communities and other innovative approaches) by identifying common needs, sparking conversations with and among affiliates, aggregating promising practices from the field, and integrating insights into content and services.

#### **Performance Expectations**

- Successful completion of annual goals connected to Expertise Hubs and Division Objectives
- Annual network engagement/customer service metrics successfully met
- Annual quality and satisfaction metrics successfully met
- Measurement of additional expectations based on Annual Job plan
- Active demonstration of living out HFHI’s core values and being an active, cooperative team member

### **Cross Functional Capabilities**

- Employees in multiple divisions with different skillsets work together to achieve Habitat for Humanity International’s mission and common strategic goals.
- Key aspects of cross-functional responsibilities in a global non-profit include: Strategic planning, program design and implementation, communication and branding, monitoring and evaluation, and compliance and risk management.
- Strong understanding of business management and operations, including board governance, financial management, and risk prevention, particularly within non-profit organizations - Proficient
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, and results-driven environment. - Proficient
- Proven project management skills, including prioritization, time management, and delivering impact amidst competing demands. - Proficient
- Experience coordinating and facilitating training sessions, webinars, and group/team meetings. - Proficient
- Ability to develop, organize, and deliver content, tools, and resources to support programmatic and/or operational application, implementation, improvement and socialization. - Proficient
- Outstanding interpersonal skills, including emotional intelligence, relationship building, and the ability to influence and motivate others without authority Proficient
- Ability to navigate ambiguity by defining success, establishing systems, and driving clarity in complex situations. - Proficient
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to quickly gather, synthesize, and summarize information for diverse audiences. - Proficient
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor communication for different stakeholders and audiences. - Proficient
- Demonstrated commitment to excellent customer service and stakeholder engagement. - Proficient
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and comfort using digital platforms (e.g., Smartsheet, SharePoint, Salesforce, other CRMs, online meeting tools). - Proficient

### **Preferred Requirements**

- Experience with Habitat for Humanity, other federated nonprofit organizations, or membership organizations
- Experience presenting or leading trainings (virtual and in-person)
- Project management experience
- Understanding of the HFH mission
- Active support of HFHI Values:
- Humility – We are part of something bigger than ourselves
- Courage – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular
- Accountability – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission
- Safeguarding: HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.

**Ready to put your expertise to work for Habitat’s mission? Apply to join our Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub.**

Please note that applications for this position will be accepted through **December 11, 2026**. Interested candidates are encouraged their applications before the deadline.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$63,900.00 USD

\-

$95,100 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

jobs.title: People & Culture Manager
jobs.description:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

**Job Overview/Summary**

The People & Culture (P&C) Manager oversees and implements people & culture activities for an assigned portfolio of IRC offices or departments, providing a spectrum of services from tactical to strategic. They are part of the local Leadership Team and are expected to contribute to strategic direction setting and operational problem solving through their areas of professional expertise. The P&C Manager collaborates with the People & Culture Director and Labor Relations Team to ensure adherence to organizational policies, procedures, and applicable collective bargaining agreements, while leading efforts to maintain compliance with local labor laws. This position can be based in Wichita, Kansas, with the expectation of regular travel between Wichita & Kansas City, as well as supporting other offices within the United States network.

**Major Responsibilities**

Provide support and drive progress of key bodies of work within a broad range of people and culture areas:

- IRC Way: model, promote and uphold a culture of values as reflected in our code of conduct, The IRC Way: Standards for Professional Conduct – Integrity, Service, Accountability, and Equality.
- HR Knowledge: serve as a reliable source of HR policies, practices and processes in response to employee and/or supervisor requests, ensuring compliance with internal and external standards and applicable labor laws, including state and city-specific labor law. Support the development and refinement of key HR lifecycle processes as needed.
- Advisor: Serve as a trusted advisor to managers and leadership on people-related matters, providing guidance on performance management, policy interpretation, and organizational decisions to support sound, compliant, and people-centered outcomes.
- Employee Support: facilitate resolution of escalated issues related to basic employee welfare needs regarding benefits, payroll, HRIS, Leaves of Absence, and general employee questions.
- Employee Relations: lead intake, make recommendations, and support resolution of sensitive employee relations matters and workplace investigations.
- Employee Experience: lead initiatives that strengthen organizational culture, drive employee engagement, and ensure an inclusive workplace where all staff feel valued and respected
- Talent Acquisition: oversee onboarding of new staff, with the goal to ensure new hire and orientation practices are implemented in accordance with IRC standards.
- Talent Management: participate in core talent activities as relevant and become proficient in delivering select training and development seminars; lead the development of a local talent-development strategy and oversee implementation.
- Employee Exits: monitor and intervene as necessary to ensure IRC standards are met for separation forms, exit paperwork, and exit surveys.
- HR Administration: Manage and maintain electronic office personnel records of employees and prepare paperwork with supporting documentation for Workday transactions to include new hires, staff transfers, supervisory changes, separations, etc.
- P&C Community: Actively contribute to a nationwide P&C community of practice, partnering with peers across the IRC network to align on best practices, troubleshoot shared challenges, and strengthen consistency in how P&C services are delivered organization-wide.
- Manage background check procedures for staff and independent contractors.
- May manage a small team.
- May support multiple offices in the south-central
- Other duties as assigned.

**Working Environment**

- Hybrid work with a minimum of 4 days in office.
- A combination of standard office environment and remote work.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Occasional travel to other IRC offices may be required.

**Job Requirements**

***Education:***

- Bachelor's degree, preferably in Human Resources or Business Administration; or equivalent experience.
- Master’s degree in human resources management a plus.

***Work Experience:***

- Minimum five (5) years progressively responsible Human Resources experience
- PHR or SHRM-CP certification preferred.
- Advanced working knowledge of at least one human resources discipline including: employee relations, compensation and benefits, performance management, learning and development, organizational development, labor relations, etc.
- Prior experience leading workplace investigations and supporting the resolution of employee relations matters required
- Prior experience working in a unionized environment is a plus
- Experience in a large, matrixed organization a plus

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Strong grasp of HR concepts, including Federal & State employment laws
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong learning agility: capable of adapting quickly to change and apply new information and skills to work duties.
- Self-motivated to plan, prioritize and problem solve independently.
- Ability to build and foster effective and positive working relationships with colleagues and maintain confidentiality to the highest degree.
- Proficient in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; experience in Workday and applicant tracking systems a plus
- Facilitation, Change Management and/or Project Management experience a plus.
- Experience successfully working in a multicultural environment.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $71,000-$74,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.description:
**OBJETIVO DEL CARGO**

El oficial de Diagnóstico, Monitoreo y Evaluación es responsable de diseñar, implementar y supervisar sistemas robustos de diagnóstico, monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y aprendizaje (MEAL), garantizando que la recolección y el análisis de datos aseguren la calidad técnica de los proyectos, el cumplimiento de los estándares globales de Acted y la transparencia ante beneficiarios y donantes para una toma de decisiones estratégica y oportuna, así como la mejora continua de los programas.

**Funciones y Responsabilidades**

1. Gestión de Sistemas MEAL

- Desarrollo Estratégico: Colaborar en la creación y actualización de la estrategia nacional, planes de trabajo, marcos lógicos de los proyectos y teorías de cambio de los proyectos.
- Aseguramiento de Calidad: Garantizar que las recomendaciones de MEAL se integren en nuevas propuestas, notas conceptuales y planes de ejecución.
- Cumplimiento Normativo: Aplicar las políticas estándar de Acted y asegurar el despliegue técnico de sistemas de recolección de datos para el personal y socios.

Ciclo de Evaluación: Diseñar TdR y ejecutar evaluaciones de línea base, intermedias y finales, cuando se requerido. Diseñar, adaptar y estandarizar herramientas de recolección de datos (encuestas, formularios, listas de asistencia, grupos focales, entrevistas a informantes claves, entre otros instrumentos claves para los proyectos), incluyendo evaluaciones de necesidades, cuando sea requerido, y monitoreo post-distribución. Garantizar la calidad metodológica de los procesos, la realización de pruebas piloto y la orientación a asistentes MEAL y encuestadores en terreno para la recolección de datos.

- Análisis y Reporte: Administrar, limpiar, validar y consolidar bases de datos cuantitativas y cualitativas, garantizando la calidad, confidencialidad y trazabilidad de la información. Analizar los datos recopilados para generar informes estadísticos, fichas técnicas y tableros de control (KPIs) que contribuyan a la toma de decisiones.
- Soporte a Programas: Proveer indicadores SMART y análisis de datos precisos y de calidad que respalden los reportes a donantes y contribuir a los esfuerzos de recaudación de fondos.
- Seguimiento y monitoreo de proyectos: Asegurar el seguimiento sistemático del avance de los indicadores en línea con los marcos lógicos de los proyectos, identificando de manera oportuna brechas, riesgos y desviaciones que puedan afectar los resultados, y proponer acciones correctivas en coordinación con los equipos de programas. Brindar acompañamiento técnico y validar el cumplimiento de los indicadores de los socios implementadores de Acted, en coordinación con los equipos de programa y conforme a los resultados establecidos.
- Realizar visitas de monitoreo a terreno para verificar el adecuado funcionamiento de los mecanismos de retroalimentación comunitaria.

2\. Gestión del Aprendizaje y Mejora Continua

- Capitalización de Conocimientos: Documentar lecciones aprendidas y mejores prácticas para facilitar la mejora de proyectos actuales y futuros.
- Eventos de Aprendizaje: Organizar talleres de cierre y reflexión para identificar éxitos y retos operativos.
- Corrección de Rumbo: Proveer retroalimentación oportuna a los gerentes de proyecto para permitir ajustes estratégicos durante la implementación.

3\. Mecanismo de Respuesta y Rendición de Cuentas (CRM)

- Diseño y Adaptación del CRM: diseñar, revisar y ajustar los Mecanismos de Queja y Respuesta (CRM) existentes para garantizar su adecuación a las realidades socioculturales, lingüísticas y operativas de las comunidades atendidas, promoviendo la participación segura e inclusiva de los beneficiarios.
- Operatividad del CRM: Implementar, supervisar y dar seguimiento al funcionamiento del Mecanismo de Quejas y Respuestas (CRM) siguiendo los estándares institucionales, asegurando su correcta aplicación en terreno, accesibilidad y socialización efectiva con las comunidades
- Gestión de Casos: Asegurar que las quejas, retroalimentaciones y solicitudes se capturen, analicen y respondan de forma oportuna y confidencial, manteniendo la base de datos central del CRM actualizada. Asegurar la activación de mecanismos de derivación seguros y apropiados en casos sensibles o de protección, conforme a los protocolos de Acted.
- Sensibilización: Capacitar al personal, socios y contratistas en temas de responsabilidad hacia los beneficiarios, funcionamiento del CRM y gestión de riesgos, con el fin de prevenir malas prácticas y asegura una interacción ética y responsable con las comunidades
- Comunicación y retroalimentación programática: Analizar de manera sistemática las sugerencias, observaciones, quejas y tendencias identificadas a través del CRM, y comunicar oportunamente los hallazgos relevantes al líder del proyecto, resguardando en todo momento la confidencialidad con las comunidades, con el objetivo de apoyar en la adopción de acciones correctivas y ajustes en la implementación de actividades para mejorar la calidad, pertinencia y aceptación de los proyectos en las comunidades.

4\. Liderazgo y Gestión de Equipo

Supervisión Directa: Coordinar el trabajo diario de asistentes, monitores y encuestadores, asegurando la comprensión de sus roles.

- Desarrollo de Capacidades: Identificar necesidades de formación, realizar evaluaciones de desempeño y brindar mentoría técnica al equipo.
- Clima Laboral: Promover un entorno de trabajo positivo y gestionar la resolución de conflictos internos.

## Requisitos

Obligatorios:

- Licenciado titulado (a) en: Sociología, Antropología, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Políticas, Ciencias Sociales, Ciencias actuariales, Economía o carrera afín.
- Experiencia profesional relevante en entorno humanitario o de desarrollo, preferiblemente en temas de monitoreo y evaluación.
- Alta capacidad de redacción, análisis y síntesis.
- Habilidad para la gestión de equipos.
- Capacidad de adaptación e interés por el trabajoen un entorno intercultural
- Manejo avanzado en Excel para el registro, descarga de datos, limpieza, organización y seguimiento de bases de datos e indicadores, incluyendo el uso de macros, Power Query y VBA.
- Manejo intermedio en programas relacionados a la gestión, limpieza y análisis de datos (R, PowerBI, SPSS, Stata, Tableau, Nvivo, Atlas.ti)
- Manejo intermedio en herramientas de recolección de datos para actividades de monitoreo y seguimiento (KoboToolbox, ODK Collect, SurveryCTO, CommCare, Microsoft Forms)
- capacidad para gestionar múltiples cronogramas de monitoreo de distintos proyectos
- Pensamiento Analítico: Capacidad para interpretar grandes volúmenes de datos y transformarlos en información estratégica para la toma de decisiones.
- Redacción Técnica de Alto Nivel: Habilidad para elaborar informes de monitoreo, estudios de caso y reportes para donantes con claridad, síntesis y rigor lógico.
- **Competencias:**
- Integridad ética en el manejo de reportes y análisis de información, evitando sesgos o manipulación de datos.
- Capacidad para interactuar con poblaciones vulnerables, garantizando un entorno seguro durante la recolección de datos.
- Mantener una postura objetiva frente a los resultados de los programas y las quejas de beneficiarios.
- Disposición para investigar la causa raíz.
- Habilidad para facilitar espacios de reflexión.

Deseables (no obligatorios):

- Experiencia en facilitación de talleres
- Manejo del idioma Inglés

## Condiciones

- Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de Honorarios Profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de Acted en Caracas.
- Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.

**Caracas – Distrito Capital**

jobs.title: GORS Program Lead - DRC
jobs.description:
**Location:** Kisangani, Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of Congo

**Position Type**: Consultancy (40 hours per week)

**Length of contract**: 3 months, Renewable subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funding.

**Compensation:** Rates competitive for DRC

**Background**

Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG) leads the Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) program in support of the U.S. Department of State. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), GORS requires effective country leadership to translate agreed program objectives into coordinated implementation in Tshopo Province, including support to provincial health authorities and implementing partners and the activation of Rapid Response Teams when required.

The position brings together program management and oversight of the support services needed for delivery. It ensures that technical activities are feasible, appropriately resourced and implemented efficiently, with clear accountability for results, expenditure, personnel and operational risk. It maintains programmatic and operational coordination with the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC), while preserving each program’s separate mandate, management, and contractual accountability.

**Requirements Overview, reporting line and working relationships**

Lead the coordinated, cost-efficient implementation of GORS in the DRC, delivering agreed results to the required quality and within approved budgets and timeframes. Align technical delivery with finance, human resources, logistics, supply chain and security support, and maintain effective relationships with government counterparts, implementing partners, DART representatives and the GORS HQ team.

The post holder reports directly to the GORS Program Director, based in Washington, DC. The Program Director sets objectives, agrees priorities and delegated authority, reviews performance and resolves matters requiring program-level approval. The position has one direct management reporting line.

The post holder works closely with the following senior colleagues, whose specialist responsibilities remain in place:

- Senior Technical Director: technical priorities, quality standards, technical supervision and validation of program results.
- Senior Safety and Security Lead: security policy, specialist risk advice, incident escalation and decisions reserved to the security management framework.
- Director of Field Operations and Security: country operational and security backstopping, preparedness and incident-response coordination.
- Senior Operations Lead: operational systems, finance and administrative support, HR processes, compliance and escalation of support-service constraints.
- Senior Logistics Lead: logistics and supply chain strategy, planning; procurement, assets and fleet standards, and technical backstopping.

The post holder coordinates agreed program priorities and day-to-day delivery and provides documented performance feedback to the designated manager. Technical personnel retain functional guidance from the relevant technical leads; security personnel retain specialist direction through the approved security reporting arrangements.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

1. **Program leadership and implementation**

- Translate approved GORS objectives into a consolidated provincial implementation plan with defined activities, geographic coverage, deliverables, staffing, resource requirements and milestones.
- Lead routine implementation reviews with technical and support teams. Align priorities and resolve scheduling, resource and delivery constraints before they affect agreed results.
- Monitor progress, quality, expenditure and delivery risks. Identify underperformance or changing needs and propose corrective actions, reprioritization or resource adjustments to the Program Director.
- Ensure that problem-solving support to selected Health Areas has an agreed purpose, defined activities, counterpart responsibilities and measurable completion criteria.
- Promote proportionate staffing and support arrangements, compare operational options and avoid unnecessary costs or duplication while maintaining delivery quality and duty-of-care requirements.

**2. Representation and stakeholder coordination**

- Serve as the official GORS focal point for the Government of the DRC (GDRC) and implementing partners within delegated authority. Maintain effective engagement with the provincial government health office and relevant national, provincial and local counterparts.
- Coordinate and document agreements on geographic areas of operation, including Health Areas receiving problem-solving support and locations considered for Rapid Response activation. Obtain required internal approvals before committing resources or changing approved scope.
- Serve as the designated GORS Program focal point for US Dept of State DART, when required. Maintain regular communication, facilitate field engagement and consolidate requests and follow-up actions in coordination with the Program Director.
- Represent GORS in relevant coordination forums, communicate agreed program positions and maintain a stakeholder contact and action record. Refer contractual, policy or resource commitments beyond delegation to the Program Director.
- Maintain a constructive support relationship with authorities and implementing partners. Distinguish GORS support commitments from decisions and responsibilities that remain with the competent public authorities or partner organizations.

**3. Rapid Response planning and activation**

- Liaise with the provincial government health office and relevant partners to identify when and where GORS Rapid Response support is needed, informed by technical assessment and operational feasibility.
- Develop a documented activation proposal specifying the response objective, location, scope, timeframe, activities, success metrics, costs, counterpart arrangements and transition or closure criteria.
- Obtain technical validation and the required program, budget and security approvals before activation. Confirm transport, accommodation, equipment, communications and referral arrangements with the responsible leads.
- Coordinate deployment and implementation, ensuring that the Response Coordinator has clear objectives, reporting requirements and support arrangements. Review progress and escalate requests for changes to scope, duration or resources.
- Coordinate response closure, handover and after-action review. Consolidate results, expenditure and lessons to inform subsequent activations.

**4. Project data and donor reporting**

- Coordinate provincial project data collection and consolidate timely, accurate inputs to support the preparation of donor-facing reports, working with technical leads, MEL personnel, and other relevant staff.
- Monitor the country team’s contribution to donor reporting obligations through an agreed reporting calendar. Assign input owners and internal deadlines and follow up missing or delayed contributions.
- Review country inputs for completeness, consistency and supporting evidence. Seek technical and financial validation from the responsible specialists and resolve discrepancies before forwarding reporting packages.
- Prepare draft donor reports, responses to data calls, briefing notes and implementation updates for HQ review. Clearly explain achievements, constraints, expenditure variances, risks and proposed corrective actions.
- Provide HQ with cleared country inputs by agreed internal deadlines and track feedback and revisions. Final donor-report approval and formal submission remain with the HQ team unless explicitly delegated in writing.

**5. Finance budget and cost control**

- Maintain oversight of the GORS program budget with the finance team. Review expenditure, commitments, cash requirements and forecasts against the implementation plan and approved funding.
- Analyze significant variances and the cost implications of changes to activities or deployment plans. Recommend adjustments early and obtain approval for reallocations or expenditure beyond delegated limits.
- Ensure that requests and expenditure have a documented program purpose, correct budget allocation and complete supporting records. Maintain separation between requesting, verifying receipt, approving expenditure, and executing payment.
- Oversee timely preparation of cash forecasts, advances, expense reconciliations and invoice packages. Follow up outstanding documentation and unresolved provider or payment issues with the relevant finance and operations colleagues.
- Review the value and performance of support arrangements with operations and logistics leads. Document cost-efficiency opportunities and apply approved cost-allocation arrangements where services are coordinated with another program (HASC).

**6. Logistics and daily operational support**

- Oversee daily operating readiness, including functional office space, utilities, staff accommodation where required, communications, equipment, transport and movement arrangements.
- Coordinate, supply chain, procurement and logistics planning with the Logistics Coordinator and Senior Logistics Lead so that technical and field requirements enter a consolidated, prioritized supply and service plan.
- Oversee vehicle and driver availability, rental-service performance, movement schedules and supporting records. Ensure that service requests, logbooks and invoices managed by the Fleet Officer are consistent with approved activities and contract terms.
- Oversee effective inventory, asset custody, maintenance and handover arrangements. Review service-provider performance and require corrective action through the appropriate procurement and contract-management channels.
- Anticipate operational bottlenecks and arrange timely support with the Senior Logistics Lead and the Director of field Ops and Security DFOS. Ensure that qualified corporate advisers, including accounting or legal support where required, address issues within their remit.

**7. Safety, security and operational risk**

- Act as the program focal point for operational risk mitigation. Maintain a consolidated risk register covering delivery, financial, HR, logistics, security and relevant health-related operational risks, with mitigation measures, owners and escalation triggers.
- Ensure that approved security plans, briefings, movement procedures, communications and tracking arrangements are applied to GORS activities, with specialist support from the Senior Safety and Security Lead, DFOS and Safety and Security Coordinator.
- Integrate security, access and emergency-response requirements into activity planning, accommodation, procurement and deployment decisions. Ensure that personnel receive required security and relevant health or IPC briefings before deployment.
- Immediately escalate incidents and significant concerns through the established notification chain. Coordinate program support to the designated incident-management lead and follow up agreed corrective actions.
- Take immediate protective action when necessary, including pausing an activity where essential controls are absent, and promptly escalate. Obtain specialist review and the required authorization before resumption; residual-risk acceptance and security approvals remain with the designated authorities.

**8. People management and team development**

- Maintain a staffing and deployment plan linked to approved activities and budgets. Define duties, duty stations, competencies, supervision arrangements and recruitment priorities with the relevant technical and support leads.
- Work with HR and recruitment colleagues to finalize position descriptions, contribute to shortlisting and interviews when required, and provide documented selection recommendations. Hiring approvals, contractual terms and contract signatures follow the authorized HR process.
- Ensure that incoming personnel DRC-based staff complete onboarding and induction and receive clear objectives, reporting lines, initial workplans and the tools needed to perform their roles.
- Set and follow up objectives for direct reports. Coordinate country work schedules, attendance, leave, travel, workload and handovers within delegation and with the designated technical line managers.
- Provide regular coaching and documented feedback. Contribute evidence and recommendations to DRC-based staff evaluations led by HQ, including probation, development needs and contract-renewal reviews, according to the agreed HR process.
- Promote respectful conduct, staff wellbeing and timely compliance with administrative requirements. Refer grievances, safeguarding concerns or disciplinary matters through the appropriate confidential HR channels.

**9. Coordination with HASC Program**

- Maintain regular programmatic and operational liaison with HASC teams in country to understand respective activities, geographic coverage, field presence and deployment plans.
- Identify complementary support and practical coordination opportunities that reduce duplication, improve situational awareness or make transport, accommodation, communications and other services more efficient. Submit proposed arrangements through the relevant program and functional authorities.
- Document approved coordination and any service-sharing arrangements, including responsibilities, access to information and cost allocation. Preserve separate program workplans, budgets, donor reporting, management authority and contractual accountability.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- Advanced degree or equivalent senior experience in international development, humanitarian response, program management or a related field.
- At least 15 years of progressively responsible program leadership in complex environment.
- Demonstrated management of multidisciplinary teams, substantial budgets and high-risk international operations.
- Strong experience in emergency-response governance, risk and compliance management.
- Proven ability to make timely, documented decisions under uncertainty and maintain constructive senior relationships.
- Fluent professional English and French.
- DRC nationality

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

Adherence and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travel Frequency and working arrangements**

The position is based in Kisangani and requires a sustained in-country presence, with regular field travel within Tshopo Province and other approved travel in the DRC as operationally required. Deployments are subject to the applicable security and movement-clearance arrangements. The post holder complies with GEG conduct, PSEA policies, security, health and administrative policies and maintains reliable communication with the HQ team. Working arrangements and availability during response activations will be agreed with the Program Director in accordance with the contract.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

jobs.title: Global Donor Engagement Officer
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

We’re striving to build an organization that is a supportive, kind and inspiring place to work. We encourage bold leadership, innovation, creative partnerships and accountability to those we serve.

The Awards Management Unit (AMU) is a global unit with teams in New York, Washington DC, London, Nairobi, Berlin, Stockholm and Amman with staff presence in many other locations around the world. Its purpose is to lead IRC’s work to engage and influence government donors, secure funding, and enable compliant and effective program delivery for our clients. The AMU sits within IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department, alongside IRC’s international country programs, emergencies unit and technical teams.

This role sits in AMU's **Global Business Development (BD) Team**, which leads IRC's public business development strategy and engagement for the organization’s international work, and helps align resources across the organization to strengthen donor engagement and drive BD to secure funding.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Global Donor Engagement Officer will report to the Donor Engagement Director, and work closely with Donor Engagement Advisors, Regional Heads of Business Development, and wider AMU, CRRD and Policy & Advocacy colleagues.

The Officer will provide flexible support across multiple donors to help IRC deliver its public BD Strategy. Specifically, the role will coordinate support for donor engagement, relationship building, and influence with the US Department of State (DoS) and other relevant US government agencies, with Green Climate Fund (GCF), Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) and other institutional donors as assigned. The Officer will draw on these relationships and networks to build a portfolio of tools, information and assets that enable IRC to engage donors proactively, influence their strategies, and pursue priority funding streams.

The Officer will serve as a key donor engagement support resource in Washington, coordinating with internal and external Washington-based counterparts.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Strategy**

- Provide support to the Donor Engagement Director in development of relevant donor strategies (which may include research, coordination and some writing) for key donors in the portfolio **(USG, GCF, and emerging MDBs)**.
- Coordinate action plans related to strategy implementation, report-on progress, lessons-learned, and how risks are being managed and mitigated.

**Portfolio Management**

- Support the Donor Engagement Director with the departmental co-leadership of the **Green Climate Fund**, working together with the Climate Global Practice team. Support efforts to drive and track GCF accreditation, pipeline development, strategy development, and donor coordination in partnership with relevant teams.
- Convene and manage info and intelligence on IRC's engagement with **US DoS** (and other USG agencies as relevant) and **MDBs**, coordinating that engagement where relevant.
- Build and coordinate a network of contacts within relevant donor teams to enable effective outreach and engagement.
- Represent the IRC at external meetings, events, and forums as appropriate.

**Coordination, Research and Knowledge Management**

- Map donor organizational structures and identify key contacts to help IRC achieve its strategic aims.
- Use Salesforce to plan, track, and maintain a register of donor engagement at country, regional, and global levels; triangulate information across levels so staff are well briefed and consistent in their donor engagement and influence.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of assigned donors' strategies relevant to IRC's work, such as funding priorities, geographic interests, and political climate.
- Analyze and summarize press releases, policies, and other announcements, and share them internally.
- Research, track, and update data and analysis on strategy, funding trends, and peer activity for US DoS, GCF, and MDBs.
- Develop materials (strategy summaries, donor profiles, primers on donor funding, talking points, etc.) that equip colleagues engaging with assigned donors to demonstrate alignment between IRC and donor technical priorities.
- Support the Donor Engagement Director in developing, maintaining, and improving donor tracking tools and resources
- Serve as the focal point enabling IRC visitors to DC (including Regional and Technical Leadership, Country Directors, Regional VPs, and the President/CEO) to engage with relevant donors, working in partnership with CRRD (International) and Policy & Advocacy, with the Donor Engagement Director, and relevant Donor Advisors, including the World Bank Donor Engagement Advisor.

**Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:**

We are seeking a candidate with diversity of experience (i.e., paid and volunteer work; lived experiences; transferable skills from another industry etc.)

**Job Requirements:**

- 3-6 years relevant experience in humanitarian and international development, business development, donor relations, policy or advocacy or a combination of these.
- Experience working with humanitarian and development donors and including experience with US Government, GCF, World Bank or other Multilateral Development Banks.
- Strong collaboration approaches, in a large organizational setting.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentations, and development of effective briefing material.
- Ability to work well under pressure in a fast-paced and changing environment with multiple stakeholders.
- Good analytical skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Experience undertaking reviews of policies and reports, producing associated written and verbal guidance to relevant staff.
- Excellent interpersonal skills. Ability to collaborate with others and work as part of a team.

**Preferred experience & skills:**

- Technical knowledge of IRC thematic work, particularly climate related work.
- Experience of having worked with new and innovative financing models in humanitarian and international development.

Candidates must have the right to work within the country they are applying. IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($68,000 - $82,023.30 annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Sterile Processing Project Manager
jobs.description:
**Who We Are**
Mercy Ships is a global faith-based charity that uses hospital ships to bring life-changing surgeries and transformational medical training to people in some of the most challenging contexts along the African coast. For over 40 years, Mercy Ships has been delivering lasting hope and healing through safe surgical care, while working alongside partners and stakeholders to strengthen local healthcare systems in more than 55 countries. Since the inception of this dream by founders Don and Deyon Stephens in 1978, Mercy Ships has served more than 2.7 million direct beneficiaries without regard for race, gender, or religion.

Do you have a heart for the hurting and a desire to invest your talents and experiences into a mission with eternal significance? For every transformative surgery that takes place onboard one of our Mercy Ships, there are dozens of men and women being used of the Lord to prepare the way through their vocational gifts and talents!

**This is a full-time position with the initial on-site deployment in Sierra Leone and requires international travel.**

As a Sterile Processing Project Manager, you will work together with the Program Director and the International Programs department, and partner country stakeholders to develop and implement sterile processing programs in the designated partner country to achieve country objectives for development and advancement of the sterile processing workforce and service delivery.

**How You Will Contribute:**

- Requires primary work location in a partner nation.
- Develop, coordinate, and maintain clear lines of communication between Ministry of Health, national hospitals and education institutions, and training participants for sterile processing training and/or mentorship programs.
- Conduct assessment of training needs in collaboration with the Program Director, Regional Director, and Country Director.
- Co-design, develop and deliver appropriate sterile processing training and mentorship programs that address the country goals for sterile processing workforce development.
- Develop relationships with national partners, healthcare agencies and other national or international Non-Government Organizations to enhance program delivery and strategic outcomes.
- Ensure practical coordination, implementation, and monitoring of project activities to meet expected results, together with partners.
- Line manage Mercy Ships Sterile Processing Technicians based in partner nation.
- Provide technical expertise and practical support for equipment selection, donation and commissioning for hospitals in the partner nation.
- Provide technical expertise and practical support for (re)design of sterile processing departments for hospitals in the partner nation.
- Provide technical expertise about consumables that hospitals in the partner nation need to procure for sterile processing activities.
- Participate in the Equipment Donation Review Team (EDRT) as needed.
- Collaborate with the Program Governance and Coordination (PGC) team Program Quality and Impact (PQI) team for the implementation of monitoring and evaluation plans and all necessary project documentation including concept papers, project plans, requests for proposals (RFPs), partnership agreements, and final reports.
- Work together with the MEL Specialist in-country to collect data at pre-agreed intervals, generate reports and deliver regular reflective reviews with implementing partners.
- Document processes related to program delivery to increase the effectiveness of future programs.
- Manage project budget and report spending in Emburse Professional, in a timely manner.
- Prepare internal and final project reports in collaboration with the Program Officer and Program Director in a timely manner, according to project reporting cycles.
- Write and create content for internal and external communication describing sterile processing projects to help share the work of International Programs.
- Support project assessment, development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation in new and existing partner countries, as requested, to expand programmatic activity (surge involves travel).
- Maintains alignment and upholds Mercy Ships Core Values, Code of Conduct, and follows the policies and procedures published on Compass.
Follows the model of Jesus and aligns with our core values by Loving God; Loving and Serving Others; Being a Person of Integrity; and a Person of Excellence in all you say and do.
- Other duties may be assigned that are not included in the information provided in this job description.

**Ideal Candidate:**

- Supportive of Mercy Ships mission and vision and committed to its core values.
- Understand and apply servant leadership, work collaboratively with integrity, and demonstrate accountability.
- Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage complex projects from creation to completion, plan and prioritize multiple deliverables, and coordinate to meet deadlines.
- Ability to adapt skills in challenging work settings.
- Must have excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Must possess cross-cultural awareness and sensitivity.
- Familiarity with medical terminology, anatomy and physiology is required.
- Possess a strong customer service mindset including attitude and approach.
- Must be fluent in English, both written and verbal.
- French language skills - International B1 Level (or equivalent) are strongly desired, B2 level desirable when serving in Francophone countries.
- Full, clean international driving license strongly preferred.

**Education and/or Experience:**

- At least 5 years' experience as a Sterile Processing Technician
- Experience providing sterile processing training in resource-constrained settings
- Experience in managing sterile processing staff
- Experience working with and/or delivering sterile processing training with educational institutions preferred.
- Certification in sterile processing from recognized professional body preferred

jobs.title: Broadcasting of Interactive Radio Awareness Programmes on Protection, Child Protection, Gender Equality, Inclusion, Technology-Facilitated Gender-Base
jobs.description:
The SMART (Multisectoral Strategic Action on Food Security and Protection for Strengthening Resilience) Project is an integrated resilience and protection initiative implemented by AVSI Foundation and Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) in Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties of Garissa County. The project seeks to strengthen the resilience of refugee and host communities while improving access to essential protection services for women, children, refugees, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable populations affected by protracted displacement, poverty, protection risks and recurrent climate-related shocks.

Under Outcome 2, the project aims to strengthen community-based protection systems and improve access to quality protection services through a combination of capacity strengthening, referral system enhancement, community mobilization, awareness raising, and stakeholder engagement. The intervention is grounded in a prevention and response approach that seeks to strengthen community awareness of rights, available services, protection risks and reporting mechanisms while promoting positive social norms, inclusion, accountability and social cohesion.

To date, the project has achieved several foundational milestones, including the completion of protection and gender-based violence service mapping, strengthening and updating of referral pathways, development of protection tools and reporting mechanisms and capacity strengthening of community-based protection structures and frontline responders. A total of 62 (**32f, 30m,43 host and 19 refugees**) protection actors, including Community Protection Focal Points, community leaders, religious leaders, government representatives, police gender desk officers, health actors and humanitarian stakeholders, have been trained on protection, child protection, gender equality, inclusion, GBV prevention and response, survivor-centered approaches, refugee protection and safe referral mechanisms. The community Protection Focal Points will be used as panelists and as community mobilisers for listener groups.

The training assessments, service mapping exercises, stakeholder consultations, and community engagement processes identified key protection concerns requiring sustained community awareness and behaviour change interventions. These include child trafficking, child labour, early and child marriage, gender-based violence, technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), family separation, discrimination, disability exclusion, limited awareness of available protection services, weak reporting mechanisms and persistent misconceptions regarding refugee rights and the implementation of the Shirika Plan, the Government of Kenya's plan, under the Refugees Act 2021, to transition refugee camps into integrated settlements with the host community. SMART is also a food security and resilience project, drought, food insecurity and economic stress drive negative coping (child labor, early marriage, family separation) mechanisms; hence the panelists will embed this agenda across their discussions.

Recognizing the wide reach and influence of radio as a community information and engagement platform, the SMART Project intends to utilize interactive radio programming as a strategic awareness-raising mechanism to disseminate accurate information, strengthen community dialogue, amplify the voices of refugees and host communities, promote positive behaviour change and increase awareness of available protection services and referral pathways.

In light of this, AVSI Foundation and Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) seek to engage a qualified radio station, media house, communications firm, or consultant to design, produce and broadcast a series of interactive radio awareness programmes that contribute to the prevention of protection risks and the promotion of safe, inclusive, and rights-based communities across Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The purpose of this assignment is to design, produce and broadcast a series of high-quality interactive radio programmes that enhance community awareness of protection risks, strengthen positive social norms, improve knowledge of available protection services and referral pathways, and promote safe and inclusive access to protection mechanisms among refugee and host communities in Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties. The assignment is expected to contribute to sustainable behaviour change by translating strengthened community protection systems, trained frontline actors and updated referral pathways into practical community knowledge and action.

**Specific objectives**

1. Increase knowledge among refugee and host communities of protection risks, rights and available services
2. Increase awareness of how and where to report protection concerns using the updated referral pathways and hotlines
3. Challenge harmful social norms that drive child marriage, child labour, GBV and exclusion of persons with disabilities
4. Provide accurate information to counter misinformation on refugee rights and the Shirika Plan
5. Create a two-way channel for community questions and feedback to inform project adaptation.
6. Contribute to the commemoration of the **16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence (25 November - 10 December 2026)** by promoting awareness, prevention, accountability, and community action to address gender-based violence and harmful social norms.

### Scope of Work

The selected service provider shall be responsible for

1. The production and broadcasting of interactive radio programmes aimed at promoting protection awareness and community engagement.
2. The service provider will work closely with AVSI Foundation and Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) to ensure that all broadcast content is technically accurate, culturally appropriate, gender-responsive and aligned with project objectives.
3. While AVSI and SOLO shall provide and approve the technical protection messaging, thematic content and referral information, the service provider will be responsible for packaging approved content into engaging radio formats that maximize audience reach, participation and behavior change.
4. The provider shall develop an implementation schedule, coordinate guest speakers and panel discussions, facilitate audience participation, produce and broadcast the programmes, document audience engagement and submit comprehensive reports on programme reach, participation and key issues raised by listeners.

### Target Audience

The radio programmes will primarily target refugee and host communities residing in Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties, with particular emphasis on women and girls, children and youth, persons with disabilities, community leaders, religious leaders, men and boys, fathers, male guardians, adolescents caregivers, community protection structures and other vulnerable populations. Secondary audiences will include government departments, service providers, protection actors, humanitarian agencies and local stakeholders responsible for prevention, response and referral services.

### Expected Results

The assignment is expected to contribute to increased community awareness of child protection, refugee protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), prevention of child trafficking and early marriage, and available reporting and referral mechanisms. Through enhanced access to accurate information and direct engagement with knowledgeable stakeholders, the radio programmes are expected to strengthen community trust in protection systems, increase awareness of available services, promote positive social norms, encourage safe reporting and help-seeking behaviour and contribute to improved protection outcomes for vulnerable refugee and host populations.

Increased community awareness and engagement during the 16 Days of Activism campaign, contributing to positive attitudes and actions towards preventing gender-based violence and promoting gender equality.

**Indicators**

1. Number of programmes broadcast (target 20)
2. Estimated listenership per session (250)
3. Number of interactions (calls, SMS, WhatsApp) disaggregated by sex and, where possible, refugee/host status (no target)
4. Percentage of sampled listeners who can name at least two protection services or reporting channels (via a short pre/post listener survey)
5. Number of protection concerns referred as a result of the programmes (no target)

### Broadcasting Requirements

The service provider shall design, produce and broadcast twenty (20) interactive radio awareness programmes targeting refugee and host communities in Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties. Each programme shall run for approximately 60 minutes and be broadcast in Somali and Kiswahili during peak listening hours like 7–9 pm or 6-9am and avoid prayer times; with a combined estimated reach of at least 5,000 listeners, verified through the station’s audience data, interaction logs and a short listener survey. The programmes shall promote community awareness of protection risks, rights, available services, referral pathways and positive social norms while facilitating meaningful participation from community members and key stakeholders. Audience engagement should include moderated discussions, call-ins, SMS/WhatsApp interactions, public service announcements, storytelling, expert panels and question and answer sessions. The programmes shall be implemented in two phases. Phase I (November-December 2026) will consist of ten (10) radio broadcasts delivered over a five-week period, with two broadcasts conducted per week, while Phase II will comprise ten broadcasts between January and May 2027 according to an agreed schedule. The bidder must confirm signal coverage in all target areas, especially remote parts of Fafi; and include airtime costs for promos, PSAs and rebroadcasts in the bid.

The radio series shall address the protection priorities identified through community consultations, protection assessments, service mapping, referral pathway strengthening, and recent capacity strengthening activities undertaken under the SMART Project. While the service provider may propose innovative programming approaches, the thematic areas and protection messages shall be approved by AVSI and SOLO prior to broadcast.

In recognition of the **16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence (25 November - 10 December 2026)**, at least four (4) of the radio programmes shall be strategically aligned with the campaign and focus on gender equality, prevention of GBV, Technology-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence (TFGBV), positive masculinity, survivor-centred support, women's rights, accountability and community action to end violence against women and girls. The broadcasts shall promote community dialogue and reflection on the collective responsibility of individuals, leaders, institutions, and communities in preventing violence and advancing gender equality.

The schedule may also benefit from moving Session 10 (Safe Reporting and Referral Pathways) closer to the start, or repeating the referral and hotline information in every session, so listeners know where to go from the first broadcast. Consider closing the series with a “you asked, we answered” episode responding to questions raised in earlier sessions.

The radio programmes shall be implemented in two phases. **Phase I** (November-December 2026) will consist of ten (10) radio broadcasts delivered over a five-week period, with two broadcasts conducted per week, with specific emphasis on protection awareness, prevention, rights, referral pathways and the commemoration of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence. **Phase II** will consist of ten broadcasts in 2027 focusing on social norms transformation, community resilience, accountability, inclusion, livelihoods-protection linkages and sustainability of community-based protection mechanisms. Across all broadcasts, presenters shall announce available referral pathways, helplines and reporting mechanisms, including Childline 116, GBV reporting channels, safeguarding, PSEA and project feedback mechanisms.

The service provider shall coordinate the participation of relevant panelists in close consultation with AVSI and SOLO. AVSI and SOLO shall support engagement with key government departments, protection actors, referral service providers, community structures, and specialized agencies where necessary. At least one representative from the project protection team will participate in the programme where necessary to ensure the technical accuracy of messaging and alignment with project objectives.

Across all broadcasts, particular emphasis shall be placed on child protection, prevention of child trafficking, prevention of early and child marriage, gender equality, prevention of gender-based violence, technology-facilitated gender-based violence, refugee protection, disability inclusion, social cohesion, accountability to affected populations, and awareness of available protection services and referral pathways. The programmes should contribute to increased community confidence in reporting protection concerns, accessing services, and engaging with community-based protection mechanisms.

#### **Reporting and Supervision**

The selected service provider will work under the overall supervision of the SMART Project Protection Officer and in close coordination with AVSI Foundation and Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO). All programme concepts, discussion guides, scripts, promotional materials and broadcast schedules shall be submitted for review and approval prior to airing.
