**Senior Manager, Programs – CARE Vanuatu**

- Lead a development and humanitarian portfolio that advances gender equality and locally led change in Vanuatu
- Based in Port Vila, Vanuatu, with travel to program locations
- Local contract; strong preference for national candidates
- Regional applicants are also welcome; Vanuatu terms and conditions apply

**The Opportunity**

CARE is one of the world’s leading international development and humanitarian organisations, working around the globe to save lives and defeat poverty, with women and girls at the heart of everything we do. In Vanuatu, CARE focuses on gender equality, disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and inclusive governance to support communities, especially women, to lead, decide and thrive.

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Manager, Programs to lead CARE Vanuatu’s development and humanitarian portfolio, with accountability for program strategy, business development, program quality and partnership integration.

**What you’ll do:**

As Senior Manager, Programs, you will be responsible for:

- **Lead and review country program strategy** across development, humanitarian and influencing work, informed by contextual analysis, community and partner priorities and national development priorities.
- **Lead the funding pipeline and proposals with the Country Director**, identifying funding gaps, prioritising opportunities by strategic fit, capacity, risk and financial viability, and leading concept notes and proposals from concept to submission.
- **Support donor engagement and represent CARE**, as delegated, with the Country Director, CARE Australia and other CARE International Members and in government, civil society, donor and coordination forums, contributing funding intelligence and technical analysis.
- **Oversee portfolio performance and financial management**, including outcomes, workplans, quality and contractual commitments, working with financeand program managersto ensure realistic budgets and forecasts and timely action on significant variances.
- **Embed CARE’s partnership standards and lead program quality**: integrating partnership approaches across programs and proposals, and providing proportionate systems and coordinated support, including designated quality and technical staff.
- **Lead and manage designated staff**, setting clear objectives, providing regular supervision and performance reviews, and addressing performance concerns.
- **Support emergency preparedness, response and recovery**, working with the Country Director to clarify and resource Emergency Preparedness Plan responsibilities and leading agreed program contributions.
- **Oversee program and partnership risks**, ensuring appropriate mitigation, clear decision thresholds and escalation to the Country Director, with risks held by those best placed to manage them.

**Why work with us?**

You’ll join a values-driven team working to advance gender equality, social justice and locally led change in Vanuatu. This role offers the opportunity to shape a diverse portfolio, strengthen partnerships and contribute to meaningful development and humanitarian outcomes.

**About You**

To be successful in this role you will bring:

- A relevant tertiary qualification in international development, humanitarian action, social sciences or a related field, with several years of relevant experience managing significant financial, human and material resources.
- Demonstrated senior leadership of a multi-project development or humanitarian portfolio, including program design, MEAL, budgets, donor commitments, reporting, risk and adaptive management.
- Proven success managing funding pipelines and leading concept notes, proposals and budgets, supported by strong donor engagement, negotiation and representation skills.
- Practical experience working equitably with local partners and leading multidisciplinary teams across complex, multicultural environments.
- Excellent written and spoken English, strong analytical writing skills and applied knowledge of gender equality, disability inclusion, safeguarding, community accountability and humanitarian practice.

**How to apply:**

For more information on this opportunity and to review the position description go to [www.care.org.au/careers](http://www.care.org.au/careers)

To apply please attach your CV and cover letter addressing the selection criteria.
Applications will be reviewed as they are received, so we encourage you to apply early.

**Applications close:** 1 December 2026 at 11:59 pm.

**Questions about the role?**
Please contact the CARE Vanuatu HR team at Dorothy.Loli@careint.org. Human Resource & Administration Officer

*CARE Vanuatu is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and encourage applications from people living with a disability and/or have lived experience of disability. We also encourage people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds to apply.*

*Should you require any accommodations or support during the application process, please don’t hesitate to reach out and let us know.*

**Safeguarding & Compliance**

*All CARE Australia employees are required to undergo a National Police Check, a Working with Children Check and sign our Child Safeguarding Policy, Preventing Sexual Abuse & Harassment (PSEAH) policy and Code of Conduct.*

*CARE Australia is part of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme and will seek information from job applicants’ previous employers about incidents of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment, and/or child abuse the applicant may have been found guilty to have committed or about which an investigation was in the process of being carried out at the time of the termination of the applicant’s employment with that employer. By submitting the application, the job applicant confirms they have no objection to CARE Australia requesting the information specified above.*

jobs.title: Endline Consultant
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference for a Consolidated Endline Evaluation Report of:**

***“Foundations: Strengthening Adolescent Girls’ Sexual and Reproductive Health in Mali, Niger and Sierra Leone”***

1. Project Summary

**Type of assignment** - Consolidated Endline Evaluation Report

**Project start and end** - 26/07/2021- 30/06/2027

**Project duration** - 6 years

**Donor** - Global Affairs Canada (GAC)

**Thematic Areas** - Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health (ASRH), Gender Equality

**Project location** - Mali (Sikasso and Koutiala), Niger (Maradi and Diffa), Sierra Leone (Kailahun)

**Estimated reach** - 429,226 direct beneficiaries (259,218 girls, 96,553 boys, 52,131 women, and 30,153 men)

**International Partners** - International Rescue Committee (IRC), Equipop, SickKids Hospital, Overseas Development Institute (ODI)

**National Partners** - Mali (ACOD/3AG); Niger (SongES); Sierra Leone (PPASL, Ndomakeh Federation)

**Overall objectives of the project** - Enhance the empowerment of adolescent girls, particularly the most marginalized and vulnerable, to exercise their ASRH rights in Mali, Niger, and Sierra Leone

2\. Project Description

*Strengthening Adolescent Girls’ Sexual & Reproductive Health* (FOUNDATIONS) is a 6-year (July 27th, 2021 – June 30, 2027) multi-country, gender-transformative project, funded by Global Affairs Canada. The project aims to enhance the empowerment of adolescent girls, particularly the most marginalized and vulnerable, to exercise their ASRH rights in Mali, Niger, and Sierra Leone. To achieve this ultimate outcome, three key intermediate outcomes are realized:

- 1100: Increased decision-making by in-school and out-of-school adolescent girls on adolescent sexual and reproductive health (ASRH) issues and the use of ASRH services.
- 1200: Improved provision of gender-responsive, adolescent-friendly and quality ASRH services for adolescent girls.
- 1300: Improved effectiveness of key stakeholders, particularly women & girls’ rights organizations and government decisionmakers, to advocate for evidence-based, accountable and equitable ASRH policies, legal frameworks and services.

The project is grounded in a rights-based and gender-transformative approach that places women and girls at the centre. In alignment with GAC requirements and its Feminist International Assistance Policy (FIAP), the project promotes gender equality and girls’ empowerment by using a socio-ecological approach that recognizes the multiple and interdependent spheres of influence shaping adolescent behaviours and norms. By engaging parents, other adult caregivers, teachers, community leaders, health providers, civil society organizations (CSOs) including women’s rights organizations (WROs), and government decisionmakers, the project addresses these spheres simultaneously to generate sustainable and meaningful change.

Save the Children implements the FOUNDATIONS project in three countries (Mali, Niger, and Sierra Leone) and in partnership with multiple international partners, including the International Rescue Committee (IRC), Equipop, ODI (formerly Overseas Development Institute) and the Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids).

3\. Endline Evaluation Background

Three baseline reports (i.e. one per country) were produced at the start of the project using a common methodology developed by Save the Children Canada (SCC). Each baseline measured around 20 outcomes indicators, which are common to all three countries. The common methodology used the same data collection tools, sampling method and data analysis plans to measure each indicator consistently. Independent consultants were hired in each country to carry out data collection using the tools developed by SCC. Consultants then handed over clean datasets to SCC along with the results from all questions disaggregated by type of respondent, age and gender. Then, SCC calculated each indicator and drafted three baseline reports using a similar structure.

A similar process will be used with the endline evaluation, but instead of SCC drafting each individual report, an independent consultant will be hired to do this work. As with the baseline, the same outcome indicators will be measured and analysed, using the same tools, sampling method and data analysis plans, to ensure consistency and comparability of results between the baseline and the endline.

4\. Endline Evaluation Purposes and Uses

The purpose of this evaluation is three-fold. First, conducting an endline evaluation meets an accountability requirement of SCC towards GAC (and more broadly to Canadian taxpayers). The endline evaluation will determine the extent to which the project has met the results it set out to achieve, whether the project was relevant to the target population and efficient, and whether it produced meaningful changes in the lives of participants, and to what extent observed results are sustainable.

Second, considering the size, complexity and duration of this project, the endline evaluation will identify lessons learned, good practices and unintended outcomes (whether positive or negative) to inform future design and implementation of similar projects. The evaluation will identify and explore key factors that may have contributed to the achievement of results, or lack thereof.

Third, SCC will use the main findings of the evaluation for dissemination purposes, including with GAC and other donors, to showcase the achievements of the project. Therefore, the consolidated endline evaluation report will highlight the project's main findings and lessons learned for dissemination purposes.

5\. Scope of the Assignment

The selected consultant will produce **three endline reports** (one per country) and **one consolidated report** using the data provided by SCC, including the values from the following outcome indicators (please refer to the Roles and Responsibilities sections for more details):

***Ultimate Outcome Indicators:***

- 1000.1: % of VYA and OA girls who report they are empowered as it relates to SRH decision-making
- 1000.2: % of adolescents (15-19 and 20-24 years) who are currently (within last three months) using a modern method of contraception
- 1000.3: Age-specific fertility rate of girls aged 15-19 years

***Intermediate Outcome Indicators:***

- 1100.1: % of VYA and OA girls (and boys) who report using ASRH information and services in health facilities covering puberty and fertility, family planning, STDs, HIV/AIDS, abortion and post-abortion care, SGBV prevention and treatment
- 1100.2: % of VYA and OA girls (and boys) who report they are able to make decisions related to their SRH
- 1100.3: % of parents/caregivers (m/f) who support (emotional, physical, financial) their daughter’s decision-making power around SRH issues
- 1200.1: Extent to which health facilities have achieved quality of care standards in providing ASRH services
- 1200.2: Extent to which health facilities have achieved gender-responsive standards in providing ASRH services
- 1200.3: Extent to which health facilities have achieved adolescent-friendly standards in providing ASRH services
- 1300.1: No. of actions (e.g. national plans, policy statements, action plans, public declarations, budget allocations, etc.) taken by the government decisionmakers to promote equitable ASRH services for adolescent girls in the past five years
- 1300.2: No. of actions taken by women and girls’ rights organizations in advocating for evidence-based, accountable and equitable ASRH policies, legal frameworks and services in the past five years

***Immediate Outcome Indicators:***

- 1110.1 % of VYA and OA girls and boys who demonstrate knowledge of ASRH topics and life skills
- 1110.2: % of VYA and OA girls and boys who hold positive attitudes towards ASRH rights and gender equality
- 1110.3: % of VYA and OA girls and boys who perceive negative social norms in their community around ASRH rights and gender equality for adolescent girls and boys
- 1120.1: % of parents/caregivers (m/f) who hold positive attitudes towards ASRH rights and gender equality for adolescent girls and boys
- 1120.2: % of parents/caregivers (m/f) who perceive negative social norms in their community around ASRH rights and gender equality for adolescent girls and boys
- 1130.1: % of male religious and traditional leaders, community leaders, partners/husbands of adolescent girls (13-18 years) and adolescent fathers (15-18 years) who hold positive attitudes towards ASRH rights, gender equality and reducing SGBV for women and adolescent girls
- 1130.2: % of male religious and traditional leaders, community leaders, partners/husbands of adolescent girls (15-18 years) and adolescent fathers (15-18 years) who perceive negative social norms in their community around ASRH rights, gender equality and reducing SGBV for women and adolescent girls
- 1220.1: % of targeted health facilities that deliver ASRH and SGBV services including puberty and fertility, family planning, STDs, HIV/AIDS, abortion and post-abortion care, SGBV prevention and treatment
- 1220.2: # of visits reported by health facilities of adolescent girls (and boys) seeking sexual health services, including family planning (on a monthly basis)
- 1220.3: # of visits reported by health facilities of adolescent girls (and boys) seeking SGBV health services (on a monthly basis)
- 1330.1: # of government officials able to identify at least two gender-based barriers to ASRH services for adolescent girls

In addition to these indicators, and considering that this is a final evaluation, a series of questions have been incorporated to the questionnaires to measure OECD-DAC criteria (relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability). It is expected that the country reports and the consolidated report will incorporate a section analysing the results against the OECD-DAC criteria.

To complement the analysis and meet the learning purpose of the assignment, the selected consultant will review and incorporate the following available secondary sources into the reports:

- Baseline reports from Mali, Niger and Sierra Leone
- Annual reports and workplans
- Qualitative data from each country, in the form of interviews, focus group discussions, stories of change, etc.
- Other assessments and research pieces prepared by SCC, Country Offices and partners throughout the project, including from SickKids (quantitative research), ODI (qualitative research) and IRC (baseline and endline of project components under their responsibility)

6\. Deliverables

This assignment has five main deliverables, as follows:

- Inception Report (an updated workplan, timeline, roles and responsibilities, etc.)
- Endline Evaluation report of Mali (in French)
- Endline Evaluation report of Niger (in French)
- Endline Evaluation report of Sierra Leone (in English)
- Consolidated Evaluation Report (in English and French)

The structure of the individual endline reports will follow the structure of the baseline reports, with the addition of a section on OECD-DAC criteria:

1. Executive Summary
2. Introduction
3. Methodology
4. Results (OECD-DAC criteria and outcome indicators)
5. Lessons Learned
6. Recommendations

As reference, each baseline report was about 200 pages long, including 80 tables and 30 figures and graphs. A copy of one report is annexed to these TORs.

The Consolidated Evaluation Report should be succinct (e.g. 20-30 pages), and focus on key findings, lessons learned and recommendations synthesized from the combined individual reports and other relevant sources. The final structure will be discussed and agreed upon with the selected consultant during the Inception Phase.

7\. Timeline

It is expected that this assignment will run over a period of six months, e.g. March to August 2027. At the time of preparing these TORs, the process to recruit independent consultants in each country is underway and should be completed by November-December 2026. It is then expected that in-country data collection will be completed between January and February 2027.

The selected consultant will review secondary data in March and draft individual reports on a rolling basis between April and July, and a prepare a Consolidated Report by August. Below is a provisional timeline for this assignment.

**Periods**

**Key milestones**

November-December 2026 - Request for proposals launched

January-February 2027 - Consultant selected and hired

March 2027 - Inception phase: desk review and short inception note

April-June 2027 - Drafting of individual reports (rolling basis)

June-July 2027 - Finalisation of Individual reports and Drafting of Consolidated report

August 2027 - Finalization of Consolidated report

8\. Payment Schedule

Payment to the consultant shall be done in accordance with normal procedures of Save the Children Canada. The consultant is expected to pay all taxes for which they are responsible.

Payments terms are net 30 and are scheduled as follows:

- 40%: after submission of the 1st draft of all three individual endline reports
- 30%: upon finalization of all three individual endline reports
- 30%: upon finalization of consolidated report

9\. Role and Responsibilities of the Consultant

This consultancy is essentially desk-based and can be conducted remotely as it doesn't require primary data collection or any travel. The selected consultant will be responsible for the following:

- Review project documents, including but not limited to: Project Implementation Plan, Logic Model, Performance Measurement Framework, Baseline reports, Annual Reports, Work Plans, annual budgets and expenditures, data collection tools, endline data analysis plan, SickKids and ODI research products, etc.
- Review the quantitative data and qualitative transcripts for FGDs and KIIs received from the three countries.
- Analyze data against the baseline and targets, and draft separate endline evaluation reports for Mali, Niger and Sierra Leone using OECD-DAC criteria.
- Incorporate other sources of data into the analysis, including qualitative data and other research pieces from partners.
- Draft a consolidated report with high-level findings, lessons learned and recommendations for wider dissemination (policy, advocacy, etc.).

10\. Role and Responsibilities of Save the Children

SCC will share with the selected consultant all data sources needed to complete the assignment in a timely manner, including indicators values, baselines, reports, assessments and all quantitative and qualitative data available, specifically:

- Clean data sets in SPSS and Excel
- Validated indicator calculations
- Analysis tables for all surveys (Sierra Leone in English; Mali and Niger in French)
- Analysis Plan for calculation of project indicators (for reference)
- FGDs and KII transcripts (Sierra Leone in English; Mali and Niger in French)
- All available secondary data (research reports, baselines, annual reports, workplans, etc.)

SCC will coordinate with Country Offices to ensure that in-country consultancies move as planned. SCC will be responsible for the calculation and verification of outcome indicators. SCC will review the endline reports on a rolling basis and will limit the turnaround time as much as possible.

The selected consultant will report directly to the SCC MEAL Team who will be responsible for overseeing and coordinating the entire process. SCC will set up a schedule of weekly check-in calls with the consultant to address any issues or concerns regarding analyzing and drafting the endline evaluation reports.

11\. Consultants Qualifications

The expected minimum qualifications of the Consultant for this assignment are as follows:

- A postgraduate degree in Social Sciences (e.g. public health, sociology, human rights, education, etc.);
- Deep familiarity with project thematic areas (sexual and reproductive health, gender equality, child and adolescent rights), including in West Africa;
- Demonstrated experience in analysing qualitative and quantitative data, using appropriate software;
- Demonstrated experience writing robust baseline and/or endline reports, including using OECD-DAC criteria, for NGOs and/or institutional donors;
- Demonstrated experience synthesizing and translating large amounts of data into high-level, succinct, jargon-free reports for dissemination purposes (e.g. decision-making, policy, advocacy, fundraising...)
- Ability to work and produce high-quality reports in both English and French

Annexes:

- Logic Model
- Performance Measurement Framework
- Baseline report from Sierra Leone

12\. Application Process

Applications for the consultancy must include the following:

1. Detailed **technical proposal** (70% of the total score) including the following:

- Presentation of the Consultant (individual, team or firm)
- Demonstrate previous experience in carrying out similar assignments, particularly endline reports of SRH projects in West Africa
- Understanding of the assignment objectives, scope, and deliverables
- Proposed approach, methodology and workplan to execute the assignment
- Proposed team structure, roles and responsibilities, and level of effort of each team member
- Detailed CVs and biographies of the proposed team, outlining relevant experience
- Names and contact information of three references who can be contacted regarding relevant experience of the proposed lead consultant.
- A copy of a previous report of a similar nature undertaken on a) baseline study; or b) endline evaluation.

jobs.title: Subject Matter Expert - Future Readiness and Employability SME
jobs.description:
**Open Request for Proposal**

**Individual Consultant**

**Subject Matter Expert - Future readiness & employability**

**Girl Effect India**

**Issue Date: 17th November 2026**

## **Procurement Summary**

## **Item**

## **Details**

## Procurement method

## Open competitive tender

## Consultant type

## Individual consultant only

## Assignment

## Future Readiness and Employability Subject Matter Expert

## Location

## India; primarily remote

## Duration

## Approximately 4–6 weeks from contract signature

## Proposal deadline

## **26 November 2026**

## Proposal currency

## Indian Rupees (INR)

## Submission email

## **suppliers@girleffect.org**

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. We use youth-centred storytelling, behaviour-change science and digital engagement to help adolescent girls make informed choices about their health, education, relationships and futures.

In India, our initiatives include Chhaa Jaa and Teeka Talk. These programmes provide trusted information and support on health, relationships, empowerment and HPV vaccination through social media, digital content, chatbots and community engagement.

More information is available at[ www.girleffect.org](https://www.girleffect.org).

## **Background and Objective**

Adolescent girls and young women in India face interconnected barriers to education, skilling, livelihoods and economic participation. These barriers are shaped not only by limited information and access, but also by restrictive gender norms, limited decision-making power, mobility and safety concerns, unequal digital access, family expectations and a lack of exposure to viable pathways.

Girl Effect India is supporting the development of a large-scale programme for girls and young women aged 14–20 in select geographies of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. The programme seeks to build participants’ life skills, digital and financial literacy, confidence, agency and ability to navigate gender norms through a facilitator-led, phygital learning model.

The programme will engage the following three audience segments:

1. In-school girls aged 14–17 through classroom-based sessions and multimedia content.
2. Out-of-school girls aged 14–17 through community platforms, including Kishori groups and Anganwadi-linked systems.
3. Young women aged 18–20 through Self-Help Group and livelihood-linked networks, supported by multimedia and digital engagement.

Beyond foundational capability-building, the programme includes a dedicated Future-Ready Pathways component to help girls and young women move from awareness and aspiration to real education, skilling, livelihood, enterprise and employment opportunities.

The pathways will be differentiated according to age, schooling status, aspirations, readiness, mobility, family support and local context. They may include higher education, open schooling, vocational and technical training, scholarships, mentorship, entrepreneurship, livelihoods, certification and placement-linked opportunities.

## **What You will do**

The Subject Matter Expert will build on Girl Effect India’s existing landscape mapping to develop an actionable Future Readiness and Employability Strategy for girls aged 14–17 years and young women aged 18–20 years in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. The assignment will combine studying the existing landscape developed by Girl Effect and strategic pathway development to identify opportunities to strengthen girls’ preparedness for education, skilling, livelihoods, and economic participation.

The assignment will be organised around three core outputs:

1. Practical future-readiness pathways: Identify realistic education, skilling, employment and entrepreneurship opportunities that girls and young women can access in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, differentiated for in-school girls aged 14–17, out-of-school girls aged 14–17, and young women aged 18–20.
2. Technical content and how-to guides: Define what each cohort should learn and develop ready-to-adapt, how-to-guides that help girls navigate these opportunities, using verified MP- and Maharashtra-specific examples.
3. Actionable ecosystem linkages: Identify which institutions, schemes and programmes the programme could connect girls to, and set out how those linkages would work in practice, including eligibility, referral steps, roles, safeguarding and follow-up.

### 1. Develop practical, cohort-specific future-readiness pathways

- Identify realistic education, skilling, employment and entrepreneurship opportunities that girls and young women can access in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, differentiated for the programme's three cohorts: (i) in-school girls aged 14–17, (ii) out-of-school girls aged 14–17 and (iii) young women aged 18–20.
- For girls aged 14–17, focus on career awareness, aspiration-building, education continuation or re-entry, exposure to vocational opportunities and preparation for future transitions. For young women aged 18–20, identify more actionable pathways towards skilling, certification, employment, self-employment and entrepreneurship.
- Identify the key steps, capabilities, enabling conditions and support mechanisms required to help girls navigate these pathways, taking into account their aspirations, mobility, family support, socio-economic circumstances and local opportunities.
- Develop a practical, age-differentiated pathways framework that illustrates how girls can progress from awareness and aspiration-building to accessing relevant opportunities, including critical transition points and potential barriers.
- Ensure that the proposed pathways reflect the specific contexts of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including differences across rural, urban and tribal settings, and are feasible within the programme's existing implementation model.

### 3. Identify actionable ecosystem linkages and opportunities for convergence

- Building on Girl Effect's existing landscape mapping of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, identify and prioritise credible education, skilling, livelihood, employment and entrepreneurship institutions, schemes and programmes in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra that could provide relevant opportunities for the programme's target cohorts.
- Undertake targeted validation of shortlisted opportunities, considering eligibility, accessibility, affordability, geographical coverage, credibility, safeguarding, gender responsiveness and suitability for the intended age groups.
- Identify practical opportunities for linkages with government departments and schemes, vocational and technical training institutions, Self-Help Group networks, livelihood missions, entrepreneurship support organisations, employers and other relevant ecosystem actors.
- Recommend how implementation partners could facilitate access to these opportunities through information-sharing, career exposure, referrals, institutional coordination or other feasible mechanisms.
- Develop a prioritised opportunity and partnership matrix outlining relevant institutions and programmes, target cohorts, geographical availability, eligibility requirements, potential collaboration models, referral processes and recommended next steps.
- Provide practical recommendations for operationalising these linkages within the programme's existing delivery model, including the roles of facilitators, implementation partners and relevant institutions, safeguarding considerations and mechanisms for follow-up.

The consultant will work closely with Girl Effect India's programme, curriculum, content, and safeguarding teams to ensure that all proposed pathways, learning resources and institutional linkages are technically sound, contextually relevant, age-appropriate and feasible within the programme's implementation model.

## **Deliverables**

The Subject Matter Expert will deliver the following outputs over the proposed 4–6-week assignment. The work will build on Girl Effect India’s completed landscape mapping, with targeted consultations and a focus on actionable programme strategy rather than duplicating existing research.

Deliverable

Description

Indicative timeline

1\. Inception Note and Workplan

An inception note setting out the consultant’s understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, analytical framework, information requirements, targeted stakeholder consultation plan, work plan, and timelines.

This deliverable will also be complemented by a document detailing an in-depth understanding of the landscape and formative reports developed by Girl Effect. This will aid the consultant towards developing a focused assessment of accessible, safe, gender-responsive, and realistic opportunities in light of girls’ aspirations, capabilities, mobility, household norms and socio-economic circumstances, and highlight gaps, barriers and opportunities for convergence across existing schemes and programmes.

Week 1

2\. Age- Differentiated Future Readiness and Employability Strategy/ framework

An actionable strategy outlining differentiated pathways for (i) girls aged 14–17 years who are in-school, (ii) girls aged 14–17 years who are out-of-school and (iii) young women aged 18–20 years.

For the 14-17 years age group, the focus should include aspiration-building, education continuation or re-entry, scholarship access, career exposure, mentoring, and awareness of vocational pathways. For young women aged 18–20, the focus should include workforce readiness, certification, skilling, financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, market linkages, livelihoods and employment opportunities. The strategy should identify critical transition points, enabling conditions, relevant support systems and convergence opportunities.

The strategy should also be translated into a clear, visually engaging and easy-to-navigate framework that illustrates the differentiated pathways, key transition points, enabling factors and support systems for each age cohort. This may be developed using collaborative visualisation tools such as Miro, Mural, FigJam, Lucidchart, Canva, Google Slides, or another suitable platform. The visual framework should clearly demonstrate how different pathways and opportunities connect, stakeholder engagement, and future implementation. The final visualisation should be shared in an editable format.

The consultant will present the proposed framework to the Girl Effect India team for review and validation, incorporating feedback and recommendations into the next iteration.

Weeks 2-3

3\. Partner and Opportunity Vetting Framework

A practical, standardised framework and checklist for assessing prospective partner organisations, institutions, employers, programmes, mentors and digital platforms. Criteria should include relevance to target cohorts, accessibility, safeguarding, gender responsiveness, quality, feasibility and potential for sustained engagement. The consultant will have to work with Girl Effect’s Safeguarding team to develop this framework.

Week 4

4\. Prioritised Ecosystem Partner Database

A curated database of approximately 15–25 high-potential partners and opportunities across the two states, drawing on existing mapping, desk research, and targeted consultations. Entries may include public programmes, educational institutions, skilling and certification providers, employers, industry-linked initiatives, SHG and community networks, mentorship providers, and digital platforms. For each entry, indicate geographic presence, target cohorts, relevance to proposed pathways, potential collaboration and recommended next steps. Inclusion does not imply a confirmed partnership or commitment to collaborate.

Week 4

5\. Strategic Recommendations and Technical Inputs for Programme Design

A consolidated set of prioritised, actionable recommendations covering institutional convergence, partnership opportunities, implementation considerations, and indicative next steps.

Include technical recommendations for integrating future readiness, career awareness, and employability concepts into programme curriculum and content, identifying suggested learning objectives, thematic areas and age-appropriate approaches.

Week 5

6\. Final Presentation and Validation

A presentation of key findings, proposed pathways, priority programme opportunities, potential partners and strategic recommendations to Girl Effect India. Incorporate consolidated feedback into the final outputs.

Week 6

The deliverables will be developed iteratively, with the landscape synthesis and sector opportunity analysis informing the strategy, partner assessment, and programme recommendations. Deliverables 2 and 3 constitute the core analytical and strategic outputs; Deliverables 4–6 translate the findings into practical programme design and opportunities.

All deliverables should be submitted in English in editable formats. The final work plan and deadlines will be agreed during inception, and the consultant will incorporate consolidated feedback from Girl Effect India into the final outputs.

A deliverable will be accepted only when it is:

- Complete.
- Accurate.
- Supported by verifiable and dated sources.
- Responsive to the approved brief.
- Submitted in the agreed editable format.
- Free from unresolved material errors.
- Approved in writing by Girl Effect.

Corrections required to meet the agreed requirements will be completed within the fixed professional fee and will not constitute additional scope.

## **Management and Working Arrangements**

- The consultant will report to Girl Effect India’s Programme and Content team.
- The consultant will work closely with curriculum, safeguarding, and other nominated Girl Effect colleagues.
- The assignment will primarily be delivered remotely.
- The consultant must be available for regular virtual coordination, review and validation meetings.
- Girl Effect will provide existing research and programme materials and facilitate agreed internal introductions.
- Girl Effect will provide consolidated feedback through its nominated project lead.
- The consultant must maintain:
- A work plan and timesheet, as required.
- Consultation record.
- Risk and dependency log.
- Feedback and revision log.
- Any travel must be requested and approved in writing before bookings are made or costs are incurred.
- No representation may be made to external stakeholders on behalf of Girl Effect without prior written approval.

## **Who You Are**

You are an experienced future-readiness, education, skilling, livelihoods or workforce-development specialist with a strong understanding of the barriers affecting adolescent girls and young women in India. You will have:

- Demonstrated experience (minimum 6 years) mapping education, scholarship, skilling, livelihood, enterprise or employment opportunities.
- Strong knowledge of government, community and private-sector opportunity ecosystems in India.
- Experience designing employability, career-readiness, transition or economic-empowerment strategies.
- The ability to assess labour-market trends and identify realistic growth sectors and pathways.
- Experience reviewing or vetting education institutions, skilling providers, employers, mentors or referral partners.
- A strong understanding of gender, safeguarding, workplace safety and the risks faced by adolescent girls and young women.
- The ability to translate technical evidence and ecosystem findings into practical programme recommendations and accessible curriculum inputs.
- Strong research, analysis, writing, facilitation and stakeholder-engagement skills.
- Strong data visualisation skills.
- A commitment to ensuring that opportunities are safe, inclusive, accessible and relevant to girls’ realities.
- Passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of young women and girls.
- Understanding of gender-responsive and gender-transformative programming, safeguarding and safe-work principles.
- Strong analytical, research, writing and stakeholder-management skills.
- Ability to provide clear and practical inputs into youth-facing curriculum and programme content.
- Familiarity with Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra is preferred.
- Ability and willingness to travel within India, if and when required.
- Commitment to Girl Effect’s mission, values and safeguarding standards.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 17th November 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: **26th November 2026**

## **Proposal Submission**

Your proposal, should you be interested, should cover (Max 7 pages):

Technical Proposal

- Credentials/CV
- Please showcase any previous relevant work experience with links to previous works.

Financial Proposal

## **Evaluation Criteria**

The criteria against which the application will be evaluated are listed below.

- Experience and qualification as outlined in your CV/credentials/profile – 20%

Girl Effect may request clarifications, creative presentations, interviews, reference checks, due diligence or best-and-final offers.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Individual engagement:** The contract will be awarded to an individual consultant. Substitution or subcontracting requires Girl Effect’s prior written approval.

jobs.title: National Anticipatory Action Manager
jobs.description:
DRC Uganda is currently looking for a highly qualified and motivated individual to join our dynamic team as National Anticipatory Action Manager.

**The overall purpose of the role:**

The National Anticipatory Action Manager will lead the national portion of the global Anticipatory Humanitarian Action for Displacement (AHEAD) project implemented across seven countries globally, funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The project will develop anticipatory action (AA) data models and approaches using local and global data for local-level analysis to help inform humanitarian actors’ decisions when deploying humanitarian assistance and to enable timelier, more dignified, efficient and sustainable assistance. He/she will also be responsible for technical coordination and representation in coordination forums in Uganda and support the Country Office with technical backstopping when necessary.

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**Management and Coordination:**

- Ensure timely and quality deliverables and spending of the AHEAD project.
- Ensure effecitve, respectful coordination with communities and partners that are part of the project’s implementation.
- Ensure effective Project Cycle Management (PCM).
- Support DRC Uganda’s Anticipatory Action (AA) sector, ensuring alignment with DRC’s global strategy and the country’s specific needs;
- Coordinate with regional and global teams to ensure effective integration of anticipatory action activities into overall program strategies;
- Facilitate awareness-raising and collaboration across sectors and with key stakeholders, including government agencies, local partners, and UN agencies
- Provide effective leadership to the AHEAD team in Uganda and to the project partners.
- Lead the AHEAD Uganda advocacy strategy so that displacement forecasting is built into national and district early warning, preparedness and disaster risk financing systems.
- Engage the Office of the Prime Minister (Department of Relief, Disaster Preparedness and Management), Conflict Early Warning and Early Response Unit (CEWERU), National Emergency Coordination and Operations Centre (NECOC), Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA) and district disaster management committees to show how displacement forecasts can inform triggers, contingency plans and early action decisions.
- Promote the use of displacement forecasts and conflict and protection risk indicators alongside climate hazard data in national anticipatory action frameworks, protocols and technical working groups.
- Represent DRC in national platforms and within the AA Technical Working Group (TWG), and push for displacement- and conflict-sensitive AA and for more locally led approaches
- Manage the project budget: track spending against plans, forecast burn rates, and flag and resolve over- or under-spending in good time
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, DRC procedures and audit requirements across DRC and partner implementation.
- Lead donor reporting and maintain good relationships with the donor, including preparing amendments or no-cost extensions where needed.
- Line-manage, and assess the performance of AHEAD team members, and identify and support their learning and development needs.

**Partnership management**

- Manage day-to-day relationships with implementing partners, including regular check-ins, joint work planning and clear communication on roles, timelines and expectations.
- Carry out partner capacity assessments and develop and follow up on capacity-strengthening plans. These should cover AA concepts, trigger monitoring, early action implementation, financial management, compliance, safeguarding and MEAL.
- Deliver or coordinate training, mentoring and on-the-job coaching for partner staff and local structures (e.g. district committees, community monitors).
- Monitor partner performance on activities, spending and reporting through field visits, review meetings and spot checks, and follow up on corrective actions.
- Review partner narrative and financial reports for quality, accuracy and compliance with DRC and donor requirements.
- Support partners in psreparing and running activations, including readiness checks, pre-positioning, beneficiary targeting and post-activation reviews.
- Manage partnership agreements in line with DRC partnership policy, from due diligence and agreement development to amendments and close-out.
- Promote equitable partnerships and localisation, including partner participation in decisions, visibility, and access to learning and advocacy spaces.

**Implementation and Technical Support of AHEAD:**

- Lead the development and implementation of anticipatory action plans, including leading the co-design of readiness and anticipatory actions, trigger mechanisms, and evidence generation frameworks, following a participatory, bottom-up design process;
- Oversee trigger monitoring and early warning analysis, and coordinate activation decisions and the timely release of pre-arranged funds.
- Lead the anticipatory action systems building, including strengthening of early warning systems, trigger development, and development of anticipatory action plans in close collaboration with duty bearers and in-country partners, ensuring they meet DRC’s standards and principles;
- Identify funding opportunities and contribute to concept notes and proposals to scale up or continue AA work in Uganda and the region.

**Data, Analysis, and Learning:**

- Model use, refinement and dissemination: Work with Headquarter's (HQ’s) Evidence, Knowledge, and Learning (EKL) team to ensure that data and displacement forecasting models are effectively used for anticipatory action; support DRC’s global and regional analysts (via coordination of AHEAD’s community protection monitoring) to monitor and analyze data related to disaster risks and displacement, ensuring that forecasts and triggers are aligned with the evolving needs on the ground;
- MEAL: Support the MEAL Assistant as appropriate in capturing and disseminate lessons learned from anticipatory action projects, contributing to global, regional and national knowledge-sharing and advocacy efforts.
- Oversee the MEAL framework, including baselines, monitoring of early actions, post-activation reviews and evaluation of anticipatory action effectiveness (timeliness, avoided losses).
- Document and share lessons learned and good practice with country, regional and global teams and external stakeholders.

**Reporting and Communication:**

• Ensure timely and high-quality reporting on project activities, in line with donor and organizational requirements; maintain strong communication with country focal points to track progress, share updates, and resolve challenges in implementation; provide regular technical support and guidance to local staff and stakeholders, ensuring clear understanding and commitment to AA objectives.

About you

- To be successful in this role, you must have at least 5 years of international experience in disaster risk management or anticipatory action programming, preferably in conflict-affected regions. Moreover, we also expect the following.

*Required*

- Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Social Sciences, Peacebuilding, or similar relevant field, or significant additional demonstrable past professional experience gained through fieldwork
- Proven track record of efective and timely project management.
- Strong knowledge of PCM.
- Proven track record of designing and implementing anticipatory action projects, including development of triggers and anticipatory action planning.
- Strong understanding of data-driven decision-making, with experience with displacement forecasting models and early warning systems being a strong asset.
- Excellent stakeholder coordination skills, with an ability to navigate diverse stakeholder groups and drive joint progress to achieve common goals.
- Excellent partner management and communication skills.
- Familiarity with conflict-sensitive programming and the impacts of displacement on vulnerable populations.
- Ability and willingness to travel, including to remote or conflict-affected areas, up to 35% of the time.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and coordination skills, with the ability to work across multiple teams and with diverse stakeholders.

*Desirable*

- Experience with programming related to climate resilience, preparedness, and conflict sensitivity.
- Demonstrated ability to innovate and take a flexible, problem-solving approach in complex humanitarian environments.
- Strong project management skills and experience with donor reporting and proposal writing.
- Familiarity with humanitarian coordination mechanisms and key international standards

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence**: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating**: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead**: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity**: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

We offer

- Contract length: 12 months
- Band: M F2
- Designation of Duty Station: Arua
- Start date: January 2027

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies).

**What we are looking for**

Are you an experienced humanitarian professional with a strong track record in donor engagement and grants management, particularly in recovery, humanitarian, or conflict-affected settings? We're looking for someone who understands the Jordanian context, has solid knowledge of National NGO operations and humanitarian sector dynamics, and ideally brings experience working with local and national civil society organizations (CSOs).

Experience in MEAL (Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning) approaches and systems strengthening is highly desirable, as these areas are central to the role.

We're especially interested in candidates with a strategic mindset and proven expertise in strengthening institutional systems on grants management, fundraising and MEAL.

If you're passionate about strengthening organizational capacity, developing people and teams, and driving meaningful impact, this could be an excellent opportunity to take your career to the next level.

**Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Amman Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.**

**What you will do**

The Programme Support Manager will be full-time seconded to NRC’s strategic partner, the Justice Centre for Legal Aid (JCLA) contributing e to achieve programme quality and accountability by strengthening overall system and managements of JCLA’s grants and MEAL functions and leading the review and improvement of internal processes and procedures.

The Programme Support Manager is responsible for leading the fundraising strategy by providing insight on funding trends, supporting donor engagement, ensuring donor compliance, leading on the development of high quality and timely proposals and reports and other external products, as well as ensuring robust MEAL systems and processes are in place to promote evidence-based decision making, project performance, and internal management.

Key responsibilities:

- **Grant Management and Compliance**: Ensure compliance with NRC and JCLA policies, donor regulations, grant agreements, and reporting requirements while strengthening internal grant management systems and processes.
- **Fundraising and Business Development**: Support the development and implementation of fundraising strategies, donor engagement, preparation and submission of high-quality concept notes, proposals, budgets, and funding applications, in close collaboration with JCLA’s Executive Director.
- **Programme Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)**: Provide technical oversight and continuous improvement of MEAL systems, complaint feedback mechanisms (CFM), data analysis, and learning processes to support strategic and programme decision-making.
- **Project Cycle Management and Capacity Building**: Lead and strengthen Project Cycle Management (PCM) processes across all stages, including staff training, technical guidance, proposal development, reporting, and integration of cross-cutting programme elements.
- **Management, Coordination and Representation**: Manage and support staff performance and development, coordinate with NRC and external stakeholders, and represent JCLA with partners and donors as delegated by leadership.

**What you will bring**

- Five years of demonstrated relevant and related experience in a similar working experience in a humanitarian/recovery context with Knowledge of the Jordan context, NGO operations and the dynamics of the humanitarian sector, preferably with a working experience with local and national CSOs.
- Experience working in complex environments and with Displacement affected people.
- Experience of donor relations and grants management. Proven skills and experience in report and proposal development and working with multiple donors and working with budgets.
- Experience in design, implementation, and oversight of monitoring and evaluation with advanced experience in qualitative and quantitative data analysis and tools.
- Good personal organizational skills, interpersonal skills, team management, including time management, and ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure.
- Demonstrated experience of contributing to positive organizational change.
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English and Arabic.
- Above average computer skills, particularly in Microsoft Windows Word and Excel.

Please download[ the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQALzwQyzc2USbBDiVJU-hvrATBWVwrB3o_NuII2shAVHBU?e=Wmbkwq) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman, Jordan
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance and availability of funding
- Travel: Up to 5%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Amman Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

**Why JCLA?**

The Justice Centre for Legal Aid (JCLA) is a Jordanian not-for-profit legal aid organisation promoting legal empowerment. JCLA was founded in 2008 on the belief that legal protection should be a basic right accessible by all, regardless of their economic vulnerability. Our intervention relies on three main pillars: Prevention through legal awareness, Response through legal services and Advocacy for institutional change.

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Jordan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/jordan)

[Learn more about the JCLA](https://jcla-org.com/en/homepage/)

jobs.title: HRO - Human Resources Officer Operation Cell 4 (M/F)
jobs.description:
## **Position Context:**

The HRO position is fully integrated into the operational Cell, a multidisciplinary team of around ten people supporting field missions and operations. The cell currently coordinates three countries (Afghanistan, Haiti, Nigeria), representing nearly 2,500 national colleagues and approximately 120 international staff. The portfolio may evolve over time.

Within this cell, the HR Manager works in body partnership with another HR officer. This organization aims to foster professional exchange, knowledge sharing, and joint reflection on key HR issues. The two managers share leadership of the countries within the portfolio as well as certain cross-functional files, while maintaining a sufficiently in-depth understanding of all contexts to ensure continuity of activities during absences, leave, or field visits by their counterpart.

The position holder acts as an HR partner for operations by providing advice, support, and expertise to field and coordination teams. He/she also contributes to the continuous improvement of HR practices within the cell and actively participates in cross-functional discussions conducted with other departments.

The position requires an excellent knowledge of colleagues at headquarters as well as of the OCP international staff pool. This detailed understanding of profiles, competencies, and career paths is essential to support missions in identifying and mobilizing resources adapted to their needs.

**Current Challenges of the Position:**

We are looking for someone with a strong interest in social dialogue issues and the ways in which it can be organized within MSF intervention contexts.

The position also involves a strong commitment to duty of care, staff solidarity, and the implementation and monitoring of support mechanisms and associated good practices.

Promoting a safe and respectful work environment is also a key responsibility. The HR Manager contributes to the dissemination of safeguarding principles, awareness raising among project and coordination teams, the establishment of appropriate reporting mechanisms, and the diligent handling of alerts, in close collaboration with the relevant specialist teams.

Particular attention is paid to supporting international staff throughout their professional pathway, notably through the organization and quality of mission departure and return debriefings.

Finally, the position offers the opportunity to contribute to high-impact cross-functional HR files linked to the cell's and organization's strategic priorities. This dimension represents an important lever for professional development and provides the opportunity to actively contribute to the evolution of MSF's HR policies and practices.

## **Responsibilities:**

Under the responsibility of the Cell Manager and with a functional reporting line to the Head of the Operational HR, the Operational HR officer is the strategic HR partner of the cell. He/she ensures, within the countries under his/her responsibility, the quality and consistency of the HR response, its adaptation to operational realities, and its contribution to mission impact. He/she supports operations in understanding human issues, identifying HR needs, and defining appropriate responses. He/she contributes to operational management through contextual analysis, advice to operational stakeholders, and leadership of the HR function within his/her scope. He/she ensures the mobilization of relevant expertise, the clarification of programme needs, and the consistency of the responses provided.

Your main activities, as a member of the Cell HR team, are as follows:

**1. Lead the HR contribution to operations management** o Participate in defining objectives and developing operational strategies for the cell’s programmes. o Bring an HR perspective to decisions, anticipate human and capacity risks, and alert the cell to these risks. o Inform decision-making and contribute to the cell’s cross-functional projects by providing an HR perspective, facilitating implementation, and contributing to prioritization. o Contribute to the cell’s strategic reflections by providing analysis of human issues, organizational capacities, and their operational consequences.

**2. Lead the HR strategy within the assigned scope** o Assess HR dynamics in the countries under his/her responsibility and contribute to the cell’s strategic reflections. o Coordinate with counterparts from other Operational Centres (OCs) on the implementation of intersectional HR policies within the scope. o Contribute to anticipating HR needs and forecasting the resources required within the scope.

**3. Identify needs and direct them to the appropriate stakeholder** o Help programmes define the actual HR need, which is not always the one initially expressed, and direct it towards the appropriate expertise or lever. o Ensure the mobilization of appropriate expertise and the proper coordination of interventions with programme needs. o Support functional managers and coordination teams in decision-making and in the implementation of HR policies, procedures, and tools.

**4. Ensure the application and adaptation of HR frameworks** o Ensure the dissemination and compliance with HR policies and procedures within the scope, relying on headquarters expertise and technical coordination. o Be responsible for their implementation and adaptation at country level, while respecting common principles. o Advise the Cell Manager on exceptions when operational constraints require them, seek arbitration when necessary, and ensure the follow-up and capitalization of approved exceptions.

**5. Support and lead the team and coordinations** o Define the cell’s HR priorities, manage the HR team, foster skills development, and strengthen team cohesion. o Ensure a coherent distribution of responsibilities, activities, and workload within the HR team. o Support HR coordinations in the countries under responsibility, while respecting the leadership they exercise within their own scope, by providing headquarters perspective and comparative insight across multiple contexts. o Promote a shared analysis of HR challenges and support the critical reflection necessary for complex decisions.

**6. Contribute to HR developments and transformations** o Contribute to HR transformation initiatives affecting the scope and promote ownership by the teams concerned. o Escalate the development needs arising from the evolution of the countries under responsibility and contribute to designing appropriate responses.

**7. Monitor, analyse and report** o Ensure the collection of management information and HR reporting within the scope. o Analyse HR issues specific to the countries under responsibility and communicate them to the Head of the Operational HR Scope. o Contribute to identifying, planning, and monitoring the resources necessary for implementing HR priorities within the scope, including their budgetary implications.

**8. Cross-functional responsibilities and contribution to the HR community:** o Contribute to the HR professional community, participate in sharing practices and lessons learned, and facilitate the circulation of relevant information between the scope, other cells, and headquarters. o Maintain working relationships with counterparts, other MSF sections, and stakeholders operating in the same contexts in order to promote alignment and the sharing of HR best practices. o Contribute, within the scope, to staff mobility, diversity, and gender balance, as well as to the recognition of career paths and expertise.

**Additional Activities:** o Contribute to the design and facilitation of HR training sessions. o Undertake short mission assignments to cover vacancies in coordination positions, according to operational needs.

## **Profile:**

**Experience:** Good knowledge of MSF, its organization, tools, and operational contexts. · At least 2 years of field experience (with MSF or another humanitarian NGO) in an HR coordination role. · Team management experience is mandatory. · Experience at OCP headquarters is an asset. · Training experience is an asset.

**Required Skills**: Knowledge of Human Resources Management techniques and tools (LIGO/Oracle/HRIS/HR Need, etc.). · Coaching and team support. · Interest in digital tools and applications (Office/Internet/SharePoint/etc.).

**Languages:** · English and French, minimum B2 level.

**Personal Attributes:** · Ability to cooperate, adapt, and work as part of a team. · Proactive, creative, and solution-oriented. · Strong dialogue and interpersonal skills. · Strong analytical and synthesis skills. · Organized, flexible, and autonomous. · Responsive, able to anticipate and manage priorities. · Willingness to travel to the field when required.

jobs.title: Public Health Medical Referent - Infectious Diseases (ID)
jobs.description:
**MSF is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. We are a non-profit, self-governed worldwide movement of more than 63,000 people.**

**We provide emergency medical assistance during armed conflict, natural disasters, outbreaks of deadly diseases and assist those who are excluded from healthcare. MSF delivers care based on need and when we see injustice, we speak out. We are an organization that remains impartial, knowledgeable, and effective, and this is what makes the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect.**

At the moment MSF-OCA is looking for a:

**Infectious Diseases (ID) Public Health Medical Referent - OCA Public Health Department**

The OCA Public Health Department is seeking an experienced Infectious Diseases professional to support clinicians working in Ebola Treatment Centres (ETCs) and other Viral Haemorrhagic Fever (VHF) contexts. The position focuses on strengthening the quality of patient care through technical support, coaching, mentoring, and field accompaniment of clinical teams.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Provide technical support, coaching, and mentoring to clinicians working in Ebola and other VHF contexts.
- Brief staff prior to deployment and provide ongoing remote and field-based support.
- Conduct regular field visits to strengthen clinical practice and quality of care.
- Support quality improvement initiatives through activities such as mortality reviews and rational prescription analysis.
- Strengthen systems and structures to improve quality of care in this and future VHF responses.
- Ensure clinical teams are guided by the latest best practice and evidence-based recommendations.
- Collaborate with relevant referents, including the current Infectious Diseases Advisors, to strengthen palliative care approaches.
- Act as a VHF technical resource for the Staff Health Unit regarding IMS and LHS Ebola-related health concerns.
- Analyze patient outcomes and programme data from OCA-run and OCA-supported treatment centres to identify opportunities for improving clinical care and patient pathways.
- Contribute to training and capacity-building initiatives for MSF and Ministry of Health staff.

**We are looking for a candidate who has:**

- Previous experience working in an Ebola response or other VHF context.
- Strong NGO field experience, preferably with MSF.
- Demonstrated experience of coaching and mentoring clinical teams.
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate clinical findings into improved patient care.
- Excellent collaboration and communication skills.
- A minimum French language level of C1.

**Deployment and Contract Conditions**

The position requires approximately 50-60% field deployment, with the remaining time dedicated to technical support, analysis, coordination, and mentoring activities.

Amsterdam or London are the preferred duty stations. Nairobi and Berlin may also consider suitable candidates. Flexibility regarding headquarters presence may be required depending on operational, travel, visa or quarantine constraints.

Please note: Accommodation is provided during field deployments only. Candidates are responsible for arranging and funding their own accommodation at their duty station when not deployed.

The anticipated start date is as soon as possible. The initial contract duration is 6 months, with the possibility of a 6-month extension.

**Information and Application**

If you recognise yourself in this profile and meet the requirements, we encourage you to apply directly via the Apply button on this page and upload the following documents:

- Your most recent CV
- A cover letter explaining your motivation to work with MSF

Deadline for applications: December 1st, 23:59 CET.

jobs.title: Terms of References (ToR) for a Consultancy to Conduct a Feasibility Study for the proposed project: A Voice for Inclusion.
jobs.description:
**Terms of References (ToR) for a Consultancy to Conduct a Feasibility Study for the proposed project: A Voice for Inclusion – Equal Education and a Strong Civil Society for Children with Disabilities in Ethiopia, The Gambia and Zambia.**

Assignment period: December 2026 – January 2027

- Location:Ethiopia, The Gambia and Zambia
- Commissioned by:ChildFund
- Main Partners: ChildFund Deutschland, ChildFund Ethiopia, ChildFund The Gambia, ChildFund Zambia, Tesfa Birhan, Saama Kairo Federation, Chibombo/Mumbwa Child Development Agency, Kafue Child Development Agency
- Donor: Project to be submitted to BMZ

## **Background and Context**

### Context of the assignment

Despite the ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) by Ethiopia (in 2010), The Gambia (in 2015) and Zambia (in 2010), many children with disabilities continue to face significant barriers to accessing and successfully completing primary education. Children with severe or multiple disabilities, intellectual or learning disabilities, sensory impairments, and disabilities that remain unidentified are often among the most excluded. Exclusion is further compounded by factors such as gender, age, poverty and geographical remoteness. In addition, the absence of systematic processes for identifying children with disabilities frequently limits their access to appropriate support services, accommodations and referral mechanisms.

Preliminary problem analyses conducted in all three countries suggest a number of common barriers and root causes. At family and community level, these include poverty and disability-related costs, transport and distance barriers, limited awareness of available support services, stigma and discrimination, weak parent support structures, safety concerns, and low expectations regarding the educational potential of children with disabilities. At school level, challenges include inadequate teacher preparation for inclusive education, insufficient follow-up coaching and mentoring, limited availability of assistive devices and adapted learning materials, inaccessible infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, and constrained institutional and financial resources. Across all three countries, gaps are also evident between national policy commitments and their implementation at district, community and school levels. Common issues include weak coordination between sectors and administrative levels, insufficient funding, limited use of disability-disaggregated data, weak referral systems, and limited opportunities for meaningful participation of children with disabilities and their caregivers in planning and decision-making processes.

In Zambia, UNCRPD commitments are domesticated through the Persons with Disabilities Act No. 6 of 2012, which provides for the right to inclusive education and established the Zambia Agency for Persons with Disabilities (ZAPD), alongside the Education Act of 2011 and the Children’s Code Act of 2022. The free education policy introduced in 2022 removed school fees, yet children with disabilities in rural and peri-urban districts such as Kafue, Mumbwa and Chibombo continue to face barriers that fee removal alone does not address, including distance to school, limited district-level assessment and specialised services, few teachers trained in inclusive or special education, and stigma.

In The Gambia, commitments under the UNCRPD are supported by the Disability Act (2021), the Children’s Act, and the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education’s Inclusive Education Policy Framework. Despite these policy commitments, children with disabilities continue to face significant barriers to accessing quality education, including late identification of disabilities, limited availability of specialised assessment and support services, inadequate assistive and learning resources, social stigma, and insufficient capacity within mainstream schools to respond to diverse learning needs. These challenges are often more pronounced in rural and underserved communities.

In Ethiopia, commitments to inclusive education are operationalised through the Constitution (Article 41), the education policy framework, and the current Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy (2022/23-2029/30), which aims to ensure equitable access to quality education for children, youth and adults with special educational needs and disabilities. Despite this strong policy commitment, significant barriers continue to hinder implementation at federal, regional, woreda and school levels, including weak disability data systems, limited early identification and referral mechanisms, shortages of trained inclusive education professionals, inadequate assistive devices and adapted learning materials, inaccessible infrastructure, and persistent stigma. These challenges are often compounded by poverty, displacement, geographical isolation and gender-related disadvantages, particularly in rural, pastoralist, conflict-affected and underserved communities.

While the analyses point to significant similarities in the patterns of exclusion across Ethiopia, The Gambia and Zambia, they are also highlighting important contextual differences. This creates opportunities for structured cross-country learning, knowledge exchange and the adaptation of effective approaches across different contexts. The planned project aims to address these challenges with an integrated micro-meso-macro approach: communities and families are sensitized and empowered; schools are developed into inclusive learning environments, mainly through training and development plans; and civil society organisations are strengthened to carry out advocacy work for inclusive education. The multi-country nature of the program offers an opportunity to generate evidence, promote cross-learning and identify scalable approaches that can strengthen inclusive education systems beyond the targeted locations.

Inclusive education is both a rights-based obligation and a strategic investment in human capital, social inclusion and sustainable development. Ensuring that children with disabilities can access and succeed in education contributes to national development priorities, advances SDG 4 commitments, and supports broader efforts to ensure that no child is left behind.

### Brief about ChildFund International as the organization commissioning the study

ChildFund International is a global child- and youth-focused development and humanitarian organization dedicated to advancing the well-being, resilience, and rights of children and young people, particularly those facing vulnerability and exclusion. Working through local partners, communities, governments, and civil society, ChildFund promotes locally led and owned development approaches that strengthen systems, build community capacity, and create sustainable impact for children and their families. Its programmes focus on education, child protection, health, livelihoods, and youth empowerment, with an emphasis on achieving lasting outcomes that enable children and young people to learn, thrive, and contribute meaningfully to their communities.

This assignment is commissioned by ChildFund International to inform the design and implementation of a multi-country inclusive education programme in Ethiopia, The Gambia, and Zambia. The International Office (IO) will provide overall strategic direction, technical leadership, and quality assurance; the Africa Regional Office (RO) will provide regional coordination, technical oversight, and facilitate cross-country learning; while the respective Country Offices (COs) will lead country-level coordination, stakeholder engagement, and contextual guidance to ensure the study reflects national priorities and local realities.

### **Brief about the proposed project**

The proposed multi-country programme seeks to improve equitable access to, participation in, and quality of inclusive primary education for children with disabilities in Ethiopia, The Gambia, and Zambia. The programme is founded on the recognition that educational exclusion results from interconnected barriers at household, community, school, and systems levels, requiring a coordinated and multi-level response.
