jobs.title: Protection from Violence Specialist Palestine
jobs.description:
**Background**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been present in Palestine since 2009. NRC implements programming directly and in collaboration with partners in five Core Competencies: Shelter & Site Management, Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH), Information Counselling and legal Assistance (ICLA), Protection from Violence (PfV) and Education. NRC Palestine implements programming both directly as well as through a wide network of partners. Last year, NRC served nearly 600,000 unique program participants. NRC’s programming in Palestine has a strong humanitarian, protection and resilience focus that looks to meet vital needs through sustainable solutions to increase early recovery outcomes through integrated programme responses. In this complex, challenging operating environment in Palestine, NRC is working to strengthen the quality, responsiveness, integration, and sustainability of our programmes. Protection from Violence is the newest program introduced into NRC Palestine’s program portfolio.

**What we are looking for**

A qualified, motivated **Protection from Violence Specialist** who will be tasked with leading the strategic direction of the program, quality, fundraising and advocacy for the PfV program within NRC Palestine. In addition, the PfV Specialist will be responsible for mentoring, training, and capacity building of PfV teams in the West Bank and Gaza Area Offices, who deliver services on the ground.

If you are a passionate, seasoned leader with extensive experience in Protection, capacity building, strategy development and programme quality, we would like to hear from you!

**What you will do**

**The role will have the following responsibilities:**

- Analyse response data to produce succinct analytical Protection reports, to be shared with both external and internal stakeholders, highlighting key protection trends and concerns.
- Collaborate with other relevant internal partners, including access and advocacy colleagues and promote alignment, integration and multi-sectoral analyses and responses.
- Maintain strategic relationship with Regional Protection and Thematic Advisors to receive technical support in implementation of the PfV program including support in aligning in-country programme with Global guidelines and SOPs.
- Ensure in-country technical standards, guidance notes, and programming resources for protection of civilians programming align with NRC global standards and are adapted to the context in each Area Office.
- Assess training and development needs within the Protection from Violence teams, develop capacity building plan and implement the plan with the support of the Protection from Violence Managers or Coordinators, develop training materials based on relevant programme guidelines and SOPs and roll-out training to the Civilian Self-Protection and Individual Response Services teams.
- Any other tasks as delegated by the line manager.

Please download the [detailed job description ](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBDOOW0AwEjQb6QYvSiOiI4AROR5T5afXDgKwvmcnZSA7k?e=hwTOPY)to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring**

- **Minimum 4 years** of experience with **Protection programming in a humanitarian/ recovery context**.
- **A bachelor’s degree** in a relevant field (law, social sciences or related disciplines). An advanced academic qualification will be an added advantage.
- Experience from working in **complex and volatile contexts**.
- **Expertise** in the field of **Protection**.
- Excellent **understanding of key technical standards** (IASC, protection mainstreaming, IHL, gender and humanitarian principles, donor markers on gender and disability etc.) and a demonstrated ability to integrate them into programming.
- Knowledge of the **Palestine humanitarian context**.
- Experience **with scale-up of projects and emergency contexts.**
- Experience in the design and delivery of **team capacity strengthening, including remote coaching, mentoring and training.**
- Experience with **remote management** and working modalities.
- **Fluency in English**, both written and verbal.
- Previous experience of **coordinating multi-agencies forum**.
- Knowledge of Arabic language, written and verbal, is an **advantage.**

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: **West Bank , Palestine or Amman,Jordan**
- Travel: Approximately 10% to areas of operation.
- Salary/benefits: **Grade 9 on NRC’s** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- For current NRC employees, please use your official email address when applying.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **mero.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

NRC currently has over 3,000 staff across the Middle East dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Libya and Palestine. Its humanitarian interventions are based upon its programming expertise in the Core Competencies of Shelter, Education, WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security, and Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) to vulnerable displaced people that were forced to flee.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

Learn more about NRC's operations in Palestine [here.](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/palestine/)

jobs.title: Senior Talent Acquisition Officer- (For Syrian National Only)Aleppo
jobs.description:
## Background and context

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 700 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery. It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and adapting to the evolving context.

With the new realities under the new government, as of December 2024, the IRC has deployed a team to Damascus to set up operations and engage in coordination structures for newly accessible areas across Syria, including parts of NES, NWS, and other previously unreachable locations in South and Central Syria, adjusting operations to maximize coverage and efficiency.

The IRC focuses on narrowing the gender gap in humanitarian aid and on contributing to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in both our programs and operations, so that our clients, including those from minority groups, enjoy the same rights, opportunities, and access to services. The IRC is also strongly committed to an equitable and inclusive culture in which safeguarding is upheld in our workplace and programs. We are determined to protect our clients and staff from safeguarding violations through prevention and, where misconduct is alleged, to address it without fear or favor.

## Job overview

The Senior Talent Acquisition Officer is responsible for filling short-term, emergency response, and full-time positions to meet the demands of donors and programs in the main office and field locations across Syria. The role leads proactive sourcing, advertising, screening, interviewing, reference checking, and final negotiations for open positions, and initiates and implements recruitment strategies that increase the IRC’s talent pool and pipelines as the program expands into newly accessible areas.

The Senior Talent Acquisition Officer provides input to ensure the IRC has diverse talent that performs at a high level and responds to the changing needs of the organization. The role applies IRC recruitment best practices to ensure the timely selection of top talent, recruits people who will support IRC’s organizational culture, and strengthens IRC’s position as an employer of choice.

## Major responsibilities

### Workforce planning and strategic talent acquisition

- Partner with senior leadership and department heads to forecast staffing needs aligned with programmatic growth, funding pipelines, and strategic priorities, including the expansion into new areas of Syria.
- Develop and maintain a workforce planning model to identify and address talent gaps proactively.
- Develop and implement strategies to build and maintain internal and external talent pipelines and rosters across all key areas and regions, especially for critical and hard-to-fill roles.

### Recruitment operations and process management

- Under the supervision of the Talent Acquisition Manager, respond to recruitment position requests and review recruitment and service requests received from supervisors.
- Coordinate the full-cycle recruitment process, including remote recruitment, to find the best talent: build candidate rosters, apply traditional sourcing strategies, actively network, and use innovative, creative recruiting methods.
- Guide hiring managers through the recruitment lifecycle, influence recruitment decisions, and build effective relationships with them.
- Review and audit job descriptions to ensure clarity and consistency, and to match IRC job bands, standards, and position titles.
- Manage job postings on IRC platforms, regional and international job boards, and social media, and screen applicants against defined criteria.
- Coordinate and conduct preliminary interviews, facilitate final interviews with hiring managers, complete reference checks, and manage candidate communications throughout the process.
- Conduct in-depth salary analysis to attract the highest caliber candidates, and educate hiring managers on the IRC’s compensation philosophy.
- Lead the offer process, including compensation negotiation, start dates, and onboarding logistics, and liaise with hiring managers on travel and logistics for new hires.
- Partner with international recruiters on dual recruitment, pursuing national and expatriate candidates simultaneously for urgent positions whenever possible.
- Manage the service contract recruitment process.
- Maintain recruitment files, trackers, and the applicant tracking system, ensuring timely and accurate records.

### Stakeholder engagement and capacity building

- Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, including country program HR staff and recruiters, the Regional HR team, partners, universities, peer agencies, and the private sector.
- Ensure timely and transparent communication between applicants, hiring managers, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Build the capacity of hiring managers and new HR or recruitment staff to identify talent through improved interviewing skills.

### Compliance, metrics, and continuous improvement

- Support implementation of the IRC Global HR Operating Policies and Procedures (HROPP) on recruitment, and ensure all recruitment activities adhere to these standards.
- Study and stay informed of Syrian labor laws and any local requirements affecting recruitment.
- Maintain confidentiality of sensitive HR and recruitment information.
- Provide weekly, monthly, and quarterly recruitment metrics and insights to the Talent Acquisition Manager & People & Culture Director
- Integrate gender equality, diversity, and inclusion (GEDI) principles into recruitment strategies, and monitor diversity metrics to drive inclusive hiring practices.

### Employer branding and talent engagement

- Promote the IRC brand as an employer of choice in Syria and the region, with a focus on creating awareness of the IRC’s response to the Syrian crisis.
- Oversee social media initiatives and apply innovative sourcing methods to support recruiting objectives.
- In collaboration with technical units, represent the IRC at career fairs, conferences, seminars, and other industry events as necessary, and partner with local schools and universities to build a strong reputation and promote open positions.
- Develop a deep understanding of the IRC’s culture and values, and align these with sourcing and attracting talent.

### Collaboration and field support

- Work closely with P&C officers and the P&C lead to ensure consistency in recruitment standards and practices.
- Travel to field sites in Syria and attend interviews/tests as required to support recruitment and operational needs.

### Partnership and representation

- Represent the department in IRC’s partner capacity assessment processes and other strategic initiatives, as required.

### Other duties

- Perform other recruitment responsibilities and additional tasks as assigned by the supervisor, ensuring a safe and compliant working environment.

## Safeguarding responsibilities

- Promote and actively participate in initiatives and efforts to build team engagement, inclusion, and cohesion in the IRC Syria team and office.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and to promote IRC values and adherence to IRC policies.

## Job requirements

### Education and experience

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Human Resources, or a related field.
- 3 to 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in recruitment and headhunting.
- Previous experience in an INGO setting is required.
- Experience with applicant tracking systems (ATS) and internal mobility processes is highly desirable.
- Experience in remote recruitment and in using diverse advertising channels to attract a broad and inclusive candidate pool is an advantage.
- Working knowledge of Syrian labor law is an advantage.

### Demonstrated skills and competencies

- Commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values, and the IRC Way: Professional Standards for Conduct.
- Credible written, presentation, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey information effectively and solid experience providing training and staff development.
- Professional discretion, integrity, and the ability to handle complex and sensitive situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and a solid ability to promote harmonious, cohesive teamwork in a cross-cultural context.
- Ability to plan long-term, organize priorities, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, high-volume environment, with strong attention to detail and follow-through.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful, able to build positive working relationships with senior management and all other partners.
- Analytical ability to create effective solutions to complex matters while adhering to labor laws and internal policies.
- Creative, solution-oriented, and resilient approach to recruitment challenges.
- Curiosity and a desire to continually learn and develop.

### Language and travel

- English and Arabic are required.
- 40% Travel to field sites in Syria as needed.

## Key working relationships

**Position reports to:** Talent Acquisition Manager

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect reporting:** N/A

**Key internal contacts:** All P&C team members, hiring managers, field managers, the finance team, and the Regional Talent Acquisition team.

**Key external contacts:** Partners, universities, peer agencies, the private sector, and job platforms.

## Professional standards and commitments

**Professional standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in the IRC Way: Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability, and Equality. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work, Fiscal Integrity, Anti-Retaliation, and Combating Trafficking in Persons.

**Returning national candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive **relocation package**. Eligibility is determined based on IRC’s operational needs and specific role requirements. The IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of the IRC’s Client Responsiveness (CR) mechanisms, preserving a culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Gender equality:** The IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce, including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols, and other supportive benefits and allowances.

**Equal opportunity:** The IRC is an equal opportunity employer and considers all applicants on the basis of merit, without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability. The IRC strives to build a diverse and inclusive team at all levels who, as individuals and as a group, embody our culture statement and create a working environment characterized by critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity, so that we can deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: A consultant for community based climate resilience through integrated climate change adaptation disaster risk reduction early warning & systems
jobs.company: Adventist Development and Relief Agency International
jobs.description:
**REQUEST FOR CONSULTANTS**

The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive changes. ADRA Somalia belongs to the worldwide network, comprised of more than 130 supporting and implementing country offices. ADRA Somalia is seeking to recruit a consultant **for strengthening community-based climate resilience through integrated climate change, adaptation disaster risk reduction, early warning and systems and anticipatory action.**

Somalia continues to face multiple and interconnected challenges, including protracted conflict, recurrent droughts and floods, displacement, environmental degradation, poverty, and increasing pressure on livelihoods and essential services. These challenges have heightened the vulnerability of communities to climate-related and other disasters, particularly among women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, internally displaced populations, and other marginalized groups.

Climate variability and the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events continue to undermine household resilience, disrupt livelihoods, threaten food and water security, and weaken communities' capacity to cope with and recover from shocks. Limited access to timely early warning information, inadequate preparedness mechanisms, and gaps in local disaster risk management capacities further exacerbate these vulnerabilities.

ADRA Somalia recognizes the importance of strengthening community-led climate resilience, disaster risk reduction (DRR), emergency preparedness, and anticipatory action as essential approaches to reducing vulnerabilities and protecting lives, livelihoods, and community assets. This requires equipping communities with the knowledge, skills, and practical tools to identify and assess risks, interpret and act on early warning information, develop locally appropriate preparedness and response measures, and coordinate effectively with relevant authorities and other stakeholders.

Against this background, ADRA Somalia seeks to strengthen the capacities of target communities to anticipate, prepare for, respond to, and recover from climate-related and other hazards. The intervention will promote inclusive community participation, local ownership, and the development of practical, community-driven resilience and disaster preparedness plans that contribute to sustainable risk reduction and improved community resilience.

**Community Climate and Disaster Risk**

Communities across Somalia face increasing exposure to climate-related hazards and other shocks, including recurrent droughts, floods, environmental degradation, resource scarcity, and displacement. These risks threaten lives and livelihoods, undermine food and water security, disrupt access to essential services, and weaken household and community resilience. The impacts are particularly severe for vulnerable and marginalised populations, whose capacity to anticipate, withstand, and recover from disasters is often limited by socioeconomic and structural challenges.

Strengthening community-based disaster risk management is essential to addressing these vulnerabilities. Community leaders, local authorities, disaster management structures, women's and youth groups, and other community-based organisations play a critical role in identifying and assessing risks, disseminating early warning information, mobilising local resources, supporting vulnerable households, and coordinating timely preparedness and anticipatory actions. Building their technical and organisational capacities will enhance community ownership, strengthen local response mechanisms, and promote sustainable approaches to climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction.

**Purpose of the Assignment**

ADRA Somalia seeks to engage a qualified external consultant to design and deliver an integrated, participatory capacity-building programme aimed at strengthening community resilience to climate-related hazards and other disasters. The assignment will equip 360 representatives from target communities with the knowledge, practical skills, and tools necessary to identify and assess risks, strengthen emergency preparedness, implement disaster risk reduction measures, and undertake timely anticipatory actions in response to emerging threats.

The assignment will encompass three interconnected components: climate change awareness and emergency preparedness; Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Anticipatory Action; and the participatory development of community-level climate resilience and disaster preparedness plans. These components will be implemented through a sequential and mutually reinforcing approach, ensuring that knowledge and skills acquired through training are translated into practical, locally appropriate actions and community-owned preparedness and resilience plans.

The overall intention is to strengthen local capacities, promote inclusive community participation, and establish sustainable mechanisms through which communities can anticipate, prepare for, respond to, and recover from climate-related and other shocks.

**OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen the capacities of target communities to anticipate, prepare for, mitigate, respond to, and recover from climate-related hazards and other disasters through inclusive, participatory, and locally driven approaches. The assignment seeks to enhance community resilience by promoting practical knowledge, strengthening local disaster risk management mechanisms, and supporting the development and implementation of sustainable, community-owned preparedness and resilience measures.

The specific objectives are to:

1. Enhance community awareness and understanding of climate change and disaster risks by strengthening knowledge of climate variability, locally relevant hazards, vulnerabilities, and their impacts on lives, livelihoods, essential services, and community well-being, while promoting appropriate climate adaptation and risk reduction measures.
2. Strengthen community capacities in disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, and anticipatory action by equipping participants with practical skills in risk identification, early warning interpretation and dissemination, contingency planning, community mobilization, and the implementation of timely actions to minimise the impacts of anticipated shocks.
3. Support participatory community risk assessments and resilience planning by enabling communities to identify and prioritise risks, assess existing capacities and resources, develop feasible mitigation and preparedness measures, and formulate, validate, and take ownership of locally appropriate climate resilience and disaster preparedness plans.
4. Promote inclusive and community-led disaster risk management by ensuring the meaningful participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable and marginalised groups in risk assessments, decision-making, preparedness planning, and implementation of resilience-building initiatives.
5. Strengthen local coordination and sustainable disaster preparedness mechanisms by enhancing collaboration among community structures, local authorities, disaster management institutions, and other relevant stakeholders to improve early warning communication, resource mobilisation, coordinated response, and the sustainability of community resilience initiatives.

**SCOPE OF WORK AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant will be responsible for designing, coordinating, and delivering a comprehensive, participatory capacity-building programme on climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, and anticipatory action. The assignment will combine technical training, practical exercises, community risk assessments, and facilitated resilience planning to strengthen local capacities and promote sustainable, community-led disaster risk management.

The scope of work will encompass the following three interrelated components:

**Climate Change Awareness and Emergency Preparedness**

The consultant will:

1. Conduct a rapid assessment of climate-related hazards, disaster risks, existing community capacities, and local preparedness mechanisms through desk reviews, stakeholder consultations, and engagement with community representatives to inform the design and contextualisation of training materials.
2. Develop comprehensive, accessible, and context-specific training modules covering climate change and variability, disaster risk identification, vulnerability assessment, climate adaptation, emergency preparedness, risk communication, community-based response mechanisms, and measures to protect lives, livelihoods, infrastructure, and essential services.
3. Design and facilitate participatory training sessions for target community representatives, using practical examples, case studies, group discussions, and interactive learning approaches appropriate to participants' literacy levels, experiences, and local contexts.
4. Strengthen participants' understanding of household and community preparedness measures, including contingency planning, safe evacuation procedures, emergency communication, resource mobilisation, protection of vulnerable populations, and continuity of essential community services during emergencies.
5. Facilitate participatory hazard, vulnerability, and capacity assessments to enable communities to identify priority risks, existing coping mechanisms, available resources, and opportunities for strengthening local preparedness and resilience.
6. Develop and administer appropriate pre- and post-training assessments to measure improvements in participants' knowledge, understanding, and practical preparedness capacities, documenting key learning outcomes and areas requiring further support.

**Disaster Risk Reduction and Anticipatory Action Capacity Building**

The consultant will:

1. Develop and deliver practical training modules on community-based disaster risk reduction (DRR) and anticipatory action, covering hazard monitoring, early warning systems, risk communication, forecast interpretation, contingency planning, anticipatory action triggers, and locally appropriate risk mitigation measures.
2. Strengthen community capacities to access, understand, interpret, and disseminate early warning information from credible sources, including relevant government institutions, meteorological and hydrological services, and established regional and national early warning mechanisms.
3. Facilitate practical exercises, scenario-based simulations, seasonal risk mapping, and participatory discussions to enable participants to apply DRR and anticipatory action concepts to realistic situations involving droughts, floods, displacement, environmental hazards, and other locally identified risks.
4. Support communities to identify and prioritize feasible anticipatory actions that can be undertaken ahead of predicted hazards, including measures to protect vulnerable households, safeguard livelihoods and productive assets, strengthen water and food security, facilitate safe movement, and minimise potential losses and disruptions.
5. Strengthen understanding of community-level disaster preparedness and response arrangements, including roles and responsibilities, communication protocols, community mobilisation, referral pathways, resource identification, and coordination with relevant authorities and humanitarian actors.
6. Promote the integration of DRR and anticipatory action into existing community structures, local development initiatives, and preparedness mechanisms, ensuring that proposed measures are practical, inclusive, locally appropriate, and aligned with relevant disaster risk management frameworks.
7. Facilitate engagement with relevant government disaster management institutions, local authorities, community-based organisations, and other stakeholders to strengthen coordination, information sharing, and linkages between community preparedness mechanisms and established early warning and response systems.

**Development of Community Climate Resilience and Disaster Preparedness Plans**

The consultant will:

1. Develop a standardized but locally adaptable community climate resilience and disaster preparedness planning framework, incorporating hazard and vulnerability assessments, community capacities, seasonal risks, early warning arrangements, anticipatory actions, emergency response procedures, resource requirements, coordination mechanisms, and monitoring arrangements.
2. Facilitate inclusive and participatory community planning workshops involving local leaders, community representatives, women's and youth groups, persons with disabilities, vulnerable households, relevant authorities, and other stakeholders to identify priority risks and formulate practical preparedness and resilience measures.
3. Support communities to undertake comprehensive risk assessments, identify existing coping and adaptation capacities, analyse gaps in preparedness and response mechanisms, and prioritize interventions based on their relevance, feasibility, potential impact, and available resources.
4. Guide participants in developing community-owned climate resilience and disaster preparedness plans that clearly define priority actions, responsible actors, implementation timelines, resource requirements, early warning and communication arrangements, and mechanisms for coordinating preparedness and response activities.
5. Ensure that the plans incorporate appropriate anticipatory action measures, including locally relevant early warning indicators, agreed triggers for preparedness actions, protection of vulnerable populations, livelihood safeguarding measures, and practical arrangements for mobilizing community resources ahead of anticipated shocks.
6. Facilitate community-level validation processes to ensure that proposed plans reflect locally identified priorities, incorporate diverse community perspectives, promote meaningful participation, and secure ownership and commitment from relevant community structures and local authorities.
7. Support communities to establish practical mechanisms for implementing, monitoring, reviewing, and periodically updating their resilience and preparedness plans, including clear responsibilities, coordination arrangements, and opportunities for integrating priority actions into existing community development and disaster management processes.
8. Finalise and compile the validated community climate resilience and disaster preparedness plans, accompanied by a consolidated synthesis report highlighting common hazards, priority vulnerabilities, existing community capacities, proposed risk reduction and anticipatory actions, implementation considerations, and recommendations for strengthening long-term community resilience.

**METHODOLOGY**

The consultant will adopt a participatory, inclusive, conflict-sensitive, and practical approach to capacity building, ensuring that training and community engagement activities are responsive to local contexts, community priorities, and the diverse needs and capacities of participants. The methodology will emphasise experiential learning, community ownership, and the practical application of knowledge and skills to strengthen climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, and anticipatory action.

The consultant will be expected to apply the following methodological principles throughout the assignment:

1. **Participatory and community-centred approaches:** Employ interactive and participatory learning methods that actively engage community members in identifying risks, analysing vulnerabilities, sharing local knowledge, and developing practical solutions. Training will incorporate group discussions, community hazard mapping, seasonal calendars, case studies, simulations, and action-planning exercises to encourage active participation and practical application of acquired knowledge.
2. **Contextualisation and accessibility:** Adapt training content, materials, and facilitation approaches to the prevailing socioeconomic, cultural, environmental, and security conditions of target communities. Community-facing training will be delivered primarily in Somali, using accessible language, visual materials, practical demonstrations, and locally relevant examples to accommodate participants with varying literacy levels and educational backgrounds.
3. **Inclusive and gender-responsive participation:** Ensure meaningful and equitable participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, older persons, and other vulnerable and marginalised groups. Participant selection will be undertaken transparently in consultation with ADRA Somalia, local authorities, and community representatives, with appropriate measures to address barriers to participation and ensure diverse perspectives are reflected in training and community resilience planning.
4. **Practical and experiential learning:** Prioritise hands-on learning and real-life applications over purely theoretical instruction. The consultant will facilitate scenario-based exercises, community risk assessments, early warning simulations, preparedness drills, and participatory planning sessions that enable participants to translate technical concepts into feasible community-level disaster risk reduction and anticipatory actions.
5. **Community ownership and sustainability:** Promote locally led approaches that recognise and build upon existing community knowledge, coping strategies, resources, and disaster management structures. Community representatives will be actively involved in identifying priorities, developing preparedness measures, validating resilience plans, and establishing practical arrangements for implementation, monitoring, and periodic review.
6. **Coordination and institutional engagement:** Collaborate with relevant government authorities, disaster management institutions, community-based organisations, humanitarian actors, and other stakeholders to ensure that training and planning processes complement existing disaster risk management frameworks, early warning mechanisms, and local coordination arrangements. The approach will strengthen linkages between community structures and relevant institutions while preserving community ownership and leadership.
7. **Conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, and protection:** Integrate do-no-harm principles, conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, and protection considerations throughout the assignment. The consultant will assess and mitigate potential risks associated with community engagement, participant selection, information sharing, and training activities, ensuring that interventions do not exacerbate existing tensions, reinforce inequalities, or expose vulnerable individuals and groups to additional risks.
8. **Monitoring, evaluation, and adaptive learning:** Establish practical mechanisms for assessing training effectiveness, documenting knowledge gains, and capturing participant feedback. These will include pre- and post-training assessments, structured observations, participatory reflection exercises, and documentation of community planning outcomes. Participation and results data will be disaggregated by sex, age, and disability where appropriate and feasible, with due consideration for informed consent, confidentiality, and secure data management. Findings will inform adjustments to training approaches and recommendations for future community resilience interventions.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

The assignment shall be undertaken by a qualified and experienced individual consultant or consultancy firm with demonstrated technical expertise in climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction (DRR), emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and community resilience programming. Preference will be given to qualified Somali national consultants and Somali-owned consultancy firms with demonstrated local expertise, contextual understanding, and operational capacity to deliver the assignment effectively. International consultants and firms may also apply; however, demonstrated experience in Somalia and meaningful engagement of Somali technical expertise will be considered important advantages.

The consultant or proposed team must possess the following qualifications, competencies, and experience:

1. **Academic Qualifications:** An advanced university degree (Master's degree or higher) in Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change Adaptation, Environmental Science, Climate Resilience, Community Development, Humanitarian Action, Development Studies, or another closely related discipline. Additional professional certifications or specialised training in DRR, anticipatory action, climate adaptation, or emergency preparedness will be an added advantage.
2. **Relevant Professional Experience:** A minimum of five years of progressively responsible professional experience in designing, implementing, and facilitating community-based climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, or anticipatory action interventions, preferably within humanitarian, development, or resilience-building programmes.
3. **Technical Expertise in DRR and Anticipatory Action:** Demonstrated understanding and practical application of disaster risk management frameworks, community-based early warning systems, forecast-based anticipatory action, risk analysis, contingency planning, climate adaptation strategies, and locally led disaster preparedness and response mechanisms.
4. **Community-Based Risk Assessment and Resilience Planning:** Proven experience conducting participatory hazard, vulnerability, and capacity assessments, facilitating community risk mapping, and supporting the development, validation, and operationalisation of practical community disaster preparedness, climate adaptation, or resilience plans.
5. **Training Design and Capacity Development:** Demonstrated experience developing comprehensive training curricula, facilitator guides, participatory learning materials, and practical capacity-building tools. The consultant must have a proven ability to facilitate community-level training using adult-learning methodologies, scenario-based exercises, simulations, and other interactive approaches appropriate for participants with varying literacy levels and technical backgrounds.
6. **Experience in Somalia and Comparable Humanitarian Contexts:** Demonstrated professional experience implementing similar assignments in Somalia, particularly in conflict-affected, displacement-affected, and climate-vulnerable communities. Strong familiarity with Somalia's socioeconomic, cultural, environmental, and institutional context, including local community structures, customary practices, and disaster management arrangements, will be highly valued. Consultants and firms with established operational experience and networks within Somalia will be given preference.
7. **Knowledge of Early Warning and Disaster Management Systems:** Sound understanding of Somalia's disaster risk management structures, relevant national and subnational coordination mechanisms, and established early warning information systems, including those supported by the Somalia Water and Land Information Management (SWALIM), Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET), and other relevant institutions.
8. **Community Engagement, Inclusion, and Protection:** Demonstrated ability to facilitate inclusive community engagement processes involving local authorities, traditional and community leaders, women's and youth groups, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable groups. Proven understanding of gender equality, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity, safeguarding, protection, and do-no-harm principles in community-based programming.
9. **Stakeholder Coordination and Institutional Engagement:** Proven ability to engage and coordinate effectively with government institutions, local disaster management authorities, community-based organisations, humanitarian and development partners, and other relevant stakeholders. Established working relationships with relevant institutions and community structures in Somalia, particularly in the proposed implementation areas, will be considered an added advantage.
10. **Monitoring, Evaluation, and Technical Reporting:** Demonstrated experience designing and administering training assessments, measuring knowledge and capacity improvements, documenting participatory processes, and producing high-quality technical reports, training materials, community resilience plans, and actionable recommendations.
11. **Communication and Facilitation Skills:** Excellent interpersonal, communication, analytical, and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical concepts in clear, practical, and culturally appropriate ways. Strong written and spoken proficiency in both Somali and English is required. The consultant or proposed team must demonstrate the capacity to deliver community-level training effectively in Somali and produce high-quality technical reports in English.
12. **Operational Capacity, Professional Competence and Local Expertise:** Demonstrated capacity to deliver the assignment effectively, with qualified personnel and relevant technical experience. In line with ADRA Somalia's commitment to localisation, preference will be given to qualified Somali consultants and Somali-owned firms with established in-country operations and relevant experience. Applicants must meet the required technical standards, demonstrate value for money, and possess a valid Tax Compliance Certificate (TCC).

jobs.title: Cash and Medical Benefits Specialist
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) provides lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to individuals forced to flee from war, persecution, or natural disasters. Operating in more than 40 countries and through 29 regional offices across the United States, the IRC delivers emergency relief, relocates refugees, and supports long-term recovery and self-reliance. In the U.S., IRC programs are designed to help refugees thrive, from enrolling children in school and helping adults find employment or start businesses, to facilitating access to health and mental health services. Our work ensures that families receive the care they need to heal and rebuild. IRC Kansas has supported refugees and other newcomers with trauma-informed family services, economic empowerment programs, education for youth and adults, and immigration legal services. IRC Kansas is committed to helping individuals rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in a new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Cash and Medical Assistance Benefits Specialist will provide comprehensive services and conduct activities related to Cash and Medical Assistance (CMA) programs that are funded by the Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR). The CMA Benefits Specialist will implement Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA), Refugee Medical Screening (RMS), and/or Refugee Medical Assistance (RMA) programs as outlined in federal regulations, by KSOR, and the Medical Replacement Designee (MRD), as applicable. The CMA Benefits Specialist will represent the IRC and collaborate and coordinate closely with the donor, other implementing agencies, local stakeholders and service providers.

**Responsibilities:**

**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:**

- Assist clients in accessing services, resources, and benefits according to program requirements.
- Conduct client outreach and follow-up through phone calls, text messages, home visits, and office appointments.
- Support client intake, eligibility verification, enrollment, and orientation processes.
- Assist clients with scheduling appointments, completing forms, and obtaining necessary documentation.
- Provide comprehensive and required services to IRC clients enrolling or enrolled in Refugee Cash Assistance, Refugee Medical Services, and/or Refuge Health Screening services;
- Review applications for accuracy and make eligibility determinations, ensuring non-duplication of services.
- Conduct monthly redetermination meetings to track and plan participation in employment services for the purpose of determining continued eligibility.
- Prepare the enrollment package including Enrollment Letter and Insurance Card and any other items designated by the Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR) or the Medical Replacement Designee (insurer) and conduct enrollment meetings to provide enrollment documents and ensure RMA recipients know their rights and responsibilities.
- Conduct RMA orientation, including in-depth orientation to benefits and local health systems.
- Provide support to recipients with billing issues and troubleshooting with providers who need verification of insurance coverage/benefits.
- Collaborate with KSOR and health clinic staff to ensure refugee health screenings are scheduled and coordinated with the direct service team, and to trouble-shoot any issues that arise.
- Prepare and disseminate case closure documentation according to policies.
- Maintain accurate and complete client files in compliance with program and agency requirements.
- Actively engage with donors and other stakeholders to develop policy and processes, identify ways to improve programs and provide feedback.
- Communicate resettlement trends, including spikes in scheduled arrivals, to donor and medical providers on a regular basis.
- Remain current on topics and the context in which CMA benefits are processed, accessed and used, including the Code of Federal Regulations that relate to each of the benefits available through the Kansas CMA Benefits Program.
- Ensure understanding of changes to TANF policies, SNAP Employment & Training, KanCare and/or Medicaid policies, employment programs and local and global medical issues, and how these changes impact clients and KSOR-funded programs.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s Degree strongly preferred, preferably in Social Work or related field.

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum one-year related work experience with human services programs and increasing levels of responsibility.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Proven ability to work under pressure with deadlines and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically in a multi-cultural setting and with limited- English proficiency speakers.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- International work or study experience a plus.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Working Environment:
- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Fleet Officer
jobs.description:
**Location:** Kisangani, Tshopo Province with travel within or to other provinces as necessary

**Length of contract:** 3 months with possibility of extension

**Start Date**: ASAP

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG), under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support enabling countries to detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GEG leads GORS as the prime recipient, building on its ongoing role as Field Programs Support lead for Team Credence on the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC). Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting/Communication Lines**

The Fleet Officer for Ebola responds to the GORS Logistics Coordinator for work planning, delivery and performance. The Fleet Officer manage vehicle, drivers, fuel monitors and fuel supplies within strict Fleet and procurement and finance procedure and processes.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

The fleet Officer is responsible for providing overall operational and logistics Procurement support to the GEG GORS Ebola ensures the safe cost-effective and compliant movement of the GORS and partners personnel and cargos in Tshopo and over provinces as required. Supporting the Safety and Security team, the Fleet Officer ensure that all vehicles with GORS personnel are tracked on a daily bases. With the Fuel Monitors, and their reports, the Fleet Officer monitor GORS vehicles and supplied fuel and vehicles to partners consumption and escalate any anomaly’s

*The Fleet Officer will:*

*Fleet operation and movement planning*

- Daily dispatch and schedule, allocate vehicles and drivers for the GORS Office and Field presence
- In conjunction with GORS Safety and security officer, ensure that all vehicles are tracked in Realtime using available technologies.
- Plan and coordinates Vehicles and cargo transfers via barges and ferries across the Congo river and other Tshopo rivers when needed
- Manage rented third party vehicles (Motorbike, cars, 4x4, light and heavy trucks) verifying rental companies compliances, vehicles roadworthiness and accurate billing

*Fuel management*

- Monitor fuel tracking and monitor fuel consumption per vehicles, manage fuel cards and coupons, bulks fuel tank reserves. Investigate and report anomalies and suspects consumption
- Compile and prepare monthly report with not limited to vehicles usages, fuel consumption, driver performance and costs

*Drivers’ management*

- Directly supervise, schedule and evaluate drivers provided with vehicles requesting drivers changes fi required
- Conduct mandatory induction to drivers regarding GEG and GORS Rules and regulation (GEG way, PSEA, code of conduct and Safe driving), driving test, basic mechanic test.

*Legal and compliance*

- Ensure to have in files all vehicles and drivers legal and necessary documentation as per DRC regulation
- Work closely with Safety and security officer on any accident and incident, to support recovery effort.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- At least 5 years of fleet experience, in humanitarian program with supply-chain, pharmacy logistics, biomedical supply or comparable experience.
- Demonstrate the management of a medium-size fleet at country or regional level
- Demonstrated work with fleet ambulances in outbreak or emergency settings.
- Strong understanding of fleet management, quality assurance, and chain of custody.
- Ability to work in a difficult environment and work under pressure.
- Fluent communication in English and French.
- Ability to use Excel and word as an advance user, designing complex excel sheet

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

- Adherence to and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travels**

The Fleet Officer may travel within the province and to other provinces in the Eastern region of the DRC for an agreed period according to operational needs, when required.

**Working Conditions**

The Fleet Officer will work from Kisangani. Working hours will be scheduled within the contracted 40-hour weekly allocation, with hours aligned to DRC GORS operations. Emergency support will follow agreed activation and backup arrangements. The Fleet Officer adheres to GEG security management directives and policies.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. For International procurement the Procurement will work with the Senior Logistics Lead and Logistics coordinator. **Scope of Work**

The Procurement Officer is responsible for providing overall operational and logistics Procurement support to the GEG GORS Ebola Response Program. - Ability to work in a difficult environment and work under pressure.

**Working Conditions**

**About Global Emergency Group**

jobs.title: Logistics and Supply Chain Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Location:** Kisangani, Tshopo Province with travel within or to other provinces as necessary

**Length of contract:** 3 months with possibility of extension

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG), under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support enabling countries to detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GEG leads GORS as the prime recipient, building on its ongoing role as Field Programs Support lead for Team Credence on the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC). Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting/Communication Lines**

The Logistics and Supply Chain Coordinator for Ebola responds to the GORS DRC Program Lead for work planning, delivery and performance and to the Senior Logistics Lead on technical requirements, priorities and technical performance. The logistics coordinator follows approved Logistics, supply chain, finance and HR procedure and processes in coordination with the respective Director/Coordinators.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

The Logistics Coordinator is responsible for providing overall operational and logistics support to the GEG GORS Ebola Response Program. This includes ensuring the effective management of medical commodities, equipment, and organizational assets, and coordinating logistics operations to support program activities in accordance with approved outbreak response priorities, organizational policies, and operational standards.

The logistics team is composed of the Procurement Officer, Fleet Officer, Logistics Focal point (2), Fuel Monitors (2) and Rapid Response Logistics officer (1)

*The Logistic coordinator will:*

*Team Management*

- Maintain the Logistics Team work plan, ensuring all personnel in the team are doing their duties in a timely manner, and follow the logistics, procurement, supply chain, fleet and finance regulation.
- Manage Logistics staff performance, with review of the performances against their Post description, and procedures.
- Report immediately any wrongdoing of a member of the Logistics teams and its suppliers for official enquiry

*Supply chain*

- With the Senior Logistics Lead, translate approved clinical and public-health requirements into costed supply plans, obtaining documented validation of specifications and proposed substitutions from the relevant technical lead before procurement.
- Receive and manage the incoming international and national supply chains, from its entry point in country to it’s final destination, following the supply chain country strategy. Proactively report and act upon any bottleneck that may disrupt the supply chain.
- Ensure all USG procurement requirements for pharmaceutical and medical commodities, including quality control, customs, storage, transport, and disposition are followed.
- Track requests, stock, orders, shipment milestones, exceptions and final delivery through approved logistics systems, with relevant operational information shared through the A2A (Analysis to Action) Hub
- Document recipient acceptance, ownership and maintenance responsibilities. Escalate delivery risks to operations and relevant technical leads; refer quality concerns and substitutions for technical disposition before release or use.
- Document shortages, substitutions, quality concerns and operational risks escalate them promptly.

*Procurement*

- Ensure that all procurement activities and procurement records from Procurement officers comply with GEG GORS procedures, and that all required approvals are obtained before procurement is initiated.
- Ensure that suppliers and vendors performance is monitored and reported.

*Fleet*

- With the Fleet Officer and Fuel Monitors, to ensure that the fuel usage for GORS Vehicles and field partners, is used according to the planning, with Logbook reports, calculation sheets and weekly / Monthly report
- Escalate immediately any anomalies to Senior team for action.
- Coordinate with the Medical Team and the Fleet Officer to ensure that vehicle requests are anticipated and that suitable vehicles are available to support program and partner operations on time.

*Assets Management*

- Ensure that all assets are formally signed out before being transferred to internal or external personnel and returned in good condition.
- Keep assets registry up to date and support asset reconciliation, disposition, demobilization and AAR.
- Promptly report any suspected misuse, loss, or disappearance of assets.

*Coordination*

- Actively participate in logistics coordination forums at the provincial level.
- Actively participate in Logistics Cluster (LogCluster) online meetings and related coordination activities.
- Actively coordinate with the logistics teams of other organizations to minimize duplication of efforts, optimize resource utilization, and promote operational efficiency.
- Maintain effective communication and collaboration with relevant stakeholders to support coordinated logistics planning and response activities.

*Reporting*

- Ensure that all officers are duly and timely report to the logistics coordinator, and participates to the Logistic sand supply chain section in the monthly country report

*Budget*

- Ensure that logistics team expenditures remain within the approved budget and that resources are managed efficiently and cost-effectively.
- Monitor logistics costs and expenditures to comply with approved budget allocations.
- Support the medical team by providing up-to-date pricing information and highlighting cost fluctuations that may impact program budgets and procurement plans.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- At least 5 years of international medical logistics, humanitarian supply-chain, pharmacy logistics, biomedical supply or comparable experience.
- Demonstrate the management of a medium-size logistics team at country or regional level
- Demonstrated work with medical commodities in outbreak or emergency settings.
- Strong understanding of procurement, quality assurance, customs, transport, warehousing, inventory and chain of custody.
- Experience with at least one relevant specialized commodity category and ability to coordinate specialist support for others.
- Ability to work in a difficult environment and work under pressure.
- Fluent communication in English and French.
- DRC nationality

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

- Adherence to and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travels and Working Conditions**

The position is based in Kisangani and requires a sustained in-country presence, with regular field travel within Tshopo Province and other approved travel in the DRC as operationally required. Deployments are subject to the applicable security and movement-clearance arrangements. The post holder complies with GEG conduct, PSEA policies, security, health and administrative policies and maintains reliable communication with the HQ team. Working arrangements and availability during response activations will be agreed with the GORS DRC Program Lead in accordance with the contract.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

jobs.title: Manager, AI Transformation Portfolio
jobs.description:
**Job Overview:**

Humanitarian needs are rising while funding falls. We believe AI, used well, can help close that gap. So we are transforming how the IRC works. We are giving staff across the organization AI tools and training. We are reshaping core work like supply chain and finance. And we are reinventing how we reach people in crisis, from detecting health threats earlier to putting an AI coach in the hands of teachers and parents.

We are hiring a Manager, AI Transformation Portfolio to join the small central team that keeps this work coordinated, visible, and on track. You will track progress across a portfolio of about 40 projects, spot risks early, and make sure senior leaders have what they need to decide. You will coordinate internal communications on the transformation. And you will work directly with the IRC’s AI Executive Lead, its Chief Information Officer, and members of the Executive Board, the IRC’s senior-most leaders.

This is a 12-month role with a clear mission: help the IRC move its AI priorities from pilot to scale. We are building the structure as we go. You will bring order to ambiguity, hold owners to their commitments, and build practices that departments can run on their own as the work matures. This is not a technical role, but you will use Claude and other AI tools every day to do it well.

**What Success Looks Like in 12 Months:**

This role will support each of AI Transformation Strategy’s 12 month Key Performance Indicators:

- A meaningful number of priority projects have moved from pilot to scale, with lessons captured and reused across the IRC. à *You will help spot and share reusable insights and building blocks across projects.*
- The Executive Board has a clear, current picture of AI spend, use cases deployed, and impact, without a heavy reporting burden on project teams. à*You will refine and maintain the high efficiency, AI-enabled system that enables this visibility.*
- Enterprise-wide risks have been identified and managed early. à*You will spot and escalate key risks.*
- Departments are advancing their own AI priorities with minimal duplication. à*You will help automate and simplify the tracking system so that, as directed by the Director, it can extend to projects outside the starting priority set without adding staff time for project teams.*

Additionally, you will help build broader organizational awareness for the IRC’s transformation agenda down to the impacts and learnings of specific projects.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Portfolio Management (approximately 60%)**

- Prepare Executive Board communications and decision-making materials. Prepare standing monthly and quarterly reporting for senior leaders, including drafting updates and keeping the transformation scorecard current. Identify the need for ad hoc meetings and prepare their agendas and materials.
- Proactively understand status, blockers, and spend across AI priority projects to support progress against KPIs. Strategically escalate issues, opportunities, and risks to Director.
- Run the weekly orchestration team meeting. Build the agenda from the tracker and other intelligence. Keep time focused on the highest-priority needs. Assign action items and track follow-up.
- Own the single source of truth on AI priority projects. Keep the portfolio tracker current by attending existing steering committees and workstream meetings, checking in directly with project and workstream leads.
- Build and maintain high-level portfolio management deliverables, such as cross-project dependency maps and consolidated roadmaps.
- Lead the biweekly AI internal communications standup, from setting the agenda to ensuring follow-through on agreed commitments.
- Support Financial Planning & Analysis in tracking central AI investment allocations.
- Serve as first point of call for staff on the AI transformation. Answer questions or redirect them to the right owner.

**Special Projects (approximately 40%)**

- Provide surge support on time-sensitive communications, from content development to stakeholder coordination. Audiences include internal stakeholders (e.g., Board presentations, intranet content) and external ones (e.g., partner presentations, donor communications).
- Provide start-up capacity to get new opportunities and projects running, for example by project-managing the launch of a new AI fellows program.
- Support organic, department-level change. Coordinate replication of high-demand AI tools across departments. Disseminate and promote broadly applicable resources. Proactively connect colleagues working toward similar aims.
- Take on other special projects assigned by the Director as the transformation’s needs, opportunities, and risks evolve.

**Job Requirements:**

- 6–8 years of experience in portfolio or program management, strategy, or operations in a complex organization. This includes experience in a PMO, transformation office, or similar cross-functional coordination role.
- Demonstrated comfort working in a fast-changing environment with an ambiguous workstream. Experience running and refining structure and reporting as priorities evolve.
- Strong synthesis skills. Able to turn messy, cross-team input into clear updates on progress, next milestones, and risks.
- Strong project management skills. Brings structure through tools such as roadmaps, action logs, and dependency maps.
- Experience coordinating across functions. Confident engaging with executives, department heads, and external partners.
- Proven ability to drive progress through influence, not formal authority.
- Excellent writing skills. Able to produce clear, polished content for executive, Board, donor, and partner audiences on short timelines.
- Hands-on fluency with AI tools, ideally Claude. Uses AI to work more effectively and understands how it applies at different levels of transformation.
- Change management literacy. Understands how adoption, training, and communications work together to drive change.
- Preferred: humanitarian or NGO sector experience.

**Work Authorization:** Candidates must have the legal right to work in the country where the position is based.

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\* Remote, hybrid, or fully in-office depending on exact location within hiring countries.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America, United Kingdom, and Colombia.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $93,860-$108,935/yr; UK Pay Rate: £52,210-£61,999/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**OBJETIVO DEL CARGO**

El/la Asistente MEAL se encargará de brindar apoyo técnico y operativo en la ejecución de las actividades de diagnóstico en terreno y monitoreo de los proyectos humanitarios en respuesta a la emergencia humanitaria post terremoto del 24-06-2026, concentrando las acciones en la zona impactada.
