jobs.title: Supply Chain and Logistics Volunteer Intern
jobs.description:
## Position overview

**This is an unpaid volunteer internship. No financial remuneration will be provided.**

Global Health Partnerships (formerly THET) is offering a volunteer internship in supply chain and logistics with the UFUQ project in Damascus.

The volunteer is expected to dedicate approximately four hours per day, five days per week to assigned activities, in coordination with the direct supervisor. The working schedule shall be flexible and mutually agreed upon.

About GHP

One billion people will never see a qualified health worker in their lives. For over thirty years, GHP ([www.globalhealthpartnerships.org](http://www.globalhealthpartnerships.org/)) has been working to change this, training health workers to build a world where everyone has access to affordable, quality healthcare. We do this by drawing on the expertise and energy of the UK health community, supporting health partnerships between hospitals, colleges and clinics in the UK and those overseas.

From reducing maternal deaths in Uganda to improving hospital care for injured children in Myanmar, we work to strengthen local health systems and build a healthier future for all. Our work is rooted in the Health Partnership Model, which builds long-term institutional relationships between health organizations in the UK and in low- and middle-income countries, based on co-development, reciprocal learning and mutual benefit.

Purpose of the internship

The internship gives a motivated graduate or final-year student hands-on experience in humanitarian supply chain and logistics. The volunteer intern will support the Supply Chain team with procurement, warehousing, asset management, transport and documentation.

All tasks are carried out under supervision and in line with GHP policies and procedures, donor requirements and applicable operational standards.

Main tasks

The volunteer intern will assist the Supply Chain team with the tasks below, under the guidance of the supervisor.

Procurement

• Help prepare Requests for Quotations (RFQs), bid analyses, purchase orders and supplier agreements, following GHP procurement policies.

• Keep procurement records and purchase files accurate and up to date.

• Update the database of suppliers, contractors and service providers.

Asset management

• Support asset registration, tagging and tracking.

• Help keep asset maintenance records.

Transport and distribution

• Help coordinate delivery schedules and the distribution of goods to project locations.

• Help track logistics movements and share updates with the Supply Chain team.

• Help prepare and share movement plans, transport schedules and logistics updates.

• Liaise with relevant focal points on deliveries, as directed by the supervisor.

Documentation and coordination

• File procurement, logistics and asset documents so they are ready for audit and compliance checks.

• Support travel and accommodation arrangements for staff and project activities when needed.

• Work with the finance, programmes and operations teams to keep supply chain processes on time.

The intern may also take on other related tasks agreed with the supervisor that fit the learning goals of the internship.

Learning outcomes

By the end of the internship, the volunteer intern will have practical experience in:

• The procurement cycle, from PR to purchase order, in line with donor requirements.

• Asset registration, tagging and tracking.

• Planning transport and distributions in a humanitarian setting.

• Keeping complete, audit-ready records.

• Working across finance, programmes and operations teams.

Scope and limits of the role

This is a supervised learning role, and the supervisor reviews the intern's work. To protect the intern and GHP, the volunteer intern will not:

• Sign, approve or authorize purchases, payments or contracts.

• Handle cash or make financial commitments on GHP's behalf.

• Negotiate with or select suppliers alone.

• Travel to field or distribution sites without the supervisor's approval and clearance under GHP security procedures.

• Replace or cover a paid staff position.

Who we are looking for

• A bachelor's degree, or final year of study, in logistics, supply chain management, business administration or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Basic knowledge of supply chain procedures and logistics standards is an advantage.

• Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office; familiarity with inventory or procurement software is a plus.

• Fluency in Arabic; working knowledge of English is preferred.

• Well organized, with strong attention to detail.

• Able to manage several tasks at once and meet deadlines.

Core competencies

• Reliability and accountability

• Efficiency and time management

• Attention to detail and accurate record-keeping

• Teamwork and strong interpersonal skills

• Practical problem-solving in a fast-paced environment

• Willingness to learn and to take feedback

What GHP offers

• Hands-on learning in humanitarian supply chain and logistics, guided by the Supply Chain and Logistics Assistant.

• Induction on GHP policies, including procurement, safeguarding and safety and security

• Certificate of completion and reference letter on successful completion

Safeguarding and conduct

Before starting, the volunteer intern must read, sign and follow \[GHP's Code of Conduct, Safeguarding and PSEA policies\]. The intern will keep all procurement, supplier, financial and security information confidential, during and after the internship.

How to apply

Applications must be submitted through the Breathe platform.

Action Contre la Faim Sénégal cherche une consultation pour l’amélioration, la visualisation et l’automatisation du Système Pastoral d’Alerte Précoce.
jobs.description:
ACF dispose d’une expérience dans le développement et l’utilisation de systèmes d’information au service de la sécurité alimentaire, de l’alerte précoce et de l’action anticipatoire. À travers plusieurs initiatives, l’organisation a renforcé la qualité, la rapidité et l’utilité des données afin d’anticiper les crises, d’éclairer la prise de décision et de favoriser la coordination entre les acteurs humanitaires, les institutions publiques, le monde académique et les partenaires technologiques.
La mission de conseil portera sur l’écosystème d’information actuellement lié au PEWS, ainsi que sur les outils, plateformes, bases de données et produits d’information associés ou complémentaires utilisés par ACF au Sahel. Elle visera à renforcer la capacité du système à intégrer, traiter, visualiser, héberger, partager et exploiter les données pertinentes pour le suivi des conditions pastorales, de sécurité alimentaire et agro-environnementales.

OBJECTIF GENERAL DE LA MISSION DE CONSEIL

1. Développer une interface configurable par l’utilisateur pour la visualisation et l’exploration des données géospatiales et des séries chronologiques associées au PEWS, permettant aux utilisateurs de sélectionner des territoires spécifiques du Sahel, de définir la période ou la plage de dates à analyser, et de choisir les variables ou indicateurs pour lesquels les informations doivent être affichées.
2. Mettre en place une solution d’hébergement dans le cloud pour le traitement, le stockage et l’accès aux données du PEWS.
3. Développer un module permettant de filtrer et de prétraiter les ensembles de données de terrain reçus des sites sentinelles pastoraux répartis dans différentes régions et différents pays du Sahel, y compris l’analyse des réponses ouvertes et la traduction des messages soumis dans différentes langues.
4. Développer des modules automatisés pour extraire et mettre à jour les données issues des sources d’information fournies par ACF sur les principaux facteurs de sécurité alimentaire. Ces sources peuvent inclure des ensembles de données et des produits d’information provenant de groupes de réflexion, d’organisations internationales et d’institutions nationales, les sources prioritaires étant notamment la FAO, la Banque mondiale, l’ACLED et le PAM. D’autres sources peuvent être proposées par le prestataire, sous réserve de validation par ACF.

La mission de conseil sera mise en œuvre selon une approche appliquée et itérative, axée sur l’utilité opérationnelle. L’objectif n’est pas seulement de produire des développements technologiques isolés, mais de renforcer un écosystème d’information pouvant être utilisé par les équipes techniques d’ACF et ses partenaires pour améliorer l’alerte précoce, l’action anticipative et la prise de décision. La méthodologie comprendra :

- Un travail collaboratif avec les équipes techniques d’ACF Sénégal et d’ACF ROWCA.
- Un examen progressif des livrables intermédiaires.
- Une validation technique des sources, des indicateurs, des modèles et des visualisations.
- Une documentation claire et suffisante pour garantir l’appropriation des développements.
- L’utilisation d’outils durables et évolutifs qui seront transférés à ACF.
- Priorité accordée à des solutions reproductibles et traçables nécessitant une maintenance relativement limitée.
- Prise en compte des principes d’éthique des données, de protection des données, du « ne pas nuire » et de transparence méthodologique.

jobs.title: Human-AI Collaboration Designer
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Habitat for Humanity International works toward a world where everyone has a decent place to live. Achieving that vision requires both direct support to families and changes in the housing systems that shape whether low-income households can access affordable, appropriate, and resilient housing. Within Habitat, the Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) leads market systems and innovation efforts that influence private-sector, public-sector, and civil-society actors to improve housing outcomes at scale. TCIS identifies constraints within housing systems and works with partners to test, refine, and scale solutions across areas including housing finance, construction products and services, and enabling policy environments. As Habitat advances its 50 for 50 strategy, TCIS is also strengthening how its expertise, evidence, tools, and approaches can be accessed and applied across teams, geographies, and the wider Habitat network.

The Human-AI Collaboration Designer helps Habitat for Humanity redesign how work is performed by integrating human expertise, organizational knowledge, applied research, systems thinking, and emerging AI capabilities into practical, scalable workflows. Working across technical, operational, learning, research, and programmatic functions, this role analyzes existing processes, identifies opportunities for improvement, and design solutions that strengthen efficiency, decision-making, knowledge sharing, learning, and organizational effectiveness.

The position leads the design, testing, implementation, and continuous improvement of AI-enabled workflows, digital assistants, knowledge systems, learning tools, and collaborative work practices that augment human expertise and relationships. Through facilitation, workflow analysis, prototyping, user testing, and continuous learning, the Human-AI Collaboration Designer supports the responsible adoption of AI while maintaining a strong focus on human-centered design and mission impact. A key focus of the role is helping TCIS scale market systems development, housing systems analyses, technical assistance, learning, and innovation efforts by redesigning workflows and knowledge systems that enable teams to deliver greater reach and impact without proportional increases in resources.

The role serves as a bridge between subject matter experts, end users, and technology platforms, translating complex expertise into accessible tools, processes, and learning experiences. It strengthens the capability of individuals, teams, and partner organizations to adopt new ways of working, apply AI responsibly, and make more effective use of organizational knowledge.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## **Human-AI Collaboration Designer**

### **Help Shape the Future of Human-AI Collaboration at Habitat for Humanity!**

**Are you passionate about harnessing the power of artificial intelligence, human creativity, and innovative thinking to drive meaningful change?**

Habitat for Humanity International is seeking a forward-thinking and collaborative **Human-AI Collaboration Designer** to help transform how people, knowledge, and technology work together.

This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of **AI innovation, human-centered design, organizational learning, and systems thinking** while contributing to Habitat’s mission of building a world where everyone has a decent place to live.

If you thrive on solving complex challenges, designing practical solutions, and empowering others to embrace new ways of working, we invite you to explore this opportunity!

This position is ultimately focused on business transformation and organizational capability, combining strategic leadership with human-centered AI product design, evidence gathering and analysis, facilitated learning and systems thinking. It is not a technical specialist or IT role; rather it requires strong interpersonal skills and a deep understanding of how people work, learn, collaborate, and adapt to change. It is about designing better ways of working through human-AI collaboration.

- **Human-AI Workflow Design and Transformation (30%)**
- Analyze, map, and evaluate existing organizational workflows, processes, and decision-making practices.
- Identify opportunities to improve workflows through human-AI collaboration
- Design and implement workflow improvements that increase efficiency, quality, scalability, user experience, and consistency.

jobs.title: 23916 Migrant Protection Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)/ Case Management) (P)
jobs.description:
IOM’s Approach to Protection promotes a coherent and accountable organizational role in safeguarding the rights of individuals across operational contexts, in line with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee definition. Working with States as primary duty bearers, IOM programmes aim to ensure respect for individual rights, reduce and address exposure to protection risks, and ensure that rights are upheld and needs fulfilled. The IOM Mission in the Central African Republic (CAR) implements migrant protection activities for vulnerable migrants, including third-country nationals, migrants in transit, returnees and persons requiring assisted voluntary return and reintegration support.

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and the direct supervision of the Migrant Protection Officer (Head of Unit), the Migrant Protection Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)/ Case Management) will coordinate the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of migrant protection, case management, and assisted voluntary return activities. The Migrant Protection Officer (AVR/ Case Management) will provide technical guidance on protection mainstreaming, safe and dignified assistance, referral pathways, and case management, coordinate with relevant stakeholders, and promote and monitor the consistent application of IOM policies and protection standards, including requirements related to informed consent, confidentiality, and data protection.

**Responsibilities**

1. Coordinate migrant protection assessments and identify and recommend practical risk-mitigation measures related to operational conditions, access to essential services, accommodation, legal identity, specific vulnerabilities, referral pathways, and safe environments across post-arrival, return, and reintegration activities.
2. Coordinate and monitor the overall implementation of IOM CAR’s migrant protection and assisted voluntary return activities, including work planning, risk mitigation, accountability to affected populations, protection mainstreaming, and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH)-related safeguards.
3. Coordinate operational case management and provide technical guidance to caseworkers and support staff, ensuring safe, dignified, timely, and needs-based assistance in accordance with IOM policies and procedures.
4. Coordinate protection information management and ensure the accuracy, completeness, and appropriate maintenance of records in IOM-approved systems, including Migrant Management Operational System Application (MiMOSA) where applicable, in line with confidentiality, informed consent, and data-protection requirements.
5. Coordinate complex case-related referrals and follow-up with competent Central African authorities, diplomatic and consular representations, relevant IOM missions, United Nations agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and specialized service providers, including for documentation, health, MHPSS, family tracing and child or Gender-Based Violence (GBV)-related protection services.
6. Maintain and periodically update referral pathways and service mapping for migrant protection and assisted voluntary return activities in the Central African Republic.
7. Provide technical inputs to project development, results frameworks, donor reporting and resource requirements in line with IOM strategies, emerging operational needs and donor requirements.
8. Coordinate with relevant staff in the Country Office, Regional Office and other IOM missions to support continuity of assistance and smooth coordination of post-arrival and voluntary return processes.
9. Prepare and review operational updates, case summaries, weekly and periodic reports, briefing notes and technical materials, ensuring accuracy, appropriate analysis and protection of personally identifiable information.
10. Participate in relevant local and national coordination mechanisms and technical discussions, as assigned, and support liaison with government counterparts, UN agencies, NGOs, diplomatic missions and other stakeholders.
11. Analyse progress and results of protection activities against agreed objectives, indicators and targets, and identify and analyse trends, operational risks and implementation gaps, and recommend appropriate follow-up actions to the supervisor.
12. Keep abreast of developments in IOM and inter-agency protection standards and promote and facilitate their consistent application in day-to-day operations.
13. Undertake duty travel as required for field visits, airport movements, monitoring, and liaison with counterparts.
14. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Social Sciences, International Relations/Affairs, Migration Studies, Research, Law, Human Rights, Psychology, Social Work, or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience supporting migrant protection, case management, assisted voluntary return and reintegration, or related humanitarian or migration programming;
- Experience providing protection and assistance to migrants in vulnerable situations and communicating with individuals who have complex needs;
- Experience coordinating with government authorities, civil society organizations, United Nations agencies, diplomatic or consular representations and service providers;
- Experience in referrals, documentation, protection information management and monitoring of activities or project indicators;
- Experience in programmes that include movement operations or post-arrival assistance is an advantage; and,
- Experience with IOM or another United Nations agency is desirable.

**Skills**

- Good knowledge of IOM and inter-agency protection standards, operational procedures and case-management principles;
- Good coordination, analytical and organizational skills;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and digital case-management or reporting tools; knowledge of MiMOSA is an advantage;
- Demonstrated judgment, initiative and ability to work independently within assigned responsibilities; and,
- Demonstrated interpersonal and teamwork skills and ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Sango or another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) or any relevant language in the Central African Republic is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23650 Programme Support Officer (Migration Health) (P)
jobs.description:
Since 2016, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has supported migration health initiatives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Within its Health, Border, and Mobility Management (HBMM) framework, IOM delivers and promotes comprehensive, immediate and longer-term preventive and curative health programmes that are beneficial, accessible and equitable for migrants, mobile populations, displaced communities and other vulnerable and hard-to-reach populations. IOM works within the existing health framework with government authorities and the health cluster coordination mechanism to address the health needs of mobile communities, including migrants, internally displaced populations, cross-border communities and the populations they interact with. IOM also provides comprehensive pre-migration health assessments and emergency life-saving assistance, while contributing to strengthening the health system, which has been disrupted by long-term conflict, frequent public health and chronic humanitarian emergencies, and continuous underfunding.

In recent years, IOM DRC has intensified its support to the Ministry of Health to strengthen health security capacity at borders to effectively prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases and other public health threats. IOM provides integrated disease surveillance and control capacity building for the frontline health staff working in border areas, necessary medical and health commodities for the border posts and health facilities, analyses on population mobility patterns in priority health zones to inform preparedness efforts, health service delivery, including vaccination, as well as risk communication and community engagement targeting mobile populations and communities living along the mobility continuum.

Through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA)-funded project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach”, IOM will support health security over an 84-month implementation period, with the objective of reinforcing community-based surveillance, preparedness and response capacities in Kalemie and Nyunzu health zones, including Port Kalemie and the Moba and Kabimba points of entry.

​​Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in the DRC and direct supervision of the Programme Support Unit (PSU) Coordinator, and in close coordination with the Migration Health Coordinator, the Programme Support Officer (Migration Health) will be responsible for supporting all aspects of the KOICA projects, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), as well as reporting requirements.​

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical inputs to support the development of new projects in compliance with the donor’s interests and requirements and IOM’s procedures and priorities, and ensure alignment with the Strategic Results Framework.
2. Draft and/or coordinate the preparation of interim and final donor reports as well as mission, regional and Headquarters periodic and project-specific reports, for the Migration Health Department, as may be required in accordance with IOM procedures and donor requirements.
3. Coordinate the administrative aspects of the project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach”, including record-keeping, to support donor contract management in line with specific IOM internal requirements and procedures.
4. Maintain and update reporting systems and schedules, including ensuring revisions to the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) are done in a timely manner and reflect changes to reporting schedules.
5. Contribute to the development of communication products for the project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach” based on the Migration Health operations and results in close coordination with the Project Manager and the Media and Communication Officer.
6. Maintain accurate and updated records of all correspondence, project files, and administration information to support knowledge management and learning.
7. Provide and/or consolidate inputs for the development of programmatic responses, recommendations and approaches, in line with the Migration Health’s strategy.
8. Work closely with the Project Manager to assist in the overall integration of M&E outputs for the project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach”.
9. Provide technical inputs and draft specific sections of strategic documents, presentations, and other documents in line with IOM Corporate Policy in close consultation with the Senior Migration Health Programme Manager.
10. Organize and ensure administrative and logistical arrangements are made for events and visits of partners and the donor.
11. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Public Health, Political or Social Science, International Relations, or other relevant sciences with two years of experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in project support, coordination and/or implementation in a crisis context;
- Experience in M&E rules, regulations, and procedures;
- Experience in humanitarian/development-related activities, budget drafting, research, report writing, liaison with governments and international agencies, reporting, and donor relations; and,
- Experience with project planning, scheduling and deployment of resources, and evaluation and assessment.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM’s services, IOM’s reporting format and styles.
- Knowledge and familiarity with humanitarian and development coordination mechanisms and experience in liaison with other UN, non-UN humanitarian actors and donors;
- Excellent strategic, analysis and drafting skills;
- Excellent writing, editorial and communication skills for the drafting of texts and reports; and,
- Demonstrated interpersonal ability.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Korean and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Agentic AI System Partner Kenya
jobs.description:
**Request for Proposal: Agentic AI System Partner**

## ***Discovery, Design, Build and Handover for WAZZII Kenya***

**Open Competitive Tender**

**Girl Effect**

**Issue Date: 16 November 2026**

**Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP title Agentic AI System Partner for WAZZII Kenya

Procurement method Open competitive tender

Eligible applicants Qualified technology firms or consortiums with agentic AI, responsible AI and production-engineering capability

Location Kenya, with remote delivery permitted and in-person Nairobi workshops as required

Contract period Up to 12 months: three-month discovery phase and an optional nine-month build phase

Contract gate Phase 2 will proceed only after Girl Effect’s written Go or Re-scope approval

Clarification deadline **20th November 2026**

Consolidated FAQ **25th November 2026**

Proposal deadline **2nd December 2026**

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology girls choose, use and trust. Across Africa and South Asia, our youth brands — including Wazzii and Tuki in Kenya, Big Sis in South Africa, Chhaa Jaa and Bol Behen in India, and Yegna in Ethiopia — reach millions of adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with content and digital tools that support the decisions shaping their lives, from sexual and reproductive health (SRH) to wellbeing, education and work. Our approach is girl-centred by design: girls co-create our products, our evidence teams measure what actually changes for them, and our safeguarding architecture treats their safety as a design constraint, never an afterthought.

Girl Effect has spent a decade building conversational products for young people, and several years deliberately and publicly charting what responsible AI for girls looks like. Our published Ethical AI Guidelines, our AI/ML Vision and our GenAI Whitepaper set out the standards all our technology partners are held to; they are annexed to this TOR and should be read before responding.

## **Background**

WAZZII is Girl Effect’s WhatsApp-based chatbot for adolescent girls and young women in Kenya. It provides confidential sexual and reproductive health information, signposting and access to human help-desk support in English and Sheng.

Human operators using the RapidPro help desk remain central to the service.

Girl Effect intends to evolve WAZZII into a trusted service-navigation platform that can help users:

- Find vetted youth-friendly service providers.
- Prepare for a service-provider visit.
- Access services through approved referral mechanisms.
- Receive appropriate follow-up and continuation support.

To achieve this goal, we envisage the use of an agentic AI solution, consisting of multiple AI-powered features serving specific use cases which work under the instruction of an orchestrator. This solution will proactively support a girl’s end-to-end journey, offering guidance, follow-up, referral coordination and continuation support within strict safety and consent boundaries. This TOR selects the partner for that exploration and, if approved, that build.

### **Existing Technology Environment**

Girl Effect has an existing Azure-hosted intelligence environment that manages interactions between its digital products and large language models.

The selected partner will be required to build on the existing codebase and work closely with Girl Effect’s DevOps, product and programme teams to deploy, monitor and manage all approved components.

### **Responsible AI Context**

The assignment must align with Girl Effect’s:

- Ethical AI Guidelines.
- Guidelines on Ethical AI-Powered Social and Behaviour Change Chatbots.
- AI and Machine Learning Vision.
- GenAI Whitepaper.
- Safeguarding, data-protection and technology policies.

These documents will form part of the procurement and contractual requirements.

## **Objective and Intended Outcomes**

Girl Effect seeks an experienced partner to investigate, design, prototype and, subject to a formal approval gate, build an agentic AI layer that supports a user’s end-to-end WAZZII journey within strict consent, safeguarding and human-escalation boundaries.

The engagement should deliver:

- A justified, secure and vendor-conscious architecture that works with Girl Effect’s existing Azure environment and codebase.
- Safe and consent-based agentic capabilities for approved WAZZII use cases.
- Clear human oversight, escalation and intervention mechanisms.
- An evaluation framework covering safety, accuracy, usefulness, efficiency and behavioural quality.
- Production-grade observability, including decision logs, traces, dashboards, alerts and audit records.
- Transparent prototype, pilot and scale cost models.
- Complete code, configuration, documentation and knowledge transfer, enabling Girl Effect to operate, audit and extend the solution independently.

## **What You will Do**

The partner will investigate, prototype and — post-gate — build the agentic layer for the end-to-end girl journey, working closely with Girl Effect’s product, safeguarding, evidence and service design teams. As part of the project, an Evaluation Framework will need to be designed which is able to measure the efficacy of the different AI-powered features and of the system as a whole, with key metrics available to the program team through a dashboard.

**Phase 1 — Discovery (months 1–3). Key activities include:**

- Architecture investigation — assess candidate architectures for an agentic layer on WAZZII, with trade-offs across capability, safety, controllability, efficiency, observability and vendor/model dependencies — options with trade-offs, not a single foregone conclusion
- Proof-of-concept — build a thin agentic slice against real (sandboxed) WAZZII flows — for example proactive follow-up and referral coordination — demonstrating feasibility, not polish
- Safety case — define how agentic behaviour stays inside Girl Effect’s escalation triggers, consent rules and safeguarding protocol: failure modes, mitigations, and the assurance approach, reviewed by Safeguarding
- Evaluation framework alignment — define how the system will be measured against Girl Effect’s evaluation frameworks — behavioural quality, safety, accuracy and efficiency — including the evaluation suites and benchmarks to be built in Phase 2
- Observability design — specify the instrumentation of agent behaviour: decision and action logging, tracing across multi-step journeys, dashboards and alerting, and the audit trail Girl Effect requires
- Efficiency and cost modelling — model running costs at pilot and at scale, aligned to Girl Effect’s evaluation frameworks
- Phase 2 build plan — scope, sprint plan, team, interfaces with the platform workstream, and acceptance criteria

**Phase 2 — Build (months 4–12, contingent on gate approval). Key activities include:**

- Iterative build — of the accepted architecture in two-week sprints, against the acceptance criteria set at the gate
- Evaluation suite implementation — the evaluation framework from discovery made live: automated evaluations and benchmarks run per release, with results reported to Girl Effect
- Observability implementation — logging, tracing, dashboards and audit trails live in production; agent behaviour reviewable by Girl Effect at any time
- Integration — with the platform workstream via interfaces defined at inception, each party naming an integration lead
- Safety testing — as sprint deliverables, with no capability touching girls going live until the safety case is satisfied
- Documentation and handover — such that Girl Effect can operate, audit and extend the system independently

## **Deliverables**

Stage

Deliverables

Onboarding

Write up of understanding of GE’s existing AI technology and its application to the use case

Discovery

Architecture options paper; working proof-of-concept; safety case (safeguarding-reviewed); evaluation framework and benchmark definitions; observability specification; efficiency and cost model; Phase 2 build plan

Gate

Girl Effect’s written Go/No-Go/Re-scope decision. No payment attaches to the gate itself

Build (post-gate)

Sprint releases against acceptance criteria; evaluation suites live with per-release results; observability live (logging, tracing, dashboards, audit trail); safety tests passing per release

Handover

Production-ready agentic capability operating within the safety case; full documentation; handover enabling independent operation, audit and extension by Girl Effect

## Girl Effect will accept a deliverable only where it:

- ## Is complete.
- ## Meets the agreed acceptance criteria.
- ## Is supported by the required evidence.
- ## Has no unresolved critical or high-severity defects.

## Correcting incomplete or non-compliant work will not constitute a change in scope or attract additional fees.

## **Management and Working Arrangements**

- The engagement will be managed by Girl Effect’s Product and Delivery Lead, supported by designated safeguarding, programme, evidence, DevOps and integration leads.
- The partner must appoint an accountable engagement lead, solution architect, AI/ML lead, safety lead and engineering lead.
- Work will be managed through Girl Effect’s agreed project-management platform.
- The partner will participate in weekly delivery meetings, two-week sprint reviews and monthly programme demonstrations.
- The partner will maintain the work plan, backlog, decision log, risk register, dependency log, architecture records, evaluation results and cost tracker.
- Material changes to the architecture, model, data, scope, budget, personnel, security controls or sub-processors require Girl Effect’s prior written approval.
- Named key personnel may not be replaced without Girl Effect’s approval and an equivalent or more qualified replacement.

## **Who You Are**

The successful bidder should demonstrate:

- At least three years’ relevant experience delivering production AI or advanced data systems.
- Recent experience with agentic or tool-using AI systems.
- Strong safety-engineering and responsible AI experience, preferably within health, youth, public-service, financial or other sensitive contexts.
- Demonstrated experience in AI evaluation, red teaming, tracing, observability and auditability.
- Experience integrating with existing cloud architectures, APIs, messaging platforms and DevOps environments, preferably Microsoft Azure.
- Strong cybersecurity, privacy and data-protection capability.
- Experience designing technology for young people or vulnerable populations, which will be an advantage.
- Capacity to work with Kenya-based stakeholders and complete the full discovery-to-handover assignment.

### **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Bidders must submit separate technical and financial proposals (Max 10 pages).

#### **Technical Proposal**

It should include:

- Understanding of the assignment, intended outcomes, risks and dependencies.
- Proposed discovery methodology.
- Architecture-investigation and proof-of-concept approach.
- Responsible AI, safeguarding, privacy, security, evaluation and observability approach.
- Indicative Phase 2 architecture and implementation methodology.
- Detailed Phase 1 workplan and indicative 12-month plan.
- Proposed team, roles, location, level of effort, availability and CVs
- Three relevant case studies, including at least one deployed AI system and one sensitive-domain assignment.
- Proposed models, platforms, tools, open-source components, licences and subprocessors.
- Approach to intellectual property, portability, documentation and handover.
- Key risks, assumptions, exclusions and information required from Girl Effect.
- Three contactable client references.

#### **Financial Proposal**

The financial proposal must be submitted in **USD** and include:

- A fixed, all-inclusive Phase 1 price, broken down by onboarding, deliverable and team role.
- A separate fixed or capped price for Phase 2, broken down by sprint, deliverable, role and workstream.
- A milestone-based payment schedule linked to accepted deliverables.
- Prototype, pilot and scale cost scenarios.
- Assumptions relating to usage, volumes, environments, support and exchange rates.
- Applicable taxes shown separately.
- Any proposed reimbursable expenses clearly identified.

No more than approximately 30% of the maximum contract value should be committed before the Phase 2 gate.

Evaluation of Phase 2 pricing does not guarantee that Phase 2 will be activated or awarded.

### **Evaluation**

Proposals will be assessed in the following order:

1. Pre-screening;
2. Technical evaluation;
3. Pitch, demonstration or clarification stage, where required; and
4. Financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criterion**

- Understanding of WAZZII, the use case and discovery challenge: 25%
- Agentic AI architecture and production-engineering capability: 25%
- Evaluation/Monitoring, observability, security and data-protection approach: 10%
- Delivery methodology, proposed team, work plan and handover capability: 10%

Technical Total 70%

- Financial proposal and overall value for money 30%

Total 100%

Girl Effect may request written clarifications, invite shortlisted bidders to a pitch or technical demonstration, conduct reference checks and due diligence, or request a best-and-final offer.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 16 November 2026
- Questions/Clarification Deadline: 20th November 2026
- Consolidated FAQ shared with all prospective bidders: 25th November 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: **2nd December 2026**

### **Clarification Process**

Bidders may submit clarification questions to **suppliers@girleffect.org** by 20 November 2026

The email subject should state:

Clarification Question –**Agentic AI System Partner Kenya – Clarification**

To ensure a fair and transparent open-tender process:

- Girl Effect will not provide substantive answers to all bidders.
- All relevant questions and responses will be compiled into a consolidated FAQ.
- The FAQ will not identify the organisation that submitted each question.
- The consolidated FAQ will be shared with all prospective bidders through the same publication or communication channels used for the RFP.
- Bidders are responsible for reviewing the FAQ and any formal tender updates before submitting their proposals.
- Verbal information or guidance will not amend the RFP unless confirmed by Girl Effect in writing.

Girl Effect may decline to answer questions received after the clarification deadline.

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Phase Gate: The successful bidder will enter into Girl Effect’s services agreement and statement of work. Phase 2 will not be authorised until Girl Effect provides written gate approval.**
- **Payment and Acceptance: Payments will be linked to accepted deliverables. Elapsed time, completion of a sprint or submission of a deliverable will not, by itself, constitute acceptance.**
- **Pricing: Phase 1 pricing will be fixed. Phase 2 will be fixed or capped as agreed at the approval gate. No price increase will apply without an authorised written change order.**
- **Expenses and Third-Party Costs: Only expenses and third-party costs expressly included in the contract or approved in writing before commitment will be payable.**
- **Taxes: Applicable taxes must be shown separately. Girl Effect will deduct withholding tax and other statutory amounts where required by law.**
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The bidder must protect Girl Effect’s confidential, personal and sensitive information and comply with applicable laws, contractual requirements and Girl Effect policies.
- **Safeguarding and Responsible AI: Appointment and continued deployment will be subject to Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical AI, safety and conduct requirements.**
- **Security: The bidder must comply with agreed security requirements, cooperate with security testing and remediation, and promptly report suspected incidents.**
- **Subcontracting and Subprocessors: No material subcontractor, model provider, hosting provider or subprocessor may be appointed, added or replaced without Girl Effect’s prior written approval.**
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Bidders must disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest, including relevant commercial relationships with proposed technology providers.
- **Tender Costs:** Girl Effect will not reimburse costs incurred in preparing, submitting, presenting or negotiating a proposal.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend, suspend or cancel the procurement; reject any or all proposals; award the full or partial scope; award in phases; or make no award.
- **No Commitment: Publication of this RFP does not commit Girl Effect to enter into a contract, reimburse proposal costs or activate Phase 2.**
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes submissions from qualified organisations that meet the stated regulatory, technical and service requirements.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.
