jobs.title: Operation Specialist - West Sudan
jobs.description:
**Location:** (Nyala / Zalingei) Darfur, Sudan

**Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt, Regular

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) ☐ **Level 3** X **Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

**About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [**here**](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption.

**The Program / Department / Team**

Prosper Global has been operational in Sudan since 2004 and currently has a country office in Khartoum and field offices in South Darfur, South Kordofan, North Kordofan and Gedaref states. We work with Sudanese communities to build resilient scalable solutions that interrupt the cycle of fragility and crisis due to conflict and climate change by improving food and water security, peace and governance and enabling economic opportunities in the agricultural sector.

**The Position**

Based in Darfur (Nyala / Zalingei) and reporting to the Operations Director, the Operations Specialist is expected to contribute to organizational strategic thinking, planning, and overall coordination efforts, in order to enable excellence in all operations functions across west region (Darfur and Kordofan). The Operations Specialist shall also oversee, both directly and indirectly, the procurement and logistics portfolio for the west, Darfur and Kordofan program, across multiple field offices and in different capacities. Working with in-country resources and with technical assistance from the Country Office and Global Procurement and Logistics units, he/she shall be a key actor in ensuring that the operations team has forward-thinking and innovative approach, with an eye toward creating plurality and innovation in the contracting of suppliers and service providers. The Operations Specialist will be hands-on and will feed directly into Prosper Globals’ best practices in procurement, logistics, facilities and office management functions, while seeking synergies across operational hubs and ensuring compliance in adherence to Prosper Global’s Global and country-specific policies and protocols.

**Essential Responsibilities**

STRATEGY AND PLANNING

- Successful contribution for implementation of country operations strategies and establishment of management guidelines.
- Advice on operations strategies, policies and plans affecting operations, program deliverables and staffing.
- Analyzing Prosper Global operating environment in the country and adjusting operations and providing advice on contextual changes.
- Mobilize support services and risk management resources to enable west-regional leadership teams to execute their respective strategic priorities.
- Lead the development and administration of regional level reports on key finance, operations and human resources indicators.
- Manage and administer regional operations budgets in coordination with west and country leadership.
- Lead on measurement and analysis of key performance indicators to inform strategic decision making.

SYSTEMS AND SUPPORT FUNCTIONS

- Manage reliable and cost-effective operations and effective implementation of the strategies of Prosper Global towards the right direction, including supervision of facilities & office management, information technology, procurement, asset management, fleet management and warehouse management.
- Supports the program team on timely provision of operations support at a higher level of standards.
- Provides management information for decision making as required.
- Support developing budgets for operations activities of country programs as an integral part of program proposal development and country level budgeting.
- Represents Prosper Global as required in coordination with country management (i.e. Local Logistics Cluster, NGO Working Groups, etc.). As a management team member, the operations specialist will have certain representation at the discretion of the operations director.
- Ensure that effective systems are in place in all west offices for the adequate management of human resources, financial and operational field support functions.
- Capture and disseminate best practices on operations, finance and HR systems across country teams to ensure highest quality and standards.

IMPLEMENTATION OF POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

Implementation of appropriate operations policies and procedures that comply with Prosper Global policies and procedures and with donor rules and regulations focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance of operations with Prosper Global Supply Chain Operations policies, procedures and processes.
- Maintain regular control on operations budget and identify any exceptions or possible implications of under / overspending in a timely manner.
- Promote continuous organizational learning culture with the empowerment of individuals and teams with the identification of learning needs. Create learning opportunities and ensure access to available learning resources.
- Ensure ongoing full compliance of Prosper Global finance policies and procedure and others (i.e. Program Management Manual, National Staff Handbook and etc.)
- Act as focal point from operations for all internal and external tasks in coordination with supervisor and country management.
- Development of local policies and procedures with the support of country management and implementation of them.

RESOURCE MANAGEMENT

Effective and efficient resources management in administration, procurement, logistics and IT on the achievement of the following results:

- Ensure effective management of administrative / logistics resources and reporting in a systematic, transparent and efficient manner to country management.
- Responsible for provision of high quality and timely procurement and other program support.
- Exercising oversight over procurement processes and logistics ensuring compliance with Prosper Global procurement policies and procedures as well donor rules and regulations.
- Oversee provision of transport and travel support (international and domestic).
- Oversight on maintenance of proper custody of Prosper Global assets, warehouse inventory and general inventory.
- Careful planning to optimally use logistics and admin resources for state and cross border movements and Chad transit.

TEAM MANAGEMENT

- Develop the capacity of the team, deepen understanding of their roles and assist with career development.
- Assist team members with information, tools and resources to improve performance & reach objectives.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations and provide constructive feedback informally and formally via regular one on one and performance reviews.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence.
- Hire – regular and short term, orient and lead team members as necessary.
- Work with all Prosper Global staff to ensure smooth introduction and adoption of operational systems.

SECURITY

- Ensure compliance with security procedures and policies as determined by country leadership.
- Proactively ensure that team members operate in a secure environment and are aware of policies.

HUMAN RESOURCES

- Support Prosper Global country and global initiatives for human resources, including safeguarding and talent development.
- Collaborate with the people team to promote staff access to high quality learning opportunities, with a special emphasis on national team member development.
- Assist with the on-boarding of operations team members, ensuring they are set up for success and familiar with agency systems, procedures, and protocols.

RISK MANAGEMENT

- Engage and support management to ensure that adequate risk management systems are in place.
- Collaborate with country leadership to support preparedness and response to major disruptive events.
- Engage with finance and operations teams on the internal audit process to track findings and ensure country team compliance with IA findings and recommendations.
- Engage with country level Ethics and Assurance leads to track and analyze trends and needs across countries.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

**Supervisory Responsibility**

Technically supervises all operations team members in west (Darfur and Kordofan) including operations officers, procurement officers, and admin officers.

**Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Operations Director

**Works Directly With:** Program teams, finance team, head of bases, Chad operations consultant and partner organizations in west and Chad.

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

**Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- BA/BS degree in a relevant field.
- Minimum of 5 years senior management experience in a corporate or INGO sector, including experience in operational support in emergency programs and fragile security context.
- Sound knowledge of administrative and logistics procedures is highly desired.
- Proven supervisory ability and/or technical skills combined with leadership.
- Strong interpersonal skills and ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues in a diversified multi-cultural and multi-ethnic working environment.
- Skills in managing, organizing, planning and implementing assigned tasks under pressure of frequent and tight schedules.
- Strong ability to apply good judgment and decision-making skills in difficult and complex working environments.
- Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills in handling management and coordination issues at country program level.
- Effective verbal and written communication, organizational, prioritization and Microsoft Office applications.
- Excellent oral and written English skills required; proficiency in Arabic is a plus.
- Ability to work effectively with an ethnically diverse team in a sensitive environment.

**Success Factors**

The successful Operations Specialist will be good at problem solving and have the ability to work out methods to deliver successful programs while demonstrating excellent stewardship of donor funds and compliance with Prosper Global and donor regulations. They will maintain strong cooperative relationships with other departments and interact effectively with international and national personnel both in a managerial as well as training capacity, while demonstrating the ability to multi-task, meet deadlines and process information in support of changing program activities. They will be able to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment and be willing to travel regularly to Prosper Global field offices and project sites. The most successful Prosper Global staff members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations.

**Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in West Sudan, covering Darfur and Kordofan regions and it requires up to 40% travel to support country programs, which includes travel between / to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are basic. Housing for this role is in shared housing and access to basic medical services and lengthy medical or emergency evacuation service.

**Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

**Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

**Safeguarding & Ethics**

Prosper Globalis committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

jobs.title: Advocacy and Policy Lead
jobs.description:
**Advocacy and Policy Lead**

**Permanent, Full Time**

**Location - Amman, Jordan**

**Salary - 58,000 Jordanian Dinars per year**

***If we receive a high volume of applications, we reserve the right to close the advert before the scheduled closing date. Therefore, we encourage interested applicants to apply at their earliest convenience.***

**About us**

Christian Aid exists to create a world where everyone can live a full life, free from poverty. We are a global movement of people, churches and local organisations who passionately champion dignity, equality and justice worldwide. We are the changemakers, the peacemakers, the mighty of heart.

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and recognise the value this brings in forming strong, creative and high performing teams. We welcome applications from all sections of the community, and from those with experience from outside of the voluntary sector. And no, you don’t have to be Christian to work here – we encourage people of all faiths and none to apply. We just ask that everyone lives out our values of dignity, equality, justice and love. We value a good work-life balance, so we’re open to part-time and flexible working. We also offer hybrid working for our office-based colleagues.

**About the role**

Reporting in to the Head of Impact for the Middle East Multi-Country Cluster (MCC), the **Advocacy and Policy Lead** provides strategic leadership and oversight of MCC policy and advocacy strategy, defining influencing priorities, and coordinates with other Advocacy leads to co-design thematic global advocacy strategies, ensuring alignment with organisational values and goals

The post-holder will collaborate with MCC Partnership and Strategy Lead , build a cohort of national and regional partnerships, including faith partnerships that strategically align and maximise impact. Provide technical support to partners for advocacy and connect partners to regional and global spaces to forefront their voices and drive meaningful change.

Some of the main areas of responsibility for the **Advocacy and Policy Lead** include:

- Drive and oversee the MCC advocacy strategy, collaborating with global advocacy colleagues to co-design thematic global advocacy strategies, so that they respond to partner voices and priorities and local contexts, aligning with organizational values and goals
- Contribute to global advocacy in global spaces, to ensure advocacy is impactful, and is in close collaboration with partners and faith groups and rooted in evidence and theological reflection and aligns with organizational values and goals
- Horizon scan and provide policy and advocacy insight to MCC Leadership and partners, including analysis of political and contextual developments and associated advocacy risks, fostering a team mindset and support a culture of knowledge sharing of ideas and insights.
- Collaborate with the MCC Partnership and Strategy Lead, build a cohort of national and regional partnerships, including faith partnerships, to ensure that there is an appropriate balance of partners working on short- and medium-term outcomes and systemic change to align with organisational values and goals.
- Act as a convenor of policy and advocacy spaces by supporting and strengthening national and regional advocacy platforms where partners, policymakers, and civil society actors can collaborate on shared priorities, fostering a mindset of connection.
- Provides technical support for advocacy planning, advocacy proposal development, evidence gathering, relationship building, integrating advocacy into programme design, and drawing on program evidence, humanitarian experience and partner perspectives to inform advocacy priorities including in designing multi-country advocacy strategies that are meaningful, streamlined and aligned.
- Act as an ambassador by representing Christian Aid and engage in regional and global spaces jointly with partners, collaborating with Policy and Advocacy Leads across other MCCs, as relevant, ensuring alignment with organisational values and goals.
- Identify evidence gaps and support partners to commission or produce policy/research/evidence work, including policy analysis, drafting policy briefs, position papers and evidence-based recommendations, connecting with relevant institutions to facilitate highly impactful and meaningful outcomes.
- Maintain up to date analysis of the country and regional context and bring evidence to the UK/global spaces.
- Act as the MCC communications focal point, coordinating with relevant organisational communications teams to ensure alignment with MCC priorities and contexts, and provide oversight or line management of dedicated MCC communications staff, where applicable.

**About you**

**Who we are looking for:**

**Essential:**

- Degree level qualification in a relevant field.
- Substantial experience in supporting national and regional organisations to develop an advocacy strategy, including integrating advocacy into programme work.
- Substantial experience of supporting and accompanying partners to navigate and influence on a global scale.
- Substantial experience of devising, leading and implementing advocacy strategies, preferably in another NGO or faith group.
- Substantial experience of networking, building alliances and coordinating initiatives in networks and faith groups.
- Substantial experience of peer-to-peer learning.
- Substantial experience of policy research and managing research projects.
- Substantial experience of public speaking to a variety of audiences, including the media.
- Substantial experience of budget management.
- Detailed understanding of the current policy debates, trends and analytical frameworks around key development issues.
- Detailed understanding of power and political analysis, and rights-based approaches.
- Detailed understanding of national and regional Civil Society and faith networks - their policy positions and dynamics.
- Understanding of how theology influences policy.
- Detailed understanding of national, regional and international institutions and processes.
- Highly developed verbal and written communications experience, especially the ability to communicate complex issues simply.
- Significant experience of political analysis and horizon scanning.
- Highly developed coaching and mentoring skills.
- Highly developed ability to work across cultural contexts with Civil Society and faith leaders in different countries.
- Highly developed ability to build lasting relationships with key networks, organisations and advocacy targets.
- Highly developed ability to negotiate with, influence and persuade others in a collaborative manner.
- Posts in Middle-east context: Fluency in both Arabic and English (written and spoken) is required.

**Further information**

*At Christian Aid we strive to be an inclusive and diverse employer and recognise the value that this brings in helping to build strong, creative and high performing teams.*

*We are actively encouraging racialised minorities, LGBTQ+, people with disabilities, returning parents or carers who are re-entering work after a career break, people with caring responsibilities, people from low socioeconomic backgrounds, women, and older workers to apply. This is because these groups are under-represented within our teams, especially at senior level, and we recognise and value the contributions members of these groups make to strong, creative and high performing teams.*

*We have a strong Christian ethos and we encourage applications from all faiths. Applicants will be expected to demonstrate an understanding of and sympathy with Christian Aid’s faith identity.*

*All successful candidates will require a DBS/police check appropriate to the role and location and a Counter Terrorism Sanction check as part of your clearance for commencing your role with us. We also participate in the* [***Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme***](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/)*. In line with this Scheme, we will request information as part of the referencing process from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.*

*This role requires applicants to have the right to live and work in the country where this position is based and undertake the role that you have been offered. If you are successful and we make you an offer for the role, we will be required to conduct a right to work check on your immigration status in the UK. We will contact you regarding the documentation you will need to provide to evidence this.*

jobs.title: Final Evaluation of BPPS2 Program in Bangladesh
jobs.description:
**About the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is a non-profit, autonomous regional organization, international in status and non-political in management, staffing, and operations, established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as an outreach center of the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), ADPC has grown and diversified its expertise across the social and physical sciences. ADPC is governed by its Charter, signed in 2005 by its nine Founding Members (Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Thailand), and has its seat in Thailand. Governed by its Board of Trustees, it supports sustainable solutions for disaster risk reduction across a broad range of specialist areas, with a wide range of professional expertise from atmospheric scientists to social scientists with experience across all levels of engagement required for effective Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC’s Strategy 2030 guides the organization in providing comprehensive risk reduction support to countries and communities in Asia and the Pacific, with various programs implemented under 15 Priority Areas of Action by three departments, namely Preparedness and Climate Action, Risk Analytics and Climate Services, and Risk Governance and Financing. The Strategy is operationalized through ADPC's Strategic Action Plan (SAP) 2026–2030, which sets out three strategic goals and nine Result Areas, tracked through an institutional Strategic Indicator Framework. In addition, ADPC integrates three cross-cutting enablers throughout all Priority Areas of Action: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Innovation, and Transboundary Cooperation. Through the SAP, ADPC supports countries in implementing the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the Paris Agreement, as well as regional frameworks. These activities are supported by proactive individual departments of Finance, Human Resources, and Administration. ADPC recognizes the importance of examining the linkages between disaster risk management, poverty reduction, gender equality, sustainability, rights-based approaches, climate change, and regional cooperation. For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net.

**About the Preparedness and Climate Action Department:**

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC advances ADPC Strategy 2030 by strengthening disaster preparedness, anticipatory action, emergency response, resilient recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. PCA supports governments, response organizations, volunteers, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, communities, and other actors in developing and operationalizing preparedness, response, recovery, and climate action frameworks, plans, systems, and capacities before, during, and after disasters. Its work contributes to the SAP 2026–2030 Priority Areas of Action on Preparedness and Anticipatory Actions, Effective Localization for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Health Risk Management, and Private Sector Engagement, in all which Bangladesh is a priority country. BPP is implemented by PCA as part of its portfolio of multi-stakeholder preparedness partnerships.

**Purpose and Objectives:**

ADPC is implementing the Phase 2 of the Bangladesh Preparedness Partnership (BPP) under the overall guidance of the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief (MoDMR), Bangladesh. BPP is an innovative partnership instrumental in supporting the government of Bangladesh in leading and operationalizing its flagship policy, the Standing Orders on Disaster (SOD) 2019, through a multi-stakeholder model. Phase 2 of BPP aspires to strengthen the multi-stakeholder partnership platform at the national and sub-national levels in Kurigram, Bagerhat, and Cox’s Bazar districts by building operational and technical capacities, research applications, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

In line with this, ADPC seeks a consultant to evaluate the ongoing Phase II of BPP, which is being implemented from September 2023 to March 2027. The Consultant will work with the program team to evaluate the program relative to its results framework.

The proposed evaluation is expected to assess how BPP, its processes, outputs, and outcomes have contributed to operationalizing the multi-sectoral partnership model at national and sub-national levels to prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters in Bangladesh. The evaluation will focus on key aspects related to the objectives of BPP, namely:

1. Strengthened inclusive BPP following the whole-of-society approach;
2. Institutionalized technical and operational capacity for disaster preparedness and response at the sub-national level; and
3. Enhanced knowledge sharing and joint research mechanisms to amplify and accelerate BPP implementation.

The learnings from the evaluation and the documentation will inform the BPP Phase III and shape similar projects in countries where ADPC is currently working and where there are synergies in scaling up activities.

The evaluation shall be guided by the six evaluation criteria developed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Network on Development Evaluation (EvalNet), namely relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability. It will adopt a mixed-methods and participatory approach, drawing on program documents and monitoring data, stakeholder consultations, key informant interviews, and field observations, including of simulation exercises or recent disaster response operations where feasible. The evaluation will also consider the progression from Phase 1 to Phase 2 of BPP, using available baseline and monitoring data to assess change over time. The evaluation/learning questions will be finalized in consultation with the BPP program team, and they shall include quantitative and qualitative aspects. Further, it is expected to document the impact of the program through three case studies using the collected data during the evaluation process.

In addition, the evaluation shall assess the strategic alignment and contribution of BPPS2 to the following frameworks, and the final report shall include a dedicated section on these findings:

- **ADPC Strategic Action Plan (SAP) 2026–2030:** the extent to which BPPS2 contributes to ADPC's three strategic goals, in particular Goal 2 (communities are aware of, prepared for, and able to respond to and recover from disasters effectively) and Goal 3 (a fair and prosperous future for all through inclusive disaster and climate risk governance systems); to the relevant Result Areas and Strategic Indicators, notably the policy and institutional environment, local actors' influence, capacity strengthening, multistakeholder engagement for a whole-of-society approach, marginalized groups' influence, and partnerships; to the most relevant Priority Areas of Action, notably Preparedness and Anticipatory Actions, Effective Localization for Resilience, and Private Sector Engagement; and to the cross-cutting enablers of GESI, Innovation, and Transboundary Cooperation. Findings should be framed to inform the SAP mid-term review in 2028, and endline values for the relevant SAP strategic outcome indicators should be reported using ADPC's standardized M&E tools.
- **Gates Foundation:** the extent to which BPPS2 contributes, directly or through plausible pathways, to the Foundation's three goals for 2045 (that no mother, child, or baby dies of a preventable cause; that the next generation grows up in a world free of deadly infectious diseases; and that hundreds of millions of people break free from poverty), and to its Emergency Response strategy. The latter includes strengthening the capacity of local, national, and regional emergency responders and institutions; supporting locally led preparedness planning and public health emergency response capacity; fostering peer learning and innovation; and shifting from reactive response towards proactive preparedness and resilience.

Additionally, indicative evaluation questions include:

- **Relevance:** To what extent have BPPS2's objectives and activities responded to the priorities of MoDMR and the disaster management committees in Kurigram, Bagerhat, and Cox's Bazar, and to the needs of women, persons with disabilities, and other at-risk groups?
- **Coherence:** How well has BPPS2 aligned with and complemented the SOD 2019, national disaster management plans, and other preparedness initiatives of government, humanitarian, and development actors, while avoiding duplication?
- **Effectiveness:** To what extent has BPPS2 achieved its three objectives, and how effectively has the multi-stakeholder partnership model, bringing together government, the private sector, humanitarian and civil society actors, and academia, functioned at national and sub-national levels?
- **Effectiveness:** How have the technical and operational capacities built under BPPS2 been applied in actual preparedness and response, for example during recent cyclones, floods, or other events in the target districts?
- **Effectiveness:** To what extent have the joint research and knowledge-sharing mechanisms generated evidence that partners have used to inform policy, planning, or practice?
- **Efficiency:** How efficiently have resources, time, and partnership arrangements been used to deliver results, and what factors have affected timeliness and value for money?
- **Impact:** What intended and unintended changes, positive or negative, can be plausibly linked to BPPS2 in the speed, coordination, and inclusiveness of disaster preparedness and response?
- **Sustainability:** To what extent have BPPS2 mechanisms, tools, and capacities been institutionalized in government systems, plans, and budgets, and how likely are the partnership platforms to continue after March 2027 without external support?
- **Cross-cutting:** How effectively has BPPS2 integrated GESI, applied innovative approaches, and contributed to regional and South-South learning, including through the Asian Preparedness Partnership (APP) where relevant?
- **Strategic alignment (ADPC):** How and to what extent has BPPS2 contributed to the SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas, particularly multistakeholder engagement, local actors' and marginalized groups' influence, and partnerships, and what does this imply for ADPC's preparedness and localization programming?
- **Strategic alignment (Gates Foundation):** Through what pathways has BPPS2 contributed to the Gates Foundation's 2045 goals and Emergency Response strategy, for example by strengthening responder capacity, protecting women, children, and other vulnerable groups in emergencies, supporting health emergency preparedness, or reducing disaster-related livelihood losses, and how strong is the evidence for each pathway?
- **Learning:** What lessons and good practices should inform the design of BPP Phase III and the replication of the model in other countries where ADPC works?

**Expected Outputs:**

The Consultant is expected to deliver the below outputs / deliverables within the given timelines.

**Key Deliverables and Timeline**

**Deliverable 1 :** Inception report, including an outline of the evaluation report with a defined methodology, work plan, and sampling approach including key learning questions / questionnaires for data collection and an evaluation matrix linking them to the OECD criteria, the BPP objectives, the SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas, and the Gates Foundation goals and Emergency Response strategy, in consultation with the project team. It should also include the template to be used in developing the case studies.

**Timeline:** December 2026

**Deliverable 2 :** First draft of the evaluation report along with the first draft of the three case studies that highlight the impact of the program.

**Timeline:** February 2027

**Deliverable 3 :** Validation workshop with ADPC program team and key BPP stakeholders.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Deliverable 4 :** Final copies of the three case studies.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Deliverable 5 :** Final copy of the evaluation report, with methodology, findings, conclusions, recommendations, and supporting annexes (including endline values for the relevant SAP strategic indicators, and anonymized datasets and data collection tools), along with a presentation deck summarizing the key findings and recommendations.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

The consultant is expected to assess and document the processes, mechanisms, and practices related to the implementation of the BPP program using secondary data and primary data from Bangladesh. Therefore, it is proposed for the consultant to use the following methods to carry out the documentation and provide the analysis:

- Desk study to review all BPP-related documents, including program framework, progress reports, knowledge products, and meeting minutes, as well as the ADPC Strategy 2030, the SAP 2026–2030, and relevant Gates Foundation strategy documents;
- In-depth interviews and focus group discussions with key stakeholders and beneficiaries using structured questionnaires and guides;
- Interviews with key informants (who will be identified in consultation with the project team and BPP partner agencies); and
- Observations through field visits to project sites as possible and necessary.

Found below is a list of specific tasks expected from the consultant:

- Design and finalize the evaluation methodology, and work plan, in consultation with the ADPC project team;
- Conduct desk research reviewing the BPP Phase 1 and Phase 2 program documents and available monitoring evidence;
- Collect primary data through interviews and discussions;
- Conduct field visits/observations in the target communities based on the work plan and the agreed methodology;
- Analyze the gathered information and summarize the findings, including program performance, institutionalization and sustainability, and contribution to the SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas and the Gates Foundation goals and Emergency Response strategy;
- Compare available evidence across BPP phases and target districts, and explain differences in progress;
- Draft the evaluation report and the three case studies;
- Conduct a validation workshop with ADPC program team and relevant BPP partners; and
- Finalize the evaluation report and the three case studies.

**Working Principles:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities indicated above, the Consultant will be
supervised by the Program Manager from ADPC under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Climate Actions and Impact of the Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC. The Consultant will work closely with other program team members, as applicable. ADPC will review the inception report, draft deliverables, and final outputs, and ADPC and BPP partner agencies will facilitate access to relevant documents, stakeholders, and project sites.

**Participation and independence:**

The evaluation will encourage the participation of government, partner, and community stakeholders in assessing progress and validating findings. The consultant must ensure that participation is voluntary, inclusive, and based on informed consent; that data are disaggregated by sex, age, and disability where feasible; and that confidentiality, do-no-harm, and safeguarding standards are upheld, while maintaining independence in the analysis, findings, and recommendations.

**General requirements:**

The consultant must operate within all ADPC guidelines, procedures, and policies and within the specific program needs.

**Qualifications:**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

- Master’s degree in the field of Community Development, Social Work, Social Sciences, Disaster Management, Program Evaluation, or any other related field.
- At least 10 years of work experience in development work, with at least 5
years in research, monitoring, and evaluation.
- Demonstrated experience with mixed-methods evaluation and community-based or participatory assessment approaches.
- Proven technical specialization in research and evaluation, including theory-based or contribution analysis approaches.
- Good understanding of disaster preparedness and response systems in Bangladesh, including the SOD 2019, and of multi-stakeholder partnerships involving government, the private sector, and humanitarian actors.
- Excellent command of English, both written and spoken.
- Excellent technical writing skills in English.

***Preferred Qualifications***

- Self-motivated, proactive, and takes initiative.
- Demonstrated ability to plan and organize work and time independently.
- Familiarity with Bangla for field consultations.
- Prior evaluation or program experience in Bangladesh.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, team-oriented work style,
and experience working in a multi-cultural environment.
- Strong networking capacity and understanding of humanitarian and
development nexus at local and regional levels.
- Strong desire to learn, undertake new challenges, work hard, and be a creative
problem-solver.
- With self-confidence and good sense of humor, but serious about the quality
and excellence of work.

**Duty Station:** Home-based, with travel to Bangladesh

**Duration:** December 2026 to March 2027
