jobs.title: Communications Associate
jobs.description:
**About the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes, with the vision of creating safer communities and fostering sustainable development through strengthened disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. Since its establishment in 1986 as a regional technical capacity-building center, ADPC has evolved into a leading regional organization supporting countries to reduce disaster and climate risks through evidence-based, innovative, and inclusive approaches.

ADPC delivers a wide range of programs across its strategic **priority areas**, including:

- Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics
- Policy and Institutional Systems
- Effective Localization for Resilience
- Climate Services
- Resilient Planning and Implementation
- Preparedness and Anticipatory Action
- Nature-based Solutions
- Financing for Resilience
- Resilient Recovery
- Food and Water Security
- Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance
- Health Risk Management
- Urban and Infrastructure Resilience
- Private Sector Engagement
- ADPC Knowledge Academy

These priority areas are reinforced by ADPC’s **cross-cutting themes**, which are embedded across all programs and operations:

- Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)
- Disaster and Climate Innovations
- Regional and Transboundary Cooperation

ADPC supports countries in implementing global frameworks including the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030**, the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, the **Paris Agreement/UNFCCC**, and the **New Urban Agenda**, while contributing to national and regional policy advancement on resilience. Through multi-sectoral partnerships, technical advisory services, capacity development, and program implementation across multiple countries, ADPC works to strengthen systems, institutions, and communities to better manage disaster and climate risks.

**For additional details, please visit:** http://www.adpc.net/

**Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Actions Department enhances the preparedness and climate action capacities of governments, NGOs, the private sector, and communities. It focuses on:

- Ensuring frameworks and implementation plans for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery are in place before disaster strikes.
- Strengthening institutional and community capacities for anticipatory action and resilient recovery.

Promoting **locally led DRR and climate resilience interventions** through multi-stakeholder partnerships.

**Purpose and Objectives:**

ADPC is implementing Phase III of the Asian Preparedness Partnership (APP), a multi-stakeholder localization platform launched in 2016 in response to the World Humanitarian Summit's call to shift power to national and local actors in disaster preparedness and response. APP Phase III is aligned with ADPC Strategy 2030, which identifies localization as a priority area of action for strengthening disaster risk reduction, preparedness, response, recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. APP has been supported by the Gates Foundation since its inception.

APP operates in seven countries: Cambodia, Lao PDR, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka. Through National Preparedness Partnerships (NPPs), APP brings together governments, civil society organizations, the private sector, and other stakeholders to strengthen nationally owned and locally led disaster preparedness. Phase III focuses on strengthening the sustainability of these partnerships, advancing localization models based on interventions supported through the Asian Disaster Readiness Fund (ADRF), and promoting regional knowledge exchange and cooperation.

As APP Phase III enters its final implementation effective communications, documentation, and knowledge dissemination will be essential to demonstrate results, and ensure the accessibility of knowledge resources beyond the program duration.

To support these requirements, ADPC seeks to engage a Communications Associate (Consultant) to provide continued support in developing and disseminating communication materials, maintaining digital communication platforms, documenting program achievements, and facilitating knowledge sharing across participating countries.

The Consultant will support the development of digital content, highlighting APP's contributions to locally led disaster preparedness.

**Expected Outputs:**

The Consultant is expected to contribute to the following outputs throughout the assignment:

1. **Program communication and multimedia products:** News articles, newsletters, success stories, human-interest stories, testimonials, activity updates, photographs, videos, interviews, photo stories, infographics, and other visual and digital materials.
2. **Updated website and social media content:** Regular updates to the ADPC / APP website and social media channels featuring program news, activities, publications, relevant resources, and communication products.
3. **Event communication and visibility materials:** Materials supporting national and regional events, workshops, webinars, policy dialogues, and partnership meetings.
4. **Knowledge dissemination, legacy, and close-out materials:** Promotional and dissemination materials for the *Ten Years of APP* publication and other program knowledge products, alongside legacy and close-out communications showcasing key achievements, good practices, and partnership sustainability.
5. **Organized communication archive for handover:** An updated archive of APP communication materials, multimedia resources, published content, and digital assets.
6. **Monthly communication progress summaries:** Summaries covering website updates, published materials, social media activities, and dissemination efforts.

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

The Consultant will provide communications and visibility support to APP Phase III, promoting program activities, achievements, and results through digital platforms, publications, multimedia products, and stakeholder outreach, including during final implementation and program closure.

**a. Program Communications and Content Development**

- Develop, edit, and disseminate news articles, newsletters, success stories, human-interest stories, case studies, testimonials, and other communication materials.
- Highlight locally led disaster preparedness, localization models, National Preparedness Partnerships (NPPs), ADRF-supported initiatives, and emerging good practices.
- Collect photographs, videos, interviews, and other inputs from program teams and partners, and support the production of multimedia products.
- Ensure consistent messaging, branding, and compliance with donor visibility requirements.

**b. Website, Social Media, and Digital Communications**

- Maintain and update the APP website with program news, events, publications, stories, and resources.
- Develop and publish content for APP and ADPC social media channels, coordinating timely dissemination across digital platforms.
- Support basic design and formatting of infographics, banners, presentations, and promotional materials.
- Monitor website and social media engagement and maintain records of published content.

**c. Event Communications and Stakeholder Outreach**

- Support communications for national and regional events, workshops, webinars, policy dialogues, and knowledge-sharing activities.
- Prepare event announcements, promotional and presentation materials, event coverage, and post-event summaries.
- Coordinate with program teams and the ADPC Communications Team to share event outcomes and strengthen stakeholder outreach.

**d. Knowledge Dissemination and Program Close-out**

- Promote the *Ten Years of APP* publication and other knowledge products developed by the Knowledge Management Specialist.
- Prepare legacy and final communication materials showcasing program achievements, good practices, and partnership sustainability.
- Update and consolidate website content and organize communication products and multimedia assets for archiving and program handover.

**e. Coordination and Reporting**

- Coordinate communication activities and inputs with APP program teams, NPPs, grantees, partners, and the ADPC Communications Team.
- Provide monthly progress summaries covering communication outputs, dissemination, outreach, and digital engagement.
- Prepare communication inputs for program reports, presentations, and management briefings.
- Undertake other communications and visibility tasks assigned by the supervisor in line with program priorities.

*This job description covers the general responsibilities and representative tasks of this position. Other tasks may be assigned as necessary according to program priorities and needs.*

**Working Principles:**

The Consultant will report to the Unit Head, Climate Action and Impact.

The Consultant will work closely with the APP Program Team and Communications Officer at ADPC, other Project/Program Managers, Specialists, and Coordinators across participating countries, as necessary.

**Qualifications:**

**Required Qualifications and Specifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Communications, Journalism, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Information Management, or other related disciplines.
- At least six months of relevant professional experience in program communications, knowledge management, digital content development, or documentation.
- Experience in preparing communication materials, success stories, news articles, publications, and knowledge products.
- Familiarity with website content management, social media platforms, and digital communication tools.
- Excellent English language skills, both oral and written, with strong editing and proofreading abilities.
- Demonstrated ability to synthesize program information into clear and accessible communication materials.
- Familiarity with development program, disaster risk reduction, or climate resilience would be an advantage.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with experience working in multicultural environments.
- Experience with basic graphic design, multimedia documentation, and digital content management tools.
- Proactive, self-motivated, and able to work independently and collaboratively.
- Familiarity with government agencies, NGOs, international organizations, and multi-stakeholder partnerships.

**Duty Station:** Bangkok, Thailand.

**Duration:** This is a time-based consultancy from January 2027 – July 2027 (Seven months).

**Itinerary:**

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local and international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs in accordance with ADPC financial policy.

Reimbursement of general and administrative expenses related to program implementation will be subject to prior approval by the respective supervisor identified below.

jobs.title: Director of Impact & Influence
jobs.description:
**As a Member of the Senior Management Team**

- Contribute to the overall leadership, management and strategic direction of the Country Office, sharing collective accountability for organizational performance, culture, sustainability and results for children.
- Champion “Children First” commitment , placing children's rights, “best interests of the child” at the heart of organizational decisions, and ensuring their voices and meaningful, safe and inclusive participation inform planning, decision-making and performance management at project, programme and organizational levels.
- Contribute to the development, implementation and monitoring of the Country Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment between strategic priorities, programme portfolios, partnerships, influencing objectives and resource allocation.
- Ensure organizational strategies, decisions and operating approaches are grounded in humanitarian principles, conflict sensitivity and Do No Harm, considering potential impacts on children, communities, partners, staff and conflict dynamics.
- Share responsibility for organizational planning, budgeting, financial sustainability, workforce planning and effective resource allocation, ensuring responsible stewardship of resources.
- Drive organizational performance and continuous improvement through collective ownership of Country Office KPIs, improvement plans and risk management priorities.
- Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, collaboration, innovation and learning, strengthening cross-functional coordination, inclusive leadership and staff wellbeing.
- Support organizational transformation and fit-for-purpose structures, ensuring the Country Office remains adaptable and responsive to evolving humanitarian, operational and funding environments.
- Share collective responsibility for safeguarding, staff safety, compliance, organizational risk management and business continuity, ensuring appropriate oversight and accountability.
- Build strategic relationships with donors, partners, civil society, UN agencies and Save the Children Members, while contributing to regional and global engagement, collaboration and organizational learning.

**Country Strategic Planning and Organizational Performance**

- Lead the development, implementation and periodic review of the Country Strategic Plan including the Humanitarian plan, ensuring alignment with global priorities, country context and organizational ambitions.
- Provide strategic leadership to country planning processes, ensuring alignment between programme priorities, partnerships, resource investments and organizational goals.
- Oversee organizational performance against strategic objectives, KPIs and key commitments, ensuring decisions are informed by evidence, learning and emerging trends.
- Advise the Country Director and SMT on strategic opportunities, risks and organizational positioning to maximize impact for children.
- Foster a culture of strategic thinking, accountability, adaptive management and continuous improvement across the Country Office.

**Impact and Portfolio Leadership**

- Lead the Country Office Impact Model, ensuring coherence between programming, evidence generation, partnerships and resource mobilization.
- Drive a portfolio approach that maximizes impact, sustainability and value for money across humanitarian and development investments.
- Ensure strategic alignment between the Country Strategic Plan, programme portfolio, influence agenda, partnership strategy and funding priorities.
- Champion evidence-based decision-making, innovation and adaptive management across the organization.
- Provide oversight of strategic risks related to programme quality, impact, influence and organizational reputation.

**Strategic Programme Development and Growth**

- Lead the Country Office programme growth agenda, ensuring strategic investments and funding opportunities advance organizational priorities and impact ambitions.
- Oversee the design of high-value, multi-sector and innovative programmes that deliver sustainable outcomes for children.
- Provide executive leadership for major funding opportunities, donor engagement and strategic partnerships.
- Ensure programme development is informed by evidence, contextual analysis, organizational learning and child rights priorities.
- Promote innovation, integration and systems-focused approaches across programme design and business development.

**Strategic Partnerships and External Engagement**

- Develop and maintain strategic partnerships that strengthen Save the Children's impact, influence agenda for advancing breakthroughs for children and child rights.
- Represent Save the Children in senior-level external forums, strategic partnerships and policy discussions.
- Position Save the Children as a trusted partner and thought leader through technical excellence, evidence and influence
- Identify and advance partnership opportunities that drive innovation, systems change and resource mobilization.

**Programme Quality and Technical Leadership**

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight to ensure high-quality, impactful and evidence-based programming across all thematic areas.
- Ensure programme design, implementation and evaluation are aligned with Save the Children's quality standards, common approaches, global frameworks and organizational priorities.
- Lead the development and promotion of integrated, child-centred and context-responsive programming that maximizes outcomes for children and communities.
- Foster a culture of technical excellence, innovation, learning and continuous improvement across the programme portfolio.
- Strengthen technical leadership and capabilities to ensure effective support for programme delivery, policy influence, resource mobilization and organizational growth.
- Champion conflict-sensitive, protection mainstreaming and risk-informed approaches across all programmes, ensuring humanitarian principles and child safeguarding considerations are systematically embedded throughout the programme cycle.
- Promote cross-sector collaboration, learning and knowledge sharing to enhance programme quality, scale, sustainability and impact.

**Research, Evaluation, Accountability, Learning and Knowledge Management (REALM)**

- Provide strategic oversight of monitoring, evaluation, research, accountability and learning across the Country Office.
- Ensure robust systems are in place to generate evidence, measure impact and support organizational learning.
- Promote the use of data, research and learning to inform strategic decision-making and programme improvement.
- Strengthen accountability to children, communities and partners across the programme portfolio.
- Ensure evidence and learning are effectively communicated and leveraged to influence policy, practice and programme quality.

**Influencing- Advocacy, Campaigns, Communications and Media (ACCM)**

- Lead the Country Office's advocacy, influence and communications agenda in support of the Country Strategic Plan.
- Ensure advocacy priorities are grounded in programme evidence, child rights analysis and organizational objectives.
- Position Save the Children as a leading and credible voice on children's rights and humanitarian issues.
- Strengthen strategic engagement with decision-makers, partners and influencers to advance policy and practice change.
- Oversee the use of communications, campaigns and evidence to amplify impact and influence outcomes.

**Staff Leadership, Management and Development**

- Provide leadership and direction to functional team under the role.
- Build and sustain a high-performing, diverse and collaborative leadership team.
- Drive workforce planning, succession planning and talent development across functions under the role.
- Foster a culture of accountability, learning, innovation and wellbeing.
- Ensure teams are equipped with the capabilities, structures and resources required to deliver strategic objectives

jobs.title: Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Development and Livelihoods)
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, proudly supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are renowned for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME) Division** is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the 165 plus staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Development and Livelihoods)** will provide practical exposure to planning, procurement, fabrication, deployment, monitoring, and reporting of national Fish Aggregating Device (FAD) programmes. The role supports SPC technical teams, National fisheries officers, and community partners while developing the skills in fisheries development and livelihoods operations, data management, field surveys, and stakeholder engagement.

**The key responsibilities of the role include the following:**

**FAD Programme Orientation, Induction and Assessment.**

- Reviewing FAD national policies, deployment records, and safety operations protocols.
- Supporting coordination of introductory meetings with national FAD, fisheries development offices and partners.
- Assisting with national FAD audits.
- Supporting inventory checks of FAD, sea safety and post-harvest materials and equipment.
- Contributing to national FAD programme diagnostic summaries and gap identification.
- Strengthen national capacity in the understanding and use of the Regional FAD registry.
- Support catch, effort data collection and biological sampling.

**FAD field surveys, fabrication, deployment, preparation and operations.**

- Support site identification, mapping, and survey planning.
- Participating in FAD programme consultations, field surveys and data collection.
- Assist with procurement preparation, logistics and FAD construction deployment, maintenance operations and documentation.
- Assist with the planning and implementation of national FAD annual work plans.

**Support training and/or train-the-trainer in safe nearshore fishing techniques, the use of boat safety equipment and post-harvest activities.**

- Providing technical advice and hands-on training in FAD fishing techniques, ensuring the integration of traditional knowledge.
- Assist national sea safety authorities (e.g. Maritime Authority) to procure sea safety equipment and in providing training to fishing communities in the use of sea safety equipment.
- Assist in providing inputs to efforts to improve sea safety for small-scale fishers.
- Assist and support training efforts in fish hygiene, onboard fish handling, post-harvest methods including cold storage.

**Monitoring, Reporting, Project management.**

- Participating in induction meetings with national and regional fisheries teams.
- Assist in the preparation of Regional Tuna Project quarterly and annual reports.
- Support training workshops and awareness activities.
- Produce reports for all activities undertaken in the appropriate format for the activity, including training, technical and trip reports.
- Maintain up to date corporate and administrative procedures records for all activities undertaken.
- Acquit any cash advances for fieldwork and training activities, with receipts to justify all expenses.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Pacific Islands**

- Only applicants from Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply.
- Applicants must be employed in a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment department or a recognised NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Qualifications**

- A recognised degree in fisheries, marine science, biology, or related fields or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least two years’ direct relevant experience in PICT FAD programme (procurement, fabrication, deployment, maintenance, monitoring).
- Interest in coastal fisheries, community engagement, or marine resource management.
- Understanding of current Pacific Island regional coastal fisheries Development or management, and experience of working with gender issues relating to fisheries
- PC based computer skills (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook)

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written) in English

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in a team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and communicate with people from various ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries, sometimes under difficult physical conditions.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Requirements:** Only applicants who are nationals and residents of Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply. Applicants must be employed in or contracted by a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment agency, or a recognized NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Letter of endorsement –** A signed letter from the employer, stating they agree to release the applicant for the attachment and that the position will be held for the applicant to return to at the end of the attachment with SPC must be provided before an appointment can be finalized.

**Contract duration –** This appointment will last for a duration of 364 days and will not be renewable.

**Remuneration –** The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Development and Livelihoods)** is a Band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a salary of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,038 per month, which currently converts to approximately XPF 438,381 (USD 4,071; EUR 3,674). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea –** SPC provides housing support in Noumea and an establishment grant, return airfare, and will reimburse excess accompanied luggage of up to two additional bags. Employees are entitled to: 25 days annual leave and 30 days sick leave per annum; medical and life insurance; and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

We encourage all eligible candidates to apply but please note that as this is a special short-term contract, the full list of benefits included in other international contract types are not available. Appointees may bring their families, but all extra costs for travel, insurance, education, housing and other additional expenses will be their own responsibility.

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Earth Observation Science Specialist
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Climate Change and Sustainability division (CCS)** strengthens and streamlines SPC’s actions on climate change by bringing together work already undertaken by the organisation under a coherent strategic and technical leadership. In addition, it leads the actions of SPC on climate change and sustainability, works with SPC’s regional and international partners and promotes the integration of these issues into all development activities conducted by its divisions.

The **Earth Observation Science Specialist** will provide scientific leadership for the design and operationalisation of decision-ready products derived from satellite imagery, analysis-ready data, in-situ observations and other geospatial datasets. It develops and validates fit-for-Pacific methodologies, algorithms and analytical workflows across climate, disasters, oceans, agriculture, land, environment and infrastructure applications.

**The key responsibilities of the role include the following:**

**Product Portfolio Management**

- Provide scientific and technical advice to hold together the Digital Earth Pacific product portfolio, including product priorities, standards, quality expectations and user value.
- Guide the development, maintenance and continuous improvement of decision-ready products and services that respond to Pacific country, regional and SPC priorities.
- Ensure product design is informed by user needs, operational feasibility, data availability, scientific robustness and alignment with the Digital Earth Pacific technical roadmap.
- Coordinate with platform, data, science and programme teams to ensure products move from concept to operational service in a coherent and sustainable way.

**Research, Development and Quality Assurance**

- Undertake hands-on applied research to develop, test and improve Earth observation and geospatial methods, workflows and algorithms for Digital Earth Pacific products.
- Develop reproducible workflows using analysis-ready data, satellite imagery, in-situ data and relevant geospatial datasets, including calibration, validation, feature extraction and spatial analysis.
- Provide scientific quality assurance for products, workflows, datasets and documentation to ensure they are technically robust, transparent and fit for Pacific contexts.
- Prepare and contribute to peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, product documentation and scientific communication products based on Digital Earth Pacific outputs.
- Maintain awareness of emerging EO missions, datasets, methods and technologies and translate relevant advances into practical product improvements.

**Cross-sector Applications**

- Collaborate across SPC divisions and sectors to identify thematic applications for Digital Earth Pacific products, including climate, disasters, agriculture, oceans, land, environment, statistics and infrastructure.
- Work with sector specialists to translate science and platform capabilities into practical information products, services and use cases.
- Support integration of Digital Earth Pacific products into SPC programmes, regional initiatives and country-facing technical assistance.
- Provide scientific advice on data, sensors, methods and limitations to strengthen sector use of EO and geospatial products.

**Capacity Building and Data Ecosystem Development**

- Design and deliver training, mentoring, guidance materials and demonstrations that build the capability of SPC staff, regional partners and member countries to use Digital Earth Pacific products and services.
- Support capacity development that strengthens a regional data ecosystem, including data access, data stewardship, reproducible workflows, product interpretation and responsible use of EO and geospatial information.
- Develop communities of practice and knowledge-sharing approaches that connect country users, SPC sectors, regional organizations, universities and technical partners.
- Translate complex EO and geospatial methods into accessible learning products for technical and non-technical users.

**Project Delivery and People Management**

- Provide technical oversight and coordination to deliver EO and geospatial project outputs, country-requested products, analytical support and scientific deliverables on time and to agreed standards.
- Contribute to work planning, monitoring, reporting, proposal development, resource mobilisation and technical roadmaps for Digital Earth Pacific and Earth and Ocean Observations.
- Manage, supervise, mentor and support direct reports and technical staff as required, including performance planning, delegation, coaching and professional development.
- Support recruitment, onboarding and task coordination for technical staff, consultants and collaborators contributing to Digital Earth Pacific product and science delivery.
- Promote a collaborative, high-performing and inclusive team culture aligned with SPC values and programme delivery needs.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Postgraduate qualifications in remote sensing, geospatial science, environmental science, geography, climate science, oceanography, agriculture, ecology or related discipline, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 10 years’ experience in applied Earth observation, remote sensing, geospatial science, product development or operational geospatial services.
- At least 2 years’ experience managing people including mentoring, developing training, and performance management.
- Demonstrated experience developing, testing and documenting EO/geospatial methods, workflows, algorithms and decision-ready products.
- Strong experience in scientific quality assurance, validation, reproducibility, metadata and documentation for EO/geospatial datasets and products.
- Demonstrated ability to produce scientific outputs, including peer-reviewed publications, technical reports, product documentation, tools or information products.
- Strong proficiency in Python or another relevant data science programming language, with experience processing large EO/geospatial datasets.
- Experience using cloud-based or scalable EO/geospatial platforms and tools such as Open Data Cube, Google Earth Engine, Digital Earth platforms, STAC-based catalogues or equivalent.
- Experience working across thematic or sector applications such as climate, disasters, agriculture, oceans, land, environment, statistics or infrastructure.
- Experience designing and delivering training, mentoring, technical guidance or user support that strengthens EO/geospatial capability and data ecosystems.
- Experience coordinating technical work, mentoring staff, supervising consultants or supporting multidisciplinary teams.

**Language skills**

- Fluent in English

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Knowledge of Pacific Island countries and territories is an advantage

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This vacant position is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on performance and funding.

**Remuneration –** The **Earth Observation Science Specialist** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale.

*For a Noumea based position* – a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 4,397-5,400 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 634,433-779,190 (USD 5,892-7,236; EUR 5,317-6,530). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

*For a Suva based position* – a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea or Suva** – SPC provides a housing allowance (or subsidised housing in Noumea). Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Deputy Team Leader
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

***Please note this is an evergreen position.** We accept applications on an ongoing basis to build a talent pipeline for roles that open regularly. Because this posting may not reflect a current opening, we may not contact every applicant. If your background aligns with an open need, our team will reach out. We also encourage you to visit our careers page to explore other opportunities.*

**BACKGROUND:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

The IRC responds to people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives. Our work gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, conflict sensitivity, coordination, and impact.The International Rescue Committee (IRC) have been working in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, the IRC has more than 2,200 staff working across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, and Yemen to support those affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

The IRC Yemen began its programs in October 2012. Since establishing its presence in the South of Yemen, in the Red Sea Coastal city of Aden, following the war which broke out in Yemen in March of 2015 and the humanitarian disaster, which followed, IRC launched an emergency response program. IRC works in Yemen to support conflict-affected and displaced communities, with programmes in Health, Nutrition, Protection (including Women’s Protection and Empowerment and Child Protection),emergency preparedness and response Mechanisms and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). IRC Yemen currently implements the FCDO-funded RISE Consortium (a health and protection programme) in southern Yemen together with national partner organizations.

**Background and Objectives of YHC**

Yemen continues to face one of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, driven by years of conflict, economic disruption and the degradation of public services. Maternal mortality stands at 183 per 100,000 live births and under-five mortality at 61.9 per 1,000. Food security and basic needs are the top priority for 80% of households; 96% of households are food insecure, and 47% report insufficient water to meet their daily needs. Intimate partner and household-based gender-based violence predominates, while services are constrained by a severe shortage of female caseworkers and fragmented referral pathways.

The Yemen Humanitarian Capacity programme is an anticipated FCDO-funded, three-year programme expected to succeed the current RISE programme. YHC is designed to deliver lifesaving, integrated health, nutrition, and protection services across Yemen.

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Deputy Team Leader is responsible for the technical quality of YHC’s integrated health, nutrition and protection services. The Deputy Team Leader provides strategic technical leadership and operational oversight for the YHC programme. Reporting to the Team Leader, this role ensures the technical quality, and coherence of programme delivery across all sectors. It also ensures effective coordination with key stakeholders. The post-holder will deputise for the Team Leader as required and serve as a senior relationship manager with FCDO, consortium partners, and national and local counterparts.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Technical Leadership and Programme Quality**

- Provide overarching technical direction across YHC’s integrated health, nutrition and protection portfolio (and any other sectors in the final scope), ensuring alignment with FCDO requirements, Sphere Standards, the Core Humanitarian Standard and IRC quality standards.
- Lead the development and regular update of annual and costed workplans jointly with consortium partners and track the delivery of outputs against them.
- Oversee context-adaptive implementation, ensuring evidence-based adjustments and a resilient delivery model that can respond to access constraints.

**2. Partnerships and Localisation**

- Lead technical support and capacity strengthening for consortium and national partners within IRC’s localisation framework, including embedding technical expertise within partner organisations.

**3. Value for Money (VfM)**

- Embed VfM across programme planning, implementation, and reporting.

**4. Financial, Compliance and Administrative Oversight**

- Work closely with Finance and Consortium partners to monitor burn rates, flag underspends or overspends, and initiate timely budget revisions and realignments where required.
- Ensure all procurement, sub-grant management, and operational processes adhere to IRC and FCDO compliance standards, including anti-fraud, anti-corruption, and conflict-of-interest policies.
- Support the Team Leader in managing partner due diligence, risk management, remote supervision and monitoring arrangements across all areas of implementation.
- Oversee the timely preparation and submission of financial reports to FCDO, ensuring accuracy and coherence with narrative reports.
- Coordinate with internal audit and compliance teams to ensure appropriate risk management and audit readiness throughout the programme cycle.

**5. Donor Relations and Representation**

- Lead the preparation of high-quality, timely FCDO narrative and financial reports, Annual Reviews, and ad hoc donor communications, ensuring accuracy, coherence, and strategic framing of results.
- Represent IRC and YHC in coordination forums, including the Health, Nutrition and Protection clusters, NGO coordination platforms, and donor and technical working groups.
- Represent YHC at national and international meetings and conferences, including presenting programme results and learning.
- Support the Team Leader in preparing for FCDO programme reviews, Annual Review processes, and any mid-term or end-of-programme evaluations, including development of required documentation and evidence packages.
- Proactively communicate programme risks, mitigation measures, and adaptive management decisions to FCDO in line with the programme’s risk management framework.

**6. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) and Reporting**

- Ensure the programme logframe, results framework, and indicator tracking mechanisms are regularly reviewed, updated, and used to inform adaptive management decisions at the programme level.
- Oversee the production of high-quality programme reports, including quarterly, semi-annual, and annual reports, ensuring findings are evidence-based, reflect programme learning, and demonstrate progress against logframe milestones.
- Champion a culture of learning and adaptive management across the consortium, facilitating after-action reviews, lessons-learned exercises, and pause-and-reflect sessions.

**7. Strategic Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Lead inter-agency and consortium coordination, ensuring effective collaboration, avoiding duplication, and maximizing complementarity across all implementing partners..
- Representing IRC in relevant technical working groups, cluster meetings, and inter-agency coordination platforms relevant to YHC’s scope.

**8. Team Leadership and Management**

- Line-manage senior technical leads and provide mentoring and performance support.
- Work with the Team Leader to identify and resolve implementation challenges and human resources issues as they arise
- Promote and uphold the IRC Way and IRC policies on safeguarding, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse, fiscal integrity and ethics across the YHC team and in work with partners.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

Education:

- Master’s degree in international development, public health, humanitarian affairs, social sciences, public policy, or a related field. Equivalent professional experience may be considered.
- Minimum 8 years of progressive experience in complex humanitarian and/or development programming, with at least 5 years in a senior technical or management role.
- Demonstrated experience managing large-scale, multi-sector FCDO-funded programmes (or equivalent bilateral donors).
- Proven expertise in two or more of the following sectors: health systems strengthening, protection (including GBV, child protection and MHPSS), nutrition, WASH, or food security and livelihoods, with technical expertise in maternal, newborn and child health, including evidence-based interventions and their integration into existing health systems, is an advantage.
- Substantial experience in conflict-affected and access-constrained contexts, and in working with national and local authorities and national NGOs.
- Track record of leading consortium partnerships and supporting localisation agendas, including partner capacity strengthening.
- Experience in applying value-for-money frameworks in programme management and donor reporting.
- Ability to prepare and present technical evidence to senior donor, government and partner audiences.
- Fluency in written and spoken English and Arabic is mandatory.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT**

The position is based in Aden with expected travel to programme and partner locations as security and access permit, and to regional and headquarters offices.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**JOB SUMMARY**

The MEAL Lead provides strategic leadership and technical oversight for Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) across the FCDO YHC consortium. The role is responsible for designing and leading a harmonised, high-quality MEAL system that ensures data integrity, robust evidence generation, accountability to affected populations, and adaptive programming across all consortium partners. The position ensures that MEAL systems are fully embedded in programme design, implementation, and decision-making processes, enabling real-time learning, donor compliance, and consistent application across all consortium partners in line with the agreed programme design, FCDO requirements and strategic programme adaptation. The role also provides critical leadership to ensure consortium results are credible, comparable, and aligned with FCDO reporting standards, while supporting evidence-based decision-making at both operational and strategic levels.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**1. Consortium MEAL Strategy & Systems Leadership**

- Establish a fully harmonised MEAL architecture across all consortium partners, including results frameworks, indicator systems, common tools, reporting formats and supervision approaches,
- Ensure MEAL systems are designed to support adaptive management, strategic decision-making, and donor accountability at all levels, and remain functional when access, funding or the operating environment change, including through contingency and remote monitoring arrangements.
- Establish and chair consortium MEAL governance structures and technical working groups, to ensure alignment and quality assurance.
- Ensure MEAL systems generate high-quality evidence for programme steering, strategic planning, and donor engagement.

**2. Monitoring Systems & Data Quality Assurance**

- Standardise indicators, measurement frameworks, and reporting methodologies in line with FCDO and IRC requirements, aligning with national information systems and cluster reporting where feasible.
- Lead Data Quality Assurance (DQA) systems, including audits, verification exercises, and routine data quality checks, including of partner-reported data.
- Design and oversee remote monitoring, supervision and verification, including third-party monitoring where required, where there is limited access, ensuring independence and triangulation of data.
- Strengthen digital MEAL systems, including dashboards (Power BI or equivalent), mobile data collection platforms, and real-time reporting systems, with data protection and security measures appropriate to the operating context.
- Ensure monitoring systems capture both quantitative performance data and qualitative insights for adaptive programming.

**3. Evaluation, Research & Evidence Generation**

- Ensure all evaluation processes meet FCDO and IRC MEAL standards for rigour, independence, and utility.
- Make use of existing data sources (such as facility availability assessments, multi-sector needs assessments and protection assessments) for baselines, targeting and triangulation.
- Ensure evidence is translated into actionable recommendations for programme adaptation, scaling, and policy influence.
- Promote use of evaluation findings in donor reporting, sector learning, and strategic decision-making.

**4. Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP)**

- Establish harmonised, accessible, and safe feedback and complaint mechanisms across all programme locations and partners, accessible to women, girls and people with disabilities, including female data collectors and channels appropriate to local gender norms.
- Ensure closed-loop feedback systems are functional, with clear response, escalation, and learning mechanisms.
- Integrate safeguarding, PSEA, and protection-sensitive reporting into all MEAL systems.

**5. Learning, Adaptive Management & CLA Systems**

- Ensure production of high-quality learning products including briefs, dashboards, case studies, and synthesis reports.
- Embed learning into programme steering mechanisms and donor reporting cycles.
- Promote a strong organisational culture of evidence-based decision-making and adaptive management.

**6. Value for Money (VfM) & Performance Analysis**

- Lead integration of FCDO VfM framework into all MEAL systems.
- Ensure VfM evidence informs donor reporting, programme design, and strategic investment decisions.
- Strengthen integration of financial and MEAL data for holistic performance analysis.

**7. Consortium Coordination & Partner Capacity Strengthening**

- Provide strategic Develop and enforce consortium MEAL standards, tools, and reporting frameworks.
- Strengthen partner MEAL capacity in results-based management, adaptive programming, and data quality assurance, through costed capacity-strengthening plans and embedded support aligned with IRC’s localisation framework.
- Lead consortium MEAL coordination forums and technical working groups and coordinate with cluster and sector information management where relevant.
- Promote transition from compliance-driven MEAL systems to learning-oriented, adaptive MEAL approaches.

**8. Donor Reporting & Compliance**

- Ensure MEAL systems generate high-quality inputs for FCDO reporting cycles (quarterly, semi-annual, annual) and Annual Reviews.
- Ensure full compliance with FCDO requirements, logframe requirements, and results frameworks.
- Lead preparation for donor reviews, evaluations, audits, and validation exercises.
- Ensure all MEAL outputs are audit-ready, traceable, and evidence-based.
- Support translation of MEAL evidence into strategic communication and donor engagement products.

**9. Leadership & Team Management**

- Provide strategic leadership and line management to consortium MEAL staff, and technical guidance to partner MEAL focal points.
- Build team capacity in advanced MEAL systems, data analysis, digital tools, and adaptive programming.
- Promote a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous learning.
- Ensure effective performance management and succession planning within MEAL teams.
- Strengthen collaboration between MEAL, programme, grants, and finance teams for integrated management.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

- Master’s degree in social sciences, Public Health, Economics, Statistics, Monitoring & Evaluation, Project Planning and Management, Development Studies, Public Policy, or a related field. A Postgraduate Diploma in Monitoring & Evaluation or equivalent professional qualification is an added advantage.
- Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in MEAL within humanitarian or development programmes, including at least 5 years in senior technical or leadership roles.
- Proven experience leading MEAL systems for large-scale, multi-year, multi-partner donor-funded programmes (FCDO or equivalent bilateral donors), with responsibility for harmonised frameworks, reporting systems, and performance tracking.
- Demonstrated experience in MEAL for health, nutrition and/or protection programming in conflict-affected contexts, ideally integrated programming and health systems strengthening.
- Strong background in designing and implementing evaluation systems, including baselines, midline/endline studies, Value for Money (VfM) analysis, and adaptive learning frameworks.
- Experience managing MEAL functions in complex consortium or multi-stakeholder environments, including strengthening the MEAL capacity of national and local NGOs.
- Demonstrated experience designing and operating remote monitoring and third-party monitoring systems in access-constrained contexts.
- Proven ability to develop and manage integrated MEAL systems, including logframes, Theories of Change, indicator tracking systems, and data quality assurance mechanisms.
- Demonstrated capacity to translate complex quantitative and qualitative data into clear donor reports, strategic learning products, and actionable programme recommendations.
- Experience working in Yemen, the wider Middle East or comparable humanitarian contexts, with familiarity with humanitarian coordination structures (clusters and NGO coordination platforms) desirable.

- Champion accountability to affected populations (AAP), including accessible feedback and complaint mechanisms, and ensure findings are used to improve programme delivery.
- Promote a culture of learning and adaptive management, including after-action reviews, lessons-learned exercises and pause-and-reflect sessions.

**7. Team Leadership and Management**

- Lead, line-manage and develop the YHC senior management team, providing mentoring and performance support.
- Ensure the YHC staffing plan is recruited and retained, with clear roles across IRC and consortium partners.
- Foster a culture of collaboration, learning, inclusion and continuous improvement, and promote staff care, safety and security.
- Coordinate closely with the Country Director, Deputy Director of Programmes, operations and support functions, and regional and global teams to ensure YHC is fully supported and aligned with the IRC Yemen country strategy.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

**Education:**

- Master’s degree in international development, public health, humanitarian affairs, public policy, social sciences, or a related field. Equivalent professional experience may be considered.
- Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in complex humanitarian and/or development programming, with at least 5 years in senior leadership of large, multi-year, multi-partner programmes.
- Demonstrated experience leading large-scale, multi-sector FCDO-funded programmes (or equivalent bilateral donors), including responsibility for results, compliance, budgets and donor relationships.
- Proven experience leading consortia, including working with national and local NGOs and advancing localisation agendas.
- Substantial experience in conflict-affected and access-constrained contexts, including remote management of delivery through partners and third-party monitoring.
- Strong understanding of donor compliance, due diligence, sanctions and counter-terrorism requirements, and risk management in complex operating environments
- Technical grounding in at least two of the following: health systems strengthening, nutrition, protection (including GBV and child protection), or food security and livelihoods.
- Experience in applying value-for-money frameworks in programme management and donor reporting.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT**

The position is based in Yemen with expected travel to programme and partner locations as security and access permit, and to regional and headquarters offices.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

## [**Risk Level**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en)**: ☒ Level 3 ☐Level 2 ☐Level 1**

- (Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.
- Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.
- Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

### **The Program / Department / Team**

The Investment & Innovation Department is Prosper Global's platform to establish and grow highly specialized, scalable models in climate resilience, economic resilience and humanitarian innovation, taking what works from first pilot to lasting scale. It brings together the organization's market-oriented, tech-enabled and impact investing work across three areas: impact investment, anchored by Prosper Global Ventures; the Innovation & Scaling Lab; and a portfolio of market shaping initiatives. Impact measurement and management, technical assistance, research and insights are cross-cutting services that we include across the three work areas. The department works in close partnership with Prosper Global's regional and functional teams and technical experts globally.

### **The Position**

The Director of Catalytic Finance owns the development and progression of Prosper Global's pipeline of catalytic finance opportunities, including funds, facilities, blended finance structures, climate finance vehicles, and disaster risk financing mechanisms designed to fill capital gaps in frontier and emerging markets, least developed countries and fragile contexts. Opportunities come from multiple directions: standalone opportunities identified by regional leadership, technical teams, and Prosper Global leadership,; and opportunities that emerge from market shaping initiatives and partnerships. The Director builds and runs a disciplined pipeline, assesses opportunities against clear criteria, develops the strongest into concepts and proposals ready for internal decision, and coordinates their progression through approval and launch. The role also determines how technical assistance and impact measurement and management are built into each opportunity, from initial design through implementation and ongoing learning.

The Director reports to the Chief Investment and Innovation Officer and engages with leaders across the organization and strategic partners. Alongside pipeline development, the Director leads capital raising for these vehicles in partnership with Prosper Global's private philanthropy and institutional donor engagement teams, builds blended finance and investment capability across the organization, and represents Prosper Global externally on the design of catalytic finance vehicles. The Director leads directly on pipeline management, assessment, develops opportunities and makes recommendations, opportunity design and capital raising, and coordinates specialist input from Finance, Legal, technical assistance and impact colleagues and external advisers for structuring, legal and delivery work. The Director also manages Prosper Global’s portfolio of investments and shareholdings in legacy vehicles and companies.

### **Essential Responsibilities**

#### **Pipeline Strategy and Management**

- Establish and manage the department's pipeline of new investment opportunities, with defined stages, screening criteria, decision points and next steps.
- Develop prioritization criteria with the CIIO and apply them consistently, so resources go to opportunities with the strongest strategic fit and realistic prospects.
- Maintain a transparent pipeline dashboard showing each opportunity's stage, owner, timeline and resource needs for the CIIO, the I&I team and other leadership.
- Run regular pipeline reviews with regional, technical and market shaping leads, so opportunities surface early and are progressed, redesigned or closed with a clear rationale.

#### **Sourcing, Collaboration and Decision-Making**

- Source opportunities with regional leadership, technical teams and Prosper Global leadership, drawing on their priorities, relationships, market knowledge and expertise, and maintain engagement.
- Document, for every opportunity, who sourced it, who develops it and who holds the decision.

#### **Opportunity Assessment & Development**

- Assess opportunities for strategic fit, market need, additionality, impact potential, financial viability, risk and Prosper Global's capacity to deliver and sustain them.
- Test the key assumptions behind each opportunity, and flag gaps in evidence, risk or readiness before it advances.
- Recommend to the I&I team, the CIIO and relevant leadership whether each opportunity should advance, be redesigned, paused or declined, with an evidence-based rationale.
- Develop promising opportunities into concepts covering the problem, proposed vehicle or structure, target investees or beneficiaries, partners, capital requirements, impact thesis and principal risks.
- Scope and coordinate feasibility work, commissioning and managing consultants and specialist advisers where needed.
- Lead the design of fund, facility and catalytic finance structures with Finance, Legal and specialist advisers, escalating structural, legal and governance questions appropriately.

#### **Market Shaping to Investment Pathways**

- Identify, with the Market Shaping Initiatives lead and leaders of relevant initiatives, where market shaping work is creating conditions for investment, and define the evidence and milestones that signal readiness.
- Co-design pathways from market shaping to investment that build on program learning, data and market relationships, applying the same criteria as for standalone opportunities.

#### **Technical Assistance and Impact Integration**

- Determine how technical assistance will support investees, intermediaries, partners or wider markets for each opportunity, including purpose, scope, funding and delivery model.
- Work with delivery colleagues and partners so technical assistance designs are practical, resourced and owned.
- Embed impact objectives, measurement, management and learning from the outset with impact measurement and management colleagues, including theory of change, indicators, data and reporting.

#### **Growth and Capital Raising**

- Lead capital raising for these vehicles in partnership with the private philanthropy and institutional donor engagement teams, in line with Prosper Global's fundraising priorities and processes.
- Identify and engage prospective capital providers and partners, including philanthropic and institutional funders, development finance institutions, multilateral climate funds, impact investors, co-investors, fund managers and intermediaries.
- Develop investment cases, investor materials and proposals setting out each vehicle's capital need, structure, risk and impact.
- Track capital raised for each vehicle against agreed targets and keep the CIIO informed.

#### **Approval, Launch and Handoff**

- Guide opportunities through review, approval and launch, preparing concept notes, proposals and decision papers and coordinating operational, legal, financial and staffing steps with the relevant teams.
- Define and document each handoff to the team or entity responsible for ongoing management, including roles, timing and any continuing support.

#### **Portfolio Management**

- Manage Prosper Global's investments held in Mercy Corps Development Holdings, monitoring each holding's financial performance, risk and impact.
- Represent Prosper Global as an investor, including governance rights and board or advisory roles where applicable, and work with Finance and Legal on valuations, reporting, audit and compliance.
- Recommend follow-on support, restructuring or exits for each holding, for decision by the CIIO and the I&I team.
- Keep portfolio performance and impact data current, and keep the CIIO, the I&I team and relevant governance bodies informed.

#### **Internal Learning and Capacity Building**

- Build catalytic finance and investment capability across Prosper Global through training, guidance and practical tools.
- Help regional and technical teams spot where their programs could support investment, and how to bring those opportunities forward.

#### **Thought Leadership and External Engagement**

- Share insight publicly on designing catalytic finance vehicles to fill capital gaps in frontier and emerging markets, least developed countries and fragile contexts, including climate finance and disaster risk financing.
- Represent Prosper Global at conferences, in industry networks and in publications, in coordination with Communications.
- Contribute to sector learning with peer organizations, investors, funders and researchers working on catalytic and blended finance.

#### **Safeguarding Responsibilities**

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

None at the time of hire. The Director manages consultants and specialist advisers engaged for specific opportunities, and coordinates colleagues across teams on opportunity development without line authority.

### **Accountability**

- **Report directly to**: Chief Investment and Innovation Officer
- **Works directly with**: Investment & Innovation team and initiatives, including the Innovation & Scaling Lab, technical assistance and impact measurement and management colleagues; Prosper Global Ventures; regional leadership, including Regional Vice Presidents; technical teams; Prosper Global leadership; Market Shaping Initiatives lead and leaders of relevant market shaping initiatives; private philanthropy and institutional donor engagement teams; Finance, Legal and Communications; portfolio companies in Mercy Corps Development Holdings and other shareholdings; external co-investors, fund managers, intermediaries, funders and advisers.

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification and Transferable Skills**

- Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, business, international development or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Significant professional experience, typically 10 or more years, in impact investing, development finance, blended finance, venture capital, private equity or fund and facility design, including direct responsibility for taking opportunities from concept to approval.
- Demonstrated experience structuring funds, facilities, investments or blended finance vehicles, working alongside legal, financial and specialist advisers.
- Strong investment assessment skills, including financial modeling, risk analysis and due diligence, and the ability to weigh financial viability against impact potential and additionality.
- Experience managing an investment portfolio after close, including performance monitoring, investor governance, valuations, and exit or restructuring decisions.
- Experience designing technical assistance and impact measurement and management into investments, facilities or programs.
- Demonstrated success raising capital from philanthropic, institutional, development finance or private investors for funds, facilities or blended finance vehicles.
- Track record of building partnerships with investors, funders, intermediaries or public-sector partners and managing complex, multi-stakeholder processes to a decision.
- Experience working in frontier and emerging markets, least developed countries or fragile contexts.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presenting to investors and senior leaders and explaining complex financial structures to non-specialist colleagues.
- Master's degree such as an MBA, MPP or MSc in a relevant field preferred.
- Experience connecting grant-funded programs or market systems development with investment or blended finance preferred.
- Experience with climate finance, including multilateral climate funds and climate focused funds or facilities for adaptation and resilience, preferred.
- Experience with disaster risk financing, including contingent, parametric or pre-arranged financing instruments, preferred.
- Record of published writing or public speaking on blended, catalytic or innovative finance preferred.
- Sector experience in one or more of climate resilience, agriculture, energy, digital employment, financial inclusion or humanitarian response preferred.

### **Success Factors**

The successful Director combines investment discipline with a real commitment to impact, and is as comfortable interrogating a financial model as a market systems theory of change. They exercise sound judgment about which opportunities to pursue and which to stop, and they say so clearly and with evidence. They move work forward through influence, building trust with regional leaders, technical teams and functional colleagues who each own their own decisions. They're credible with investors and funders, and generous with what they know, helping colleagues across Prosper Global build confidence with blended finance. They're rigorous about assumptions, candid about risk and readiness, and steady in the ambiguity of a department that's still taking shape. They know when to bring in specialist expertise so the work gets done well without everything resting on them.

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in US, UK, NL, Kenya,or Colombia and requires up to 25% travel to support regional teams, partners and opportunity development, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited. Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

### **Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

#### **Disclaimer**

*We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.*
