**Vacancy Announcement**

Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

**(REF. 2026-12)**

Position title: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

Team: Performance and Impact

Required FTE: 80%

Required travel: Some travel, up to maximum 10% of time

Reports to: Head – Performance and Impact

**Scope of the role**

Violent extremism is a direct threat to international security, economic growth, and development. GCERF works to prevent violent extremism by investing in people. As the only global fund dedicated to preventing violent extremism (PVE), we connect local communities to global resources and support grassroots initiatives that are often out of reach for international donors. We fund community-centric initiatives led by civil society organisations to address the local social, economic, and political drivers of violent extremism.

The Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will be part of GCERF’s dynamic and high-performing team of Monitoring and Evaluation experts. This role is responsible for ensuring the quality of monitoring, evaluation and evidence across assigned grants, including results frameworks, assessments, and evaluations. Provides technical support to the Performance & Impact unit in line with the role holder’s expertise.

**Principal accountabilities and ownership**

**Grant-management:** Responsible for ensuring M&E quality throughout the management of assigned grants, including oversight of results frameworks, and capacity building needs. Coordinate with the P&I Associate on routine results reporting, data quality and related monitoring processes, providing technical review and guidance as required.

**Assessments and Evaluations:** Responsible for planning, managing or advising on assessments across assigned grants, including baselines, endlines, evaluations and third-party monitoring (TPM). Ensure the methodological quality of assessments and support the use of findings for programme and grant management.

**Coordination:** Liaise and coordinate with Portfolio and Finance teams within each Country/Regional Team.

**P&I support:** Contribute to Performance & Impact unit priorities in areas aligned with the role holder’s technical skills and expertise, including technical analysis, methodological support, development of tools and guidance, and other technical inputs as required.

**Knowledge/Experience/Qualifications**

- Fluency in English and Russian; working knowledge of French is an advantage (B2-level).
- Strong, proven monitoring and Evaluation experience, specifically assessment experience, is required, as well as project management or applied research. We expect this to require at least 6 years of progressively responsible experience in a similar role. At least two years’ professional experience in one of GCERF’s partner countries or similar contexts.
- Master’s degree in Economics, Data Science, Statistics, International Relations, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Previous experience or demonstrated interest in the prevention of radicalisation to violent extremism will be an advantage.
- Programming and/or impact evaluation (especially quasi-experimental designs) experience is an asset.
- Detail-oriented, excellent coordination skills, must be able to work independently and have a keen interest in seeking tech solutions to improve efficiency.

**Values**

Demonstration of alignment with GCERF’s key values is a critical component of the selection process:

Make a difference

Achieve together

Uphold integrity

Respect yourself and others

Learn and improve

Be Kind

**Personal attributes based on GCERF competencies**

Be proactive

Work collaboratively

Be accountable and drive for solutions and results

Communicate effectively

Embrace learning and entrepreneurial spirit

**General information**: Our office is located in Geneva, Switzerland. Swiss residency or work eligibility is not a requirement.

GCERF values diversity, equality and inclusion, and we hire globally. We are committed to hiring qualified candidates irrespective of age, disability, ethnicity, national origin, family status, sex, gender identity or expression, physical characteristics, race, religion, spirituality or sexual orientation. GCERF has a zero tolerance policy towards sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as any form of discrimination or harassment. GCERF stands by its commitment to welcoming persons of all backgrounds into a safe work environment.

All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference checks and anti-terrorism screening.

Contract: 1 year, renewable. Part-time 80% (32 hours per week). The arrangement of days and hours worked is flexible.

GCERF allows a limited number of remote working days per week.

Competitive compensation package.

Overview of position

**Nature of the consultancy:**

**Deliverable Based Consultancy (output-based)**

Research, data, consultation and in-person facilitation support to the International Consultant for the gender-sensitive Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic for Somalia and for the co-creation and validation of the Climate Mobility Programme for integration into the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible.

**Project Context and Scope:**

**Background**

Recurrent droughts, floods and environmental degradation, combined with fragility and conflict, drive large-scale human mobility and displacement in Somalia. The National Adaptation Plan (NAP 2.0, 2026–2030) and the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) both recognise human mobility in the context of climate change as a priority. However, limited consolidated data and institutional capacity make it difficult to turn these commitments into investment-ready interventions, and human mobility is not yet well reflected in the NDC 3.0 Investment Plan 2025–2030 launched by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MoECC) at COP 30. The MoECC has asked the client to help address this.

This consultancy is part of the client’s Development Fund project “Strengthening Climate Mobility Investment Readiness in Somalia: Advancing NAP and NDC Implementation”, under Output 1.1 (Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic) and Output 1.2 (Climate Mobility Programme).

Role objectives

**Working arrangement**

The assignment is delivered by two consultants working as one team. The **International Consultant** (home-based) leads the technical work and presents online at all workshops (unless travel is confirmed). The **National Consultant** (Somalia-based) starts one month earlier to compile data and map stakeholders, supports the data collection and consultations and organizes and facilitates all workshops and events in person, with logistical support from the client’s project team. All work is carried out with the MoECC and its Inter-Ministerial NDC Taskforce. The client’s Climate Action Department and Regional Climate Action Unit (Nairobi) provide technical support and quality assurance.

**Main tasks**

Under the supervision of the client and the day-to-day technical guidance of the International Consultant, the National Consultant will:

**Data and evidence:** compile a literature review and secondary data (climate, socio-economic, displacement and human mobility) from national and international sources, and complete a stakeholder mapping.

**Consultations:** adapt and translate (English/Somali) the KII/FGD guides developed by the International Consultant, and conduct consultations with government, technical agencies and communities, including women and girls and other vulnerable groups.

**Workshops and events:** organize and facilitate in person, with logistical support from the client’s project team and the International Consultant presenting online: (i) the inception workshop; (ii) a combined workshop to validate the Country Diagnostic and co-create the Climate Mobility Programme; and (iii) the Programme validation workshop. Provide interpretation, minutes and a consolidated summary of feedback for each.

**Coordination with the MoECC:** support a climate mobility working group under the existing Inter-Ministerial NDC Taskforce, and liaise with the MoECC to obtain and compile relevant information on the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

Community Stabilization Unit, Transition and Recovery Pillar (TRP), the client.

Project: “Strengthening Climate Mobility Investment Readiness in Somalia: Advancing NAP and NDC Implementation” – project code SO10P0800, funded by the client’s Development Fund (IDF).

**Tangible and measurable outputs** **of the work assignment**

The National Consultant will deliver the following outputs on a three-instalment payment basis. Months refer to the months of this contract (Month 1 = the month the Consultant starts); the International Consultant starts in Month 2:

**Deliverable 1 – Workplan and Stakeholder Mapping (max. 10 pages).** – Deliverable by email by mid-Month 1.

**Deliverable 2 – Literature Review and Secondary Data Compilation (max. 20 pages, plus dataset):** ready for the International Consultant when they start in Month 2. – **First instalment payment (Deliverables 1–2)** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 1.

**Deliverable 3 – Inception Workshop and Stakeholder Consultations Report (max. 20 pages):** inception workshop facilitated in person (end of Month 2) with minutes; translated tools; consultations conducted and findings summarized. – Deliverable by email by end of Month 3.

**Deliverable 4 – Validation and Co-Creation Workshop:** workshop facilitated in person in late Month 4 to validate the Country Diagnostic findings and co-create the Climate Mobility Programme; minutes and consolidated results. – **Second instalment payment (Deliverables 3–4)** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 4.

**Final Deliverable 5 – Programme Validation Workshop:** workshop facilitated in person (mid-Month 6); minutes and consolidated feedback for the final Programme; compiled information on the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible. – **Third and final instalment payment** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 6.

Each deliverable may go through more than one draft; it is considered complete once the client’s feedback has been incorporated and the client has approved it.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

Deliverables submitted on time and approved by the client.

Data compilation and consultations complete, well-sourced and inclusive of women, girls and other vulnerable groups.

All three workshops held as planned, with MoECC and Taskforce participation, and minutes and feedback delivered within one week.

Effective coordination with the International Consultant and the client’s project team.

**Payment terms and conditions**

Lump-sum fee paid in three instalments against approved deliverables:

**First instalment – 25% :** Deliverables 1–2 – Workplan and Stakeholder Mapping; Literature Review and Secondary Data Compilation (Month 1).

**Second instalment – 50% :** Deliverables 3–4 – Inception Workshop and Consultations Report; Validation and Co-Creation Workshop (Month 4).

**Third and final instalment – 25%:** Deliverable 5 – Programme Validation Workshop (Month 6).

Payments are released upon the client’s approval of the respective deliverables, together with a short progress report (achievements, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations against the approved workplan), and are subject to satisfactory confirmation by the Programme Manager. jobs.description:
- Exciting senior leadership opportunity on a flagship FCDO-funded HEROS 2.0 programme
- Fixed Term
- London, United Kingdom

## **About us**

With over 40 years of humanitarian and development experience, [Tetra Tech](https://www.tetratech.com/) is a trusted humanitarian delivery partner globally. We have tried and tested **a humanitarian response capability, spanning** logistics, humanitarian advisory, operational and technical expertise, and people who can deploy rapidly. We are a gold-level supplier to the FCDO and the lead contractor for the DFAT-funded **Australia Assists Phase 2, Humanitarian Logistics Capability Phase II, and the Pacific Humanitarian Warehousing Program** **Infrastructure Specialist Unit ISU**.

Tetra Tech International Development Europe is Tetra Tech’s European business unit focused on international development project management, technical advisory, and monitoring and evaluation services. We have a 40-year history of successfully delivering humanitarian and international development projects on behalf of donors around the world, including the UK’s Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the European Union (EU), Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), the United States Department of State (DOS), development banks and multilateral institutions. We are a trusted provider of humanitarian and emergency response assistance globally. Our people are focused on improving lives and work side by side with local partners to support sustainable economic growth, stability, governance, and environmental and climate practices. You can find out more about our international development work with UK and European clients [here](https://intdev.tetratecheurope.com/).

## The Programme

The upcoming Humanitarian Emergency Response Operations and Stabilisation programme (HEROS 2.0) will enable FCDO to respond rapidly, at scale, to global humanitarian disasters and support work on protracted crises, chronic emergencies and humanitarian reform. It will provide FCDO with a flexible model to support the UK Government’s conflict, stabilisation and security work in fragile and conflict-affected states, both during steady state periods and in response to new crises. HEROS 2.0 will deliver the following overarching capabilities:

1\. Humanitarian & Conflict Early Warning & Analysis (EWAR): Expert analytical capability to provide horizon-scanning for global humanitarian and conflict risk drivers, presenting this information and analysis to FCDO.

2\. Standing Humanitarian Expertise: Technical expert capacity to provide advice, analysis, and evidence products in support of FCDO’s humanitarian planning, preparedness and response. This capacity will be deployable globally to provide ‘first response’ support to sudden-onset humanitarian crises, in addition to supporting protracted crises and system reform. This capacity will cover a range of technical specialisms alongside a core generalist humanitarian skill set (Indicative specialisms include: Shelter, WASH, Health, Cash, Preparedness, Protection & Inclusion, Resilience, Localisation & Participation).

3\. Scalable Expertise: Capability to deploy, at pace, technical expertise for FCDO to fulfil specific, time-limited advisory and analytical requirements across humanitarian, conflict and security objectives.

4\. Humanitarian Logistics: End-to-end logistics function to plan, scope, source and deploy equipment and humanitarian supplies in response to crises, as required by FCDO. This capability may include the management of UKAid stockpiles, in the UK and globally, as well as rapid sourcing and delivery in response to crisis demand.

## The Role

Duties and Responsibilities

This is a unique role and opportunity to lead one of FCDO’s largest humanitarian programmes providing leadership to a flagship humanitarian support activity. The **HEROS 2.0 Director** will provide senior leadership and overall management of the HEROS 2.0 programme, leading the core delivery team and acting as the main counterpart to the FCDO. The role will ensure effective delivery across all programme components, including early warning and analysis, expert advisory support, deployments, procurement and logistics, standby partnership deployments, and UNDAC-related support. The Director will be responsible for strategic oversight, stakeholder engagement, programme performance, risk management, and ensuring the programme remains ready to respond rapidly to humanitarian emergencies and protracted crises.

## The Person

*Essential:*

- Minimum 15 years of relevant experience in the humanitarian sector
- Proven experience in humanitarian delivery, including first-phase emergency response.
- Demonstrated experience working with FCDO in the UK and overseas Posts.
- Proven experience in senior leadership positions, with responsibility for teams, strategy, and delivery.
- Experience leading or working within humanitarian networks and coordination mechanisms.
- Knowledge of the UN humanitarian system and experience of working with UN programmes and agencies.
- Strong leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills.

*Desirable*

- SC or DV security clearance
- Technical knowledge of conflict and stabilisation
- Direct experience of humanitarian assistance implementation with NGOs
- Previous Team Leader experience on FCDO programmes
- Prior experience of HSOT delivery or similar humanitarian response programmes
- Familiarity with the UNDAC deployments
- Familiarity with humanitarian procurement, logistics and warehouse management
- Confidence with MIS solutions and technological developments in the humanitarian space

jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate and Cause Marketing Partnerships, the Director, Cause Marketing & Workplace Giving is responsible for developing national and global cause marketing partnerships in support of HFHI’s mission. The Director will work closely with development leadership and key HFHI program stakeholders to maximize fundraising opportunities for unrestricted funds. Lead revenue development of $10+ million annually and significantly grow revenue over time.

**Develop fundraising strategy and pipeline to steward current donors and grow the portfolio (35%)**

· Develop and execute strategies to increase partner engagement and revenue in cause marketing initiatives, workplace giving and other sources of unrestricted revenue, including leveraging partners’ employees and customer spheres of influence to fundraise on behalf of HFHI.

· Lead and expand the fundraising and execution of “Home is the Key”, Habitat’s annual cause marketing platform and rollout of a multi-channel, integrated national cause marketing platform that appeals to existing partner portfolio as well as new industries including retail, CPG, QSR and others to broaden the base of HFHI support.

· Lead and support team in development of account-specific strategies that deepen partner engagement with Habitat and foster mutually beneficial, sustainable, mission-centered partnerships.

· Develop and execute strategies to increase partner participation in workplace giving campaigns; rollout toolkits and other support materials.

· Stay current on opportunities, trends, and best practices in cause marketing, retail, digital, corporate sponsorship and workplace giving; convert insights into actionable programs and new revenue streams and identify potential prospects for cultivation.

**Carry a personal portfolio and lead/coach staff on key partnerships (15%)**

· Develop and deliver creative and powerful presentations and proposals for corporate partnership opportunities; ensure organizational leadership involved in pitch are briefed and prepared for meetings.

· Ensure 100% partner satisfaction through thoughtful stewardship and best-in-class customer service.

**Collaborate cross functionally within Habitat to work on continuous process improvement and partnership development (20%)**

· Serve as cause-related marketing and workplace giving subject matter expert across the organization; ensure compliance with all applicable charitable sales promotion regulations; provide on-going training and support to Resource Development team.

· Provide leadership to team regarding structuring/managing their cause marketing partnerships and advancing global multi-national partnerships.

· Collaborate with HFHI leadership to develop relationships with key stakeholders at multiple levels across partner organizations.

· Partner with HFHI Marketing and Communications, key Resource Development teams and other organizational stakeholders to create and implement sound cause marketing strategies that beneficially advance HFHI fundraising and brand awareness goals and priorities.

· Establish strong relationships with HFH affiliate Executive Directors and resource development teams as well as HFHI regional staff; support the collaborative development efforts among Habitat for Humanity entities including the identification of opportunities to share prospects with HFHI resource development colleagues and local Habitat affiliates, as appropriate.

**Lead and coach the team (20%)**

· Through regular communication, and a strategic, forward-looking approach, work with each member of the team to create development plans that enhance their skill sets and achieve revenue goals. Lead the strategy for engaging new partners in cause and workplace activities / campaigns and ensure the proficiencies of the team.

**Administration, Reporting & Analysis (10%)**

· Oversight of deal terms and collaboration with HFHI legal and finance teams to ensure compliance.

· Maintain systems for metrics tracking, analytics, and knowledge sharing.

· Provide accurate activity and pipeline reports including situational analysis, revenue and expense forecasts as required.

· Maintain current prospect and partner records in donor management system.

**Other duties as assigned by supervisor**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

· Education: Bachelors Degree or equivalent experience

· Years of Related Experience: 6-10 years of related experience; 3-5 years in leadership capacity.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

· Experience in securing complex, six-and seven-figure cause marketing commitments from Fortune 500 companies.

· Experience leading a team and collaborating across a complex organization.

· Working knowledge of principles of corporate social responsibility, cause marketing, employee engagement and sponsorship.

· Superior skills in project management, metrics, analytics and reporting.

· Highly collaborative; optimistic personality with winning relationship skills to build internal and external partnerships.

· Creative, quick thinker who thrives in brainstorm sessions and who can think past obstacles to achieve a bigger vision.

· Highly proactive and autonomous, capable of driving projects through in a complex and layered organization.

· Outstanding oral and written communication skills with excellent interpersonal, presentation and negotiation skills.

· Solution-oriented with commitment to delivering excellent internal and external customer service.

· Ability to complete multiple projects concurrently while balancing competing priorities; ability to meet deadlines.

· Ability to effectively manage HFHI resources including travel expenses and unit budget.

· Computer literate; able to use word-processing, spreadsheet, database and project software.

**Preferred Requirements:**

· Knowledge of and passion for Habitat's worldwide mission preferred

· Established media relationships and deep knowledge of media and entertainment sector; track record of building media partnerships.

· Experience with international partnership strategy and development.

**Culture and Values**
At Habitat for Humanity International, you join a community that believes in:

**\*Humility:** We are part of something bigger than ourselves.
**\*Courage:** We do what is right, even when it is difficult.
**\*Accountability:** We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.

jobs.title: Senior Specialist - Management & Operations Expertise Hub
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Job Summary

Are you ready to make an impact in the world? Join Habitat for Humanity’s Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub as we multiply Habitat’s impact in the United States.

Habitat for Humanity International’s U.S. Expertise Hubs are teams of subject matter experts and collaborative thought partners that – in partnership with local affiliate staff and leaders from across the country – create, connect and curate resources, trainings, and promising practices along dedicated practice areas in support of capability building within the U.S. affiliated network. The Management and Operations Expertise Hub drives the aggregation and exchange of practice-based knowledge and application among affiliates and other subject matter experts in nonprofit management and operations, including topics such as governance and board management, finance, human resources, information technology, administration, compliance and risk management, and other day-to-day operational topics.

The Sr. Specialist will manage and support the development, delivery/facilitation, evaluation and socialization of new and refreshed resource/training content, services, and support within the Management and Operations Expertise Hub to maximize the management and operations of U.S. Habitat affiliates. The role supports the thoughtful and intentional curation of existing content/expertise from both the Habitat community and external partnerships to advance promising practices. The role must collaborate closely with HFHI affiliate-facing learning professionals to ensure that hub content is packaged and delivered in the most accessible and useful way to be relevant and accessible to Habitat’s diverse network, and is responsible for that delivery and facilitation.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## **Senior Specialist – Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub**

**Help strengthen the organizations that help families build a better future.**

Bring your expertise in nonprofit management, learning, and relationship building to Habitat for Humanity International. In this role, you’ll turn knowledge into practical tools, connect affiliate leaders with promising practices, and facilitate learning experiences that strengthen Habitat’s impact across the United States.

**Work setting:** Remote/home office (may work in-person or hybrid if desired and near an HFHI office and space is available)
**Domestic travel:** 20%

#### **Product and Services Development, Delivery, and Evaluation (60%)**

- Lead and/or contribute to the review, refresh, development, design, testing, delivery, and evaluation of quality, relevant, and timely content, products, and services (e.g., templates, toolkits, websites, webinars, peer learning and connection experiences, trainings, and other innovative learning approaches) aligned with hub topic areas for affiliate capability/capacity building and organizational/departmental standards and processes

- Stay informed on nonprofit management and operations trends, risks, and opportunities (e.g. topics such as governance and board management, finance, human resources, information technology, administration, compliance and risk management, and other day-to-day operational topics) to ensure content, resources, and services are relevant, timely, and impactful for the US affiliate network.
- Support other key initiatives, as directed, through project management, stakeholder engagement, subject matter expertise, and effective use of data and content curation tools.

#### **Network Outreach, Engagement, Relationship Building, and General/SME Support (40%)**

- Provide high-quality service and support to the affiliate network, answering inquiries, identifying needs, and creating opportunities for peer-to-peer learning and community building.

- Successful completion of annual goals connected to Expertise Hubs and Division Objectives

- Active demonstration of living out HFHI’s core values and being an active, cooperative team member

jobs.description:
?Our organization is an international NGO operating in 41 countries, committed to addressing global challenges through international cooperation projects. We work with an impact-oriented approach, collaborating with local and international partners to respond to humanitarian emergencies and promote sustainable development.

We are looking for a dynamic and passionate individual to join our team in Burundi as **Project Manager.**

jobs.title: Human Resources Expert - CDR
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/228**
- **Position Title**: Human Resources Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 16 November 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 23 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zPWKGabdFSzUtF9pkcm7vR_poJ8-_L84/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zPWKGabdFSzUtF9pkcm7vR_poJ8-_L84/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

To this end, there is a need to strengthen the human resource function itself, including its organization, processes, policies, systems, and service delivery arrangements. A strengthened HR function is essential to support workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, career progression, and other core personnel processes, while also providing the institutional capacity required to support the wider CDR reform programme. In this context, the HR function needs to move beyond the administration of personnel matters toward a more structured and integrated approach to workforce management aligned with CDR's functions, organizational structure, and operational priorities.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Human Resources Expert to support CDR in implementing the human resource measures under Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will review and update the existing and proposed job descriptions against the applicable legislative framework and operational requirements, reassess the HR function identified, and translate the findings into an HR Strategy, HR Policies and Procedures Manual, and target operating model for the Human Resources Department. The assignment will also ensure that the HR Strategy incorporates the human resource requirements arising from other reform areas, including change management and the development and implementation of a Human Resource Information System.

Through this assignment, the Expert will contribute to establishing a clearer, more functional, and sustainable human resource framework for CDR, with defined roles and responsibilities, updated job descriptions, appropriate HR policies and procedures, and an operating model capable of supporting both CDR's immediate staffing needs and the longer-term institutional reforms identified in the roadmap.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Human Resources Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Assessment of the Human Resource Function and HR Strategy**

- Review human resource arrangements, relevant institutional findings and proposed reform priorities to establish the baseline for the assessment.
- Review the legal and regulatory framework that governs CDR staff, including Decree No. 10941 of 2003, Decree No. 10942 of 2003, Section 54 of the 2004 Budget Law, the Council of Ministers freeze on hiring and promotion, the allowance decrees issued between 2021 and 2025, the Council of Ministers decision of 19 June 2025 and the internal regulations of CDR, and record for each human resource process the rule that governs it and the authority that approves it.
- Validate the workforce baseline with the Administrative Affairs Division, covering filled and vacant mandated posts, individual contractors, project implementation unit personnel, projected retirements, resignations and multi-role assignments, and identify any figures that are not substantiated by the available records.
- Assess the mandate, organization, staffing and capacity of the Human Resources Department within the Administrative Affairs Division.
- Map the human resource processes as they operate today, covering workforce planning, recruitment and onboarding, personnel records, attendance and leave, performance evaluation and promotion, training, discipline, and separation and end-of-service, and record where a process is informal, paper-based or undocumented.
- Identify the gaps between current practice, the legal framework and the needs of the reformed structure, and distinguish the gaps that CDR can close within the current legal framework from those that depend on the amendment of Decree No. 10941 and Decree No. 10942.
- Establish the baseline and the method of measurement for human resource indicators including the employee-satisfaction baseline survey, coordinated with the staff survey used for the change indicators so that staff are surveyed once.
- Prepare the HR Strategy for CDR, setting out its objectives, priority measures, responsibilities and sequence, aligned with the Target Roadmap and the Interim Arrangements, and addressing the vacancy, multi-role and key-person dependency risks identified.
- Set out in the Strategy the recruitment route for the transitional period and the longer-term recruitment model, consistent with the position on the Civil Service Board mandate.
- Define the target operating model of the Human Resources Department, comprising its functions, roles, reporting lines and staffing, and its role as business owner of the Human Resource Information System.
- Set out in the Strategy the human resource input to the Change Management Committee on the resistance factors linked to restructuring, redeployment and remuneration, and coordinate the staff messages on these matters with the Change Management and Communications Expert.
- Set out in the Strategy the business requirements of the Human Resources Department for the Human Resource Information System identified, validating the human resource process definitions, the business rules for attendance, leave and missions, and the employee data structure, and confirming the legal basis of the end-of-service calculation before any procurement.
- Prepare the action plan that implements the Strategy, with responsibilities assigned by post and timing reconciled with the master roadmap.

**Workstream 2. Review and Update of Job Descriptions**

- Compile the inventory of the job descriptions already prepared, comprising those prepared by the Administrative Affairs Division including identified positions, Terms of Reference, job description summaries and IT Department job descriptions, and identify the existing and new posts for which no description exists.
- Review each JD against the applicable legislation, including the ranks, sub-grades and qualification requirements under Decree No. 10942, the divisional and departmental mandates under Decree No. 10941 and the reformed structure, and, for procurement posts, the requirements of Law No. 244 of 2021 on the competencies and career paths of procurement staff.
- Review each description against the operational needs of CDR, testing with the Heads of Division whether the scope of work, reporting lines, decision rights and qualifications correspond to the work the role performs under the redesigned business processes.
- Harmonize the descriptions into a single template that records, for each post, the interim placement within the current structure and the position under the reformed structure, so that the same document serves recruitment now and redeployment later.
- Update the descriptions on the basis of the review, remove overlaps between posts, reflect the segregation of duties required in the financial management, procurement and ICT processes, and complete the descriptions for the posts not yet covered.
- Reconcile the rank assigned to each post with the indicative costing identified, and record each discrepancy for the remuneration and financing proposal.
- Confirm the updated descriptions with the Heads of Division and prepare the submission through which the Board approves them.
- Prepare the procedure through which the Administrative Affairs Division maintains the descriptions as the structure changes, and brief the Division on its application.

**Workstream 3. HR Policies, Performance Management and Capacity Development**

- Prepare the HR Policies and Procedures Manual, documenting each human resource process with its steps, responsibilities, approvals, time standards and forms, and removing steps whose risk does not justify them before the process is digitized.
- Review the performance-evaluation system for promotion reactivated in 2025, and propose how it draws on the updated job descriptions within the promotion rules of Decree No. 10942.
- Prepare the human resource provisions on employee protection, covering discrimination and workplace misconduct, conflict-of-interest declarations for staff holding more than one role, and disciplinary consequences for retaliation, in coordination with the Audit Committee, which owns the whistleblower policy set out, and with the Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert.
- Prepare the competency-based capacity development strategy, consolidating the role-based learning pathways with the identified function-specific training and defining the training-needs assessment method, the format of the annual training plan and the pre- and post-training assessment of competency.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 11 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within three months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Human Resources Management, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Management, Public Policy, Law, or a related field.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) assessing and strengthening human resource functions and organizational structures, including workforce planning, HR processes, job descriptions, performance management, recruitment, staff development and HR policies; and (ii) designing and implementing HR strategies, operating models, policies and procedures, including HR information systems and competency-based capacity development frameworks.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Protection from Violence Programme Development Manager Ethiopia Addis Ababa
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a dynamic and strategic **Protection from Violence (PFV) Programme Development Manager (PDM)** to provide technical leadership and drive the growth, quality and impact of its Protection from Violence programming.

In this role, you will lead the technical development and strategic direction of the PFV Core Competency, spearhead programme development and fundraising initiatives, and ensure high-quality programme delivery across the operation. You will also strengthen technical capacity through staff mentoring, training and coaching, while providing oversight of programme quality, MEAL, budget management and procurement to ensure effective implementation and accountability.

We are looking for a leader who can translate protection priorities into impactful programmes, build strong technical teams and drive sustainable programming that responds to the needs of people affected by displacement and violence.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your generic responsibilities:

- Develop and implement the Protection from Violence strategy for NRC Ethiopia including Macro Log frames that are aligned with country and global strategies priorities.
- Develop technical standards, SOPs, guidance documents for PFV across NRC Ethiopia, under the guidance of NRC’s PFV Global Advisers
- Promote the rights of conflict- and displacement-affected people in line with the advocacy strategy. Undertake Protection Advocacy initiatives.
- Contribute to fundraising, develop and revise funding proposal, budgets and donor reports.
- Overall technical management and mentorship of project staff across NRC Ethiopia
- Provide systematic training and build capacity of technical staff, in approaches including cash-based interventions and market-based programme
- Oversee PFV project(s) implementation across NRC Ethiopia, including development and oversight of Community Feedback Mechanism
- Lead the localization agenda of NRC Ethiopia for PFV. Identify meaningful partners for strategic cooperation aiming to advance PFV portfolio across Ethiopia.
- Follow up on compliance with contractual commitments within PFV, ensure high technical quality products
- Ensure that key learnings are extracted from Protection from Violence implementation, and incorporate them in Protection from Violence and staff development processes
- Represent NRC in relevant forums/clusters, including with national authorities and donors

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAt92z8Iv4rSqzgkeTdghASAZNyyCLKN07CJRmwR94cBx8?e=poxnT3) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Graduate degree with minimum 5 years of relevant experience from a senior level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- Excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency and displacement situations
- Detailed knowledge of humanitarian and protection principles and guidelines for humanitarian assistance
- Good understanding of Protection Cluster coordination mechanisms
- Strong coordination, representation skills and inter-personal skills, working well both in teams and independently
- Self-motivated and excellent observer of protection issues
- Able to work under pressure and good at timely decision making
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets
- Strong experience in programme development and management
- Experience in training facilitation and capacity-building
- Experience in Ethiopia mandatory
- Willingness to spend a significant period of time at NRC’s Area Offices
- This position is open to Ethiopian nationals only.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

## **We are seeking a Senior Training Lead for 2-year-regular position (renewable) to work within Africa Regional Office at the International Vaccine Institute in Kigali, Rwanda. (Duty station: Kigali, Rwanda)**

This role is responsible for the technical aspects of transferring, adapting and delivering VEA4A’s GxP+, MSAT, Advanced Regulatory Science and Train-the-Trainer programmes in Rwanda. Its responsibilities also include institutional readiness, programme performance, monitoring, evaluation and learning, inclusion, safeguarding coordination and implementation learning for VEA4A. The role works with the Program Director, participating institutions and other partners to monitor progress and inform programme adaptations.

**1. Institutional readiness assessment and programme performance monitoring**

- Lead HEI readiness assessment, institutional-strengthening monitoring and readiness recommendations with the Training Lead and HEI teams.
- Lead the MEL framework, indicator definitions, data-quality arrangements, performance dashboards, quarterly reviews, learning briefs and programme reporting.
- Integrate evidence from training, HEIs, participants and employment pathways and recommend adaptations to the Program Director.
- Facilitate narrative and performance reporting to the Foundation and ensure timely technical, budget and partner inputs.

**2. Programme planning and implementation**

- Translate the approved proposal, workplan and budget into integrated annual, quarterly and detailed implementation plans.
- Own the master workplan, critical path, milestones, dependencies, resource plan and consolidated delivery calendar.
- Coordinate routine implementation across ARUA, HEIs, IVI technical teams, functional units, providers and all programme workstreams.
- Manage scope, schedule, deliverables, risks, issues, decisions, changes, assumptions and corrective actions through documented project controls.
- Monitor partner deliverables and programme commitments and ensure that delays or performance concerns receive timely action.
- Chair routine implementation meetings and act for the Program Director on operational matters when formally delegated.

**3. Budget tracking and programme document preparation**

- Monitor programme expenditure and support budget phasing and forecasting, working with the Project Administrator and relevant colleagues to identify and communicate variances against the approved budget.
- Contribute to the preparation of programme-related agreements and contracts with participating institutions, service providers and other partners, in coordination with relevant IVI functions.

**4. Systems oversight and safeguarding & inclusion facilitation**

- Oversee programme-wide digital operations, including the relationship among applications, LMS, participant records, course records and reporting systems.

**Job Requirements and Qualifications**

**1. Education Requirements**

- Advanced degree in health sciences, public health, project management, development, education, social sciences or a related field.

**2. Related Field Work Experience**

- 8+ years with Master’s degree

**3. Technical and Professional Skills / Knowledge**

- Substantial experience managing complex, multi-partner and donor-funded programmes, preferably across more than one country.
- Demonstrated knowledge of project planning, scope and change control, risk management, partner performance, budget monitoring and donor reporting.
- Experience in monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), data quality and institutional-capacity assessment.
- Understanding of safeguarding and inclusive programme delivery.
- Experience in workforce development, higher education, health training or vaccine-related programmes is desirable.
- Integrated project and programme management.
- Analytical problem-solving and prioritisation.
- Programme performance monitoring and use of evidence.
- Cross-functional coordination and collaboration.
- Donor reporting and concise writing.

jobs.title: Cientista de Dados (Office Based) [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Descrição do Tier

Tier 0: Funcionários IP do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações permanentes (PA) e por prazo determinado (FTA), cujos contratos serão rescindidos ou não renovados durante 2026

Tier 1: Outros funcionários do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações permanentes (PA) e por prazo determinado (FTA) (definidos como candidatos “internos”)

Tier 2: Funcionários do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações temporárias (TA), pessoal com contratos PSA regulares e Voluntários da ONU Expert e Specialist

Tier 3: Todos os demais tipos de contrato do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV e de outras agências, e outros candidatos externos”

Descrição do Escritório/Unidade/Projeto

O PNUD oferece soluções integradas de programas, políticas e financiamento para alcançar os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). Nesse contexto, o PNUD criou a Rede Global de Políticas (Global Policy Network – GPN), uma rede de especialização técnica, de campo e global, em uma ampla gama de áreas de conhecimento e em apoio às soluções-chave (signature solutions) e às capacidades organizacionais previstas no Plano Estratégico. O Birô de Políticas e Apoio a Programas (BPPS) e o Birô de Crises (CB) são os dois birôs âncora da GPN. Nesse contexto, o Hub de Governança, Estado de Direito e Construção da Paz (GRP), um esforço conjunto com o BPPS, oferece liderança e serviços de assessoria para ampliar o impacto do PNUD em governança e construção da paz, assegurando a integração da governança democrática e dos direitos humanos na resposta e na recuperação em situações de crise.

Os governos locais e regionais já são responsáveis por mais de 65% das metas dos ODS, a maioria delas ligada à prestação de serviços básicos, como água, saneamento, mobilidade, ação climática, saúde ou educação. Cidades e territórios têm um papel central na implementação dos ODS, que estão se tornando um novo instrumento de planejamento estratégico e orçamentação no médio e longo prazo. Desde 2015, os governos locais e suas associações têm atuado de forma cada vez mais ativa na promoção dos ODS, por meio de advocacy e do trabalho com a população local e com parceiros para transpor o espírito da Agenda 2030 para cidades e territórios. Os governos locais também passaram a usar os ODS como marco estratégico para oferecer serviços públicos melhores e mais inovadores, vinculados às metas e aos indicadores dos ODS. No âmbito do projeto SDG Local Action, o PNUD é um dos parceiros implementadores do Mayors Challenge, uma iniciativa global para repensar os serviços mais essenciais que as cidades prestam aos seus moradores.

Nesse contexto, o projeto SDG Local Action busca contratar um(a) Cientista de Dados para apoiar a implementação do projeto Mayors Challenge 2025 no Rio de Janeiro, Brasil. O projeto implementa uma metodologia de política pública orientada por dados para antecipar as necessidades dos cidadãos e oferecer serviços de forma proativa, com potencial de replicação em diferentes públicos-alvo. Sua aplicação inicial se dá por meio da Plataforma Pequenos Cariocas, iniciativa prioritária da Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro voltada à primeira infância. O projeto utiliza o Registro Municipal Integrado (RMI), base de dados consolidada no data lake municipal que integra informações de Saúde, Educação e Assistência Social, possibilitando análises avançadas e uma visão mais integrada dos cidadãos. Com base nessa infraestrutura, o projeto combina modelos analíticos e comunicação proativa, especialmente via WhatsApp, para ampliar o acesso aos serviços e gerar dados que apoiem políticas públicas mais efetivas.

O(A) Cientista de Dados será responsável por liderar iniciativas analíticas e garantir a qualidade e a confiabilidade dos dados que orientam as decisões de políticas públicas, atuando principalmente com o RMI (Registro Municipal Integrado) – data warehouse estratégico que consolida informações de saúde, educação, assistência social e dezenas de outros sistemas municipais – no desenvolvimento de análises, métricas estratégicas e visualizações que apoiem a tomada de decisão baseada em evidências.

Escopo de trabalho

A. Garantir análises exploratórias e estatísticas para apoiar decisões

- Liderar análises exploratórias para identificar padrões, anomalias e oportunidades de melhoria nas bases municipais (saúde, educação e assistência social).

- Criar queries analíticas complexas em SQL (BigQuery) para extrair insights e validar hipóteses.

- Realizar análises estatísticas para apoiar a alocação de recursos e a identificação de vulnerabilidades.

B. Garantir métricas, indicadores e visualizações estratégicas

- Desenvolver e manter métricas estratégicas, KPIs e dashboards que monitorem a efetividade de programas e políticas públicas.

- Criar visualizações e narrativas baseadas em dados para públicos técnicos e executivos.

C. Garantir a qualidade, a confiabilidade e a governança dos dados

- Identificar inconsistências nos dados e propor melhorias sistêmicas.

- Estabelecer e documentar padrões de qualidade de dados, metodologias analíticas e boas práticas para o time.

D. Garantir a articulação com as equipes e os gestores públicos

- Colaborar com as equipes de engenharia de dados, produto e gestores públicos para traduzir requisitos em soluções analíticas robustas.

E. Apoiar a construção e o compartilhamento de conhecimento

- Realizar análises que identifiquem lacunas, oportunidades de integração e necessidades de dados do RMI.

O(A) ocupante da posição desempenha outras atividades compatíveis com seu perfil funcional, conforme necessário para o bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo institucional

Esta posição reporta ao Gerente de Projeto, Rio Mayors Challenge. O(A) ocupante trabalhará em estreita colaboração com a IplanRio, as secretarias municipais relevantes, as equipes técnicas e as contrapartes do PNUD para apoiar a implementação, a coordenação e a elaboração de relatórios do projeto.

Competências

Essenciais (Core)

Alcançar resultados: NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora o próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes, entrega trabalho de qualidade no prazo

Pensar de forma inovadora: NÍVEL 1: Aberto(a) a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, resolve problemas de forma pragmática, promove melhorias

Aprender continuamente: NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar-se com agilidade: NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se a mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Agir com determinação: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra iniciativa e motivação, consegue entregar com calma diante de adversidades, tem confiança

Engajar e construir parcerias: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão em relação aos outros, constrói relações positivas

Promover diversidade e inclusão: NÍVEL 1: Valoriza/respeita as diferenças, tem consciência de vieses inconscientes, enfrenta a discriminação

Competências transversais e técnicas

DATA Data analysis

Capacidade de extrair, analisar e visualizar dados (incluindo dados em tempo real) para gerar insights relevantes e apoiar a tomada de decisão eficaz.

DIGITAL Data governance

Conhecimento de ciência de dados, habilidade para desenvolver ferramentas de gestão de dados, organizar e manter bancos de dados e operar tecnologias de visualização de dados.

DIGITAL Data storytelling and communications

Habilidade para construir uma narrativa em torno de um conjunto de dados e de suas visualizações, de modo a transmitir o significado desses dados de forma poderosa e convincente.

DIGITAL Data strategy and management

Conhecimento para elaborar ou executar uma estratégia de dados ou um marco de gestão de dados.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Working with Evidence and Data

Capacidade de examinar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, embasar conclusões e apoiar a tomada de decisão.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Communication

· Comunicar-se de forma clara, concisa e inequívoca, tanto por escrito quanto oralmente; adaptar as mensagens e escolher os métodos de comunicação conforme o público;

· Capacidade de gerir a comunicação interna e externa, por meio da mídia, das redes sociais e de outros canais apropriados.

Qualificações mínimas do(a) NPSA selecionado(a)

Requisitos mínimos de formação

Diploma universitário de nível avançado (mestrado ou equivalente) em Ciência de Dados, Estatística, Ciência da Computação, Matemática, Economia, Políticas Públicas ou área afim é requisito. Ou

Diploma universitário de primeiro nível (graduação/bacharelado) nas áreas mencionadas acima, combinado com dois anos adicionais de experiência qualificada, será considerado em substituição ao diploma de nível avançado.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante

Candidatos com mestrado (ou equivalente) em uma área de estudo relevante não são obrigados a ter experiência profissional. Candidatos com bacharelado (ou equivalente) são obrigados a ter um mínimo de dois (2) anos de experiência profissional relevante em análise e ciência de dados.

Habilidades desejáveis, além das competências previstas na seção Competências

- Experiência em SQL para queries analíticas complexas, otimização de performance e modelagem de dados (BigQuery).

- Sólida experiência com Python para análise de dados (Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn).

- Experiência em Base estatística forte: análise exploratória de dados (EDA), estatística descritiva e inferencial e testes de hipóteses.

- Experiência comprovada com qualidade de dados, validação, governança e boas práticas de documentação.

- Experiência em ferramentas de visualização e BI (Looker, Metabase, Power BI ou similar) para a criação de dashboards estratégicos.

- Experiência em traduzir perguntas de negócio complexas em análises técnicas e comunicar resultados para diferentes públicos.

- Experiência com versionamento (Git), reprodutibilidade de análises e boas práticas de desenvolvimento analítico.

- Experiência com dbt para transformação, modelagem e documentação de dados.

- Experiência em Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Looker Studio, Cloud Functions).

- Experiência com dados governamentais, políticas públicas ou projetos de impacto social.

- Experiência em ferramentas de qualidade e observabilidade de dados (Great Expectations, dbt tests ou similar).

- Experiência com análise de séries temporais, análise de coorte ou análise geoespacial.

- Experiência com orquestração de pipelines (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster).

- Experiência prévia em definição de padrões, documentação técnica ou mentoria de analistas.

Idioma(s) exigido(s)

Fluência em português é requisito.

Conhecimento funcional de inglês é um diferencial.

Igualdade de oportunidades

Como empregador que oferece igualdade de oportunidades, o UNDP valoriza a diversidade como uma expressão da multiplicidade de nações e culturas onde operamos e, como tal, incentivamos candidatos qualificados de todas as origens a se candidatarem a funções na organização. Nossas decisões de emprego são baseadas no mérito e na adequação à função, sem discriminação.

O UNDP também está comprometido em criar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, onde todo o pessoal seja capacitado a contribuir para nossa missão, seja valorizado, possa prosperar e se beneficiar de oportunidades de carreira abertas a todos.

Assédio sexual, exploração e abuso de autoridade

O UNDP não tolera assédio, assédio sexual, exploração, discriminação e abuso de autoridade. Todos os candidatos selecionados, portanto, passam por verificações relevantes e espera-se que cumpram os respectivos padrões e princípios.

Direito de selecionar múltiplos candidatos

O UNDP reserva-se o direito de selecionar um ou mais candidatos a partir deste anúncio de vaga. Também podemos reter candidaturas e considerar candidatos que se candidatem a este posto para outras posições semelhantes no UNDP, no mesmo nível de classificação e com descrição de funções, experiência e requisitos educacionais semelhantes.

Alerta de fraude

O UNDP não cobra nenhuma taxa em nenhuma etapa do seu processo de recrutamento. Para mais informações, consulte www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Partnership Analyst (Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants Only)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The UNV Field Units (FU) are mainly accountable for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes focused on peace, development and humanitarian needs. The UNV Field Units represent and position UNV in the respective countries and bring UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners from governments, UN entities, civil society and private sector.

Scope of Work

1. Coordinate Country-level partnership development, demand analysis and volunteer mobilization

- Proactively develop and sustain partnerships at the country level with UN agencies, government institutions, civil society and partners to advance UNV’s mandate, identify collaboration opportunities, and ensure effective integration of volunteer solutions into programme delivery.

- Participate in UN collective planning processes (CCA, UNSDCF, humanitarian response plans, thematic task forces) to integrate volunteerism in their implementation.

- Analyze the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, Country Programme Documents, and sectoral strategies to identify priority entry points for integrating UNV volunteer solutions.

- Analyze partner demand and contribute to the development and execution of country-level volunteer mobilization strategies in line with UNV’s Strategic Framework.

- Identify and assess opportunities for the deployment of onsite and online Volunteers across development, humanitarian, and peace portfolios, in line with partner priorities.

- Promote volunteerism at the field level by organizing outreach activities, supporting awareness campaigns, and engaging partners and communities to integrate volunteer solutions into local development and humanitarian initiatives.

- Articulate and present UNV’s value proposition and volunteer modalities to partners through data‑driven briefing materials, presentations, and analytical notes.

- Support national talent attraction and pipeline management based on country demand forecasts and recruitment priorities, in coordination with the Regional Talent Acquisition Analyst.

2. Ensure Business intelligence, demand analysis and planning

- Develop and maintain structured country‑level business intelligence on UN partner mandates, programme pipelines, and emerging priorities relevant to volunteer mobilization.

- Monitor mobilization trends, track key performance indicators, and use corporate tools (CRM, BI reports, UVP) to support planning, forecasting, and strategic decision making.

- Contribute to adapting regional volunteer mobilization priorities into country-specific recommendations, based on partner needs, data analysis, and local context.

- Contribute to the identification of thematic volunteer solutions, pilot initiatives, and joint approaches aligned with national needs and UN priorities in the country.

3. Ensure Duty of Care

- Coordinate closely with the Field Security Officer and host entities to ensure that UN Volunteers are adequately informed of, and compliant with, all applicable security policies, procedures, and risk‑mitigation measures.

- Ensure timely and compliant medical evacuation support for UN Volunteers, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV

- Ensure the well‑being and performance of serving UN Volunteers by maintaining regular contact, conducting periodic field visits to duty stations, and engaging with supervisors and counterparts to address emerging issues and support effective service delivery.

- In consultation with relevant sections, provide timely support to the UN Volunteers throughout their volunteer’s journey

4. Ensure Management, knowledge building and sharing

- Develop and manage the implementation of the Field Unit’s annual work plan and set performance indicators, including management and reporting on UNV operational support funds and budget;

- Facilitate the effective functioning of the UNV country presence by ensuring coordinated service delivery and promoting a supportive and collaborative work environment that supports learning, professionalism.

- Manage any UNV assigned personnel within the FU including supervision, performance assessment and capacity development.

- Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: May supervise the Communications personnel in the Regional Office.

Institutional Arrangement

Reporting to the Portfolio Manager/Specialist, Regional Office, the Partnership Analyst leads country‑level analytical and partnership support to advance UNV’s volunteer mobilization agenda in the country. The position combines strategic partnership analysis, business intelligence, and operational coordination, while overseeing the team of UN Volunteers supporting Field Unit activities.

The incumbent is responsible for strengthening UNV’s positioning as a solution provider for UN partners, supporting increased and diversified volunteer mobilization, and ensuring coherence between country‑level engagement and regional and global UNV priorities.

As UNV is a systemwide service administered by UNDP, FUs are hosted within relevant UNDP offices, collaborating closely with the UNDP Resident Representative and the UN Resident Coordinator. The Partnership Analyst ensures compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations.

Competencies

CORE

Achieve Results

- Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively:

- Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously:

- Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination:

- Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner:

- Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Negotiation and Influence:

- Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Results-based Management

- Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Partnerships Management

- Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

Event planning and execution

- Ability to plan, manage and execute of public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNV's overall brand and mandate.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in partnership, social sciences, international development, project management, public/business administration or related fields is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) in partnerships, development cooperation, international relations, research, programme analysis, preferably in a humanitarian, development and/or peace related field;

- Experience in partnerships, inter-agency collaboration, or stakeholder engagement is required.

- Experience conducting analytical work such as partner mapping, business intelligence, demand analysis, preparation of briefs, concept notes, or knowledge products.

- Strong drafting, analytical, and communication skills, with the ability to translate strategic priorities into clear, actionable inputs.

- Proficiency in the use of standard office software and digital collaboration tools.

- Openness to embrace Digital Transformation and use of new technologies.

- Experience working directly with the United Nations system, UNDP, UNV, or other international organizations is an asset

- Previous experience in volunteer management, promotion of volunteerism, or engagement with civil society organizations is a distinctive advantage.

- Experience supporting partnership development is a strong advantage.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and Arabic
