This position will be located at the Department of Forestry (DOF), Misnitry of Agriculture and Forestry (MAF), Vientiane Capital, with occasionally travel to project offices in Savannakhet, Saravan, Chamapsack and Sekong provinces.

Duties and Responsibilities

The position will have lead technical responsibilities under the overall guidance of the Director General of the Department of Forestry (DOF), who serves as the National Project Director, and the supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Lao PDR and the Head of the Natural Resources Management, Climate Change, and Disaster Risk Reduction Unit. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: (i) technical project activities with a focus on monitoring, evaluation, and reporting; (ii) developing annual workplans and budgets, (iii) ensuring integration with all outcomes; (iv) guiding activities in provinces; (v) coordinating with other related projects; (vi) day-to-day project management; (vii) and following up on monitoring results and findings related to project outputs and outcomes.

S/he will provide high level advice and guidance to DOF/Government of Lao PDR and UNDP in the following areas:

- Technical and strategic guidance : Provide rigorous analysis and advice to the Government of Lao PDR on the assessment and formulation of national policies and regulations related to Primary Forest Landscapes (PFL). This includes capacity assessment and development planning for key institutions and private sector entities to mainstream PFLs in safeguard assessment and planning approaches. Develop the Annamite Management Strategy, ensuring consultation with all relevant stakeholders, prioritizing investments for PFLs, establishing coordination mechanisms, and monitoring the effectiveness of the planning process. Support the re-alignment of policies, planning, and financial systems to promote the implementation of the Annamite Management Strategy.

- Provision of technical advice: Offer technical advice, capacity building, institutional support, and project management support to the Government to ensure the effective and timely delivery of the Project.

- Support resource mobilization : Strengthen partnerships with relevant development organizations, UN agencies, and within the government network. Enhance coordination with key stakeholders to generate multiple benefits through strengthened protection of primary forest landscapes in Lao PDR

1. Strategic guidance, rigorous analysis and advice to the Government of Lao PDR to effectively consider, develop and implement sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry.

- Provide technical input and policy advice and supervise implementation of project activities with a special attention on planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting, and quality control of project outputs;

- Advise the Government and UNDP on the linkages with other major programmes or projects of other agencies, organizations or departments and UN agencies;

- Advisory and support in drafting and review of strategic and technical documents on sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, strategic environmental assessment, sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry such as policy papers or other analytical products in collaboration with other technical staff and consultants and Government counterparts;

- Ensure the development of cross-project linkages with other relevant UN and development partner projects for maximizing impact;

- Facilitate information sharing and dialogue within the donor community and prepare briefs and policy papers related to the context and focus of the project;

- Assist the Government in information sharing/knowledge management in the themes related to the scope of the project;

- Provide other advice and support as may be required by the Government and UNDP as is to be expected in a dynamic process of project implementation and changing circumstances;

- Systematically record the results of the project and provide substantive contribution to the UNDP/GEF annual reports as well as knowledge products.

2. Provision of technical advice, capacity building, institutional support, project management and implementation support to the Government to ensure effective and timely delivery of the project.

- Advise, support the relevant parties to develop a realistic annual and quarterly workplans and a corresponding budget plan with clearly stated milestones contributing to the achievement of target outcomes and outputs defined in the project document;

- Ensure the participation and involvement of relevant stakeholders in project activities at national, provincial and district levels in the project planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting;

- Support implementation of project activities to ensure delivery of resources and results according to planned targets, activities, and prepare the budget plan at the national, provincial and district levels;

- Ensure the development of linkages across the project outcomes and outputs, as well as advice and update the National Project Director and UNDP on the project progress on a regular basis;

- Advise, support and implement Annual Project Reviews, annual audits, mid-term evaluation and final evaluation of the Project in collaboration with the project team and consultants;

- Support recruitment of competent national and international experts that are needed by different outcomes/components of the project;

- Organize and oversee consultant input, develop detailed Terms of References for national and international consultants and contractors in collaboration with Project Manager, National Project Director, UNDP and support in procurement of goods, organization of training sessions, seminars, etc;

- Liaise with all consultants and project teams to ensure that the planned deliverables are completed in timely manner within the contract period;

- Support and be involved in organizing and facilitating project meetings, workshops etc. with relevant substantive inputs;

- Identify and develop synthesis of best practices and lessons learned for organizational sharing and learning;

- Closely work with the Project Coordinator/Monitoring & Evaluation and Reporting Officer to provide capacity development for key government staff at the national, provincial and district levels to support better informed and planned for the project, protected area conservation, sustainable forest and land management, protected area management, spatial planning, agricultural and agro-forestry;

- Closely work with the Project Coordinator/Monitoring & Evaluation and Reporting Officer to provide capacity development for key government staff at the national, provincial and district levels to support and complete the Protected Area sites’ Management Effectiveness Tracking Tool (METT), Capacity Development Monitoring Scorecard and other tools as required by GEF 8;

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Energy and Environment Unit of UNDP Kazakhstan supports national efforts to advance a green, low-carbon and climate-resilient economy and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Its portfolio covers climate change mitigation and adaptation, renewable energy, energy efficiency and power system modernization, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture and food systems, sustainable land and water management, waste management, disaster risk reduction and sustainable natural resource use.

Working with government institutions, the private sector, civil society, academia and international partners, the Unit provides policy advice, technical assistance and capacity development. It promotes green and sustainable finance, supports access to international environmental and climate funding, and helps develop investment opportunities and innovative financing instruments aligned with national development priorities. The Unit also strengthens institutional frameworks and supports the application of innovative and digital solutions, while integrating gender equality and inclusive development across its work.

Within this portfolio, the Government of Japan-funded project “The Project for Development of Sustainable Rare Metal and Rare Earth Minerals Value Chains through Environmental Measures” supports the sustainable development of Kazakhstan’s minerals sector. The project combines policy and analytical support, environmental monitoring and capacity development to promote environmentally responsible mineral value chains.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Policy Advice

- Provide specialized knowledge and expertise in critical minerals, sustainable mineral value chains and natural resource governance within the context of the project;

- Analyze existing policies, frameworks and regulations governing the minerals sector at various levels to identify opportunities, gaps, and barriers for sustainable sector development;

- Assess the regulatory landscape to ensure alignment of mineral sector policies with national development priorities and relevant international environmental and sustainability standards;

- Support the development of policies, strategies and action plans for environmentally responsible mineral sector development, considering input from stakeholders and best practices;

- Establish mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of relevant sectoral policies, providing recommendations for improvements;

- Analyze financial mechanisms and funding opportunities for sustainable mineral value chains and related environmental measures, identifying potential sources of support;

- Advocate for the integration of environmental sustainability, responsible resource management and value chain development into relevant sectoral policies, plans, and programs;

- Support the strengthening of institutional arrangements and procedures for sustainable mineral resource governance in Kazakhstan.

Collaborate with relevant government, industry representatives, research organizations and other stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of sustainable mineral sector policies and practices;

- Engage with policymakers, government officials, the private sector, NGOs, and community leaders to build consensus and support environmentally responsible mineral sector development;

- Coordinate between various stakeholders involved in mineral sector policy development and implementation to ensure coherence and efficiency;

- Translate complex technical and policy concepts into accessible language and communicate the importance of sustainable mineral value chains and environmental responsibility to different audiences;

- Design and conduct capacity-building activities related to critical minerals, sector governance and environmental sustainability, enabling stakeholders to understand and contribute to effective policy development and implementation;

- Prepare technical reports, policy briefs, and communication materials to communicate policy analysis, progress, and recommendations.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the project.

- Organize training, workshops, and capacity building activities in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on project related issues. Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

- Promote advocacy on development trends and opportunities to collaborate in coordination with the project partners, stakeholders, and UNDP communications staff.

The Project Analyst reports to the Project Manager. The job holder will ensure to provide quality advice to Project manager and comply with appropriate UNDP policies and procedures.

Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

UNDP is working to strengthen new frameworks for development, disaster risk reduction and climate change. We support countries' efforts to achieve the new Sustainable Development Goals, which will guide global development priorities through 2030. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Jordan supports national efforts to achieve sustainable development through integrated programmes aligned with the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). UNDP Jordan works across key pillars including Governance and Social Cohesion, Inclusive Growth, Climate Change and Energy, and Environment and Biodiversity, with a strong focus on advancing resilience, institutional effectiveness, and inclusive development.

The Governance and Social Cohesion Pillar at UNDP Jordan Country Office leads the design and implementation of integrated programmes that support inclusive governance, social cohesion, rule of law, and peacebuilding. The Pillar focuses on strengthening institutional effectiveness, promoting civic engagement, enhancing accountability and transparency, and supporting national efforts in preventing violent extremism (PVE), human rights, and inclusive political participation.

The Programme Analyst will contribute to a diverse and evolving portfolio of projects implemented in close partnership with government entities, civil society organizations, development partners, and UN agencies. The position plays a key role in advancing UNDP’s strategic positioning in governance and social cohesion by supporting programme delivery, strengthening partnerships, and contributing to knowledge generation and policy dialogue at national and sub-national levels.

Bhutan has established a strong legal and institutional foundation for the rule of law and access to justice. The justice sector continues to strengthen coordination, professional capacity, service delivery and institutional accountability so that justice services are responsive to people’s needs.

The Justice Sector Strategic Plan II provides a framework for coordinated reform, including effective leadership and collaboration, competent justice service providers, responsive and accountable services, accessible and inclusive justice services, and adequate infrastructure. These priorities are also aligned with Bhutan’s 13th Five-Year Plan objective of strengthening inclusive, effective and accessible institutions and promoting transparent rule of law and public oversight.

The EU- and UNDP-supported project “Strengthening People-Centric and Inclusive Access to Justice in Bhutan” contributes to these priorities by supporting justice institutions and partners to improve access to justice, particularly for women, persons with disabilities and other groups that may face barriers when seeking legal information, assistance and remedies. The project promotes people-centred justice, disability inclusion, gender equality, legal aid, institutional coordination, capacity development, accessibility, and evidence-based programming.

The internship will provide a structured learning opportunity for a motivated young professional to contribute to the implementation, monitoring, documentation and communication of project activities while gaining practical exposure to UNDP programme management and Bhutan’s justice sector.

The internship is intended to support the Access to Justice Project with research, coordination, documentation, monitoring, knowledge management, communications and administrative tasks. The intern will work under close supervision by Project Manager and will be given assignments that contribute to both project delivery and professional learning.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Governance Portfolio Manager and the direct supervision of the Project Manager or designated supervisor, the intern will support the following areas:

- Research and Technical Support

- Conduct desk research on access to justice, people-centred justice, legal aid, disability inclusion, gender equality, youth participation, digital justice and related governance issues.

- Assist in preparing background notes, briefing materials, presentations and summaries of good national, regional and global practices relevant to the project.

- Support the collection, organization and basic analysis of project data, including information disaggregated by sex, age, disability and location where such data are available and appropriate.

- Support preparation of technical input for trainings, consultations, accessibility audits, monitoring visits and stakeholder meetings.

- Programme Implementation, Monitoring and Reporting

- Support preparation and updating of activity plans, participant lists, agendas, minutes, action trackers and follow-up notes.

- Assist with documentation of project activities, outputs, results, lessons learned and emerging risks.

- Contribute to draft progress reports, donor updates, presentations, human-interest stories and other project documents.

- Support compilation and filing of evidence required for project monitoring, results reporting and quality assurance.

- Stakeholder Coordination and Event Support

- Provide coordination support for engagement with justice sector institutions, civil society organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities, Local Governments, academia, development partners and other stakeholders.

- Assist in organizing workshops, meetings, trainings, consultations, monitoring visits and public awareness activities.

- Prepare logistical and administrative documents, including invitations, attendance records, meeting materials and activity files.

- Participate in relevant project activities and prepare concise records of key discussions, decisions and action points.

- Knowledge Management and Communications

- Support development of knowledge and advocacy products such as briefs, presentations, factsheets, stories, social media content and communication materials.

- Document good practices and lessons from legal aid, disability-inclusive justice, accessibility, capacity building and community-level initiatives.

- Administrative Support and Learning

- Provide routine administrative and logistical support to the project team as required.

- Participate in team meetings, learning sessions and relevant UNDP events.

- Undertake other related tasks that are consistent with the purpose and learning objectives of the internship.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

La promoción de la igualdad de género y el empoderamiento de las mujeres constituye una dimensión central del mandato del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD). El Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2029 orienta el trabajo de la organización hacia cuatro objetivos estratégicos —prosperidad para todas las personas, gobernanza eficaz, resiliencia ante las crisis y un planeta sano—, impulsados por tres aceleradores del desarrollo humano: la transformación digital y la inteligencia artificial, la igualdad de género y la financiación sostenible. Esta posición se sitúa particularmente en la intersección entre los aceleradores de igualdad de género y financiación sostenible, buscando que las decisiones económicas y financieras contribuyan de manera más explícita a resultados de igualdad.

La Estrategia de Igualdad de Género del PNUD 2026-2029 reconoce que las desigualdades se reproducen también a través de las instituciones, las políticas y las decisiones de financiación. En el marco del acelerador de financiación sostenible, el PNUD plantea apoyar a los países para alinear recursos públicos y privados con la igualdad de género y el empoderamiento económico de las mujeres; movilizar inversión privada hacia empresas lideradas por mujeres y mercados inclusivos; fortalecer las finanzas públicas para generar resultados de igualdad; y promover enfoques integrales vinculados con los Marcos Nacionales Integrados de Financiamiento (INFF), la cartera de Finanzas Públicas para los ODS y otras iniciativas corporativas como Equanomics.

En Ecuador, esta agenda abre oportunidades para fortalecer la incorporación de la igualdad de género en la política fiscal, el análisis económico, las finanzas públicas, la inclusión financiera, el financiamiento sostenible y los instrumentos de financiación para el desarrollo. Asimismo, permite ampliar el uso de datos y evidencia económica para comprender las brechas que enfrentan las mujeres en materia de ingresos, empleo, cuidados, pobreza, acceso a activos y servicios financieros, emprendimiento, participación económica y acceso a oportunidades productivas, y traducir esos hallazgos en mejores políticas, programas e instrumentos.

Una prioridad inicial de la posición será apoyar el proyecto “Advancing Fiscal Policy Coherence for Climate, Nature and Inclusive Development in Ecuador”, que busca fortalecer la inteligencia fiscal, la coherencia de políticas y las capacidades institucionales para mejorar la calidad del gasto público y orientar futuras reformas. Tras la reorganización institucional del Ejecutivo, el trabajo se articulará principalmente con el Viceministerio de Economía y Finanzas del Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo, así como con otras instituciones y actores vinculados con la gestión fiscal y financiera desde una perspectiva de género.

El componente de igualdad de género del proyecto busca evitar que el gasto relacionado con clima y naturaleza sea considerado neutral al género. Entre sus prioridades se encuentran la incorporación de criterios sensibles al género en el Clasificador Verde; el desarrollo de una metodología e indicadores para analizar el gasto climático y de naturaleza desde la igualdad de género; el fortalecimiento de esta dimensión en la Coherencia de la Política Fiscal y los procesos vinculados al INFF; y la construcción de una ruta institucional para el Sello de Igualdad de Género o un mecanismo equivalente de fortalecimiento y rendición de cuentas. La hoja de ruta técnica identifica además oportunidades para avanzar en análisis de incidencia fiscal, evaluación ex ante y ex post de medidas fiscales y una mayor utilización de datos desagregados para la toma de decisiones.

De manera complementaria, PNUD Ecuador busca consolidar un portafolio más amplio de género y finanzas para el desarrollo. Esto incluye el acompañamiento a instituciones financieras públicas y privadas para fortalecer productos, servicios, carteras e instrumentos con perspectiva de género; el trabajo con mecanismos de regulación y supervisión financiera; la integración de género en iniciativas de financiamiento de biodiversidad y sostenibilidad, incluido BIOFIN; el fortalecimiento de la inclusión financiera de las mujeres; y la exploración de soluciones como seguros, microseguros, seguros paramétricos, garantías, mecanismos de distribución de riesgos, financiamiento combinado y mercados de capitales. Estos esfuerzos podrán articularse con procesos del Sello de Igualdad de Género para Instituciones Financieras y para el Sello para el Sector Privado, complementando el acompañamiento institucional con una mirada especializada sobre resultados financieros y económicos.

En este contexto, PNUD Ecuador requiere incorporar un/a Asociado/a en Género y Finanzas para el Desarrollo que brinde apoyo técnico especializado al Analista de Género y contribuya, en articulación con el/la Analista de Programa-Economista de la Oficina País, a conectar la igualdad de género con las agendas económicas, fiscales y financieras. La posición tendrá un carácter de análisis aplicado, ejecución técnica, acompañamiento programático y seguimiento, con capacidad para trabajar con datos, indicadores, herramientas cuantitativas y evidencia económica, así como para apoyar el desarrollo de nuevas alianzas e iniciativas en este ámbito.

Acuerdo institucional

La persona contratada estará bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Género de PNUD Ecuador. Además, el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto efectuará co-supervisión de esta posición, y la persona contratada trabajará en coordinación técnica con el/la Analista de Programa - Economista de la Oficina País. Asimismo, coordinará con las áreas programáticas y operativas, los equipos de proyecto, las contrapartes nacionales, instituciones financieras, socios, consultores/as y equipos regionales o globales pertinentes. La posición no tendrá responsabilidades de supervisión de personal.

Duties and Responsibilities

Bajo la orientación y supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Género, y en coordinación técnica con el/la Analista de Programa - Economista de PNUD Ecuador, la persona contratada brindará apoyo especializado para fortalecer la integración de la igualdad de género en la política fiscal, el análisis económico, las finanzas públicas, el sector financiero y las soluciones de financiación para el desarrollo. Su prioridad será la implementación del componente de género del proyecto de Coherencia de la Política Fiscal, sin perjuicio de apoyar otras iniciativas y oportunidades de la Oficina País relacionadas con género, empoderamiento económico y finanzas. Sus principales funciones y responsabilidades serán las siguientes:

- Apoyar la integración de la igualdad de género en la política fiscal, las finanzas públicas y los instrumentos de planificación financiera: Apoyar la incorporación de criterios sensibles al género en los Clasificadores de Gasto del Gobierno Nacional y en las orientaciones, herramientas, reportes y procesos presupuestarios asociados, de manera que el gasto público pueda analizarse también por su contribución a la igualdad de género y al empoderamiento de las mujeres. Contribuir al desarrollo y aplicación de metodologías, indicadores y campos de información para el análisis fiscal sensible al género, incluyendo ejercicios piloto sobre gasto climático, de naturaleza u otras áreas de política pública. Apoyar la integración de la perspectiva de género en los análisis de Coherencia de la Política Fiscal, los procesos del INFF y otros ejercicios de política fiscal, incluyendo análisis de incidencia, impactos diferenciados y opciones de reforma cuando corresponda. Apoyar la construcción e implementación de una ruta institucional con el Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo para fortalecer la gestión fiscal sensible al género, incluyendo el Sello de Igualdad de Género para Instituciones Públicas o un mecanismo alternativo de institucionalización, capacidades y rendición de cuentas. Preparar y dar seguimiento a insumos técnicos, matrices, reportes, reuniones y productos del componente de género del proyecto, en coordinación con el Analista de Género, los equipos responsables, las contrapartes y el/la Analista de Programa - Economista de la CO.

- Desarrollar análisis económicos y cuantitativos para la igualdad de género, el empoderamiento y la inclusión económica de las mujeres: Recopilar, depurar y analizar información económica, social, fiscal y financiera proveniente de encuestas, registros administrativos, bases de datos y otras fuentes, incorporando desagregaciones relevantes para identificar brechas y resultados diferenciados. Apoyar el desarrollo y aplicación de indicadores, métricas, modelos, simulaciones y ejercicios de análisis distributivo o de incidencia que permitan comprender los efectos de políticas, programas e instrumentos económicos y financieros sobre mujeres y hombres. Contribuir a análisis sobre de las mujeres, incluyendo pobreza y pobreza multidimensional, empleo e ingresos, cuidados, acceso a activos, emprendimiento, mercados, crédito y servicios financieros, de acuerdo con las prioridades de la Oficina País. Preparar notas técnicas, visualizaciones, tableros, resúmenes ejecutivos y recomendaciones de política basadas en evidencia, y apoyar iniciativas corporativas o nacionales que vinculen economía e igualdad de género, incluyendo enfoques como Equanomics cuando corresponda.

- Fortalecer la integración de género en el sector financiero y en las soluciones de financiación para el desarrollo: Brindar apoyo técnico a iniciativas con instituciones financieras públicas y privadas, entidades de regulación o supervisión, cooperativas y otros actores del sistema financiero para identificar y reducir brechas de género en productos, servicios, carteras, datos, gobernanza e inclusión financiera. Apoyar los componentes económicos y financieros de procesos del Sello de Igualdad de Género para instituciones públicas o para el sector privado vinculados con entidades financieras, en articulación con los equipos responsables de dichos procesos. Contribuir al diseño o adaptación de instrumentos y soluciones de financiación para el desarrollo con perspectiva de género, incluyendo crédito, garantías, seguros y microseguros, instrumentos paramétricos, mecanismos de distribución de riesgos, financiamiento combinado u otras soluciones pertinentes. Apoyar iniciativas de financiamiento sostenible, biodiversidad y naturaleza, mercados de capitales y otras agendas relacionadas con BIOFIN, banca de desarrollo, bolsas de valores u otros socios, identificando oportunidades para ampliar el acceso de las mujeres a recursos, inversiones y beneficios.

- Apoyar el desarrollo del portafolio, las alianzas y nuevas iniciativas de género y finanzas para el desarrollo: Identificar y sistematizar oportunidades de programación, cooperación y movilización de recursos en la intersección entre igualdad de género, economía y finanzas, contribuyendo al fortalecimiento del pipeline de la Oficina País. Preparar insumos para notas conceptuales, propuestas, términos de referencia, análisis, presentaciones y otros documentos relacionados con nuevas iniciativas de género y finanzas para el desarrollo. Apoyar la articulación técnica con instituciones públicas, entidades financieras, organismos reguladores, sector privado, academia, sociedad civil, organismos internacionales, donantes y otros actores relevantes para desarrollar alianzas y oportunidades de colaboración. Brindar apoyo, cuando sea requerido, a otras áreas y proyectos de la Oficina País en asuntos relacionados con análisis económico, empoderamiento económico, inclusión financiera, política fiscal y financiación para la igualdad de género, dentro del nivel de responsabilidad de la posición.

- Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes: Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos. Brindar apoyo a otras actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción. Brindar apoyo en la difusión e intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas. Realizar contribuciones valiosas a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas.

El/la titular desempeñará otras actividades dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y de la Organización.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities.

The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia for its current Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

(1) Human Development

(2) Nature, Decarbonisation and Resilience

(3) Economic and Digital Transformation

This position is located primarily in Communication Unit under overall guidance of the Head of Communication. The team has identified a growing need for effective communication across various language barriers. To ensure accurate and efficient exchange of information, the team aims to establish a comprehensive framework for interpretation, translation, and editing services. This will enhance the overall quality and accessibility of documents and reports, enabling seamless communication within and outside the organization.

The position is designed to provide high-quality interpretation services for meetings, conferences, and other official gatherings to ensure effective cross-language communication. The post holder is also expected to facilitate accurate and timely translation of various documents, particularly large reports, to enable broader accessibility and understanding. And he/she is expected to enhance the quality and coherence of English language documents through professional editing, ensuring clarity and consistency in content.

Translation Services focusing on the following results:

• Translation various reports, official documents, and correspondences including technical documents.

• Linguistic and cultural adaptation to ensure accurate conveyance of messages.

• Production of 100% accurate translation from Indonesia language to English or vice versa of various documents, written/ recorded speeches, talking points, presentations, brochures, fact sheets, reports, website content, press releases, etc. as assigned b UNDP.

• Utilization of the appropriate terminology considering the style and nuances of the original text. Areas frequently covered by such documents include legal, public relations and Business, and technical texts, etc.

• Corrections as required by UNDP or its partners and re-submission of corrected text within the agreed timeframe.

Interpretation Services focusing on the following results:

• Consecutive and simultaneous interpretation provided during project events, including ceremonies, workshops, webinars, trainings, conferences, and community information events.

• Consecutive and simultaneous interpretation provided during technical working group meetings and meetings between international advisers/experts or UNDP representatives and local counterparts.

English Editing Services focusing on the following results:

• Comprehensive editing and proofreading of publications, reports, documents, and presentations to ensure clarity, coherence, grammatical accuracy, and formatting consistency.

• Quality review of translated and edited materials to ensure accuracy, consistency, and error-free final outputs.

• Identification and mitigation of language-service risks, including contingency measures for unforeseen challenges or delays.

• Provision of advice to colleagues to use gender sensitive language in translation.

The incumbent of the position should avoid any kind of discriminatory behavior including gender discrimination and ensure that:

• Human rights and gender equality is prioritized as an ethical principle within all actions;

• Activities are designed and implemented in accordance with "Social and Environmental Standards of UNDP";

• Any kind of diversities based on ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, disability, religion, class, gender are respected within all implementations including data production;

• Inclusive approach is reflected within all actions and implementations, in that sense an enabling and accessible setup in various senses such as disability gender language barrier is created;

• Necessary arrangements to provide gender parity within all committees, meetings, trainings etc. introduced.

• The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the Head of Communication will provide the interpretation and translation services on an ongoing basis, adhering to the specific timelines of the events and document submissions.

Editing services will follow a predefined schedule to ensure timely completion without compromising quality.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is a global organization that is part of the broader United Nations System, dedicated to promoting sustainable development. Established in 1965, UNDP plays a pivotal role in supporting nations in their efforts to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and advance socio-economic development. With a focus on inclusive and equitable growth, UNDP provides technical expertise, mobilizes financial resources, and delivers policy and other services to support the formulation and implementation of effective development strategies and solutions that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates in over 170 countries and territories, collaborating with local partners, governments, and other stakeholders to build resilient communities and foster sustainable development. UNDP's initiatives span a wide range of areas, including climate change, gender equality, governance, and crisis response, embodying its commitment to creating a better and more sustainable future for people across the globe.

The Office of Human Resources (OHR) is part of the UNDP Bureau for Management Services (BMS) of UNDP. It is the anchor of the global HR function for UNDP, providing strategy and policy setting, guidance and oversight. In addition, BMS/OHR provides a broad range of HR advisory and talent management services enabling UNDP to deliver fully integrated development solutions to enable its workforce to deliver more and better results. BMS/OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by developing high quality and innovative human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

With its People for 2030 strategy, OHR aims to be at the leading edge of HR in the international development sector by strengthening and innovating its human resources solutions and driving transformation across UNDP.

Within this innovative, ambitious and dynamic context, BMS/OHR is seeking high calibre HR professionals with a strong HR background, and the capacity, commitment, and attitude needed to drive a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, transformative results, as well as inclusion, respect and trust.

People Programmes and Partnership team (PPP) works to enable a diverse pipeline of people programmes, hereunder Early Talent initiatives and outreach with a vision to nurture the rejuvenation of UNDPs workforce, as well as manifesting itself as a Centre for Excellence in providing solutions and services on Early Talent programmes and Management across UN system agency clients, member states as well as other potential partners.

These programmes include the Junior Professional Officer, Specialist for Development, Graduate Programme as well as Internship and Fellowship Programmes. PPP also manages the Technical Expert Secondment Programme, and it equally engages in designing and developing new people programmes meeting strategic organizational objectives of both UNDP and Partners

Position Purpose

PPP provides end-to-end HR Services to Donors, UN Agencies and staff members hired under these programmes. Hereunder, services on recruitment, assessment and selection, HR services, advisory, learning and career development, partner relations and reporting, and financial oversight.

Under the strategic leadership of the Chief, People Programme and Partnerships (PPP), the HR Specialist will contribute to the development and roll out of the Early Professionals for Impact and Change strategy (EPIC), as well as provides oversight in management of People Programmes (JPO/SDP, Fellowship, Secondment Programmes, and oversight of HR services ensuring their transparency and integrity. The HR Specialist acts as team lead of HR Associates providing HR services to young professionals in both UNDP and 14 partner agencies, and government secondment programmes as well as leads a part-time Learning analyst to deliver learning and development offerings to early professionals. The HR Specialist promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and promotes the maintenance of high staff morale and engagement.

The HR Specialist works with a wide range of strategic partners and clients including staff, donor governments, UN partner organizations as well as UNDP offices. The HR Specialist works closely with the OHR HR Business Partners, Talent Development Unit, Talent Acquisition, Deployment and Succession team, People Analytics Unit, GSSU-HR and UNDP hiring offices in delivering client-oriented services in People Programme management, HR service delivery and design of talent acquisition strategies.

UNDP has adopted a portfolio approach to effectively respond to changing business needs and leverage relevant synergies and linkages to achieve its strategic goals. This is in recognition of the interconnected nature of development challenges that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated and systemic response. Therefore, all UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

3. Coordinate and manage recruitment and career services for People Programmes to UNDP and Partner Agencies.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. It is comprised of the Audit Section and the Investigations Section. The Investigations Section (OAI/IS) is charged with conducting misconduct investigations and with compliance review of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures and has sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

In its performance of misconduct investigations, OAI/IS addresses allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations and policies that govern the conduct of UNDP staff and other personnel. OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP. OAI’s capacity includes specialized SEAH, IT forensics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), data analytics, and proactive investigations units and resources.

As the provider of a professional, secure and reliable mechanism that responds to and addresses reports of possible misconduct or fraud, OAI is the sole and centralized custodian of a unique dataset of information regarding possible irregularities across UNDP’s operations. As such, OAI has a role to play in providing real-time and data-supported advice to management on wrongdoing risks, controls, lessons and mitigation strategies, and to use this information to develop intelligence-led detection, diversion and proactive investigation strategies that prevent and deter wrongdoing without relying solely on received reports.

OAI conducts misconduct investigations in accordance with the Uniform Principles and Guidelines for Investigations endorsed by the 10th Conference of International Investigators, with the UNDP Legal Framework for Addressing Non-Compliance with the United Nations Standards of Conduct, and with the OAI Investigation Guidelines.

OAI’s Investigations Section has established Units, under the supervision of Investigation Chiefs, that are comprised of (a) functionally specialized teams and (b) regionally focused misconduct investigation teams. This structure facilitates the accessibility of specialized functions to the entirety of the Investigations Section under the guidance and leadership of a manager and ensures close and rigorous oversight of investigation matters, also under the appropriate level of leadership.

Position Purpose

The Investigations Team Lead (HQ/LAC) functionally reports to the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1, under the overall supervision of the Deputy Director (Investigations). Under the supervision of the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1, the primary role of the Team Lead (HQ/LAC) is to oversee, supervise and conduct investigations into alleged misconduct that falls within OAI’s mandate, as outlined in ‘Organizational Context’ above, and that relates to UNDP Headquarters and the Latin America and Caribbean region.

The Investigations Team Lead (HQ/LAC) will supervise the work of the team, including but not limited to Investigators at the P3 level and all other personnel assigned to the investigation team covering UNDP Headquarters and the Latin America and Caribbean, and will complete their annual performance appraisals.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Lead investigations management and lead and manage Headquarters / Latin America and Caribbean (HQ/LAC) team

- Under the overall supervision of the Chief, Investigations, provides day‑to‑day operational leadership of the HQ/LAC Investigations Team, ensuring the effective delivery of investigative activities in line with OAI priorities, policies, and performance expectations.

- Manages the assigned investigative portfolio, including allocation of cases, prioritization of workstreams, workload balancing, and monitoring of progress to ensure investigations are completed timely, efficiently, and to a high professional standard, escalating risks and capacity issues to the Chief as appropriate.

- Overseas and directs investigations, ensuring that appropriate investigative strategies are developed, all relevant lines of inquiry are pursued, and investigative resources are deployed proportionately and effectively.

- Reviews and edits of investigation reports prepared by team investigators and other relevant documents to ensure they are of a high standard, providing an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations.

- Leads and personally conduct investigations only in complex, high‑risk, or sensitive matters, while otherwise providing technical direction, oversight, and quality assurance to investigations conducted by team members.

- Provides first line managerial and functional supervision to investigators and other personnel assigned to the team, including setting expectations, clarifying priorities, and ensuring alignment with OAI standards and values.

- Conducts regular and structured case and performance reviews with team members to assess investigative progress, identify quality or procedural gaps, and provide corrective direction where necessary.

- Holds direct accountability for the quality, timeliness, and defensibility of investigative outputs produced by the team prior to submission to the Chief, including investigation reports, findings, and recommendations.

- Identifies and addresses underperformance, skills gaps, or conduct issues at first instance through coaching, feedback, and performance management measures, escalating matters to the Chief in accordance with UNDP procedures where required.

- Ensures that investigations conducted by the team comply with international investigative standards, UNDP legal and policy frameworks, and OAI Investigation Guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures.

- Ensures due process, confidentiality, information security, and victim‑centered approaches are consistently applied, particularly in sensitive cases involving sexual misconduct, retaliation, or abuse of authority.

- Oversee the collection, handling, analysis, and safeguarding of evidence, ensuring proper chain of custody and appropriate handling of physical, digital, and testimonial evidence.

- Identifies investigative, procedural, or institutional risks emerging from casework and escalates systemic or high‑risk issues to the Chief to inform broader oversight, mitigation, or proactive responses.

- Oversees and promotes the effective use of investigative technologies, including case management systems, analytical software, open‑source intelligence tools, and artificial intelligence–enabled solutions, to enhance investigative efficiency, accuracy, and timeliness.

- Guides team members in the responsible and ethical use of AI and advanced analytics, ensuring compliance with confidentiality, due process, and information security requirements.

- Identifies opportunities to streamline investigative processes, improve workflows, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives under the strategic direction of the Chief.

- Acts as a key operational interlocutor with internal stakeholders (including legal services, HR, ethics, procurement, and management) on investigative matters, escalating sensitive or high‑impact issues to the Chief as appropriate.

- Ensures that case records, databases, and documentation for matters under the team’s responsibility are accurate, complete, and up to date, supporting institutional accountability and auditability.

- Formulates and recommends case closure decisions, including assessments of evidentiary sufficiency and proportionality, for review and approval by the Chief.

- Supports the Chief through the provision of operational briefings, trend information, and case‑related inputs relevant to regional or functional oversight.

- Undertakes and, where appropriate, leads investigative missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including in hardship or hazardous duty locations, providing on‑site leadership and oversight for investigative activities.

- Sets the appropriate professional tone and workplace culture within the team, leading by example through ethical conduct, collaboration, and respect; fosters a culture of constructive, collective problem‑solving, open dialogue, and shared accountability; and actively models and reinforces behaviors that support teamwork, learning, and continuous improvement.

- Performs other duties within the functional profile as required for the effective functioning of the Investigations Section and the Office.

- Plans the work of the HQ/LAC Team and distributes workload among the HQ/LAC Team appropriately.

- Provides senior expertise and advice to the HQ/LAC Team so that the work of the HQ/LAC Team is performed in the most professional, efficient and timely manner.

- Appraises the performance of the HQ/LAC personnel.

- Recruit personnel for the HQ/LAC Team as necessary.

- Leads by example, setting the tone for the HQ/LAC Team. Consciously builds a supportive, collegiate and positive team culture within the HQ/LAC Team.

- Works collectively and professionally with peers to provide thought leadership and constructive challenge to ensure that the HQ/LAC Team is a dynamic, reflective unit that keeps pace with best practice.

- Actively engages and promotes discussions aimed at continued improvement of the HQ/LAC Team and the investigation function, ensuring highest impact and efficient, effective practices.

- Supervises staff and non-staff personnel in the HQ/LAC Team and provides clear, fair, support, and balanced performance feedback and reviews.

- Engages productively, professionally, collaboratively and efficiently with peers, team members, and parties internal and external to the Section to problem-solve as necessary, seek solutions and achieve positive and impactful collective outputs.

- Actively employs management techniques that ensure balance in prioritizing quality output of a high standard and a healthy workplace culture.

- Ensure field work and mission travel, which are mandatory for the position.

Ensure efficient Client Services.

- Maintains a role as a visible, active and accessible team leader, including by liaising with senior officials within the region and bureau; sharing insights from the caseload with senior managers; receiving and considering feedback on OAI investigation services; participating in regional or country level conferences or meetings to raise awareness of fraud and other control risk mitigation services.

- Liaises with the Office of Legal Services (OLS), the Ethics Office, Regional Offices and counterparts, and other relevant offices in UNDP.

- Liaises with the investigation sections of other international organizations and with national anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies as appropriate.

- Where appropriate, provides advisory support to policy managers to help strengthen risk controls within UNDP, drawing on insights gleaned from the caseload.

Facilitate knowledge management and other tasks

- Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within OAI.

- Assesses the potential for misconduct in UNDP offices and operations.

- Contributes to risk assessment planning.

- Participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

- Keeps abreast of the jurisprudence of the United Nations Dispute Tribunal (UNDT) and United Nations Appeals Tribunal (UNAT).

- Performs other assignments or tasks as determined by the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1 and/or Deputy Director (Investigations).

- Contributes to knowledge‑sharing, lessons‑learned, and capacity‑building initiatives within OAI, supporting the strengthening of investigative practice across the Section.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The Central African region is home to the second largest tropical rainforest in the world, is sucking out about 1.5 billion tons of CO2 of the atmosphere or 4% of the world’s emissions every year and provides a habitat to more than 10,000 plant and animal species. Forest loss is accelerating despite ongoing efforts, as government action alone has not been enough to establish an effective balance between the interests of the forest and of economic development. On this basis, a coalition of donors – the European Union, the Federal Republic of Germany, the Kingdom of Norway, the Republic of France, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Republic of Korea – together with Central African partner countries – Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Cameroon, the Republic of Congo, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, and the Republic of Gabon – have decided to enter into a collaborative partnership to establish the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI).

CAFI’s objective is to recognize and preserve the value of the forests in the region to mitigate climate change, reduce poverty, and contribute to sustainable development. This objective will be attained through the implementation of country-led, national scale REDD+ and Low Emissions Development (LED) investment frameworks that include policy reforms and measures to address the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation and promote sustainable development. The CAFI Trust Fund is the principal means to implement the Central African Forest Initiative. It is administered by the MPTF-O, that also provides the Secretariat services. The Congo Basin, home to over 200 million hectares of tropical forest, represents one of the world’s most vital carbon sinks and biodiversity reservoirs. Sadly, the region continues to experience alarming rates of forest loss. Over one million hectares of forest is lost annually, driven by small-scale agriculture, infrastructure expansion, and unsustainable logging practices. Despite its ecological and climate significance, Central African forests receive only 11% of forest climate financing worldwide. This deforestation not only undermines global climate goals but also threatens the livelihoods of over 75 million forest-dependent communities.

3. Scope of Work

This assignment aims to strengthen the CAFI Secretariat’s strategy for policy dialogue & country engagement by addressing the institutional, governance and capacity challenges within the Congo Basin’s forest and climate agenda.

The purpose of this assignment is to support CAFI partner countries in strengthening national and subnational institutions to directly access, manage and implement financing from CAFI and other global environmental and climate funds such as the Green Climate Fund and the Adaptation Fund.

The Institutional Support and Capacity Building Specialist will lead the design, coordination and quality assurance of CAFI support through the direct-access readiness lifecycle from initial gap assessments and systems strengthening to accreditation, pipeline development, compliance and monitoring and continuous improvement. Ultimately, this tailored, country-owned support aims to ensure that partner institutions meet formal eligibility or accreditation requirements and the capacity to manage and implement high-quality investment programmes.

Under the overall guidance of the Chief Policy Dialogue and Country Engagement, the Institutional Support and Capacity Building Specialist will include the following main functions:

1. Lead the Provision of Expert Support for Institutional Capacity Strengthening

• Assess institutional capacity gaps within national and subnational institutions, including government entities, public financial institutions, civil society organizations and other eligible entities seeking direct access to the CAFI Fund or other global environmental funds.

• Support the development and strengthening of policies, procedures and governance frameworks aligned with the CAFI Investment Framework, CAFI policies and procedures, country priorities and, where applicable, the requirements of the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and other global environmental funds.

• Facilitate institutional coordination among ministries, departments and stakeholders, including institutions responsible for forestry, environment, climate, planning and finance, as well as national designated authorities and other entities involved in direct-access processes.

• Analyse institutional, governance and political economy factors that may enable or constrain direct access and the effective implementation of nationally led programmes.

• Contribute to the design and operationalization of national PES institutional frameworks, action plans and roadmaps, where relevant to the investment pipelines and delivery systems of institutions seeking direct access.

2. Ensure Fiduciary Readiness

• Support the development and implementation of fiduciary management systems and capabilities required for national and subnational institutions to directly access, manage and implement financing from the CAFI Fund and other global environmental funds. Areas of support may include;

o Financial management and accounting; budgeting and expenditure control; treasury and cash management; financial reporting; internal and external audit;

o Internal controls; procurement and contract management; grants and asset management; management of executing entities and other recipients; segregation of duties and delegated authorities; risk management; information systems, data integrity and record retention;

o Fraud and corruption prevention; conflict-of-interest management; counterparty screening; anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism; and whistleblower and witness protection.

• Guide and build capacity for institutions in documenting and demonstrating the effective application of their fiduciary systems during eligibility, due diligence and accreditation processes.

• Ensure that proposed institutional improvements are proportionate to each institution’s intended role, financing instruments, programme size, delivery arrangements and risk profile.

3. Development and Implementation of Grievance Redress Mechanisms related to Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSHEA)

• Support the development and implementation of institutional policies, procedures and operational systems relating to:

o Feedback and Grievance Redress Mechanisms; ensuring mechanisms are accessible and effective; and

o Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSHEA); the prevention of and response to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

• Build capacity for institutions to demonstrate the effective application of these mechanisms as part of CAFI eligibility, due diligence and, where applicable, external accreditation processes.

4. Ensure Direct Access, Accreditation and Institutional Readiness

• Under the oversight of the Chief Policy Dialogue and Country Engagement support, support institutional readiness assessments of potential national and subnational implementing entities, financial intermediaries and delivery partners against the requirements of CAFI and, as applicable, the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and other global environmental funds.

• Assess institutions against their proposed role, mandate, financial instruments, project size, environmental and social risk profile, geographic reach, delivery model and implementation arrangements.

• Support candidate institutions in defining realistic and strategically justified pathways to direct access, including their institutional role, accreditation or eligibility scope, intended financing modalities, comparative advantage and priority investment pipeline.

• Translate assessment findings into costed, sequenced and time-bound institutional strengthening plans specifying responsibilities, milestones, evidence requirements, dependencies and residual risks.

• Support institutions in preparing accreditation, eligibility, due diligence and partnership documentation, including evidence mapping, documentary reviews, mock assessments, management responses and the closure of identified gaps.

• Maintain an institutional readiness dashboard and evidence repository for supported entities, with clear version control, confidentiality safeguards and status tracking.

• Liaise with national designated authorities, ministries of finance and environment, fund secretariats, delivery partners and technical assistance providers to ensure country ownership and avoid duplication of institutional support.

• Guide institutions during CAFI eligibility, due diligence processes and, where applicable, external accreditation reviews, including by coordinating responses to follow-up questions, supporting the establishment of legal and institutional arrangements, addressing conditions and operationalizing direct access once secured.

• Monitor changes in the policies, standards and accreditation frameworks of relevant global environmental funds and translate them into practical guidance for CAFI partner countries.

• Support both the achievement and effective operationalization of direct access, recognizing that eligibility or accreditation alone does not ensure the development, financing and successful implementation of national programmes.

• Monitor the implementation of institutional strengthening plans and support institutions in establishing continuous improvement processes following eligibility, accreditation or the establishment of direct-access arrangements.

5. Capacity-Building Management and Knowledge Sharing

• Support the Head of Secretariat, the Programming Team and the Partnership Unit in managing institutional technical assistance and direct-access readiness facilities across the CAFI Trust Fund, ensuring that institutional strengthening and direct-access support are linked to a credible and actionable investment pipeline.

• Conduct baseline studies and capability assessments to identify institutional, organizational and technical capacity gaps in entities seeking to access, manage or implement CAFI and other global environmental financing.

• Design and deliver tailored capacity-building solutions – covering fiduciary, environmental/social safeguards, gender and project management cycles including workshops, training, technical assistance and capacity-building frameworks, to support direct access to the CAFI Fund and, where applicable, the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and other global environmental funds,.

• Develop guidance materials, standard operating procedures, training materials and toolkits related to institutional readiness, direct access, accreditation, fiduciary standards, safeguards, programme development and implementation readiness.

• Coordinate and mobilize specialized technical assistance in key areas, including institutional governance, fiduciary management, environmental and social safeguards, gender, forest governance, emissions-reduction strategies and sustainable land-use planning.

• Support the integration of PES into broader national climate policies and contributions, including nationally determined contributions, where PES forms part of the country’s investment pipeline or proposed delivery systems.

• Advise and support national access entities in identifying, prioritizing and developing forest, climate and environmental programmes or projects aligned with country priorities, CAFI objectives and, where applicable, the investment criteria of other global environmental funds.

• Prepare terms of reference, workplans, budgets and quality standards for specialized institutional capacity-building assignments.

• Monitor the performance of technical assistance providers and ensure that their outputs contribute to agreed institutional readiness and direct-access milestones.

• Assess and ensure candidate entities have, or can establish, adequate implementation arrangements involving executing entities, financial intermediaries, local governments, civil society organizations, Indigenous Peoples, local communities and private-sector partners, as applicable.

6. Promote Stakeholder Engagement

• Contribute to the development of partnership engagement plans across the Secretariat, with particular attention to country-owned direct-access strategies.

• Facilitate engagement and coordination with key stakeholders, including government agencies, development partners, non-governmental organizations, local communities, national designated authorities, candidate national access entities and the secretariats of relevant global environmental funds.

The IPSA shall perform other duties within the scope of this Terms of Reference as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The incumbent will work under the direct supervision of the Chief Policy Dialogue and Country Engagement.

5. Competencies

Expected Demonstration of Competencies Core

Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Business Management - Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business management - Portfolio management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

2030 Agenda - Planet Climate : Climate Strategies and Policy: Policy and Institutional Building

Partnership management - CSO engagement: Knowledge and understanding of CSOs and the ability to engage with CSOs

Partnership management - Relationship management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Finance Due diligence management Ability to conduct a comprehensive appraisal of an organization or opportunity to be undertaken by a prospective investor or partner, especially to establish its assets and liabilities, as well as evaluate the potential opportunity and its related risks; knowledge of respective methodology and tools.

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Academic Education

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental Science, Forestry, Climate Change, Natural Resource Management, Public Policy, Law, Public Administration or a related field, is required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant Work experience

Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in coordination of institutional/political engagement and capacity building activities to high-level and multi-stakeholder platforms, preferably involving national and local government agencies, CSOs, and Donors.

Required skills and competencies

• Experience working in the development sector particularly working with international organizations, national and local government agencies.

• Experience with development and/or improvement, and implementation of fiduciary management systems for funding engagement of interested Parties.

• Experience in developing capacity building programs for government partners.

• Experience in working with the United Nations, including its policies and procedures pertaining to partnership engagement.

• Experience with accreditation to vertical funds or national execution of development programs (either multi or bilateral experience)

Desired additional skills and competencies

• Experience in land use, forests, climate projects.

• Relevant experience in the Congo Basin region.

• Experience in organizing training, organizational development, and strategic planning

• Proven experience managing partner and stakeholder relationships at the national or international level.

• Demonstrated experience of budget management, work planning, monitoring, and reporting.

Required Language(s) (at working level) Fluency in English and French is required.

7. The following documents shall be required from the applicants:

a) Personal CV or P11, indicating all past positions held and their main underlying functions, their durations (month/year), the qualifications, as well as the contact details (email and telephone number) of the Candidate, and at least three (3) the most recent professional references of previous supervisors. References may also include peers.

b) A cover letter (maximum length: 1 page) indicating why the candidate considers him-/herself to be suitable for the position.

c) Managers may ask (ad hoc) for any other materials relevant to pre-assessing the relevance of their experience, such as reports, presentations, publications, campaigns or other materials.
